text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure

Playin' Possum This is a great family friendly game that people of all ages can play. The concept is simple in that you need to just try to anticipate what others will play, sort of like rock-paper-scissors. But this game can have multiple players at a time and last until someone either collects enough winning cards (pieces of garbage) or is the last player standing.
The caveats are that you have the ability to "play it safe", which can avoid getting out if someone accuses you of trying to steal on your turn. This can lead to many rounds where nothing happens as someone needs to steal or accuse of stealing for the game to progress. It is also possible to start feeling repetitive after some time as the gameplay does not allow for much variation to keep it interesting. For what it is, it is a fun quick game that doesn't require a lot of setup or learning. But don't expect it to last a long time before people want to do something else instead.
text_fidelity_b: Playin' Possum

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Silver There have been a number of games based on the the concept of the Golf card game. Like that game, the point of this game is to have the lowest amount of points in your hand while having a number of blind cards that may be high or low. So you need to replace them while possibly and accidentally passing a great card to the next player in the discard pile. Much like Golf, once you think you have the best hand, you call and end to the game and everyone gets one more round to try to improve them hands. If you are lowest, you get zero points, if you are not, you take a penalty.

So that is the basic idea behind the game, but from there, there are many twists to make the game more interesting. Each card has a secret ability to allow you to see the other card in your village (hand.) Also, there is a mechanism to remove duplicate cards which allows you to quickly dump a lot of points from your hand (village.)

The cards are very nice, the amulet is also nice and allows you to lock a great card so that neither you or others can mess with it. The box could be a lot smaller, basically this is a deck game with a single piece for locking a card. you could put it into a box for a pack of hoyles cards.

All in all, an interesting twist on a classic card game concept.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Silver

Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up Kinetic sand is a fun activity for young kids, like regular sand it has tendency to get all over the place if not contained in a tray or plastic dish but it is easy to clean up and unlike play-doh and other similar modeling toys it doesn't ever dry out. This bake shop set comes with a roller and variety of stamps and molds to make cookies and cupcakes which are all nice quality. I especially like that the molds can fit within the roller for easy storage.

The only downside to this set is that kinetic sand is not really ideal for molding since it has a tendency to flow and collapse if not packed very tightly. Our 5 year old was trying to reproduce some of the cupcake designs shown on the box and was getting frustrated because the sand kept falling apart when she added the icing on top of the cupcake base. I tried to do it myself and was able to reproduce the design but it required packing the sand very tightly and then being very delicate when removing from the molds..

We like kinetic sand, and we like the molds that come with this set but we will probably use them primarily with play-doh instead of kinetic sand because these small molds are kind of difficult for kids to use with kinetic sand. We have some other larger ice cream molds that we have used with kinetic sand in the past, they are easier to use because they are smoother and release the sand without requiring such a delicate touch to prevent it crumbling.

GPS Drones, Potensic D50 Quadcopter with Camera Live Video,GPS Return Home, Follow Me, Long Control Range, 5G WiFi Transmission, Great Gift Just a quick note of things you need to know before buying your first drone (and this really is a good choice for a first drone). A drone of this size must be registered with the FAA, and there is a fee associated ($25-$50 for three years -- all prices referenced here are as of the time of this writing). Drones aren't allowed just anywhere, and by "just anywhere" I mean some cities don't let you fly them in your own back yard. They have to be at least 5 miles from an airport, and there are city and state specific regulations. Some entire cities want to be no-fly zones. It's a good idea to check and be sure before you fly.

In New York City, for example, there are five parks in which drones are permitted (none in Manhattan). The best of them, Calvert Vaux Park, requires a membership in the Academy of Model Aeronautics (ModelAviation dot com ) before you can fly there. That organization is recommended by the FAA when you register. Membership will cost from free (for kids) to about $75 a year for the best plan, and that includes liability insurance. Yes, drones can cause damage and if your drone does, you are liable. That's a good resource on where you can and cannot fly and about short term blackouts, such as for public events.

Drones are a learning curve, and classes are very expensive. This particular drone supposedly has a return feature that brings it back to you if the battery is low or if it goes out of range, which is great if you're worried, as I was, about the drone leaving and being lost forever, however the instructions say the remote will beep if the drone is about to go out of range and you need to fly it back or it could fly away and be lost forever. I haven't tested that yet, thankfully, so I'm not sure what to make of it. It has a return button to recall your drone, so long as it's still in range. You can track the GPS of it on the phone as well if that helps and it does have a one key return to call it back. It's a challenge. All drones are. But I find it a little easier than the other few I've had experience with. I'd call it a great first drone for a beginner pilot.

It also has a follow me feature, which basically follows your the controller more or less, which is nice is if you want to go for a run with your drone. Actually, one purpose I had for the drone was to take it on my runs to record my feet, so to watch that I wasn't landing on the side of the foot only to learn I can't have a drone follow me around a random Brooklyn neighborhood. This is great for the extreme sports buff. It can also lock the altitude for easier operation, which is a nice thing. I tend to have problems with drones drifting too high (an issue with my skill, not this drone, but a common issue for new pilots.)

This drone lists as a mini drone, though at 2 pounds it's not like the tiny mini drone that flies only in the house. I'm tempted to try flying this indoors. It seems small enough. It flies for 20 minutes on a charge.
text_fidelity_b: GPS Drones, Potensic D50 Quadcopter with Camera Live Video,GPS Return Home, Follow Me, Long Control Range, 5G WiFi Transmission, Great Gift

It takes a ton of scenes and people from the 1980's, and turns it into a wonderful painted collage.

The quality of the puzzle is top-notch. The pieces are very thick, and so they fit together well. The backing is a nice blue color, so you can easily tell which pieces are upside down. The border is awesome. The puzzle is surrounded by a red and orange line. This makes the border really easy to put together, and it makes it very easy to identify the edge pieces.

I felt entertained and challenged throughout. It's also a great conversation starter, because it has so many iconic people and scenes. I especially liked the Atari, Donkey Kong, Pac-Man, and Mr. T.

text_fidelity_a:
The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games The first TCG I was hooked on was Pokémon, which was about 10 years ago. I grew up with the Pokécraze in the 90s, and still collect the cards. Thankfully, I full unlimited sets of the first three sets. Over time, and of course with life's changes and demands, I stopped playing the game. Thank goodness, too, because what a money sink that can be. I played MtG for a bit, but thankfully convinced myself to stop playing because of the money factor alone. But I still love playing card games because of the physical cards and the resource management. Then I discovered Fantasy Flight's LCGs. I got into tabletop games from Europe before TCGs, so I was familiar with Fantasy Flight. I found out about their Lord of the Rings Card Game when it was first announced, but didn't bother to understand what an LCG was. With the pandemic, my interest in tabletop games peaked, but I still didn't want to get into TCGs. Then I was reminded of this game with the re-release and ordered the Core Set. What a wise choice.

The rules are a beast to master, but they are clear and guide you with a comforting hand without feeling like they're holding your hand like it's a child's. If ever I was confused, all I had to do was look in another section of the manual and my confusion dissipated. To start, the game comes in that oh-so-ever-nice cardboard box Fantasy Flight games are known for. Upon opening, the game greets you with the rule book, an instruction guide, sheets of tokens and build-your-own life counters (Who doesn't live opening those fresh token sheets and popping them out?!) and a plastic insert with the sealed cards. What did I do next? Go to Board Game Geek and look up sweet printables the community made. Using the insert alone, I was able to organize the cards in a utilitarian manner. While the tokens and life counters provided are nice, I used third-party options that I'll explain later below.

Finally, I sat down one night, blocked off two hours, and opened the instruction manual. The manual gives four starter decks to build. I built each played each against the first scenario. The first game took me the full two hours due to the learning curve. There's definitely a lot to keep track of. The game uses some mechanics from other TCGs, but does so in a way that makes it feel like I'm actually in a Middle-earth adventure. Almost like a choose-your-own adventure. Because the game can be played solo, I took my time to absorb every step and read each card's text in full. I know there can be only so much text on the small cards, but the font is *teeny*. The game certainly needs a well-lit table.

After I tested each deck, I moved on to the next scenario, which helped me nearly memorize all the steps. To this day, I sometimes forget a step, so I made my own mini rule book that fits inside a deck box. (By the way, I use an Ultimate Guard Twin Flip'n'Tray, which comfortably holds two decks and the scenario deck--all double-sleeved--a handful of dividers, and two slim life counters.) Once I got to the third scenario, though, I hit a block. Another reason I steered clear from TCGs is the process of deck-building. It's long, tedious, and I just don't want to use what little time and memory I have to maintain decks. Thankfully, the years before the re-release have seen lots of contributions from the community. I recommend going to the game's Subreddit, which provides extremely useful and informative links on deck-building and steps for beginners. With Beorn's Path, I finally found fantastic decks to crush the third scenario--mostly. It's still a monster. Before the third scenario, I was hesitant on using more than one deck while playing solo. Keeping track of all those steps twice intimidated me, but I realized playing the third scenario with just one is impossible and only will cause you torment. Plus, there are mechanics that are available only with more than one deck. Once I confronted my fear, I soon realized how much more fun I was missing out on from using only one deck. The game does a wonderful job at incorporating other players.

The game is fun, but can be frustrating. Some enemies are obscenely strong, and the rules (if followed strictly, which I do) can be unforgiving to follow. Playing a scenario for two hours or more only to lose makes for a frustrating experience. I thought finally beating the third scenario would be cathartic, but it was underwhelming. I won! ...Yay... The only prize was putting all those parts away.

Now for the accessories. If a game has a good following on Board Game Geek, chances are the community will make fun accessories or suggestions of accessories to use. LotR: LCG utilizes turning the cards and tokens to show certain choices made throughout the game. This became a tedious process and quite messy; moving all those parts every step became a burden. Plus, the game needs a *lot* of table space. After consulting the internet and performing my own trials and errors, I've come to the setup in the picture attached to this review.

- d20 for first-player token and round count
- Thin, plastic life counters that I can store in the deck box
- White and black stones for unperformed actions
- Small d6 for anything requiring numbers (life, quest progress, resource, etc.)
- d10 for heads/tails and randomizer
- Wooden card stand for staging area (optional, but helps)
- Large mouse pad for gaming area; I didn't like the large options game companies offer, and found that a large mouse pad met the size I needed and is very inexpensive compared to “official” options
- Deck box trays to hold player cards and unused tokens
- Beverage and edible optional, but strongly recommended

This may seem to cause confusion, but this is what helps me keep track of every possible option in the game without getting lost or having to move a lot of cards/pieces compared to what's in the box. Yes, it adds more cost to the game, but it's completely optional. While this provides what I require for the Core Set, I will amend or append as necessary with each expansion.

I finally found a card game I can play on my own and enjoy without having to pay big bucks.

Note: If any of the review is confusing, please let me know. I never edit my reviews, but am more than happy to help.
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces This retails for about $30. At that price I think it's a great little toy and highly giftable. For whatever reason the price is crazy high on Amazon at the time of this review (about double the retail price). It is not worth nearly $70. That is just crazy.

Going with the retail value, I will review it as a $30 toy.

It does feel a bit flimsy with how the pieces snap in and out of the arena. You may need to help younger kids, and it's best if you really do try to line up the teenie tiny triangle on each piece with the triangle printed on the arena piece. Makes it much easier to snap your fighter in. Also, make sure you cut off the plastic rubber band harnessed around each fighter. Otherwise they are invincible, that was a fun discovery when kiddo went undefeated and we realized it was because his guy couldn't die.

Speaking of kiddo, my son is 9 and LOVES this thing. I was bored in about 10min, but I'm guessing mid-40s mom is not the target demographic. My husband had a bit more fun, and those two really got crazy with it. There does seem to be some technique involved, past just smashing into each other until someone wins. But hey, its how I played Street Fighter back in the 80s, and mashing all the buttons is how I play Akedo in 2021.

Also, the numbers on the pieces for offense and defense are pointless. Some fighters are just better, there isn't any way around it. The defensive pieces usually just mean you will never land an attack and are pointless.

TL;DR: for the $30 the kid loves it. I could see this being a popular birthday party gift.
text_fidelity_b: Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Party Board Game "Logo Party" gives players the chance to guess famous logos in a variety of ways. Depending on what type of card you draw, you will try to have other players guess the logo by drawing the clues (like Pictionary), acting out the item (as in Charades), or describing the brand (like the old game show "Pyramid".) Players have twenty seconds to guess the brand from the clues provided. Each team has a token to move around the board and try to get to the end first by guessing more brands than the other team. The game includes a tablet for the drawing clues and a box to hold the cards during play and for storage. Unfortunately, the box is too small and the cards don't fit well.

The game is designed for four or more players divided into two teams. The recommended ages are listed as eight and up, but most eight-year-olds would be unfamiliar with many of the brands featured in the game. In fact, even older teens and adults won't know some of these brands. Also, I would call some of the items products and not brands. For example, one of the "brands" is Chicken McNuggets (as opposed to McDonald's.)

The game is somewhat fun, but would be much better with a large group of people. My family found it almost impossible to act out most of the brands, but it was funny to see people try to act things out like "Tupperware". With more people, I'm sure it would be even funnier.

Throughout the boards, there are spaces called, "Reveal It". When landing on this space, players from both teams try to guess a brand by looking at the logo. This is also how the winner is ultimately determined when teams reach the end of the game board. The timer that comes with the game doubles as a holder for these cards. The card starts out fully covered and then parts of the brand are slowly revealed. This is a clever idea, but it's hard to place the card in the holder without looking at. Also, it makes an annoying buzzing sound (like the sound of a small wind-up toy.) Because of the sound, we used a different timer during regular play and saved the timer for the "Reveal It" cards.

The game would be more fun for a large group of people. My family had some fun playing "Logo Party", but got bored after a while since some of the brands were unknown to some of the players and it was hard to act out the brands and actually get someone to guess them.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Mix BY HAND all ingredients, except flour and chips (mixing by hand makes them taste better, trust me).
Then add flour and chips and stir BY HAND. Bake @ 350 for 9-11 minutes on ungreased cookie sheet. Enjoy the preciouses.

Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary Ok. Here's the deal. If you actually order and receive the Elefun version produced with/through Hasbro as the current item listed as of this date shows, here's the real review by an adult:

There are 10 monkeys in a barrel. It is listed on the plastic, throw away wrapping. And that's what you get from this brand. 10. Each barrel has ten color corresponding monkeys.
About the monkeys: they are durable and not flimsy. The monkey's tails are part of the body and are not useable. All monkeys are the same mold.....BUT there are 2 each of different facial expressions. This is not so easy to notice while playing but yes, the monkeys are in facial pairs. All monkeys are the same size.

Now.....lol....from a serious player (lol) that grew up with the 60s, 70s versions: these monkeys have....two arms....one arm is bent closer to the head so it's open loop is a tad smaller. Meaning....it makes a differnece in how easy or hard it is to link them. Also....the hand shape....well....it isn't as pointed and hook like as it was years ago. So yes....it is harder and I think that's a reason there is only 10 now.

Is it fun? Yes. Worth the money?? To me....because a fast food meal costs this much. And replayablity is very high. Also....you can buy two and do color challenges. Or time two players....or lots of creativity to play.

I would rather have a reproduction of the original. BUT these are functional and in my honest review, more difficult to chain over 7; making for more competition.

I think this is a good product for children, teens, families and elderly.

**I also think this could help anyone with motor skill issues or be good for even Alzheimer persons who enjoy things simple and close up.

This is a good product.
text_fidelity_b: Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Entomologist Doll and Playset, Blonde, with 20+ Accessories Inspired by National Geographic ... and my girls' too! (Ranging in ages 5-10).

PROs:
--product received is exactly as pictured (we all know online toy purchases can be a gamble)
--the 10 tiny bug pieces included in the kit (which my kids would usually lose within a week) are kept perfrctly in place because they attach practically anywhere upon the included tree, flowers, rock, puddle, and leaves (and are also removeable) so Barbie can also take them to her "lab desk" later to study under the microscope.
--The accessories included were very well-thought out (for example, there is an area on the tree where a butterfly emerges from a cocoon, various pollinators that can "help" the flowers, and Barbie can gather the bugs from the tree and take them back to her "lab desk" to study under the microscope). In other words... this is a VERY "open-ended toy," and as such, would be also be appropriate for learning environments (I homeschool two of my children and also substitute teach preschoolers so open-ended toys that encourage imagination and learning are a MUST)
--Tree and desk are both sturdy enough to stand up without support
--The concept itself is pretty innovative and yet simple: STEM-toy-meets-Barbie is really the best of both worlds and can help encourage a love of science (science IS glamorous and Barbie is gonna prove it haha)
--In my personal experience, it is autism friendly, ADHD friendly, and even adolescent-friendly (I have all 3, and they are having a blast with this toy as we speak)
--a great gift for both kids and classrooms

CONS:
--Yes, this Barbie is high quality (it'll never be mistaken for any Dollar Tree knockoffs) but do keep in mind that this is Entomologist Barbie, NOT Yoga Barbie lol. So tiny fingers might need adult help dressing/accessorizing her.
--Barbie does not stand on her own without support (as is the case for most Barbies).
--no caterpillars included (not complaing because there are 10 bugs in the kit, including the cocoon that turns into a butterfly which was an awesome surprise. But a catepillar in the kit would have been SUPER helpful for helping explain metamorphisis.) All in all, this product is well-thought out, and certainly the coolest Barbie that my "geeky science mom self" has ever come across, so in my book it still deserves 5 stars and honestly more if I could.

If you're on the fence about purchasing this for your budding scientist who happens to love Barbies, go ahead and be the hero and take the plunge.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Entomologist Doll and Playset, Blonde, with 20+ Accessories Inspired by National Geographic

Having found a work-around so I could use white substrate, I find this decal material relatively easy to use and can say the end result is quite suitable.

Here's what produced the best results:
1) Printed the images (inkjet Epson ET) and let them dry at least over night.
2) Sprayed them with one coat Krylon Crystal Clear Acrylic Coating, and let that dry for an hour or so. Acrylic clear coat is essential to getting a high quality finished result.
3) Applied a second coat of the Krylon and let is dry for about an hour.
4) Cut the images very close to remove as much of the white backing as possible.
5) Placed the decal in water with the backing side in the water. The edges curled up and I had to hold them flat for a few seconds to get the decals to lay flat in the water.
6) When the edges of the decal substrate (what the image is printed on) began to curl away from the backing sheet, I removed the backing sheet with the now loosened decal from the water and gently slid the decal off the backing sheet and onto my project surface.
7) Patted the decal gently with tissue to remove excess water from under and around the decal.
8) Set the project aside and allowed all moisture to dry. This assures the decal is set onto the piece.
9) Sprayed the project with two top coats of Krylon, with about two hours between spraying. This assures the decal is not easily scratched or marred.

What DID NOT WORK was floating the decal design side down in the water. This wets the Krylon coat too much and when you slide the decal off the backing and onto the project, some ink leeches out into the water and moist Krylon creating a slimy, grayish muck and tends to ruin the graphic.

I also searching for another brand that offers more and larger sheets for just a little more money.
text_fidelity_b: Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201)

Kid is off playing with the very small toy car that comes with the kit, but doesn't look like it belongs at all.

This is a lot like Spot it in that regards, where a 7 year old can compete fairly well with a 47 year old once everyone knows what they are looking for. The reaching for the bell is kinetic enough to engage kids to make them want to be the first to slam the ringer, and the rules are so easy they can immediately be digested. The action is fast and again engaging, and we had a lot of laughs with the came, and surprisingly few injuries and fights.

The game in its simplest form is almost too easy, but it lends itself to more and more levels of complexity. There are three variables, numbers, color (8 or more) and a shape. You can play complex combos like match a shape and a number, or two numbers must add up to ten and there needs to be a match. Instant ring it and visually similar don't ring it cards cause quick victories as well as quick penalties.

This is a perfect game to pull out for some quick games. The container holds all the pieces and makes it wonderfully portable. The parts are decent quality and I expect it to hold up well.

text_fidelity_a:
Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray) For my daughter's sake, I would give this camera 5 stars. It is the longest lasting favorite toy any of my kids have ever received, EVER. I bought it for my then 7 year old daughter for Christmas 2 years ago, and it is still her very favorite toy at age 9. She plays with it almost daily, takes it with her on trips and to important events, and shows everyone the pictures she takes. I think not much more praise can be had for a toy than for it to be beloved after two full years of daily play! But I wills say, her expectations for it are different than mine. She doesn't care about printing the pictures out. She likes taking them and looking at them on the viewfinder, projecting them on the wall, and using the added features to make funny frames around the people and funny sounds. That's all she wants from it, and it delivers that perfectly.

BUT, as a parent, I would have hoped the screen would be better quality. When you look at it, it's sort of blurry and got lines through it. Frankly, sometimes it's hard to tell what I'm looking at. This doesn't bother my now 9 year old daughter AT ALL. But it is disappointing to me because I know the technology exists to make that better.

The quality of pictures is also not great when uploaded onto my computer (which I've only done a couple of times). It's VERY pixelated. Again, this isn't a feature my daughter cares about, so take that into account, but for me I wish that the option were there to print out a decent quality print because sometimes she takes really awesome shots that I wish I could save.

This camera is also super tough. Despite being dropped and thrown around and fought over by siblings for the last 2 years, it still works perfectly. The batteries last her generally a few months, depending on play. But they're just AA's, so no biggie to change them out.

Really, I am most impressed that this toy continues to make her so happy. I think Playskool could go a long way to making the picture/screen quality better, even for kids, but that's just a mom talking!
text_fidelity_b: Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray)

text_fidelity_a:
ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs This set consists of thirteen #1 bags for Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes (the purple and orange building), eight #2 bags for Flourish and Blotts (the green and brown building), one bag of plates, instructions, and a small sticker sheet.

The bags are not numbered individually. Trust me, open all the bags for a building. So all #1 bags or all #2 bags. You’ll need a lot of space for the pieces, but it’s less frustrating in the long run. Steps require pieces from every bag as you go. Finding the pieces for each step took the longest part of this build.

The instructions are mostly clear*, but the build experience itself is frustrating. Some pieces stay together and some do not. I spent so much time rebuilding because a section would break when I put new pieces on. For example, the window section for WWW, I had to test window pieces to see which would stay together and then stay on the building. For the upper window section, where the arms come out, I had to redo that three or four times, carefully holding the windows together.

*Step 64 has the wrong pieces, there is a sheet to show the proper pieces.

The buildings are delicate. On my Flourish and Blotts building, the bottom barely stays together, so I can’t take it off the base. The buildings are hollow inside, so you can hide items. The F&B building has a tray inside, and the WWW building has a rod to use to pop the tray out. If I popped the tray out, I’d have to put the F&B building back together. I don’t care for the hiding space, I’d prefer buildings that were more stable, especially if they’re supposed to be bookends.

Some of the stickers go over multiple pieces, one sticker on 2 or 3 pieces. The Dark Mark sticker is misspelled: DRRK MRRK.

Overall, the finished set looks good, but getting to that finished set was a somewhat frustrating experience.
text_fidelity_b: ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs

4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi This is a "dig kit", which I didn't realize when I got it. My oldest has a huge obsession with dinosaurs, and they are all his brain thinks about, so I thought a dinosaur DNA kit looked like something cool for him. It's really just a dig kit, though, with some added features that require a smart phone. Honestly, we just skipped all that, and used it as a simple dig kit. Even then, we'd already did a couple of them just before this one, so the whole digging process had become a little old for him.

Aside from that, it's an okay kit. The quality of the items to dig out usually aren't great, and this was no exception. My son has had trouble getting all the pieces to stick together as they should with all the dinosaur dig kits he's ever had, and again, this one was no exception. He became a little frustrated at some of the pieces.

If you've never used a dig kit before, they're messy! We've found them to be slightly less messy done inside a pie pan. Even so, outside is always better with these things(on a warm, windless day). Also, they require patience. This one wasn't near as hard to dig through as some of the other ones we've had, but it's definitely not the easiest, either. I'd say it's a medium level on hardness. It takes time to get all the pieces, and that's part of the process. It teaches a young person a bit of what it's like for archaeologists. If they rush the dig, they end up damaging pieces.

Overall, this is a fun little lesson in patience, for both children and adults, but it wasn't quite what I was expecting.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories There are really only two things one need know about any Schleich product in my experience.
1) They’re a bit pricey.
2) You get what you pay for.

The brand oozes quality and that holds true with the barn as well. It’s compact, well-made of quality material, and is smoothly fluid in all its moving parts. It comes hinged together and easily opens up to reveal a nice size play area. The wood is real and solid, the paint job nicely finished. The windows, corral doors, and back door open and close smoothly and easily, and the large doors in the back slide open and shut, also smoothly and easily. It comes with a large cow, a lamb, a donkey, and a rooster, each of them quite solid and hefty in the hand. And again, nicely finished and detailed. A few accessories complete the package--a bale of hay, a crate of apples, a pitchfork and a broom.

Really, as mentioned at the start, there isn’t much to say about Schleich beyond the fact that quality quality quality is the mantra. Based on our experience with other Schleich products, I imagine this barn and its animals will give years of imaginative play regardless of how often or how hard that play is. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

When I was a kid, I thought they were the coolest things. Sign of the times I guess. Plus, we have a swimming pool, so not much space in the backyard to play rc cars. So when I saw this boat, it was a must try! The packaging, the unknown brand, the Styrofoam, everything was nostalgic. Because it reminded me of those toys you would find at downtown swap-meets, or Chinatown. LOL! But I must say, it works very well. When I want it to turn, it turns, it is very accurate. I like making it go in circles. One last thing I'll mention, there is a clear plastic piece that seemed important because it was in its own little bag. The instructions didn't talk it and for the longest time, I didn't know what it was for. When I went to take pictures for this review, it became obvious... it's a stand for the boat. LOL! I was going to knock a star for pricing, but then I decided to do a little research first, and I realize these things aren't cheap. This is as low as it gets on Amazon for a decent size boat. So I give it 5 stars.

Regarding accessing the battery...
---------------------------------------
You might find that the seat cover is too difficult to remove. You'll have to yank it out the first time. But after you do, you can loosen the screw for the black tab to make it easier on you the next time. We've been pulling it several times now, and I can start to see the stress in the plastic. Loosening the screw makes it a lot easier. Look at the last picture.

LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces) Because I love all LEGO building kits for heavy construction equipment (e.g., [[ASIN:B07Y8T4WHC LEGO Mobile Crane]]), I couldn’t resist this cute little LEGO DUPLO MY FIRST TOW TRUCK 10918 (New 2020 (6 Pieces)). It’s absolutely charming, all 6 pieces of it!

I really like the drivers’ windows, with a boy on one side and a girl on the other. It makes this into a truly unisex toy. I love the big blue traffic cone that fits between the drivers’ cabin and the moveable crane for transport. Tow trucks always set out traffic cones, for safety, when they’re readying a tow. The crane itself is fun because it swings up and down freely.

The building instructions are on the outside of the retail box. The toy takes about 30 seconds for an adult to assemble, as the wheels are already attached to the truck base. When the toy is finished, it makes a terrific truck for general play. The wheels turn freely, and the truck feels solid and satisfying when it’s pushed around.

Inside the box is a printed city street layout. The paper is very thin, so this won’t last long unless it’s glued to some sort of heavier backing. However the street layout fits the assembled tow truck, and is a nice detail.

Note that this is a LEGO duplo model, intended for very young children. The pieces are much larger than standard LEGO pieces. They are compatible with other duplo building sets, but NOT with standard LEGO elements.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces)

It's a great way to teach a little independence, and give this mama a moment of peace. ;) It's also been great for organizing projects for my 3 year old to work on while his older brothers do schoolwork. My goal has been to simplify for more peace, and this little kit has been a blessing in that goal.

Of course, you can use the portfolio to organize finished projects, but I typically throw stuff like this in the garbage after the newness has worn off. I only keep the more original, creative things my children create, and these project aren't original or overly creative. Sometimes easy projects like this are just what a child(and mommy/daddy/other person in charge) needs, though, and I appreciate having them around.

It will hold paper or shapes or buttons without the worry and mess of glue.) It also comes with various shapes and sizes of paper for sticking on pages, colors, buttons, and stickers. *Note: In one of the other kits from Alex Jr., the whole sticky part came off while trying to pull the paper off. My kids were disappointed, but that page can then just be used as a sticker page or coloring page. My youngest two highly prefer the sticky pages, though!

Overall, this is a nice kit! It's been a blessing to have a few "busy" projects around.

Parentswell Inflatable Mermaid Pool Floats, 71'' Swimming Pool Tube Mermaid Floaties, Huge Pool Float for Adults, Mermaid Swim Tubes for Pool Party Lounge Birthday Gift Having an inground pool means constantly looking for ways to enhance the experience. We don’t do much actual swimming in our pool. We mainly hang out and float, so having pool floats is a necessity. A recent addition to our backyard recreation was this inflatable Mermaid Pool Float from Parentswell.

Pulling this float from the package and unfolding it, you can see that it’s going to be larger than most, and it is. The lengthy tail is the reason. Inflating it will require a powerful set of lungs, since it is larger than average. I didn’t have a suitable pump for mine, so I did have to inflate the old- fashioned way. Once inflated, it was ready to test in the pool. The opening in the middle is narrow enough that you can either lie on top of the float without worry that you will fall through. Or, you can stick your body through the center and wear the float, as you drift around in your pool. It works as well as any and the mermaid design is certainly cute. In fact, I would say that the cuteness factor is possibly it’s strongest point. It will be a huge hit with anyone who love mermaids.

Pools are better when you have things to enhance the experience. This float from Parentswell is a good one overall. It can take time to inflate but once ready, it holds its own and it does look cute inside my inground pool.

text_fidelity_a:
Learning Resources STEM Explorers Geomakers - 58 Pieces, Ages 5+ STEM Toys for Kids, Kindergartner Learning Toys, Shapes for Kids My son and I love Learning Resources toys. I have purchased several items from them over the years. My son thinks he's just playing, but he's actually learning at the same time. Additionally, this kid is super into science and math since he wants to be a robotics engineer. (A decision made at the ripe old age of 6.) So, I will jump that the chance to add anything to his toy collection which will facilitate that.

Learning Resources, Geomakers, seemed like a great idea. Upon opening the package, my son immediately got to work. He started creating all kinds of shapes and things from his imagination. He made a "vision scanner," a dinosaur jaw, a tent. When you open the box there are 58 pieces total. 30 sticks in 3 different lengths, 12 curved sticks, and 16 connector spheres. The stick are all plastic and are not bendable. The spheres, which feel like rubber, have holes in them to put the sticks in. The set has a pamphlet that shows you how to make various types of objects most 3D prisms.

Cons:

It would be nice if these were laminated cards for durability.

Needs more building ideas.

The age on the box says 5+, but I would suggest this is a 4+ toy. Younger kids may not want to build what is on the pamphlet, but they can let their imagination run wild like my son, who also made a crown with this set. However, my son will be 7 soon and seems like he will age out of this quickly.

Pros:
The box that it came it was a little banged up, but otherwise it appears durable and holds all the pieces nicely. Most importantly, the stick stay inside the box and do not poke out.

I will say that my son wanted to stay up and play with this for longer and well past his bedtime. He was very interested in how many different shapes he could make.

Good for kids who hate coloring and drawing, but you want them to physically manipulate something to understand shapes.

So, three stars because the age range suggestion seems a bit high and I am uncertain of how much use my son is going to get out of this set.
text_fidelity_b: Learning Resources STEM Explorers Geomakers - 58 Pieces, Ages 5+ STEM Toys for Kids, Kindergartner Learning Toys, Shapes for Kids

Fisher-Price 3-in-1 Bounce, Stride and Ride Elephant A good toy for toddlers, the Fisher Price 3 in 1 Bounce, Ride and Stride Elephant helps youngsters develop while having fun. The toy lets then bounce, ride, and walk along as they listen to the sounds and enjoy the light up buttons and songs.

This toy is intended for toddlers under the age of 3 and most will take to it right away. Those on the younger side will like bouncing more than anything while those toward the upper end of the recommended age range will like riding and pushing. My youngest child is outside of the recommended age range, but she is lightweight for her age and liked riding the most. It takes a little bit of effort, but with just a small amount of leg power, young children can push themselves along without any assistance.

Kids will love the sounds and lights that are part of this toy. The good news for parents is that you can shut off the sounds- a feature you don’t always get with similar toys. This is nice for adults who get impatient with the constant sounds coming from kids’ toys. In truth, the sound isn’t that loud or that bad with this toy, but it’s nice to know that it can be shut off, if desired.

A toy that encourages activity, keeps kids interested, and helps them develop has all the makings of a keeper and this toy is just that. The price could turn some people away, but it’s not too bad and the fun and other advantages make this toy worth the money.

text_fidelity_a:
VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version Kids like to do grown- up things and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera allows them to do just that. This is a fully- functioning camera specifically designed for the needs and desires of youngsters and it allows kids to take pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even upload them to a computer for further viewing and editing.

Many qualities make this camera one to consider and the first is the memory. This is sold as a child's camera, but it has a surprisingly high level of memory and is capable of holding up to 400 pictures! This is much better than I expected and with this much memory, it will take a long time before kids exceed the available space. They can walk around the house ansd snap picture after picture without worrying that the memory will fill.

Another positive aspect with the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is its durability. This camera is made from plastic with a rubberized edge that makes it easy to hold and highly resistant to breakage. My girls have dropped it several times and it continues to work regardless. It is also very entertaining. Not only can kids take their own pictures of mom, dad, the family dog, and their friends, but they can also add to the fun by using the editing feature. The silly editing allows kids a chance to take an ordinary picture and make it look funny.

So, the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is fun for kids, but are there any cons? Well, there are a few but they are minor enough to overlook. One is the viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is quite small and some images will be barely perceptible. It would be completely unacceptable to adults, but kids will likely find it perfectly fine. Then, one has to consider the picture quality. This camera has only 0.3 megapixels and that means the clarity of the pictures is well below average. Once again, kids are not likely to care. They will so enjoy having their own camera and taking their own pictures that they won't even notice or mind the fuzzy images.

Kids like to mimic adults and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is likely to be a hit with most youngsters for this and other reasons. As I said, the clarity of the photos isn't the best and the camera does have a few other minor flaws, but none of this will matter to most children. The ability to take their own pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even view them on a computer will be more than enough to please the young camerabug in your home.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version

text_fidelity_a:
Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive First the good.
I shot light rapids in this puppy on the Blackfoot River in Montana. The collapsibility makes it easy to bring even if you don't have a pickup truck. You could put several in a compact car. You can blow it up with your own lungs in under five minutes, easily. It has good back support, very comfortable. The nylon cover protects from rocks. The foot rest and low profile give unparalleled maneuverability in rapids. You can get your arms deeper into the water than a traditional tube and the brace your feet on the foot rest to keep your seat when the ride gets wild. The handles allow you to stay in when it gets hectic. I got dumped once and because I was holding the handles, I was able to spin in a downhill rapid and shove it underwater and back under my tuchas to regain my seat.
It has all the advantages of an innertube and a kayak with the comfort of a recliner. The cup holder is also handy.
The bad:
The mesh is flimsy. All they need to do is use the stuff that more common blue and white float tubes use and they have a far better product. I got two small holes going over rocks. That doesn't happen with the blue and white tubes.
Fortunately, I can sew. I'm going to get some better mesh and pimp my floaty!
text_fidelity_b: Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive

Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games For this game, you really need to know what you're getting.

This is a strategy deckbuilding game with a lot of silly, and a little stupid. And if you're OK with a lot of silly and a little stupid, you will probably love Challengers! if you have a even number of players.

In Challengers, you are deckbuilding in preparation for a game of War. Yes, that game of War where you mindlessly turn over cards and hope for high numbers, even knowing that there are a bunch of low numbers in your deck.

The only player choice is made during the deckbuilding phase, and then you get to sit back and watch the chaos.

And if you're OK with a chaotic game like this, where choices are limited and it's all down to luck, then you've found a winner with Challengers! If you think this sounds like a waste of time, then for you, it probably is. We had a few stand up and cheer come-from-behind moments and a lot of inglorious losses.

This is a great deckbuilding intro for kids, and for the grownups with the right tastes, this will be a hit, but I think a lot of people will absolutely hate it also.
text_fidelity_b: Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games

All in all, this is a set that could make a nice gift for a Minecraft and/or Lego fan.

I wasn’t expecting such a large finished figure, but it’s big! The mech is almost as big as the box, if you include the translucent green “wings.”

The mech is a good size for kids to be able to grab easily for play, without having to be super careful. Unlike some of Lego’s more fragile sets, this one won’t lose pieces easily.

The mech balances reasonably well, and has enough articulation to be posed, so it could also work as a display piece.

I do wish the back of the mech had more detail and wasn’t quite so flat, but the front is almost cool enough to make up for that. The streamlined look of the armor, and the use of sand green, gold, and even some printed pieces is pretty cool. I also wish the head of the mech had some protection for Lloyd.

I like the detail on the armor of the included minifigs. Quite frankly, they just look cool!

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos A Column of Fire: The Game When I first asked my family if I should get this game, they were not quite sure what to think. We went and looked at a bunch of videos and it looked really good. So, I ordered it. Then I watched a few more videos and wondered.. did I make a mistake?

WHAT IS THIS GAME LIKE?
This game is based upon a book. I have not read the book so if you are concerned that might affect your like of this game, keep in mind that I had no idea about this series of books, so it did not affect game play for me.

The game comes with a board that folds into a fourth of its size- a real plus for storage. It has a plastic storage area which holds all of the pieces- and yes, there are pieces. You press out the cardboard pieces so that you can keep them to play the game in the future. It is not hard to do and they pressed out cleanly.

There are cards and several sets of dice. Each player gets a set of dice. Maximum players are four. You can play successfully with two players.

HOW IS THE GAME TO LEARN?
I have to admit when we got the game, I was overtired, and very frustrated as it was. When one of our kids wanted to play, I was so afraid that I made a mistake and would hate this game. It really overwhelmed me. I could not make heads or tails of the instructions, and when trying to watch videos, well ,I was SURE I made a mistake in choosing this game.

Finally our child said, "How about we just try to play and walk through it?" I was not in the mood, but knew I had to test this out.

So... out came the very detailed instruction booklet. The beginning to set it up did not take too long, but it was not starting to make sense yet. I was not thrilled. Then as we read each move and worked through it, I was having a headache.

I kept with it, and about a half hour into the game, suddenly it all began to make sense. Then suddenly, I was enjoying it. In fact, I could not wait to play it again!

WHO MIGHT LIKE THIS GAME?
My kids who liked this were early teens and above range. It is really beautifully rendered, the cards and pieces are interesting, and the board itself is really nice to look at. It needs to be played at a nice table with room on it- like you might use for Monopoly or Life.

I would say that anyone who enjoys history, games that have purpose, and home educators might enjoy playing this game. It is not boring, nor is it a thrill ride, but it is a nice entertaining game that is interesting and did keep my attention.

If someone has an overabundance of energy and can not sit still unless entertained by a screen in constant motion, this might not work out for them. If someone has patience and enjoys artworks and interesting things (like playing with Legos or other similar things) this might be a game to try out for them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite being a bit overwhelmed at first, once we plunged into the game, after a little while, I found it fun, interesting to play and found myself looking forward to playing it over again which is the same sentiment from the rest of the family as they have played it too.

MY RATING
Five stars for this. If you watch videos, don't get too overwhelmed, just plunge in and play it as a learning experience and it will suddenly click and off you go. I have to say it is one of the limited number of board games that make me want to play again and I look forward to it.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos A Column of Fire: The Game

Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up We tried this recently on a rainy evening, and it was a fun family activity. However it feels like some things weren't fully thought through and could have been easily made better.
For example, the spinner needle feels like it stops exactly on the line more than half the time, causing much arguing and debate over which side it actually landed. If you have ever played the game Life or used a spinning prize wheel, you know there is a much better way to do this: Have plastic borders that catch on the needle so it stops in one space clearly (and makes a cool motor noise as it click-click-clicks quickly). Once you're making giant playing pieces and a large floor mat board, this would not have added a lot of cost and would have made the game infinitely more fun and smooth to play.
And speaking of giant playing pieces, once you assemble them, they don't fit back in the box unless you break them apart, something that probably won't last if you do it every time you put the game away. It could have come with a bag or something to store the game board and pieces in. As of now, I'm pretty sure the pieces and board are going to get separated from each other in our family room. It's a fun game, but unlike giant versions of Jenga, Connect Four or Chess, the novelty of giant Sorry wears off quickly and at some point my mother-in-law actually asked why we can't just play it on the table like a regular game. It's fun for the novelty, but the caveats and game mechanics make this not worth more than 3 stars in my opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up

Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit I thought this would be a cool activity to do with my 6 year old. She LOVES crafts, and I actually bought a coloring "stained glass" art book by Klutz for her in the past (which she loved)
It was a little hard to tell exactly what the process was of making them just by looking at the pictures, and It was actually a bit more difficult than I assumed.

So you take the colored film paper, trace the shape out of the book, cut it out, then place it on the sticky paper to puzzle all the colored pieces together like a mosaic, to make up the whole picture. You youths choose to do them any color you want, but the more colors you use to make up the picture, the more patience and precision you will need.
We started off simple with the strawberry (only 2 colors) which was pretty easy.
I went to apply the puff paint and it would not come out of the top of the tube. I tried to cut the nozzle down, squeeze it out slow which ended in it coming out the side of the bottle, and getting all over my fingers. It was so thick, I assumed it got semi dried out, so I threw it away to prevent any further mess.
Since we were unable to use the puff paint, my daughter outlined the strawberry with black sharpie. Unfortunately without the puff paint, the film paper is pretty flimsy.
Even though we did not get the full effect of the project, we still had some fun doing the craft together.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll I have been around Barbie dolls my entire life. My mom collected them and my sister got into it. My daughter has had a few here and there, but none of them was the quality that this doll is. I did not expect it to be fantastic quality, but it even fell short of my lower expectations.

WHAT IS THE DOLL LIKE?
The doll comes in a clear plastic package which is not overly attractive, in fact it looks stark and not like the usual Barbie stuff. The doll itself is packaged with two pieces of plastic sticking out from inside her head. It is then attached to the board in the back so you have to cut those pieces to get it off of the backing. That means you have to be careful of the hair. Once you managed to do this, you have to stick the plastic ends back into the skull of the doll to keep the sharp ends from pricking your child or you.

The outfit is kind of cute and the colors are attractive. The doll itself is a rigid plastic doll- not the bendable twist and turn type that they have had in the past. The head piece has a knob type attachment which makes it able to move in almost any direction. The problem is in this case, the head is so easy to move it is borderline bobble head.

HOW DOES THE HAIR COLOR WORK?
The hair color looked like it would be a lot of fun! It has a plastic piece that is similar to a flat iron in shape. Inside the *flat iron* piece are a group of colored waxy blocks. The idea is that you comb the doll's hair and separate it into strands. You press the flat iron type piece over the hair, squeeze it shut as you draw the hair through and it leaves the color on the hair.

The hair is waxy in feel, probably to make the color work better than traditional Barbie hair. In this case, however, it does not seem to do much for the process. The hair colors are not too great. They come off as crumbly and waxy and very spotty on the hair. If you run your fingers over it, you will get some on your fingers. This will stain so if your child plays with this near anything white or light colored, it could stain it.

The color blocks are almost like you mix waxy crayons with silicone to make it a bit softer. The result is uneven kind of unimpressive color on the hair. It is not overly bright and does not look like the pictures promised.

THE BOTTOM LINE
My daughter was not impressed by this doll. The body is very rigid, making for a boring play toy. The hair is very uneven and has a waxy feel to it. The colors come out crumbly and uneven, and color blocks probably will only last for a day or two of constant play and then run out. The colors will stain some things so if you plan to let your child run free with this, you may regret it if you have anything white you don't want stained. The head is so easily moved that it is unpleasant to play with and use. The outfit is cute and colorful and the shoes are not too bad either.

My daughter kept saying that she expected more substantial color that was like a watercolor marker or something instead of a crumbly waxy substance that barely sticks to the hair in a few random spots. She kept taking out her other Barbie dolls and saying how much more she liked those. I give this two stars because it has a nice outfit, and if you want a disposable toy for your child, it will serve the purpose. If you want a sturdy toy they will play with over and over, I am thinking this might not be it for you.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

Tektalk 1000 Piece Puzzle Jigsaw Puzzle for Teens & Adults (Budapest) I'm not sure why "Easy to assemble" is a feature for a jigsaw puzzle. It's a puzzle. Is five stars "this took a while and I had a lot of fun" or "this practically assembled itself"? But I digress. The tricks to assembling this are actually one of the more interesting features about this.

The back of the puzzle has the areas laid out with letters printed A - H. A is the top left.D is the top right. E is the bottom left. H is the bottom right. So there are a few things you can do with this information.

First, split the groups up, one letter in a pile or even a baggie. If you have kids, you can assign letters per kid so they won't argue about who stole whose piece or who is hogging pieces. If you don't, you can work the puzzle a section at a time to take up less room and make it easier.

Second, if you want it even easier, orient the pieces based on the letter on the back. Now you don't have to turn the piece or visualize it upside down or sideways to know if it fits. If you have a slot for a piece that has a protrusion to the top and a cavity to the left, you only need look for that and ignore anything with a cavity on top but a protrusion on the bottom. It's not the right piece upside down.

The pieces are well made. No funny bits of cardboard torn, sticking out, and no damaged pieces. Assembled it looks beautiful.

It's not terribly giftable only because there is no picture on the top of the box. It's small on the side, and then inside there is kind of a perforated poster you can take apart with each panel mapping to the letters. It should probably have the letters listed on the panels, otherwise it's hard to figure out who should get which panel if you're splitting things up. But since you've read this far you know the layout.

This amused two adults for most of a day. That's about all one could ask of a puzzle. I liked it.
text_fidelity_b: Tektalk 1000 Piece Puzzle Jigsaw Puzzle for Teens & Adults (Budapest)

KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S) This is yet another variation of the "Boogie Board" drawing tablet. If you are not familiar with the concept, it is NOT a digital tablet, but essentially a reusable drawing tool much like a whiteboard. It starts off as an opaque black surface that reveals a different color underneath with pressure. So you can draw on it using the included pen, a fingernail, or anything with enough pressure really, and then erase it all at once with the erase button on the bottom. The only electronics involved is a battery that "zaps" the display back to opaque to start over. This battery should last years as it only gets used when erasing for a split second.
I actually like this one better than some of our other ones as the contrast between the black and revealed color is quite high. Some of the inexpensive Boogie Board clones lack contrast and can be hard to see sometimes, but that is not the case here. It also seems to have a multi-colored background, so as you draw or write, it feels like the color is changing (really it is just revealing a different part of the material behind the LCD). I also really like the size of it, as our other drawing tablets were small whereas this one feels closer to a sheet of paper. My 12 year old son actually finds this comfortable for using as a scratch pad for his math homework, which is a great environmentally friendly alternative to scrap paper. And my younger kids like drawing pictures on it or playing games like tick-tack-toe.
You do have to be a little bit careful about resting your hand on it as it seems even that amount of pressure will leave a mark, and sadly you can't erase part of a picture, you can only erase the entire thing in one shot with the button. But this is true of all similar drawing pads due to how it works, so that is no fault of this product. As far as the Boogie Board clones go, this is my favorite so far.
text_fidelity_b: KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S)

Star Realms: Deckbuilding Game What can I say? This has quickly become my favorite card/board game for several reasons.

1. It's quick. Many games can take hours to play. We play best 2/3, and it usually takes about an hour. Or: about 20 minutes per game.

2. It's variable. What flops on the first turn can change the whole game, because each player has to react to it. Each player is, of course, also reacting to the other player. This translates into a number of different strategies, so each time you play it, it ends up being 'new' in some way, even if you're playing with the same person. This variability makes it more fun because you can never just 'phone it in'.

3. It's easy to learn. There aren't too many rules, so you can teach it to a new player in a few minutes. Of course, they usually have to play several games before they start winning, but that's just a matter of learning the different strategies involved.

Conclusion: HIGHLY recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Star Realms: Deckbuilding Game

VTech PJ Masks Super Learning Headquarters My 4-year-old LOVES this toy. He calls it his "PJ Masks Computer" and wants to play with it constantly. Even when he's not allowed to turn it on (before we leave in the morning), he plays with the vehicles and has a great time. He loves packing it with him in the car, and the sides act as convenient handles for carrying. Do note that the vehicles are not locked down in any way, and are prone to falling off and getting lost if carried around or dumped on the ground in a car tantrum.

Unpackaging the toy is fairly straightforward: you'll need scissors and a screwdriver (or coin). Once you remove it from the box and cardboard packing, you'll find two screws on the back that lock in the Gekko-Mobile and Owl Glider. These unscrew easily with a screwdriver or coin. Catboys vehicle is secured with a zip tie that requires cutting. The toy comes with demonstration batteries (2 AA). They recommend you replace them for full play

The toy is easy to play with. Select your car (character), choose a mode (Vehicle, Science, and Problem Solving) and select a location (Park, Fun Fair, Museum, and Headquarters). There are three activities and four locations, resulting in a total of 12 activities. The games vary and involve avoiding obstacles, sorting items, matching, completing patterns, and learning facts.

This toy is recommended for ages 3-6. Some of the games feel advanced for the younger age range but will give them something to grow into while keeping the 6-year-olds engaged. I'm not sure that my 4 yo really "gets" some of the games, but that doesn't stop him. My 7 yo really loves to play this when she gets a chance.

Like any interactive toy, the volume is higher than necessary. You can adjust the volume (press the volume button, click the car to the left a few times, then click the windshield to set the volume level). Even at the lowest setting, it still feels too loud. It's not too bad if you are a few feet away, or it's in the back seat of the car.

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. LEGO NINJAGO Jay’s Cyber Dragon 71711 Ninja Action Toy Building Kit (518 Pieces) The Lego NINJAGO Jay’s Cyber Dragon set includes 4 numbered bags, a sticker sheet, and the instruction book. The included minifigures are Digi Jay, Digi Nya, Unagami, Richie, and Hausner. I believe this is the only way to get the Digi Nya minifig in the January 2020 NINJAGO sets.

The Cyber Dragon looks super cool when finished. He does have some sticker details on his neck and tops of his wings, but unlike with the Empire Dragon, the Cyber Dragon doesn’t need the stickers to look cool. The mix of light and dark blue adds some nice details, and I like the translucent green tiles used as tail spikes. The way the dragon’s head is built out adds a lot of character in my opinion. And of course, since his wings, limbs, and tail move, the dragon is poseable.

Most of the dragon is very sturdy and suited for play, though the sword pieces used at the end of his tail do come off easily. There are two shooters in the middle of his body. Richie’s hoverboard has two stud shooters.
