text_fidelity_a: Scrabble Turbo Slam A large square cardboard box with plastic shell encase this small rectangular plastic game.  When we opened the box, we thought items were missing because the package was so much larger than the game and there were no visible instructions visible anywhere.  On the rear of the box is a picture of a family of four, a man, woman, girl and boy, all with their mouths agape as they appear to be thrilled with an opportunity to slap the large TURBO SLAM! button.  My family does not look like the people on the box and we never opened our mouths like the people on the box.  We love to play Scrabble but this game did nothing for us.  Fingernails were broken while attempting to slide out the drawer which contained the playing cards and instructions, but we had no difficulty inserting our own 3 AAA batteries with our own screwdriver.  The Turbo aspect of this game which includes "music, sound effects and other cool features" did not "boost the action into high gear!" as the game advertises.  It's simply too cheaply made, loud and annoying, much more than the original SCRABBLE SLAM.  The box has written, "More Ways to Play!  Go to [...]."  I could not find anything at the website which even recognized this game and therefore saw nothing about more ways to play.  We adults thought all sounds of this product were annoying.  I doubt that young children would be entertained for long by this game and would not consider giving it as a gift or including it in a toy drive for children.  I cannot recommend this game.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Turbo Slam

text_fidelity_a:
YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls [[VIDEOID:258489d4261f7a5b0f26535ccf27c4f9]] The plusses: The game is beautiful to look at and feels good quality. The print quality is very very good, these cards do not feel cheap, they feel almost like fancy plastic. It’s also a standard size which means if you are heavy users it’s not challenging to find sleeves to accommodate. I’m also pretty sure the box is big enough to handle sleeves. The rules are relatively simple, and the instruction manual provides a QR code that leads to a video of the gameplay combined with errata to the rules as written. You will *need* the errata because the rules do not answer very basic questions. It makes me wonder how much this was play-tested with strangers before release. It’s great to see a company offering solid support after release though!

At more than 100 cards, the deck is very unwieldy to shuffle, this is definitely one that needs to be broken into smaller piles to handle and then combined.

The rounds are much shorter than expected, some rounds were over in a 2 player game in as little as three fast turns. The actual gameplay is not one “game” but to have the least points over the series of many rounds (the most “loses” the game night.) There was very little tension or any emotional investment because of the fast turnover–that might work for some folks but it didn’t feel like it was worth working on big words without stalling. There were two rounds where the game was over in two turns before my husband could even play a card. It feels like more luck than skill which is not desirable in a word game. My biggest criticism is that due to the number of repeated vowels, gameplay can feel repetitive, we started round after round with “e” or “a” despite shuffling many times. I would love to see a second deck of a different color with starting letters distributed in a more logical way because the starting letter affects the gameplay variety over time. My husband and I love wordplay and puns as a rule and this game was not skill-based enough for the two-player version for us to want to invest too much more time on it. Maybe if we played it for longer there would be more to it but we both got bored after playing 10 or so rounds and probably wouldn’t give it a second try.

The idea itself is an awesome one, when it works it’s like combining scrabble with Uno. There is solid product quality and marketing. It just lacked the skill vs luck factor for us, which may be personal taste

I really think this game needs some tweaks to the gameplay to make it better before I’d really recommend it, at least on the game shelf of a couple. It says ages 8 and up, but I can’t imagine playing this with my almost 8yo, especially without eliminating some of the rules regarding “made up words” because 50 points penalty is pretty punitive for what might be an accidental misspelling, and even with some coaching it would be pretty difficult (And my kiddo has an above-average vocabulary). Maybe several 8yo together do well? We may try to break it out at a party among adults in the future.
text_fidelity_b: YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls

text_fidelity_a:
Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer) This is a very complex and detailed game. It's not for children and it requires that the people playing are ready to spend several hours dealing with the complexities of the system.

At the same time, its a fun game. There are no dice which would be used to randomize events. The game is affected by your play and that of your opponents.

Overall, this is a resource allocation game. You start with two "meeples", who are effectively workers on you farm. Each turn you can send them out to collect resources or to perform special actions that build additional space or activate a special card. After certain turns you have to "feed" your meeples giving up some resources you had previously collected. In the end points are scored based on how big of a home and farm you have grown over the course of the game. The game winner is the one who manages to plan ahead and use his meeples wisely.

Of course, the challenge is to collect the resources at the right times. Most stocks grow if no one collects them that turn, so there is a bit of tactically plotting. Do you send someone to collect the small amount of wood this turn, or do you let it go and hope no one claims it. All of the resources play out this way, you have to decide which is going to be the most value at that time.

If you can find people willing to put the time in, this Is an excellent game.
text_fidelity_b: Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer)

The guilding is quite beautiful and it's actually one of my favorite shades of gold hot-foil (there are dozens, lol). The edges are completely foiled and look beautiful when stacked. The back of the cards use a mix of the gold foil and taupe ink. The face of the cards are not foiled at all, but the taupe shade is both attractive and visible in low white, red, green, blue, and even black light. On that note, the manufacturers were smart enough to use UV reactive paper in the guide, so reading it while working should be easy.
This is my first deck and I'm looking forward to having lots of fun with it. Considering the size, they were surprisingly easy to shuffle like playing cards. For what it's worth, my first (ever) self reading was excessively accurate.
The artwork is top-tier, clean, and "finished" looking. Idk if it matters, but the images don't match up perfectly with the descriptions in the guide book. Aside from this, the guidebook is well written and makes it easy to understand (or at least grasp) the meanings and concepts of the cards. There's also a short guide showing several basic card layouts for both self readings and working with others.
I would definitely recommend these as either a personal or gift set. I think it would be attractive enough for professional work, but that would depend on the look you're after (they don't use ANY colors in the artwork besides the taupe ink).

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+ The instructions in the box are lacking and the website is only slightly better. There isn't anything to download to get it to work. It works, the few times it works, via a web browser.

The device itself has a built in WiFi connection. You can, I think, secure it with a password if you want. It's open by default. You connect to it as a WiFi connection then go to its website to get it to work. I find it hangs nearly constantly. Out of the first ten tries, it worked once, each time running the same code. Here I will point out, I can't get it to go and I'm a senior software developer.

It runs on a very small surface. A sheet of 8 1/2 x 11 printer paper is perfect. It has no edge detection, so mind it doesn't wander off the edge of the table. It starts with the pen fully down by necessity, or at least I can't get it to do anything unless I fully seat the pen, which means it will touch the paper when it is set down,, so it will leave a blob that will bleed through the average paper. Indeed, these bleed almost as bad an an alcohol-based marker.

While it will work with JavaScript or Python, it provides no insight into how to use these languages, so if your kid knows Python they can learn to code the robot in Python, which just means learning its custom library. I would not go so far as to say it teaches much of anything. Hour of code shows as much, is free, and is far more reliable.

It's cute, but until the bugs are worked out, it's not worth the hassle.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+

CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver [[VIDEOID:a47326bb48b328d18558c86fcccc38a1]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very high quality. The handle alone is 12.4 ounces.
* USB-C charging port.
* Belt clip included.
* Decorative blade plug is included. This is cool if you just want to display the handle without the blade. You can cap off your handle with this decorative plug.
* Bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap instead of a pommel/coupling.
* Hilt is 1-1/4 inch. This will connect with other 1.25 inch handles to create a duo saber. Another dominant size on the market is a smaller 1 and 1/8th diameter version. This one will not thread onto 1.25 hilts, so to create duo sabers with different brands, be sure the hilts are the same size.
* All the special effects are pretty much standard: Lock up effect, changing colors, steady, pulse, unstable, etc. This version also has quotes. Watch my video to see a demo

THE BAD:
------------
* Pommel or coupling is not included. As mentioned above, bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap. When you remove this speaker cap, the bottom of this hilt will be male. So to create the duo saber, your other saber should have a coupling so that it's female.
* My light saber did not charge properly out the box. When you plug it in to charge, it'll loudly announce, "Charging!" Then the red light will blink slowly. When it is complete, it will say, "READY," and the red light will be stable, no blinking. Chances are you're not going to be present when the saber says READY. But as long as you see the red light is stable and not blinking, then you'll know it's fully charged. My issue was that after 10 hrs of charging, the red light was still blinking slowly, and the saber wouldn't turn on. I contacted customer support and they had a solution ready to go. So this seems like a common problem. I talk about this at the end of my video, so watch it if you have a charging issue. My saber is charging properly now. So the word to describe this saber is, finicky.

I'll give this an overall rating of 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver

Adora Baby Bath Toy Llama-Corn, 13 inch Bath Time Doll with QuickDri Body My four-year-old granddaughter has been very pleased with every Adora doll I have given her so far, including this one. She likes cuddling this baby doll and carrying it around and, of course, wanted to give it a whirl using it in the tub. Based on that experience, I've listed below some pros and cons of the doll that have been more of an issue for the adults in my granddaughter's life than for her. In other words, they did not seem to lessen her appreciation of the doll but can make caring for the doll a real hassle for adult caretakers of very young owners of this doll.

Pros:

1. This is a very cute doll. It has a sweet face with lifelike detailing of its features and real eyelashes (versus ones that are painted on). The plastic used for the head, arms, legs, hands, and feet is not hard and unyielding but appealingly soft and pliable. The hair is painted, raised plastic rather than rooted hair since this doll is meant to be immersed in water.

2. The doll can suck its thumb, and its eyes open and close.

3. The doll is wearing a non-removable swimsuit and an adorable, removable, terrycloth robe whose hood is the head of a baby unicorn. It also comes with a monogrammed towel.

4. The doll is machine washable in cold water on delicate cycle, but I'm not sure why anybody would want to put a doll in the washing machine. It seems more sensible to take a far less aggressive approach by simply using a damp washcloth to wipe it down. Note that you absolutely cannot put this doll in the dryer.

Cons:

1. The body of this doll seems to have stuffing made of some kind of beads, possibly Styrofoam pellets, similar to what is found in beanbag chairs. Whatever it is that is inside the body, it absorbs water like a sponge, making it very difficult to get all of the accumulated bath or pool water out of the doll. As a result, it can take up to 24 hours for the doll to dry fully. And there's a real risk that the inside of the doll will potentially, perpetually retain enough dampness that it becomes a breeding ground for mold.

2. As seems to be a company policy for all Adora dolls (at least for the four or five Adora dolls I've purchased), this doll has a fake sent of baby powder that's quite unpleasant for anyone sensitive to chemicals. I seem to be the only one in my immediate and extended family with this problem so, fortunately, it did not bother my granddaughter or her parents.

3. The doll's thumb does not fit securely into its mouth, and it pops out far too easily.

4. This doll seems priced too high for what it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Adora Baby Bath Toy Llama-Corn, 13 inch Bath Time Doll with QuickDri Body

Playz Premium Solar System Model Kit for Kids - 4 Speed Motor, HD Planetarium Projector, 8 Painted Planets & 8 White Foam Balls with Paint and Brush for a Hands-On STEM DIY Project for Space Toys After my son and I finished this project, we were pretty underwhelmed. The price is $50, and that's on sale from $99? There is no way this thing should sell for $99, it's still a bit overpriced at $50. Some issues...

1. Our set came with 2 Saturn Arms, missing the Neptune arm. So we had to do a replacement with Amazon.

2. Inserting the pin rods in the planets, then into the arms. This was a pain. There is no way an 8 yr old would have been able to do this. I had to put on gloves to get a good grip to push the pins into the planets. Some of them, you hear a click, and some of them, you get no clicks no matter how hard you push.

3. The center projector that projects each planet is TERRIBLE. You need all the lights off, and you need the whole system to be close to the ceiling for you to see what planet its projecting. Out of focused and blurry. No way to focus it. The only way to get a sharper image is to put the project as close as possible to the wall.

4. Though the arms rotate around the sun, the individual planets do not rotate. So to explain night and day to your child, you'll need to manually rotate Earth. That would be asking too much, but hey, I thought this retails for $99? If they did charge $99, those planets better rotate by themselves. LOL!

3 stars.

Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended The telescope itself is really very good. Even with the lowest magnification lens attached The Housemate and I were able to see Saturn and discern the gap between the planet and its rings. With a higher magnification, things became much clearer, and even more exciting. The first clear image of the moon took my breath away.

The drawbacks? It's very hard to use standing up. I realize it's made for children, but I think a taller tripod might have been a plus here. Even sitting we had to hunch down to see anything at a 45 degree angle or above. Also, the viewfinder did not help at all. I found all the objects we wanted to see by sighting along the barrel of the telescope itself. Now possibly I attached the viewfinder the wrong way, though there really only seems to be one way to do it. Either way, we saw what we intended to see which made the exercise worthwhile.

Why a telescope? Aren't you and your children worth it? Don't you want to learn more about even our part of the universe? This is an amazing gift for the children in your life, or even for yourself. It's lightweight and easy to transport and with the help of something like Google Sky, you can figure out what it is you're looking at with ease. It's a step on the road to becoming better educated in Astronomy, and it should spark a sense of wonder anyone who looks up and longs to know more.

The set is in a metal tin with some wells in the lid, which can serve as a palette, it folds out on two hinges. A color chart is included along with a small pad of water color paper, a small brush and two pen brushes. The pen brushes will open to fill by turning the opposite direction than you may expect. I would not recommend this set for small children, and this is stated on the package. It contains small parts that may pose a choking hazard. This is a great budget set, a fair value and would be excellent for hobbyists and budding artists. I would not recommend it for professional artists, or upper-level students for course work, as this set is not designed for these users. Even when using the right control stick, it seemed to only acknowledge forwards, and wouldn’t respond to the other direction. Then the drone suddenly dropped the WiFi connection within 10 minutes. Powering off and on didn’t fix it. I took the battery out, put it back in and was connected again for a minute or two before the battery just died completely. Yes, I fully charged the battery before use. Surely this products battery should last more than 15 minutes of intermittent usage.
Overall, as someone familiar with remote control devices and technology, I found this drone difficult to control and hence no fun to use.

Zobmondo!! GoLo! Golf Dice Game for Families and Kids, Award-Winning Fun Game for Home or Travel, Quick to Learn, For 1+ Players, Ages 6 and Up This game is pretty simple. Each time you take the dice you'll basically be playing nine holes of golf. The dice are set up with 2 for par 3 holes, 2 for par 5, and the remaining 5 for par four holes. When you start you'll roll all 9 dice. You must keep at least one, but can reroll all the others, and you continue to reroll until you've set aside all 9 dice at which point you score the dice.

Its that simple. Lowest score over X number of holes wins (the game suggests playing 8 rounds to simulate a full 4 day golf tournament).

Fun, portable and very easy to play. It does have the downside of basically being completely random, and in someways its a variation on Yahtzee, but its well themed. If you want a good dice game for trips and don't want Yahtzee, this is a good one to choose.
text_fidelity_b: Zobmondo!! GoLo! Golf Dice Game for Families and Kids, Award-Winning Fun Game for Home or Travel, Quick to Learn, For 1+ Players, Ages 6 and Up

This is a wonderful tumbler set for any age and because I make jewelry it helps cut down on a lot of the cost when it comes to buying pre-polished stones. text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Definitely an enjoyable set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset

HOT WHEELS IRON MAN REPULSOR BLAST LAUNCHER Kid enjoys it, but it's not the thrilling launch you were expecting.
The packaging on this Iron Man Hotwheels launcher is eye-catching - the type of thing your child would be immediately drawn to. My 4.5 yo has been pining for this item ever since he caught a glimpse. The toy was easy to remove from the packaging, something we can all rejoice over. The instructions are straightforward, but it was unclear to me if the toy needs to "click in" to be launched or if it is simply placed on the track inside the larger car (the launcher). The mask doesn't close all the way if you click it in, which tells me it's not really meant to be there. I was expecting more of a spring action launch, but it's really just a result of the handle shooting it forward. The results are hit and miss.

As an adult, I found the movement needed to pull back the mask for loading to be slightly awkward (it's a slight lifting motion on a very small tab). My 4.5 yo managed to do it no problem: smaller fingers I suppose. I also found the launching slightly difficult as you need to hold onto the larger vehicle with one hand while pulling back and releasing the handle with enough force to *actually* launch the car. My child thinks any amount of launching is thrilling and doesn't seem to mind that the car sometimes barely leaves the launcher, so I suppose it's fine.

The larger car does have fittings to connect with a track, so that may be helpful (we don't own any HotWheels tracks).

All-in-all, your little Iron Man fan will likely be delighted by this. The adults in your house may not be.

text_fidelity_a:
Hygge Games How did You Know That? – Trivia Party Game, White As a lover of board games… Our family members each receive a new addition to the game closet in their stocking every year… With kids off to college- I am constantly looking for new and fun options that don’t take a lot explaining or, learning and can peek their interest, liking them to be a bit competitive yet, can be played with minimal effort- So, a hard combo to find! So, I’m happy to say… “How did You know That-“ falls into this category!!

DID YOU KNOW THAT is easy enough to learn and that’s a perk! Also, a big plus is the fact, it’s easy to explain it to those who have a tendency to not pay attention during rule reading (we all know a few of “those type” people- ha ha..!!) BUT, with an easy concept they’ll be playing like pros in no time.. LOVE the fact, this game can be tweaked and adapted if necessary.. and we always love those! (Anything that allows you to simplify or shorten a game as needed.. is like sprinkles on top!)

Basic idea: one person reads 4 questions in a row off of x1 card. All other players write their 4 answers down… THEN, players will correct answers as revealed for all 4 questions asked. giving x1 pt. per correct answer. If only x1 person gets it right the crowd shouts “how did you know that!” and gets double points. Its that simple..

This is full of Quirky odd questions at various levels of some useful/not trivia! Winner is whoever has most points at the end of game..
Best part is: YOU decide do you play to a certain point level (1st one to 10, 20 wins?) OR, do you give everyone certain amount of cards so, everyone has a turn or two to read questions.. if so then, at the end of all reveals.. they tally up those points received to see who’s the winner! That’s it..!!!

This would make a great game for the dorms- (especially during the time of the pandemic.. these kids have a lot of Shelter in place/quarantine time!) for those old enough, I could see it turning this into a drinking game of sorts (good or, bad?!) it would easily adapt.
Definitely, feel this is geared toward older teens or, adults.. it’s too hard for younger kids. I do feel this has a niché for academics and know it alls! Any with mega time spent learning, reading, gaining random facts off the Internet- it’s a great way to share that trivial academia skills.. Ha! Some things will just be fun facts you picked up thru life, in elementary school or, info. From those who’ve raised you.. tossed with real trivia facts. So, the smartest person doesn’t always win!? Fun for a competitive group with a plethora of knowledge and facts to share!!
Played with our college kids over holiday and it went back to the dorm bc, of its fun factor- with x3 college kids and/or, recent graduates.. we had a ball! I hope this info can help your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Hygge Games How did You Know That? – Trivia Party Game, White

I would have given it five stars if it weren't for the clay and eraser kits which seemed easier and kept the kids engaged better.

The kit does have all you need to make some pretty adorable creations. Three of the four of us made donuts as our test creations and one tried the lemon. Hot Wheels Split Speeders Blade Raid Action Track Set This hot wheel set suffers from a similar issue to many other hot wheels sets we have tried: it doesn't hook up well with other hot wheels sets, most parts aren't interchangeable even when they look like they should be, and the action of the intended set will likely only be fun for a few days of play before becoming an oversized dust catcher.

I'm a big fan of the hot wheels sets that you can extend with other parts and enjoy in multiple ways. This set, the main launcher and the orange tracks can be used with normal cars and other sets. But obviously the splitter parts can only be used with the one car they give you.

I will say that it is more fun than the last hot wheels set we brought home, which is a closed system in which none of the parts can be used in any other way, and the action of it was lackluster. This set, at least sending the car through the tracks and launching it with the launcher is really cool.

A few of the parts look kind of flimsy, for example there are a few parts that move and function only because of skinny rubber bands that are visible and obvious on the back. I'm not sure I want teeny rubber bands in the same part of the house as a toddler, and i don't see why they couldn't enclose that area or use better parts.

Overall, I feel like this set is going to be really fun for a few days until part of the splitter car is lost, and then I'll harvest what parts we can use with normal cars and move on. It would be a decent choice to perk up a holiday gathering and be fun for a short time, but it packs staying power.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Split Speeders Blade Raid Action Track Set

PopSockets Fidget Train with Expanding PopSockets , Premium Fidget Toy, ASMR, Toys for Adults and Kids I am a terrible fidget and I am always on the lookout for toys and gizmos that will keep me focused so I can sit still and not distract everyone around me. I selected this thinking it would be similar to those blister-type pop toys. It's not, but it's still an effective toy for stress relief and focus. It's possibly a little too noisy for a meeting, though.

At a glance this thing looks like the sections might come apart. They do not. Instead, this is an accordion-style fidget toy that you pull and push on the ends to make it expand and contract. It can be bent, twisted slightly, partially expanded and completely expanded. The colors are soothing and the tactile feel is nice.

When expanding the toy the sections are not silent. They're not loud, but they have a noticeable popping sound that's lost in the background in a normal environment but draws attention to itself in a more quiet area like a meeting room. It can be expanded more quietly with a little thought. If in an area where making a small amount of noise is acceptable, the sound is satisfying.

As I write this, this toy is close to $30 which seems high. This is really my only reservation with it.

I like this toy and will get some good use out of it. I usually mess with it when I am sitting at my desk and I want to sit still. It has a satisfying sound when popped, it's easy to work, and it looks pretty. It's a little on the expensive side, though.

Mecha Beasts Playing Cards by Gent Supply I have a few “collectible” decks of playing cards, this one among them. These are fancy cards that are made well and I like them, but the color scheme is a bit off for the black suit cards due to the background.

I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. A bright purple, or even a strange color choice like orange or blue, would have worked better.

The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

This are well made cards, coated and designed so they will not stick together even in damp climates. They come in a beautiful tuck box with reflective highlights in purple.

These are not bad cards at all. They’re beautiful and they’re well made, and they have some incredible artwork. However, the color scheme is not the best and these cards would be even better if the background and black suit colors were chosen a little more thoughtfully.

LEGO City Fire Helicopter Response 60248 Firefighter Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (93 Pieces) What I love most about Legos is the they are really limitless and the LEGO City Fire Helicopter Response 60248 set is proof of that. You really don't need bells and whistles with Legos because you can create anything with them. However, the company keeps engineering great sets that just keep pushing the envelope. A Lego Helicopter than can actually fly is just what my 7 year old has been wanting, but didn't know he wanted it. The excitement over making the helicopter fly without touching it is the pinnacle of every little boys' dream. Because it is Lego City it's a piece of cake to assemble. I would say this would make an awesome birthday or holiday gift because it's not your typical Lego set. Any Lego masterbuilder would love to have this!

This is a quick, easy build. The helicopter flies by using one of those old fashioned rip cord like contraptions that other helicopter playsets had from back in the day when we were kids. 3! 1, 2, 3, 3 minifigures! And it falls in line with other Lego City set, so this is a perfect addition to our collection. It's a little pricey for 93 pieces in the box, but I think it's because of the novelty the set brings to the table that others do not. Most Lego City sets are less expensive than this and have more pieces. However, this set is special and different.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Fire Helicopter Response 60248 Firefighter Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (93 Pieces)

Genuine Fred Beach Trash by Emily Blincoe, 500 Piece Puzzle, Multicolored (5281199) I recently started doing diamond painting which takes a lot of patience and determination to finish. When I saw this puzzle, I thought perhaps it would be a fun family project of a similar nature.

PLASTIC
This comes shrink wrapped in plastic. That is important if you are concerned about the delivery being in the rain. We had our box soaked when the delivery person put it in a puddle before, but being wrapped in plastic protects it from problems of that nature in case you were concerned about that.

BOX
The box that this comes in is VERY attractive. It is a step above the usual boxes. The bottom is even colored pink. The picture on the front is very clear and easy to see.

BAG
The bag that the pieces come in is resealable.

PIECES
The pieces upon first examination are well cut and I did not have any issues so far with cut being off or anything.

POSTER
The larger picture inside the box is really pretty to hang up. Honestly I like it so much I might just do that.

FINISHED?
We have not finished the puzzle yet so I can not comment on missing pieces or any other issues. So far everything is good.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This puzzle is so pretty- I am really excited to do it. It has pretty colors, great shapes, and is cheerful too. 500 pieces is a perfect puzzle for my family. We don't have a lot of room for anything more.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is one of the first puzzles in a very long time that I have wanted to do. My whole family likes it. I love that it has a poster for hanging up. This is one of those I will do that with.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Juniors Cruz Ramirez Race Simulator 10731 Building Kit If you are not familiar with the Lego Junior sets, here is the run down. The Legos are same size as the regular Legos. So tiny pieces for you to step on and feel a pain beyond your wildest imagination is highly probable. These are not a size of Lego that is between Duplo and Lego, which is what I initially thought they would be. It's what I hoped they would be. Instead, Lego Juniors are the first step to learning how to build sets with Legos using instructions. There are fewer pieces and the builds are more simplified for a younger child.

The instructions are similar to Ikea instructions, no words, but pictures that show you each step towards your newly assembled Danish minimalist furniture. The instructions are actually easy to follow and my five year old can mostly figure it out. However, I would not recommend this for any child under the age of 5, and I would highly advise to supervise while building. When I mean supervise, I don't mean just be in the room. I mean actually be there next to your child. Why? Because at 4-6 years of age, kids want to play with the Legos. It's not about building and then displaying them, they want to actually roll the cars around and move the people and have the cars crash into each other and the people jump off of buildings. Why is this a problem? It's not a problem until the pieces go missing and then you cannot build the set anymore. Lego Juniors does not realistically take into consideration that its intended age target plays rough and they are not going to be mindful to keep track of all the pieces. Thus, this exposes one of the issues with specific building sets. With free form building sets losing several pieces this is not much of an issue, but since every piece must be placed in a specific order, upon losing several, the set becomes unusable.

All that being said, if you kid loved Cars 3 and loves Legos, then this is the set for you. Just to give you an idea, this item retails for $9.99. Over the holidays, it was on sale here on Amazon and at places like Target, Walmart, and ToysRUs for $7.99. I've seen it retail for $12.99 at small business toy stores.

In addition, do not buy any Lego building set without a Lego tool. A lot of these sets have flat pieces that will get stuck and the Lego tool is your only key to sanity of getting those buggers apart! [[ASIN:B0076VIZBW LEGO Classic Brick Separator 630 Building Kit]]
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors Cruz Ramirez Race Simulator 10731 Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years Here are some observations from my wife.

My almost-5-year-old daughter LOVES this owl pillow craft project, and so do I! She and I have just begun working on sewing with a needle and thread, but I must be sure to be with her every minute, with my hands along with hers on our first sewing projects. This pillow, however, is so smartly designed that it allows her the freedom to practice sewing buttons ON HER OWN, and she loves that freedom. I can be close to her, at the sink, putting away dishes, while she creates her pillow all by herself. It’s a big deal to her. : )

I definitely had to sit with her at the start to go through the simple instructions and to get her started on the process. She enjoyed choosing her own pattern for the owl and decided to choose the same pattern as the owl of the adorable girl on the box. I showed her how to do the first few stitches, and then she was off and running. Once she got going on her own, she kept saying, “This is so easy! This is so fun!” while working on stitching through the felt buttons.

After our first hour on the project today, she’s definitely getting the hang of the process, and she can work on it on her own with me close by for the occasional help with knotting off a thread. And though she really wanted to be able to sleep with the pillow tonight, she’s excited to spend more time stitching the felt buttons onto her owl over the coming days. I’m glad that the project will take 5-7 days of stitching for her to complete. It’s longer than just an hour or even one-day project for her, since she’s at the young side of the recommended age range (6-10 years old). It’s possible an older child could finish this project in a few hours of an afternoon.

And I have to say that I’m thrilled that it’s machine washable. Overall, this is a fantastic and adorable craft for a little one at the very beginning stages of learning to sew.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years

text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy His torso isn't soft, but Elmo's arms and legs are, and that's what my dog went for as we attempted to unpack this toy from his tied down cardboard home. That's after getting through the mega cellophane tape that sealed the box. Your kids will need assistance in accessing the toy for play but they can press his stomach through the package opening to activate the Demo mode. Included in Elmo are AA demo batteries and I haven't opened the compartment to see what they look like or assess how they are different. Nowhere on the box are instructions, so first of all, know that you must switch from Demo to On by opening Elmo's bottom. I am happy to know that it's also possible to turn him off.

Elmo looks just like Elmo and when he talks or sings, his wide mouth moves. His voice is not very clear, but as kids play with him, they intuitively know what he will say. His songs are pleasant, directions are simple, and he doesn't provide negative reinforcement if his orders are not completed properly. This is important in keeping a child interested. Each of the 3 enclosed hard plastic hats has molded into the base a key which let's the toy know which activity to generate. This is very smart and it works well. Initially, it's not easy to get the key to settle, but I suspect that over time it will become more easy. I expect that younger children will need assistance in changing the hats.

The Playskool Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo is a fine toy that I'm confident can entertain and even educate many children. I am curious to know if he is produced in assorted languages as well as the English which ours speaks.
text_fidelity_b: Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Most of that time was spent putting on the wheels. The directions aren’t clear and some of the screws are hard to get to and there isn’t room to use an electric screwdriver. As long as you allow enough time for assembly and charging the battery, this dune buggy will be a hit.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Spy Squad Barbie Secret Agent Doll Barbie is an iconic doll and one recognizable to most anyone. The manufacturer keeps doing what it can to keep people interested, coming out with new versions of Barbie every so often like this one, Secret Agent Barbie.

My girls don’t rank Barbie as their favorite doll character, but they do like her and so they welcomed the chance to add Secret Agent Barbie to their collection. They and I both agree that Barbie’s outfit is cool, with lots of color and style. She looks like a million bucks, ready to take on any secret mission that comes her way.

The extra feature with Secret Agent Barbie is the attachable device that can be used to assist Barbie with flips and cartwheels. The device attaches to her back, but we found it only semi- useful and not that much fun. The problem is there are limits to what this device can do and it doesn’t always work the way it should. It just seems very artificial to have these moves initiated by a device stuck in the doll’s back. My kid quickly grew tired of the attachment, tossed it aside, and played with the doll her own way, which was actually better because it encouraged her own imagination.

So, overall, Secret Agent Barbie seems like an okay doll and an acceptable addition to your child’s collection. It seems more of a gimmick than anything else and it makes you wonder how the idea got past the new product development team, as it isn’t that fun or interesting. Still, it’s got enough going for it to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Spy Squad Barbie Secret Agent Doll

text_fidelity_a:
Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

*The attached photos are of the ant farm on day 3.

Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces) The Mega Construx Kadabra is better suited for display rather than actual play. His hands fall off quite easily. The play feature of the purple orb is pretty meh. But due to his ball and socket joints, he stands without needing assistance or to lean against anything.

Assembly takes about 30 minutes. The instructions are clear; the hardest part is often clicking the pieces together. My fingers actually hurt after I was finished, due to the pressure I needed to exert to get some of the pieces to fit together. I’ve noticed this with other Mega Construx sets. I wish they would fix this, as it makes it harder for young kids to do this on their own.

The set is rated 6+, which I would say is accurate for the instructions and building. The main difficulty will be snapping pieces together. I had imprints on my fingers -- that’s how hard it can be to get some pieces to fit. Which is ironic, considering how easily some other pieces, like Kadabra’s hands, fall off the finished Pokémon.

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. This way you can ensure it’s evenly lined up.

SwimWays Paddle Paws Spring Float Dog Raft, Large (65 lbs. and Up), Blue This isn't really the proper review as I just received this product yesterday, but I did want to point something out for others maybe thinking of this product so they can get a fuller vision of it.

1st - it came ridiculously fast so shipping = excellent. I purchased on the Sunday before Memorial day and received the item the following Wed. afternoon with Amazon's Super Saver free shipping.

And now to the product -

Obviously I'll have to update this review with durability, but for now I can say that I took my dog out on it yesterday (the day we got it) and her monster-claws (that need a serious trim which she will receive today!!) didn't even phase this thing.

The part that's concerning me about this product is just how much water the dog sits in while floating. My dog LOVES water and so of the two choices of dog-float that Amazon offers I figured this was the better choice because the other one doesn't look like the dog gets wet at all and I figured that would get pretty hot for the pup. And even though there are many good pics for this item, I guess I was still envisioning that the dog would be floating with maybe an inch or two of water in the bottom - just enough to keep her cooled down. That's not the case. For my 100# girl, she is laying in about 4-5 inches of water at all times. Cooling? yes, but comfortable? I'm thinking no, not for a dog; at least not for any real length of time. Buyers should be aware that the pic with the Portuguese Water Dog (that I thought was only THAT full of water because the dog is laying over the edge of the float) is a perfectly accurate pic of just how much water the dog will be sitting in at all times while on this float.

In the future hopefully someone will come out with a product that offers just a little LESS contact with the water to create a more perfect balance of cooling and comfort for the dog.

UPDATE: So I actually purchased this for a tubing trip that the dog was going to come along on, which we did this weekend.

End result for this product: The river was super low so we had a LOT of the dog jumping in and out as we'd hit rocks, a LOT of dragging over long distances of rocks, and some fast moving water - over endless rocks! lol I know this wasn't the intention of this product but as far as any 'ripping' there was absolutely none - and we couldn't have put this thing through it's paces any more than that river trip was!! But as far as the durability of the small ring that makes this hold it's shape - that broke just while refolding the item and I learned quickly how important that was within about 30 minutes on the river. :( The product won't hold it's shape very well at all without it. Oh, also, the air stopper kept randomly coming open and not due to the rocks, just whenever, even in calm water. So that was a problem too.

As speculated in the original review, the dog did NOT like being in that much water for an extended amount of time, AND the fabric seemed to almost stretch out a bit because she sat lower and lower (in more water) the longer we were on the river.

Now, all that said, in a pool, I think this product would do just fine - where the dog could get out whenever it got sick of laying in so much water - but I still do think the plastic ring will snap in a heart beat just due to regular un/folding, and needs to be rethought by the manufacturer.
text_fidelity_b: SwimWays Paddle Paws Spring Float Dog Raft, Large (65 lbs. and Up), Blue

As most are familiar with the game Jenga, this is essentially played the same way - pull a block from the stack and place it on top. If your block causes the tower to tumble, you lose. In addition there is a white board with a dry erase marker for listing the rules you’ve set for the numbered blocks. Baby Alive Lulu Achoo Doll, 12-Inch Interactive Doctor Play Toy with Lights, Sounds, Movements and Tools, Kids 3 and Up, Brown Hair This baby alive doll was an excellent find. From the moment I pulled her out of the Amazon box, she has been my youngest new favorite thing. It's been a couple of weeks now and my daughter still carries her around the house all day long. I was worried some of the features would get "old" and then soon we just have another doll to add to the toy pile. Lucky, that hasn't happened the thrill hasn't worn off. This achoo doll is very captivating.
This doll's features are just to cute too. When her cute little button nose turns pink, even I can barely stand it... my instincts tell me to go fix it, lol. Needless to say, my daughter absolutely loves taking care of her sick baby. It's the diagnosing and healing her baby's ailments with medicine that is very rewarding. Plus, all the accessories that come with a doll are cute too.
But what I like the best about the doll is she is inspiring additional pretend play. My daughter has pulled out her doctor kit far more often and is inventing other problems to fix, lol. Over all it's a really cute doll and my daughter is getting her money's worth. I probably wouldn't recommend this for a very young toddler or as a child's first baby doll. The achoo version is little big and clunky in comparison, and doesn't feel like a traditional newborn baby doll. That's not to say that I don't recommend this one because I certainly do. It just feels like a step up from the first round of baby doll to me. But even then, I bet kids who aren't into swaddling and carrying around newborn baby dolls, would still love this because of the interactive features. And even cut my older preteen boys playing with it, so kids of any age do enjoy it!
Hope this review is helpful.

text_fidelity_a: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield When I saw this product was available, I thought that I would order it for my 10 year old son, who wants to see the movie Captain America when it is released later this summer. After receiving it, I asked him to write a review from the perspective of a 10-year-old. This is what he had to say: "The Captain America Shield is really fun. It is easy to put together(he literally read the directions and assembled the parts all by himself). I just had to add 4 batteries and place the foam discs in it. When you shoot the discs you hear a sound, like a siren. But the sound can get kind of annoying. Other than that, the shield is pretty fun". From a parents perspective, I thought that (1) the easy to read instructions allows kids to problem solve and work independently. (2) The sound when the discs are fired acts as a warning system (kind of a fail safe although I don't think the foam discs could cause any damage). And if a child ever accidentally fired the discs in the direction of another child's eyes, although I don't think that they will be injured, they will at least hear it coming. (3) The armband and handgrip are perfect for holding the shield. And (4) it seems like fun. While my 10 year old (it was his birthday today) had fun, I do think that a slightly younger child (7 or 8) would have more fun and not become bored as quickly as an older one.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield

For instance the gymnastics show set and the dolphin rescue set from this year both have fewer pieces than this one yet they both end up much larger once built.

This set does have a few rare/unique pieces. The pink beehive piece used as cotton candy only appears in this set and the creator expert roller coaster set from last year, and the lilac truss piece is unique to this set.

LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink Mix feelings about this product. Had it over a year with minimal travel usage. We usually leave it in our dining room on our kids table so they can do activities while mom cooks. We loved it when it worked but once the batteries died and I replaced the device with new batteries, it turns on and does nothing. It doesn't sense the stylus. It will on a random occasion after multiple attempts say one or two words when pointed on the stylus but then stops again. Changed batteries out a couple of times and unfortunately didn't help. Now, I have two disappointed kids with numerous of these books and told family to get more books for Christmas which will only be to their disappointment that they have no device to use them with.

As for when the device worked, we would loved it and would recommend to any parent with kids under 7. My son is almost 5yo son and 3yo daughter love this. They take turns using it since I only had one of the Leap Start devices but numerous books. My daughter was heart broken after multiple attempts to try new batteries.

I hate to give one start but given the longevity of this product for the price, it needs to last more than a year. I mean one year for a $45 device. Maybe some would say that's worth it but not when you shell out $10 - $15 on each of the books. I might of gotten a faulty device so maybe it's just poor luck on my part.

UPDATE—7/1118
We’ve had our new leapstart book (this time I bought at big box store with a warranty) for 5 months now since the last broke, so far so good but I’m still not sure on longevity still, however i have changed batteries a few times since we use ours alot and have had no issues. I am adding a star as my kids fight over this all the time. I’ve got 6yo boy who LOVES it who is also my reader and 4yo girl who always wants what her brother has but genuinely love this thing. I struggle with getting my kids to play with their $100 toy they got for Christmas but love this thing and it’s a plus for me since it’s educational. So i still can’t give this item as high of a star as I would like because of durability I would recommend it if you don’t care if you have to replace it. I’m glad I did but recommend getting some warranty because after investing in the books and how much my kids like It, you may want to get another.

text_fidelity_a:
My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set This is a fun little train set for toddlers. The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. It comes in a handy carry bag with large plastic track pieces and two toys: Thomas the Tank Engine and Harold the Helicopter. Not quite sure why they include a helicopter to roll around a train track, but I suppose he is one of the more popular characters in Thomas' world. Regardless, they are both cute and large enough for a toddler to get his hands on and push around the track.

Thomas and Harold come attached to a piece of cardboard which keeps them in place. Before you go crazy on how to get these off - after a bit of struggling myself, I realized that all you have to do is rotate the plastic tab things that are holding them in place (located on the bottom). Just turn the tabs 90 degrees (doesn't matter which way) to free Thomas and Harold.

You will definitely need to help your put this together as the track pieces have a snug fit. they may loosen with time, however. There are instructions on how to put the track together, though I'm sure you can figure out your own unique layouts as well. The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

This is a really fun little set with a a nice carry bag to store all the pieces and even take the set with you on adventures. Little ones will love it!
text_fidelity_b: My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set

text_fidelity_a:
Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces THE GOOD:
--------------
* Perfectly priced toy for the quality you're getting.
* Collectible.
* Like Rock-Em Sockem, but with electronics, and the figures will split when getting knocked out.
* This version come with an arena, but you can fight without it if you wish.
* Two warriors included to get you started.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Nothing I can think of. The price is just right for what you're getting. I don't recall an actual arcade game in the past called Akedo. It seems this toy is simply inspired by all the classic arcade fighting games such as Street Fighter, Fatal Fury, Tekken, etc. It will keep your children occupied for awhile and away from tablets.

One more thing, the two default figures that's already installed in the arena have clear bands wrapped around them. We saw the vertical bands on their bodies and cut them off. But when we battled, we still couldn't split each other. My son realize there are more tiny bands in the neck that needs to be cut. So if you're playing for awhile, and you can't knock anybody out, check to see if rubber bands are still holding their bodies tight. You can manually check... you are free of bands when you can pop their heads back and split their bodies. If you can't do that, it probably means there are some bands you still need to cut off.

5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces

LEGO DUPLO Disney Princess Frozen Ice Castle 10899 Building Toy with Light Brick, Princess Elsa and Anna Mini-Dolls Plus Olaf Figure, Gifts for 2 Year Old Toddlers, Girls & Boys [[VIDEOID:1c8150e87e66d2b60e0ec8095157a4f1]] If you’re an adult, this LEGO DUPLO DISNEY FROZEN ICE CASTLE (10899; New 2019; 59 Pieces) takes less than half an hour to assemble, but it’s a terrific set. DUPLO blocks are intended for very young builders, and are much larger than regular LEGO blocks. Thus this “Frozen” ice castle set lacks the detail of the regular [[ASIN:B07TB4WCJM LEGO “Frozen” ice palace]] (see photos). But this DUPLO set has a light brick!

The light brick is powered by 3 button cell batteries (pre-installed). When you press the button on the brick, it cycles through a series of colors for a short time, then stops automatically. By repeatedly pressing the button, you can get all white lights; or all blue, red, yellow, green, purple, orange lights. The batteries are replaceable, but you will need a small Phillips head screwdriver to open the light brick. The batteries are NOT accessible to small children.

In comparison to the regular LEGO set, the other great thing about this DUPLO set is the size of the play figures. Elsa, Anna, and Olaf are much larger than regular LEGO mini-figures, so they’re more fun to play with or display. Elsa and Anna have skirts with elastic waists that go on over the plastic figures. Elsa has a sparkly cape, and Anna has a dark red cloak. Olaf is just himself!

It’s kind of amazing, how much the look and feel of the LEGO “Frozen” ice palace set is retained in this simplified DUPLO set.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Disney Princess Frozen Ice Castle 10899 Building Toy with Light Brick, Princess Elsa and Anna Mini-Dolls Plus Olaf Figure, Gifts for 2 Year Old Toddlers, Girls & Boys

Mattel Games ​Mattel Games PIC FLIP Card Matching Game with 110 Cards in a Decorative Tin, Makes a Great Gift for 7 Year Olds and Up [Amazon Exclusive] My family and I look forward to family game night and Uno has been the game of choice on more than one occasion. It's a fast-paced game that requires luck as much as strategy, and that works well for all of us. We have a couple of Uno variants that we like, and with two adult sons that grew up with Mario games this is a good fit for our family.

This game plays identically to regular Uno in almost every way. It has all of the expected elements of the game - 4 colors, skip, reverse, wild cards and more. However, it also has a special card that changes the game in a fun and often unexpected way, allowing a player to dodge attack cards and send them back to the one who played them. It's powerful enough to change gameplay but not enough to ruin the game.

The cards are decorated with the familiar characters of Mario Brothers games - Bowser, Mario, Luigi, Donkey Kong Jr. and more. Fans of the Mario Brothers franchise will like this deck.

The game is packed nicely in a metal tin that protects the cards and keeps them together.

I am not the least bit unhappy with this game and my family and I have been enjoying it. We look forward to game nights and this game will be a part of those nights.

LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces) I think this line of Disney Storybook Adventures sets is a pretty cool idea, to put a playset inside a book. I was a fan of the Lego Ideas Pop-Up Book set, so I like that Lego took that concept and redid it for younger builders.

The Mulan Storybook includes 2 micro-dolls of Mulan, each with a different expression, outfit, and hair piece. There’s also a micro-doll for Li Shang, Khan the horse, and a printed Cri-Kee brick. Micro-dolls are smaller versions of Lego’s mini-dolls. But their bodies don’t move, and their hands are small circles, so Mulan can’t hold a sword, for example. Mulan stands on Khan’s back to ride the horse, which looks a little silly to my eye.

The build is pretty simple and folds into the storybook. I like this aspect of the set the most, but it is a little delicate. If you toss the storybook around after closing it, you might need to do a little fixing.

The set includes a lot of stickers, so kids can decorate the storybook as they want. Only a few are necessary for building elements, like the sticker on the “spine” of the book, so kids can put the rest wherever they want.

So much laughter and I look forward to playing it anytime I can!

For those interested on how we played as a large group: we divided up into teams of two or three. Each team got one white (character) card and two black (attribute) cards. They had a minute or so to talk about strategy amongst themselves. Then - the SuperFight was on! We went around the group and each team got to tell everyone about their character (& abilities) and then debate with each other on why they would win. Everyone as a group agreed or disagreed depending on the strength of the debate. We didn't keep score, but just round by round. Lots of fun and easy to play anywhere!

Hot Wheels Track Set with 1:64 Scale Toy Firetruck, City Fire Station with Dragon Nemesis and Track Play, Dragon Drive Firefight We've owned plenty of hotwheels sets, some pretty standard and some pretty creative. This is one of those interesting ones I couldn't really understand until we got it. The car is sort of on an "assisted loop", in that there are points that require your intervention to continue. It starts off being "spit out" by the dragon, then fired from a booth, then launched up a loop, and- if everything goes according to plan - it lands on the head of the dragon which will either fall forward or to the side (not knowing which way is part of the fun). However, if you don't have everything 100% seated properly, it just fails miserably. My kids had trouble getting it to work until I came and reseated some parts more forcefully, but even then we still had a few misfires that caused it not to work.
But I suppose that's the tradeoff of the more obscure track sets, sometimes they are more difficult to operate successfully. Part of the fun is making it work, I think. But if you have a kid who isn't up for that challenge, maybe this isn't the set for them. We actually really liked it, and the payoff when it DOES work is the sort of moment that gets high fives and cheers all around.

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. If you want more control, though, then you should get the CX-10. Or, you should get both, since their parts are all interchangeable.
text_fidelity_b: Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone

Clicformers Basic Set (150 Piece) Educational Building Blocks Kit, Construction STEM Toy, Creative Building Bricks This CLICFORMERS BASIC SET (150 Piece, Multicolor) is a high-quality building set. The pieces are solid, uniform, smooth-edged, and easily snapped together. However, the pieces aren't particularly versatile--most builds seem to use a chain of connected basic pieces rolled or wrapped around an accessory piece, or folded into boxes.

Also, the finished builds don't look much like a “duck” or a “penguin” or a “necklace” or a “truck”. It takes imagination to see the build as the thing it is intended to be. To me, the builds always look like an aggregation of Clicformers pieces, instead of transforming visually into an entirely different object.

This set includes a booklet of clear instructions for a variety of builds. There is also a sheet of stickers to apply to the pieces, either for decoration or for birds’ or animals’ eyes. The set is fun to play with, if you like building toys.

I think that LEGO sets give better value, because you can build so many different, recognizable things from the basic bricks (LEGO, or LEGO Duplo for younger children), without needing a lot of special connectors. If Clicformers offer something that LEGO doesn't, I don't know what it is. Clicformers certainly aren't cheaper (as are K’nex and Mega Blox building sets).
text_fidelity_b: Clicformers Basic Set (150 Piece) Educational Building Blocks Kit, Construction STEM Toy, Creative Building Bricks

Melissa & Doug Princess Design Activity Kit - 9 Double-Sided Plates, 4 Colored Pencils, Rubbing Crayon When I was a kid, I had one of these fashion plate toys. It was fun. You set the outfit, rub the crayon over it, then color it. So, although the primary purpose of this toy is vanity, I like the creative and artistic aspect of it. My 6 year old daughter was thrilled when she saw it. The packaging leaves much to be desired. It is a clamshell package. I took it out, showed her how it worked, and set her to work on creating some outfits. There are 3 bottom plates (6 options), 3 top plates (6 options), and 3 head plates (6 options). All the plates fit inside a little drawer. It comes with one crayon to rub with an attachment so you don't have to get your fingers all messy and 4 colored pencils.

This is super cheap quality. The lid only closes (on the top) when you have the drawer pushed in. The plates themselves are not exactly even, they are a bit warped and don't lay flat. The drawing area is too small for a regular sheet of paper, but slightly larger than half a sheet of paper. You cut paper in half to use half sheets and they slide around a bit in the top area. Since the plates are a bit warped, you can't get a good rubbing of the pictures. (One skirt and top is polka dotted and not even half the dots will transfer to the paper.) The top is difficult to open. It also easily pops off on the opposite side that should not be opening. The eyes usually don't transfer to the rubbing either.

The colored pencils it comes with are pretty poor quality and not good color choices. (Brown, indigo, light pink, and yellow.) They don't have very much pigment in them and you're coloring on top of a rubbing, so you need much more vivid pencils than it comes with.

Within about 20 minutes of use, my 6 year old had already found the duct tape and taped the lid down. She likes the product and said other girls would like it too, just use duct tape.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Princess Design Activity Kit - 9 Double-Sided Plates, 4 Colored Pencils, Rubbing Crayon

I remember my mom's old set was chipped in a few places, particularly the notches. These don't look like they will chip at all. His comment started a converation about what other games might fit that category.

Munchkin could be the sibling to those old games. Even in this first set, the puns are everywhere and the game is more about having fun and socailizing than winning. Sure it almost requires that you backstab each other freely, but its also the kind of fast paced and humorous game that keeps the players from becoming too serious about what's happening. The humor can be crude and a bit adult, but other than that Munchkin has proved to be a great game.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit As will become clear in this review, I am a true fan of Lego. Does that bias my review? I dont think so, you may disagree...

This is a big set. This is not a set for your younger Lego builders, not because its too hard, but because some of it will become tedious to younger minds. But us older people refusing to grow up (46 and still building with Lego!) will love this. There are several points during the build where you think "Oh WOW, thats clever" - very good.
The end result is bigger than I expected. Most of my recent large set builds have been the modular Lego City sets, which are built the right size for Lego Minifigs - this is much smaller than that! So you cannot add it to your Lego City, but you can have it in the back ground.

Its about an 8 hour build. The manual is excellent, but with less writing than some of the other ones - the Lego Eiffel Tower's Manual had a lot more information on the history of the Tower. This has a few snippets about the history, the Big Ben bell, but more would have been appreciated.

When finished, it is beautiful. You can turn the knob on the back to adjust the time - you cannot really adjust the time - the hour and minute hand are tuck, so as one turns, so does the other. But its still awesome!
The tree outside the main entrance is wonderful! one of my favorite parts of the build!

I believe that Lego is the best toy ever made. This set only re-enforces that opinion. Some Legos, when complete can be played with (the Lego City ones, for instance) but others not so much. I dont see this being played with, just built, displayed, and maybe dismantled and rebuilt.

5 stars though. A wonderful Lego set. A must have for collectors big kids, and us huge kids!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

This glue mixes easily with slime activators to create slime.
When the glue gets warm it turns pink.
If you want a slime that is a light purple/pink then just simply mix this glue with some regular white glue until the desired color is achieved.

text_fidelity_a:
hp Old I have raised sea monkeys off and on since I was a child. I was a huge fan of them as a child and had almost all the memorabilia/sets. I was a member of any sea monkey forum and was always checking out the official and unofficial sea monkey pages. I can keep a tank of sea monkeys alive for years with ease.

That being said, all mine died. I followed the directions to a tee, and nothing in them was really wrong. But when I added the food, they all died. I can't figure out why, but it had to be the food. I added in the right amount. Maybe just over population? I had to have had about three hundred babies. But whatever the case, it's one star because there is absolutely something wrong with this set.

The tank is nice, and I liked the sticker that goes on the bottom, it would have helped to cover up the muck that would have built up over time if the brine shrimp had lived. I would have liked more color options. The instructions were quite good. Not including everything dying, the set would have got four or five stars. It was a cool set.
text_fidelity_b: hp Old
