Nowhere in the instructions does it mention this. Oddly, the magnets are separate and not pre-attached to the pieces. Of course, you can place the card on any flat surface, but the magnets will not stick unless you place it on top of the lid.

This comes in a very nice, heavy cardboard box as shown in the pictures. The box measures 9.5” x 8” x 2.5”. You have to work a little bit to get the lid off. The box is actually about twice the thickness that it needs to be. Nonetheless, you can store other things in it if you wish.

There are 30 sheets/levels to complete. But you’re doing the exact same thing on all of them. Meaning that you are connecting the water inlet from one side to the other so the crocodile can take a shower. All of the cards are numbered in the lower right corner. Each card is a little more challenging than the last. But, to be honest, after doing a few of these, some kids may find it boring. It would’ve been nice if the cards had more variety. Meaning different subjects and such, even if the actual tasks were virtually the same.

Personally, I think this is more of a “one and done” sort of item. I highly doubt kids are going to want to do this again and again. Works better for a classroom setting. So multiple children will be able to use it.

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Short version of the review: it’s a fun game with a pretty good first-game learning curve that settles in pretty quickly in subsequent games. It can be long (though you can adjust it). We’ll add it to our rotation of “lengthy” games

Longer version

1) Packing
I’m going to ding the game for packaging because while everything comes fine (as is typical, there’s a lot of popping pieces out of their cardboard sheets), I like when games include easy ways of keeping thing together and/or organized once you’ve played the first game. Even if it’s as minimal as separate small plastic bags. We used our own tiny bags (we’ve learned to keep ones that do come with other games if they’re extra thanks to consolidation) and a few regular small baggies, but I don’t think it’s too much to ask that those things be included

2) Materials
All the materials seem of good quality. Cards are not super-thick but they’re not at all flimsy, the non-plastic pieces feel solid and you don’t have any sense that they’ll start coming apart or getting dented/torn. The plastic cities are a nice touch, but the capital cities could perhaps have been made a little more distinctive. Not at all a big deal; a close look is all you need.

3) Instructions
The big sheet of instructions is fine. Generally clear and well written, with a few “clarification” points at the end, which is a nice touch. We had a few questions that weren’t included, but they were easy to find online. A few individual player cards with a stripped down bit of instruction for quick, easy reference would have been nice to toss in

4) Set up
As noted (and as is usual for these types of games) there’s a lot of popping things out and organizing. Once that’s done the first time, set-up is relatively quick. You put together some map tiles which is easy enough (though this 50+-year-old wouldn’t have minded if the organizing numbers were a little bigger on each tile). Each player gets tokens, a set of cards five of which are laid out in a particular order under their “Focus” bar (the cards are in these areas: Military, Technology, Culture, Economy, Industry), a set of “diplomacy” cards, a “leader” card (who they “play”—Cleopatra for instance), a few caravans (little wagons used for trading). After you’ve done it a few times it’s a pretty quick set-up. You also set up some cards to the side of the play area (World Wonder cards and City-State Diplomacy Cards and Victory Cards (these are what determine how the game is won). This is always an issue in these sorts of game because of course they’re not going to be truly “visible” to all the players. Someone is going to have to move or ask to see them to see what they say (some change throughout the game). I have no idea how to get around that though; it’s just a matter of physical setting.

5) game play
I’m not going to detail it. But generally, the Victory cards have two “agendas” on them, such as build two Wonders of the World, and a player who achieves one agenda from each of the cards is the winner (this is nice because you can shorten the game if desired by simply playing with fewer Victory cards). As far as the play itself
1) Players can “resolve” (do what it says) any one of the five cards below their Focus bar. This might mean building a city, attacking someone, moving a caravan, laying out a “Control” piece to claim a hex space (i.e. territory).
2) Once they’ve done that, that card gets move to slot one under the bar and all the others move one slot to the right. This is key because the slot number affects how the card is resolved. For instance, when you attack using your military card, you roll a die and add the slot number (and possibly other bonuses) to your roll. So you’re going to want to attack when that card is in the 4 or 5 position typically, not the 1 or 2 slot. This adds a nice bit of complexity to your action choices.

That’s pretty much the gameplay for players. A few other factor include
1) You can swap out a card under your focus by advancing your “Tech” counter a certain number (you do that using one of the cards). Once you hit a certain level, you can exchange one low level card for one that’s a bit more powerful. There are 4 levels of cards.
2) Barbarian tokens on the board move at regular periods and they can end up destroying one of your caravans or claiming territory from you (which affects how much money your cities earn and how much you can advance)
3) Caravans allow you to gain trade tokens that can be used to increase the impact of your cards. For example, if you have two trade tokens on your military card, you can spend one or both to add a bonus to your roll. Caravans can also garner you another player’s Diplomacy card, which has certain benefits dependent on the card.
4) Placing a control tokens mean you’ve claimed territory (that particular space), which is necessary for collecting trade tokens (a “mature” city garners you a set number of trade tokens once you’ve “controlled” all adjacent tiles), collecting resources such as marble or diamonds, or for building cities (your build cities a certain number of spaces from a space you’ve controlled with a token).
5) The terrain has an impact on your choices. In order of scaled “easiness”, the terrains are 1-grasslands, 2-hills, 3-forest, 4-desert, and 5-mountains. To travel through a desert is considered difficult, so that 4 means your Economy card (the one that moves your caravan) needs to be in the 4 or 5 slot. Similary, to build a city in a mountain space means your Industry card has to be in the 5 slot.

There are more rules and factors that come into play, but that’s the general gist. As noted at the start, I’d say the learning curve is relatively steep the first time ( a lot of going back to the instruction booklet), but past the first game or two, it comes pretty easily. I’ve certainly played games with a far steeper curve and one that takes longer to get to know game play well. If I were ranking learning curves on a ten-point scale, I’d probably put this around a 6.

Turns move slowly the first time or two as people try to remember what they can do, what they need to do, etc. But after the first hour each player moves pretty quickly through their turns as you’ve gotten used to how to deal with the complexities of those shifting slots under the Focus bar. As people get closer to each other, things slow again as players try and figure out cost-benefit of attacking, but then as before, after a few attacks those move quickly.

I liked the game quite a bit. More than my two family members, but I tend to have more patience for the slowness of things and I mind long game less than they do. They did like it enough to play again. And as mentioned, I like that you can self-adjust your length simply by cutting out one of the agendas. It’s a game we’ll definitely keep and keep playing.
text_fidelity_b: Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Thames & Kosmos My City | Family – Friendly | Legacy Board Game | Kosmos Games | 2 to 4 Players | Ages 10 and Up | Award Winning Designer Reiner Knizia , Blue We have never played a legacy game like this before. I like that the rules are pretty easy and it works a little like tetris as you try to cover space and penalty areas with rocks while protecting bonus areas with trees. It is a nice little exercise in spatial relations and simple long term strategy. We actually restarted once a couple of us had epiphanies about what they should have done. But the kind of cool thing is that as you go on and build on what you know and have played, your open new rules and get new pieces introduced that again challenges your placing skills. I found it to be a unique game. We played it with four people ages 13-50s and it played well for those ages, but might not be good for the under 10 crowd. Also, the game took a few evenings, so you need to be able to put the game aside and have the same players available to pick it up again.

The game pieces are nice and I love the enveloped stages. It is a well made game and a good idea. Simple to play, but with enough mental challenge to get you thinking a little. Love it for its uniqueness and I think we will be able to play through it again a couple times.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos My City | Family – Friendly | Legacy Board Game | Kosmos Games | 2 to 4 Players | Ages 10 and Up | Award Winning Designer Reiner Knizia , Blue

Got very scared and thought I might lose it so I hit the home button. Within 10 seconds she was back in clear view. The views are amazing. I didn’t know there were so many interesting things around my house. I can’t wait to take it to my office and take some videos of my dealership. After this flight, I can say I’d definitely buy it again. I’ve never had so much fun without leaving my driveway. So again, get you one. Thanks Deerc.

Science Kit for Kids Crystal Growing Kit + Light Up Display Dome for Kids by Creative Kids, Make Your Own Grow 4 Large Crystals, DIY Educational Experiment - Cool STEM Gift for Boys & Girls Lengthy process and involved more parental involvement than anticipated but it was worth it and kiddo loves his new room decor. We did have to clear out a small cupboard for a little over a week to keep the growing crystals away from our cats. They couldn't be trusted to leave it be.

Tips:
1. Stir stir stir. The more complete you get the powders to dissolve the better the crystals come out.
2. If the crystals start to peek outside the top of the water, pull that one out and let it dry (Ours didn't all grow at the same rate). They come out smoother if they don't keep growing out of the water.
3. Once formed the crystals are delicate and brittle so this really is a place and leave alone type thing.
4. We let ours grow for a little bit over a week, so they got pretty sizable. I would suggest leaving them in there until they start to peel above the water, then pull them out.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces) The first thing I noticed about this set was the weight. This is the first LEGO set that I've gotten that I would actually describe as heavy. That's a lot of brick. The box is nice, and contains several smaller boxes. Those boxes have some blueprint art on them, but no useful labeling as to where to begin. You need to open them all anyway, because the unlabeled bags of large parts are mixed in with some of the later bags, despite being needed early on. The bag numbering only goes up to about 20, but there are many bags for each number and the bags have bags in them. The instruction book is huge and spiral bound, with some nice history in the early pages.

The set goes together surprisingly quickly early on, starting with the display base and docking clamps, which the ship is built on, with sections being build and then clipped on. The internal support structure is well engineered and solid. You get a good impression of the overall size and shape of the ship by the time you are done with bag 2.

At first glance, this may look like a tedious grey set where all the parts look the same, but the insides are brightly colored. This is really nice because the parts being built are often rotated between panels, and the colors really help with both finding the parts and orienting with the instructions. When you're done, it also makes it easy to spot anything you missed, because the grey exterior will have rainbow colors there.

One disappointment is the thin area down the sides of the ship. I like them fine individually, but the instructions have you build them identically, so rather than being bilaterally symmetrical, one side looks like it's upside down compared to the other. I understand this saved them some pages, and made construction a little easier, but I would've appreciated a heads up so I could build it mirrored, since I think that would've worked out fine, at least for the greebles on the outside. I may actually take one side apart and redo it, though It's the kind of detail that an observer might not notice because this thing is so big. There are other areas that are more obviously asymmetrical, which is true to the movie, but looks really jarring to me the way they implemented it.

After completing it, I feel like it was designed by two different teams of people. The interior structure is an awesome feat of engineering, and so sturdy you can carry the whole thing by an interior handle, despite its great weight, and they did it with all existing parts. The exterior is about as expected in a Lego set. The transition between the two is weak. Brushing against it risks knocking things off. Sometimes it's just some barely attached pieces on the back, other times something obviously comes apart inside that's going to take some doing to get to and fix. The different sections are often just resting loosely on each other and sometimes look uneven. There is a tiny and comically inadequate clip to hold the four sections of the front in alignment. You may want to think about what you're going to do with it when it's done. It's large, heavy, and oddly shaped. Comes on a nice stand though.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces)

Deep Dilemmas - 'Would You Rather' Conversation Cards for Ridiculous Debates & Funny Interactions. 200 Original Ice Breaker Question Cards for Adults, Couples, & College Students - Ages 16+ I've picked up a bunch of these conversation starter games and some are better than others. I would say this one is right down the middle. It's a very straightforward concept - on each card is two choices and you're supposed to pick each one. The problem is that maybe half of them are real dilemmas, while the other half are no brainers. For instance - "would you rather live on a 50th floor penthouse with no elevator or have $2 million in dimes". These are the kinds of questions that might as well not be there because everyone just picks one of the answers and there's no discussion needed, which defeats the point of the game. In some ways I feel like they knew this going in - on the side of the box, it's actually printed that the playtime is up to 60 minutes - with 200 cards, that averages out to 3 cards per minute.

All in all, can't really recommend. You could probably spend an afternoon and come up with better ideas on your own.

text_fidelity_a:
Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated This is just a first-time playing review, which I'll update as we continue to play. But at this point it wouldn't surprise me if the score gets bumped up to a five.

Components: high quality. They seem quite well made, durable, and are beautiful looking.

Set up: Set up is pretty easy and quick despite the number of materials (we played with three)

Gameplay: Deceptively simple. Your goal is to build structures using blocks which you quarry then place on a boat then sail to one of four places then unload them, with various points scored at the ends of rounds and the game depending on what you achieved. It is, as mentioned, deceptively simple because though you only have a few options, the other players of course get to do their own thing, which often involves blocking your thing. So that ship you were planning to load up with that particular stone you needed? Somebody just decided to sail it away. Those stone you loaded on that ship to build a pyramid? Somebody docked it instead at the obelisk area. So you need to work around what your opponents are doing, try to anticipate what they're going to do, as well as try to block them as well. It's fun, frustrating, stimulating, engaging, and did I mention fun?

We really enjoyed playing it even with the usual slow-down issues of playing a game for the first time. Even with those first game issues, the game was finished in under an hour and I would imagine you could get through it in 30 minutes regularly. An additional plus is that although the game will play differently lots of times obviously with all the variations on situations, the game itself comes with a "B" side (in other words, its own variant)

I'll update as we get more games under our hat, but right now Imhotep seems like a winner
text_fidelity_b: Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

Seedling Design Your Own Virtual Reality Viewer: The Dark Side Activity Kit We are a technically competent family. Our experience as real users of this product was very underwhelming. The first step on their instructions is to download the Seedling app from their website, but we had to search their website for a good 20 minutes before we found the link to their app. The app is 128MB (for Android) which takes a good amount of time to download, as well as filling up a large amount of space on our phone.

While I'm waiting for the app to download, let me review the other parts of this package. What you're getting is essentially a basic Google Cardboard viewer (available separately for $5-$10 from various Amazon sellers) plus pieces of arts-and-crafts paper and plastic that you can glue to the cardboard viewer (a bottle of white glue is included). Maybe you can finish the glueing in about the time it takes for the 128MB app to download. There are no templates included in the directions and no photos of possible finished products (except for the 1 on the Amazon product description), but you're just glueing pieces of paper and plastic, so don't expect much.

Once you get the 128MB app downloaded and running, it asks you to download the Google Cardboard app, which is another 48MB. Download that and now you can play their maze game. There are a few pre-configured mazes and an apparent editor mode that lets you design your own maze. Designing your own maze is also discussed on the Amazon product description. I could not figure out how to get the maze editor to work in the app and the printed documentation included in the box is no help. Playing the pre-made mazes a couple of times gave me a headache, so designing my own maze doesn't sound very interesting anyway.

Now that I do have the Google Cardboard app on my phone, I'll probably just delete their maze app and try some of the Google Cardboard apps. I could have done that by just buying a $5 Google Cardboard instead of using this kit for $30. There really is nothing more to this product than their maze app, a Google Cardboard viewer, and some pieces of paper and plastic that you can cut up and glue to the Google Cardboard viewer. If your kids are into arts-and-crafts, they may get more out of that part of the product than I did. However, the arts-and-crafts has no association with the software and I don't see the point to mixing 2 unrelated projects. They should have put more work into their maze designer app. Maybe let you draw out mazes as the arts-and-crafts project and then scanning those into the software.
text_fidelity_b: Seedling Design Your Own Virtual Reality Viewer: The Dark Side Activity Kit

Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy The Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is an educational toy in the shape of a clock, made from wood, with small wooden sorting blocks that fit into designated spaces. This toy helps to teach kids how to tell time and match shapes and it makes a great toy option for youngsters in the preschool age group.

Educational toys are the preferred toy from a parental point of view, but it is sometimes a challenge to find an educational toy that my girls will enjoy for an extended period of time. With the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock, it appears I have achieved victory in this area. Even weeks after their initial encounter with this toy, my girls still enjoying sorting the blocks and reading the numbers on the clock dial. Each of the blocks is colored differently and shaped differently and my girls enjoying figuring out which block fits into which slot.

One of the many advantages with the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is its ability to educate in multiple ways. Not only does it teach kids spatial skills and how to tell time, it also teaches kids how to match numbers, count the minutes and hours, and arrange the hands of the clock to a certain time. With the blocks, younger children will have two ways to match: By shape or by number. If they cannot match the number, they can match the shape that fits, thus eliminating frustration and eventually learning the number in the process. Yet another advantage of this toy is that it encourages more imaginative play. There are no bells or whistles and no batteries. The hands of the clock are moved only by pushing with the fingers. These facts make the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock a little on the old- fashioned side, in a sense, but in a positive way.

Educational toys are the best but it is often a challenge to find an educational toy that children will enjoy. This toy has passed the test with flying colors, offering satisfaction to both child and parent. It is true that the small blocks can get lost in due time, but other than this, the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is an excellent toy overall. It teaches children several skills and offers great durability, is made from wood, and requires no batteries. My little ones love it and continue to enjoy it day after day. It's an easy winner that belongs in every child's toy box.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy

Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4 The idea is great and at $20 (Black Friday) it’s not the worst toy. The problem is that all of the mechanisms are so flimsy that it’s just not a good toy for the age it is meant for. They get frustrated when things don’t work and don’t understand why things don’t work when they take the correct action. Add to that the helicopter mechanism not working at all because it’s too far away from the car, and you just can’t enjoy the toy.

So I mentioned the helicopter doesn’t work. It’s too high for the magnet to grab the car. So your 2 or 3 year old won’t understand at all why one of the knobs doesn’t work. Then the car gets to the bridge, which at least works most often. Then the grey lifting part which constantly comes out of its socket. Then the area where the cars turn…if you aren’t slow and gentle the cars will get bumped off the track. Everything is just so flimsy.

Due to all the issues, as an adult it’s impossible to get a single car all the way through the circuit, even when being as careful as possible. So there’s no way a child can possibly make it happen. Don’t get me wrong, my kid is still playing with it but she doesn’t use any of the buttons or levers…just kinda pushes the cars around the ramp (which comes off every single time she moves the toy)

2 stars because my toddler is enjoying the toy, despite all of its flaws. But none of the things it claims to do…are happening. We will trash this toy in about a week or two.
text_fidelity_b: Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4

text_fidelity_a:
T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set This is a great set to introduce kids (as well as adults) to the art of latch hooking. The instruction book is colorful and easy to follow, with clear directions and beautiful graphics. I would give this a five-star review except for two things:

The book gets you and your child excited to start making beautiful projects (including your own customized designs), yet it provides only enough yarn and canvas to make ONE double-sided, child-size pillow. If you want to make bigger and more complicated projects, you have to order more supplies. Because of this, I felt this was more of a "sample" kit, aimed at giving newcomers a "taste" of latch hooking to get you "hooked." For $30, I expected enough material to make at least two projects. Also, what yarn there is of so-so quality - it's rather light and thin, "play yarn" for children, I guess.

Also the packaging felt odd. The book is tied to an empty cardboard box that seems to have no function other than to fill space to make the kit look bigger and more substantial than it is. It's tied so tightly with pipe cleaners that you can't help but tear the back of the book as you try to free it. Another reviewer commented that this may be due to craft stores experiencing a lot of shoplifting - but the book could have been easily secured using double sided tape or light adhesive.

Other than that, this kit will provide hours of enjoyment for adults and kids, especially those (like me) suffering from cabin fever thanks to an interminably long winter. I would definitely buy more as gifts if it were less than the current price.
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set

Colored Pencil Set with Case, 7-Inch, Pack of 72 As an artist, I like to keep a variety of pencils on hand for different projects. I decided to test these out in an adult coloring book (with a fairy) and I am actually very impressed. I had low expectations, a lot of people seem to dislike them, but personally I really like them. My husband works at an art and craft store so I have tried a lot of brands and styles. This pack is a great one for starters or to add to your color palette in pencils. Colored pencils can be blended, but it's a lot easier to have a variety of colors to get the shade you want. I spent about 2 hours coloring this page using only pencils from this pack. There are a few colors I would like to have seen, but over all it's still a very diverse pack. There are a lot of lighter and brighter tons than I have in my other pencils.

The pencils themselves have not given me any trouble. The wood is a little lighter than say the Crayola brand ones, but they sharpen fine and as long as you aren't pressing extremely hard the lead does not break. I pressed fairly hard to blend the trees and none of the pencils broke for me. While this was not an art venture, this page was used for me to test the pencils and I am happy with the results. Before I would color on the page, I used a blank page to scribble a little as it can be hard to differentiate some of the colors from the other shades, but I do this anyway so I am sure about the color I want before I get it on the page and accidentally wreck something.

The colors blended fine, I probably should have gone back and finished shading, but as a test page it worked fine. I mixed this pack in with my other pencils so I can choose from any color I could need. When I started out I used the cheap brand from the craft store and these are much higher quality than those ever were.

I wouldn't consider the plastic thing a case though, it's more like a package. Not easy to use. I put my pencils in a storage tote so I could easily go through and choose the one I need. I may end up buying another pack for my mother down the road, she likes to color and basic pencil sets do not have this variety of colors. The price is extremely competitive as well. I paid almost this much for my set of 48 Crayola pencils.

text_fidelity_a: BARWA 41 Pack Doll Clothes and Accessories 5 PCS Fashion Dresses 5 Tops 5 Pants Outfits 10 PCS Mini Dresses 10shoes 6 Necklace 5 Glasses for 11.5 inch Doll In fact, I just ordered another set. As an adult fashion doll collector and semi-professional photographer, I appreciate the fact that the clothes are from a variety of dolls. Some of the clothes are standard, wide hip Barbie size, while others are slimmer in the hips and torso (more like Model Muse) and still more fit dolls who are short and petite (like Barbie's sisters Skipper and Stacey). The Skipper and Stacey size tops look cute as midriff baring tops on a regular Barbie. I read a complaint below about the pants not fitting, but that's the way Mattel has been making pants since about 1999 when they introduced the first wide hip Barbie doll (the doll that we know today as a regular Barbie). The jeans are meant to fit below the waist and you have to tug to get them on and close them completely because they are meant to fit snugly. It's true, the clothing seams aren't always perfectly straight, but I have the same issue with Mattel Barbie clothes that I buy in person. Plus, the fabrics for these fashions are - for the most part - nicer than what Mattel has been offering lately. At the end of the day, when you consider that SINGLE ITEM Barbie brand clothing packs currently sell for $2.44 - $5.00 each, and Barbie brand complete fashion sets with shoes retail for $5.00 - $35.00 each, spending just under $2.00 for complete outfit is a great deal.

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome I figured the Fisher-Price Power Wheels Dune Racer would be a great way to keep my nieces' occupied when they visit. It certainly made them very happy when they saw it! Over all, it's a great power cart and an improvement on the one they have at home, but there are one or two minor issues.
It was delivered in a large box, and since is a 'some assembly required' type of toy, some components were not secured in the box. These parts were in plastic packed within thin foam, along with heavier parts, and had been bounced around in shipping. Because of the way the racer was packed, this meant that there were some scratches on some of the smaller chromed plastic pieces. A minor detail, but some people might not be happy to have a toy arrive in less than pristine shape (also, know that a VERY large box may be just left on your porch or by your garage).
Assembly took the boyfriend about 45 minutes using a screw gun with no issues... but he's pretty good about putting things together. Might take some others a bit longer.
While we tested the battery and found out that it had a little charge right out of the box, for a full charge, you pretty much will have to charge it overnight (about eighteen hours). So yeah, there's a bit of delayed fun-time with the toy. Might be some disappointed kiddies if they see it and then find out they can't do much more than sit in it for about a day.
The decals were tough to peel from the sheet. The wax paper was peeling off along with the sticker due to how thin the stickers were, and they were cut too deep into the backing paper. All in all they were a bit of a pain to put onto the racer - might not be worth it to put them on at all (not sure my nieces care about them, to be honest).
Another minor issue is that the gas pedal is in the middle of the cart, causing the driver to stretch a little to reach (especially when you add that you can't move the seat forward). The shifter was also in the center, as well as directly under the driver’s right knee (at least for my nieces, who are a little more than four years old). So when they were touching the gas pedal, it would sometime shift gears on them, between reverse, low and high. They seem to be learning to be more careful, but still, something to be concerned about when this happened, especially in reverse when they would hit the gas, and their leg would bump the shifter into forwards, causing the cart to lurch in that direction.
A nice thing about the Fisher-Price racer is that it goes well on both grass and on hills with a 30 degree angle. Compared to an older power wheels toddler 6v that the girls have that couldn't manage going up hills, they're having so much more fun (and want to take it home). The seat is comfortable and the racer looks great (scratches aside).
There is no 'brake' to the racer, but once the foot is removed from the gas pedal, it stops.
All in all, the racer is a hit and I'm sure the girls will be begging to come over to use it. One or two features could be better designed (I have to wonder if it's to fit to older kids as well to younger), but on the whole, it's a very nice cart that kids should be able to enjoy for a couple of years (depending on their age).
Overall the kids love it and have a blast with it. Giving 4 stars because of packing, QC issues, and some ergo issues.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

text_fidelity_a:
LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship) When I got this, I still didn't solve the Rubik's cube. I know there are all kinds of tutorials, but I wanted to solve it on my own. Fast-forward 11 years later, I flipped the table (so to speak) and watched a couple tutorials. This was the cube I used to solve the puzzle for the first time. I watched a couple videos of the cube before receiving mine to get a better understanding of the mechanisms and design. During my first session, I set the magnets to the strongest and left the dials as they were. Two hours is how long it took me to solve it on the first try.

I like that this cube comes with a handful of accessories. I use the case to carry the cube with me to and from work. It stays on my desk; whenever I have to read something on my monitors and not use the keyboard, I solve a little bit. Now I can solve the cube in minutes, though it took me a few days to get to this point. I now have the spring and tension set to the strongest for how much force can be pulled and weakest for how fast turns can be. (Apologies for not using the correct terms, but I tried looking up what the dials exactly do and I still can't figure out which does what with regard to the terminology, but I base it off feel.)

The cube comes with a leather bag and a tool to adjust the magnets. The first time I accessed the dials, I used a pen to pop off the tiles. They can be difficult to pull off by hand alone, even after being pulled so many times. The lever for each dial also was difficult to pull. Now, I leave it semi-flush to the dial to make it easier to access in the future. They also pop off easily, but are [somewhat] easy to put back. The magnet levels sometimes move on their own. If I happen to notice a magnet at a strength I didn't set it at, I'll re-adjust. Annoying, but an easy fix. I no longer use the tool that came with the cube because any item small and flat enough will work. The bag is kept in the box for now.

There are two manuals that come with the cube: one for the cube itself and the other on how to solve it. I tried using the solve tutorial but found it confusing with some typographical errors, so I used videos. I learn better visually anyway. Even though the cube's manual has great illustrations for the mechanics, I failed to understand what they actually do, so I looked up videos for that too.

This is the third cube I own and currently it's my favorite. Each time my time lowers after solving, I adjust the settings. I'm becoming a speedcuber without realizing it.
text_fidelity_b: LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship)

Fisher-Price Dora Fiesta Favorites Kitchen Fisher-Price has made learning to cook a lot of fun for both girls and boys with this Dora The Explorer Fiesta Favorites Kitchen. The kitchen itself is made of a high grade, colorful and sturdy plastic that you have to put together with a screwdriver. You'll spend around a half hour screwing the walls and shelves together and to the base, and that's it. The batteries that make Dora talk to the little cook are already included and inserted in the compartment.

This colorful kitchen is very compact and everything gets conveniently stored inside the roomy refrigerator and oven. The sink is over the refrigerator and the burner and grill is over the oven. Above the sink/stove top is a window and a place to slide in the recipe card, and above this at the top is a shelf. Next to the recipe card is a cell phone holder. Dora stands behind the stove cooktop to the other side.

The recipe card is double sided, with 2 recipes on each side for a total of 4 recipes included. When you slide the card in, you can then press one of two flower buttons that speak to you with directions for your recipe. Sometimes the phone will ring as well and speak to you. There are over 60 phrases in English and Spanish. One side of the card has 2 recipes for a Barbecue- hamburgers and ice cream and the other side of the card has 2 recipes for a Spring Picnic- huevos rancheros and tacos. Step by step, Dora tells the little cook exactly what to do.

All the ingredients and cooking utensils your little chef will need to create these 4 recipes are included. There are 20 play accessories, including: plate, spatula, pan, cup, fork, spoon, phone, salad dressing, milk, hash browns, egg, lettuce, hamburger patty, tortilla, chicken breast, buns, banana and ice creams. Some of the food items are hard plastic and some softer, like the real food.

Your kids will have so much fun learning to create scrumptious dishes with Dora in this wonderful talking kitchen. I'm already looking for more recipe cards for this kitchen and I found a great Holiday Cookies one for this Christmas for them. We've had other play kitchens, but this talking one gets all the play time by both the girls and boys.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Dora Fiesta Favorites Kitchen

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Dual Defenders Blaster As a caveat, we are a Nerf gun family. We have spent a lot of time in the basement setting up forts, donning safety glasses, and trying to nail each other with darts. So we were a little skeptical about a "copycat" gun system just as we are of Lego rip offs. But this gun had a few happy surprises, like the way the darts stick to the special target and the incredible range we were getting on the darts.

Quality - the plastic seems a little more brittle than Nerf guns, and in general, I don't feel that they are quite up to the same level of quality. However, they have stood up to a lot of firing by the boys and are still going. And the darts are rigid and seem to be holding up to the abuse better than the foam Nerf darts do.

Aim - These have fairly decent aiming and you can consistently hit the target if not the bullseye. During battles they are fairly deadly, especially since the dates have a little more zing.

Fun factor - It's up there with Nerf. We don't include them in our battles because they have a little more zing than we want. They are good for target practice although since the darts only stick to the magic targets, you are limited with what you can aim at to get a satisfying hit. The fact that this set comes with two guns is pretty key to fun. Shields are a little gimmicky, but the boys love to pop them open and closed.

Value - They are in line with the Nerf guns. We have an arsenal of Nerf and many refills of Nerf darts so we will probably not expand into the Boomco system. Also, the refills of darts are fairly expensive, but if they end up like Nerf, you should be able to shop clearances and sales to refill.

Summary - They are not bad guns, they just aren't Nerf. The boys have enjoyed playing with these, but I think that barring an amazing design on something from Boomco, we will stick with Nerf.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Dual Defenders Blaster

Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi I haven't gotten any feedback on this from the people I gave it to.. I would normally not bother with a review, but I thought it looked promising enough that it was worth recommending (even sight unseen, but I at least has opportunity to really look at it eventually, just not play it through). I bought it as a christmas gift for a couple of young boys- ages 10-14ish. Not entirely sure. When I am selecting gifts I always buy games or books for kids, always looking for educational offerings.. and given the theme of this and how it is designed for education in mind.. I thought this one seemed right up their ally. I had read reviews, looked over the details of the game, and while it cost a little more than I would normally spend on a token gift for kids I don't know real well, I thought it was interesting enough sounding to me- and educationally interesting that it would be worth a bit of a splurge (hoping they liked it and benefited from it!). Math, imagination, intrigue, magic, economics, strategy, skill development.. all UNPLUGGED- no need for apps, electronics. Can play under kitchen table light, or by candlelight. *I* thought it sounded fun. I may have to pick up another game for my own use at home.

I also liked the look of the box and the components. The colorful thick cards, bright potions in bottles on a rack, thick play currency.. It just didn't/doesn't look cheap. I was able to look over the materials, and it is a solid looking game. I just didn't have chance to actually play it. I really hope they liked it,and that the parents appreciated it. It seems like a game to hold on to, take care of and use time and time again.

It is because I am considering purchasing again for future gift giving, and have recommended other people to check it out, and that I keep it book marked to come back to, that I am going ahead with a full 5 star rating. It looks good, has quality look and feel, has game play with both education and imagination in mind. Instructions are straightforward- not too awkward or frustrating. The marketplace reminds me of any of the online game play (especially mmos) but all without the need to be attached to electronics.
text_fidelity_b: Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi

text_fidelity_a:
Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1 I really like that green toys uses recycled plastic and makes a variety of very simple, imagination based toys that are fun for kids to play with. This toy really seems to have a lot of potential in that regard. There are large barn doors on both sides of the barn that open and shut, and it open and airy second level where the sheep and pigs can hang out and look out the window, etc.

The fencing and the little covered area presumably for a trough are getting ignored at our house, I have a three-year-old and a not quite one-year-old, but the barn itself, simple animals, and truck were greeted with boos and eyes upon opening, and have been in play ever since, not only with the things that came in the set but with their other toys, which is really what one hopes when buying an open-ended toy like this. The truck has enough room to put action figures, Lego bricks, pig, etc. in there, and the barn is the same.

I have one quibble, actually two: while the barn seems like it should fit the truck, when you try to close the doors, the truck squirts out the back doors. When you go to close the back doors, it squirts out the front doors. There's not enough room in the barn to park the truck, even though (and this is what my problem with it is) it looks like it was meant to be parked in there. My toddler can be a little bit uptight about these types of things and when he is in a bad mood, this failure of the truck to park properly in the barn really upsets him. How hard would it have been to design these figures so that they all worked gracefully together? I think many toddlers would have really appreciated that thoughtful touch.

My other minor quibble is that the cow figures stand on two legs and are dressed as farmers. We try to present things that are at least a little bit based in reality to our children of this age, and so a cow dressed as a farmer would not have been my first choice. I would've preferred one farmer and one cow that actually looked like a cow, or two cows and no farmer, if they were worried about what color of plastic to make a farmer so that it appealed to everybody. I think they wanted a farmer figure to sit in the truck and drive it, and that is nice but not 100% necessary.

Overall, this is an awesome set and would make a fabulous gift for families that have kids of different ages. I personally am getting rid of the fencing and covered outdoor red thing, plus the weird cow farmers, but the base set – a barn, some pigs and sheep, and the truck, are awesome. Even though you would give the gift perhaps to one child, it is nice that everybody can play with it, it is not gender-based, and it has potential to be played with in a variety of ways as the child or children grow. Another win for green toys!
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1

text_fidelity_a: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use Started to buy one of the more expensive models but noticed this one didn't have any mention of foaming issues so decided for the price to give it a try. WOW! This thing is great! Thousands of bubbles most just under tennis ball size but some smaller. If you use the Gazillion Bubble solution you get beautiful iridescent bubbles that drift a long way before breaking. It works best and the bubble sdrift farther if you can get it up off the ground. A breeze helps too. I set it on the top step of a 3-step ladder and that was perfect. This machine is a bubble solution hog but it couldn't be any less and produce this volume of bubbles. Seems to run maybe 20 minutes or so on a fill and you get about 4 fills from a bottle of the 2 liter Gazillion Bubbles solution. It can make a but of a mess on the ground under the machine so be sure to place it somewhere that doesn't matter or is easy to clean. I didn't find the machine all that difficult to clean after using but you have to have a little patience. Hold it upside down and use the garden hose on low flow to wash out the solution tray being careful not to wet the motor or switch.. We ran this off and on over the 3 day July 4th weekend and it ran perfectly. Kids and adults both were amazed. If you want a bubble machine and don't want to spend a lot of money get this one.
text_fidelity_b: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use

-- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. [[ASIN:B00JBP32A0 JST JST-XH 3S Balance Wire Extention 20cm adapter 11.1v LiPo Battery Cable Li-Po]] This also allows you to put the cells into a fireproof bag during charging. [[ASIN:B005Q3VSZC Bluecell Black Medium Size Lipo Battery Guard Sleeve/Bag for Charge & Storage]]

One other accessory that really helps is a compact voltage indicator [[ASIN:B003Y6E6IE Integy C23212 Lipo Voltage Checker/Warning Buzzer]] that you plug into the balance port on the battery. Not strictly needed for recharging, but is very useful to monitor voltage after charging.

You'll need to consult YouTube for useful instructions on how to manipulate the four buttons and why, unless you want to read the manual. And who reads manuals anymore when a good ten minute video is clearer and simpler?

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900 The foldable flyer is so far so good--easily put together, nicely constructed, easily foldable and relatively compact.

Packaging: It comes in a large box already folded. Separate parts are minimal: the canopy (folded), the handle, two wheels packed separately with their screws, the four rods that hold up the canopy. Everything is clearly packaged, plastic is wrapped with very easily removable tape, several soft cushions protect from banging/scratches. Took about a two minutes to pull everything out and remove them from their bags.

Assembly: You need a phillips screwdriver and a wrench. From already having the parts out of their bags and laid out to completely done and mobile took exactly 14 minutes. It’s an extremely easy, simple, and fast assembly.
1) Pull up on the handles to unfold the wagon
2) Press down on the middle panel to snap into rigidity
3) Attach the two separated wheels, each of which is labeled L or R accordingly (the label is sort of a raised letter--black on black--you may need to look closely at the wheel strut to see it. Attaching the wheels consists of dropping the wagon atop the wheel struts, placing a washer and screw, and tightening. Simple, fast, easy.
4) attach the handle--one bolt and nut. Simple, fast, easy
5) Push the four rods into the holes for the canopy and press down
6) Attach the canopy via four snaps onto the top of the rods

The holes/snaps all lined up perfectly. There was no difficulty, no manipulation, no cursing. All as easy as could be.

To fold, simply remove the canopy and lift up the center panel. Again, worked flawlessly.

It’s a mix of plastic and fabric. But the plastic doesn’t feel cheap and the fabric seem pretty rugged. Overall build quality seems solid and as if it will last through the years with little kids.

It moves smoothly and easily. It’s very light and maneuverable. The handle is not adjustable, but it does allow you to contract it for storage. There are cup holders on either side of the inside and cup holders on the outside end at the handle.

The seats have a “seat belt”. They cannot be removed, nor do they fold flat. The canopy is a nice touch for shade and rain (though it won’t stop kids getting wet if there’s any wind slanting the rain).

Really, there’s nothing at all to complain about. If you don’t mind the price, this is an excellent and convenient pick-up
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900

Hot Wheels Track Builder Unlimited Slide & Launch Pack for Kids 6 Years & Older with a 1:64 Scale Hot Wheels Vehicle, Moveable Kicker Booster & 3 Track Pieces that Connect to Other Sets This is a redesign of previous Track Builder Loop Kicker, and it does same job - a rubber band powered leg gets triggered by car passing through to "kick" the car faster through the loop - but this one changes the pieces. Gone is the ball-joint of the center tower track mount from the older version (mount is still there, but fixed to flat position), and the 2 track pieces and center connector that make up the loop have been replaced by 2 fixed, hinged pieces of pre-curved plastic that snap together. Redesign comes with 2 less pieces of flat track.

Pros
- Kicker loop quicker to assemble than previous version
- Loop doesn't flex as much as old version, so cars keep more speed through the loop
- Includes 2 pieces of straight, low-sidewall track
- Includes 4 newest track connector pieces despite not needing any
- Includes 1 car that works with track (not all Hot Wheels work with all track sets)
- Kicker leg has a safety hinge so a second car can pass under it

Neutral
- The included car is an easily-found 2019 basic release, the mint Speed Blur series version of Exotique

Cons
- Isn't that much faster than just setting up or taking down track
- When folded down, takes up more space than the older one where you disassembled track
- Not that easy to remove the center tower from the base
- Smaller base is harder to put weights on to keep the track from moving when it kicks
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Unlimited Slide & Launch Pack for Kids 6 Years & Older with a 1:64 Scale Hot Wheels Vehicle, Moveable Kicker Booster & 3 Track Pieces that Connect to Other Sets

text_fidelity_a:
CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party Late last year, for a week or so, all 3 of our cats sat gathered around the stove in the kitchen just staring at it. I quickly figured that was probably NOT a good sign-that we likely had an uninvited guest in our home. A few days later, I was proven correct. Got up early one morning to take the dog out and there was a dead mouse by the front door waiting to greet me, with 2 of the 3 cats sitting close by, proud of what they had left for me. (I don't think I've ever screamed louder in my entire life than I did that morning! lolol-I did heap praise on them after I calmed down) Unfortunately, the cats were once again gathered around the stove watching...and a few days later, mouse #2 was waiting for us to clean up. (Thank God I didn't find that one)

As soon as I saw this cat toy, I immediately ordered it. Though one of our 3 cats who helped catch the mice has since gone to the Rainbow Bridge, I knew the other 2, Miss Piggy and Squeaky, would have loads of fun playing with this toy. (And if I'm being honest, I want to keep them in tip-top shape in case any further 'uninvited guests' find their way into our home! lol) The mouse (I see it more of a rat than a mouse) is nearly 11 inches long from the tip of the nose to the end of the tail. It has beady red eyes that light up. From a distance, I believe people (who don't know its fake) could mistaken it for a real mouse (rat). It has gray fur and what appears to be sharp teeth sticking out of its mouth. (The teeth are NOT sharp, they only appear that way) The mouse takes 3 AAA batteries (not included) and the remote controller takes 2 AAA batteries as well. (not included) The only assembly required is placing the batteries in the mouse and controller. A nice, small screwdriver comes with the toy, something I especially appreciate! (Works on my eyeglass hinges as well!) The controller allows you to move the mouse forward and backward. (Both of our young kids were able to operate the remote control without issue while we stood with them) It does work on carpet but works far better on flooring. As soon as we turned it on and began steering it around the room, 2 cats immediately popped out of their beds, their curiosity piqued. Both cats watched the mouse zip around the floor for a bit. As soon as it got close to Miss Piggy, she jumped and ran under the bed. lol. But Squeaky...he was far braver than Piggy and watched it up close. We'd stop it for awhile and he'd creep closer and closer to it, staring at it....and then we'd start it up again. lol. It was loads of fun to watch him with this toy. It certainly kept him entertained for quite some time! Piggy stayed hidden but she's a nosy cat...she'll get the hang of it before long.

This is a fun toy not only for cats but for cat owners to operate for their cats! We had loads of fun watching the cat's reaction. Its a great way for your cat to get some exercise as well. Very easy to operate also!

UPDATE******************

We got this out again tonight to play with. This time, the dog had more fun chasing it than the cats. However, after just under 15 minutes of use, it stopped working entirely! Even though I had used brand new batteries in the mouse and the controller when I first got it (a day ago), I replaced all 5 batteries. It does NOT work at all. Nothing happened to it. It did not fall, it didn't' crash, it was not damaged in any way, it simply stopped working altogether in the blink of an eye. And that's a darn shame because my cat AND dog had fun with it. Due to the fact that it stopped working entirely after just under 30 minutes of total use since we got it, and the fact we did nothing to break it/make it stop working, I've changed my rating/review of this item. I cannot recommend an item that stops working out of the blue as this did. For the minutes that it did work, my pets loved it. And we loved watching them have fun.
text_fidelity_b: CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party

Educational Insights GeoSafari Day 'N' Night Ant Factory (Glow Ant Factory) STEM Learning, Ages 7+ We have made a number of forays into this concept with mixed results from DOA ants, to decent tunneling ants. It can be fascinating to watch their progress or frustrating when it is more a lesson of life and death as you ants die one my one without really doing anything.

In this case the biggest differences in the concept is that it can be lit with LED's to give a spacy look at night. This doesn't add anything for the ants and not much for the viewer except for a little coolness.

My biggest beef with this is the current $30 price tag. For that price you should be more than just a piece of plastic with fifty cents of electronics. At the very least it should be free ants with free shipping. It just seems a little steep compared to earlier farms we have had. Also, know that you can refill the tank and reorder ants (which have generally short lifespans - a couple months.)

It's ok and we are looking forward to our ants, just a little pricey for something that is not appreciably better than other sets.

ETA hand2mind Connecting People, Set of 96 This educational toy consists of small, easily swallowed pieces, making it a choking hazard. Thus, it is not recommended for children younger than age 5 and should be kept well away from pets, especially puppies who like to chew things. This toy is recommended for grades K-4, which is approximately ages 5-9. It's primary purpose is helping children learn counting. They can also use it to learn to sort and classify.

The set includes 96 pieces of sturdy, plastic, free-standing, girl and boy figures. Half are male and half female. The pieces come in three sizes, each in four colors, yellow, red, green and blue. The sizes are all rather small, ranging from only 1/2 inch to 1 inch in height. The larger figures weigh about 3-4 grams and the smallest figures weigh about 1 gram. The figures are well made in terms of having smooth surfaces, which is important to avoid harming small fingers. The figures are stored in a zip-lock type plastic bag.

As advertised, the pieces do stand up by themselves, and they can be linked together. However, it can be difficult for younger children to clip them together. They each have a protruding peg on one hand and a hole on the other hand. It takes hand-eye coordination to match up a peg and a hole, and some finger strength to shove a peg into a hole. Taking them apart is even harder. Thus, this toy can be frustrating to kids on the younger end of the recommended age range, 5-6 years old, and is most likely to be handled smoothly by children on the higher end of the scale, age 7-9. Some of these problems might have been avoided if the figures came in larger sizes.
text_fidelity_b: ETA hand2mind Connecting People, Set of 96

VTech Touch and Explore Activity Table (Frustration Free Packaging) This was an excellent find. Activity tables, in general, have always been a huge hit with all of our babies, but this one is more unique in the sense that it encourages a lot of pounding. Let's be honest, babies have no fine motor skills; so slamming their little puggy fists down on anything is about all they have. And that's ok, because they love it (while strengthening their gross motor skills)! So what I found extra neat about this table has lots of areas that entourages that and will keep their attention. The xylophone part, especially!!!
The table itself feels heavy duty and well made. The plastic is very thick and durable; and it will be easy to wipe down and keep clean. The legs are easy to attach too. The only thing I didn't like about this toy had to do with my love/hate relationship with frustration free packaging. I love and prefer it because it's better for the environment... but it isn't very visually gift friendly. Of course I would prefer the recipient to see immediately the awesomeness they just unwrapped, but it's not a deal breaker. Overall though, I think this is the nicest table I've come across yet.

Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.

text_fidelity_a:
UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017) This UBTECH JIMU ROBOT-BUILDERBOTS KIT (Interactive Building Block System (357 Piece)) is so beautifully packaged, you’d almost think it was a smartphone or an Apple product. It comes in a heavy-duty, magnetic-closure box that opens like a book. Inside, the main controller, connectors and fasteners are packed in colorful paper boxes that nest perfectly in the big outer box. Is such a lovely unboxing experience wasted on a kid’s toy?

This kit will make either a “Grabberbot” or a “Digbot”. I say “either”, because the building components are extremely hard to take apart--you are NOT going to want to try a rebuild of either completed robot. Some (but not all) of the components are similar to LEGO Technic elements, but they’re smaller and definitely NOT compatible with LEGO.

In an afternoon (about 4 hours), I built the Grabberbot, which I like a lot. Using the Jimu app (iOS or Android), it’s easy to drive, very responsive, and actually picks things up. Grabberbot has a cool, multicolored LED light (you can program custom colors), and he has a voice cube with a large repertoire of sounds (also programmable).

Grabberbot is controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once he’s turned on or plugged into a power source. He does NOT have a separate controller, so you must have a tablet or a smartphone to make him work. (I use an iPad Mini.) It’s a good idea to charge the controller cube before you start building--it takes an hour or so. You do NOT want to spend an afternoon building a robot, and then have to wait for the battery to charge before you can play with it!

You can’t build the Grabberbot without a tablet or smartphone--you have to download the app to get the building instructions. (This is a pet peeve of mine; I believe that the instructions for building toys belong in the box.) However, in defense of the download-only instructions, they are presented in 3D! If you’re unsure about a particular step, you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

Grabberbot is more difficult to build than a motorized LEGO set. There are three reasons for this: (1) the instructions don’t always show the elements recognizably or exactly the way they go together (e.g., the sensor box has fewer connector holes than the one shown in the instructions); (2) the instructions don’t always start at the easiest place for the next step in the assembly; and (3) the components click together so firmly, you need pliers to separate some of them if you make a mistake.

Sadly, the color-changing LED light needs to be programmed if you want it to do more than flash colored lights for a few seconds when Grabberbot is first turned on. I did very little with the programming portion of the app, which requires you to identify which of the four servo motors you want to give instructions to (they are numbered), to choose commands for the motor(s), and to name and record the resulting
action. Programming doesn’t seem to be hard, but it does take some study and practice.

There is a charger with an AC adapter included. The red light on the controller box changes to green when the battery is fully charged. A firmware update starts automatically when you first connect the Grabberbot; it takes only a few minutes.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017)

Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig UPDATE: Oh, the poor little Bandit! Bandit has been Bingo's security blanket, humping companion, BFF, and "only other dog in the house" until we got a real-live lifewire little dog, Doobie, who is a Jack Chi. Doobie is one high-energy chewing fool. Doobie has gotten up inside of Bandit and pulled his guts out of his butt and also chewed his eyes out, leaving holes. Bingo is not happy and so is trying to tug his dear Bandit away from Doobie, so I knew Bandit was not going to be long for the world. I ordered a new Bandit for Bingo, and he is thrilled, but I'm going to have to put him up until Doobie is over his puppy stage. But this Bandit racoon puppet is a fantastic purchase for a little dog.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Move over Gator. Hit the box, Fox. Bandit has arrived.

Our 10-week-old Chiweenie puppy wants to bite-shake play, and even though he's careful not to be too vicious with DH's hand, he was breaking the skin. I got this puppet as a way to protect us from those sharp little puppy teeth.

Bingo went nuts for Bandit, and we did, too. On my hand, I don't like the fit on my thumb, which tends to slide out of the arm, but it seems to be fine on DH's larger hand. I just lift Bandit by the back and march him up and down, and the puppet is floppy enough, but also firm enough, to seem like a living critter.

I can't emphasize enough how nice the contrast between his nose and white snout is. When we say "bite his nose," he goes right for that little black nose. The nose and the eyes are sewn in very well so I don't worry so much about our dog pulling them off and choking them. Another thing really nice about this puppet is that it has some movement to it even when we are not assisting him in playing with it. He will pick it up and shake it, carry it around like it's his prize possession (which is funny, because it's bigger than he is), and put it in his "room" (a small rug) with his collection of squirrels and such.

UPDATE: Oh, Bandit is such a hit! Bingo sleeps with Bandit, pees on Bandit, madly humps Bandit, chases him all over the house when we throw him, carries him proudly to show "Bingo too" in the mirror, jumps up into the back of the loveseat in the living room with Bandit so Bandit can look out the window with Bingo at the neighbors passing by. Bandit has had to go in the washing machine quite a few times now, and with vicious chiweenie tug-of-war play, poor Bandit's scalp is starting to come unsewn. I can sew him up by hand and he'll be fine, but I'm already thinking I'd better get another Bandit to have on hand for when Bingo's BFF is in complete shreds! Bandit has shrunk some with washing, so it's hard to get a large adult hand into him, but he's still more than doing his job. He and Bingo now are about the same size. Bingo's eight months old and seven pounds.
text_fidelity_b: Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig

Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles [[VIDEOID:886df78722d87a8bdca79a9702180ce2]] This set is awesome!! There are a couple things to note about it that could be potential downsides/issues, if not prepared for-- but otherwise, everything is great! Below I will group the main points and for the 3 potential issues I'll mark it with this symbol:🔴 to hopefully make it easier to read through!

•We received all pieces included, and boxing, in great condition.

•1 car is included

•The quality of materials are true to Hot Wheels- great and sturdy plastic.

•It's a fairly easy set-up. My 9 year old put it together on her own by reading through the instructions step-by-step. It took around 30 minutes, may have been quicker but she often took short pauses, though she didn't need any help.

•There are about 3 different configurations you can do with this set. The video I posted shows each of these.

•Can connect to other Hot Wheels tracks and sets. (Including the colossal crash set that can be seen some in the background of the video I posted)

•Does not require batteries

•There are no levers that need to be reset for cars to go through the loops- my daughter has other loop sets that have those.

•You can set it up so that the launcher connects and starts at any of the loops. For example- you can connect the launcher to just the middle loop and the smallest. You can also try to launch it opposite- starting at the smallest loop and ending with the largest.

•You don't have to use the jumping ramps…you can have the cars finish the loops on a flat track.

🔴 One of the potential issues is the launcher- maybe it's just our launcher, or how we use it, but it can be a bit tricky to hit it with the right amount of pressure. Too hard and it knocks it off track. Too soft and it won't go around the loop. Sometimes it can take many tries and others it works right away. We have a few other types of launchers-- the long white one that is shown in the video I posted is the one she prefers to use since it seems to work better. Not everyone will have extra launchers, though. My daughter usually has no problem with trying multiple times with the one included in the set but I figured it's worth noting that it may not be a perfect launch each time.

🔴 The other possible issue are the cars used with it. You'll likely want at least a handful of different types of cars on hand, just in case. The one included does work pretty good. My daughter has a decent sized collection of cars and there a quite a few that often don't make it through the biggest loop. This could either be the car itself that doesn't work well or could also be an issue of the launcher (as just mentioned above). Some of her cars struggle on the biggest loop with the launcher provided- but when connected to the "stronger" launcher, they do great. And there's a few that still just don't make it. This could be an issue if this were very first set for a kiddo and if they have only 1 or 2 cars…just something to keep in mind if considering purchasing this set, you may want to consider also purchasing a handful of cars so that they can get the most use from it.

🔴 When you have it set-up as the Daredevil Jump or Gravity Drop, it sort of seems like the track isn't long enough since the cars shoot further past the cup a lot. So we added extra tracks (which aren't included in this set) and it helped a lot…the cars land in the cup more times than not. At the very end of the video I posted, you can see how we added an extra track to the Daredevil Jump set-up.

All-in-all: We love it! It keeps my 9 year old busy-- even if she doesn't connect it to her other tracks. She likes trying to get the cars in the cup and thinks that the triple loop feature is awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles
