Super quiet brushless motors, 1 battery and usb charger, nice controller. Comes with decent quality carrying case that stores everything perfectly, along with a zippered compartment area, where you can keep the manuals and spare props, yes you get a set free with the drone!

Flies well in the wind I put it up in winds that were around 15-18 mph and it handled them well, of course the advertised battery life suffered and was only about 17 minutes but it was fighting the wind the whole time. On a less windy day it was almost 24 minutes of total flight time!

If your looking for a drone to learn on at a decent price point this is a good one and it's the right size, this is my 3rd Holy stone drone and I'm pleased with the product, I own the 700d, 270, and now this bad boy. All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner This toy is plenty entertaining for a short while. It is great fun to make the art, and the paint colors are bright and contemporary (neon green, yellow, coral, blue, and purple). The spinner is seemingly durable, powered by one C-cell battery (which is not included).

But, consider --

The bottles of ink are teeny-weeny -- .6 fl oz each -- about the size of a small hotel shampoo bottle. The jars of glitter are even tinier. Although the kit contains glitter, there is no glue to apply it. The glitter seems like a bit of an afterthought. And for some reason, even though there are five colors of paint, spinner device contains only three holes to hold the paint.

The cards to paint on are tiny as well -- there are ten cards that are about 4"x 4" each, and another ten cards that are about 3" x 3". Half are black and half are white. You may be able to make "beautiful art" (says so right on the box) but at 3" x 3", it's hard to make much of a statement.

The kit contains a clear plastic "splash guard" That is labeled in tiny font as such, along with a "do not discard" warning. If you happened to overlook the label, you would likely discard the splash guard, as it is indistinguishable from much packaging.

I have a similar spin-art painter from Crayola, the color spinner -- hard to say which one of these two items would be preferable. This Alex spinner is battery-operated, the Crayola one is not. This Alex spinner definitely has cooler paint colors. The Crayola spinner has circular pieces of cardboard to paint on. They are much larger and the shape is more interesting. Either kit would be fun for kids. Once or twice.

This would be a fun toy to play with once or twice, but I wouldn't expect it to be something you will return to again and again. And if you purchase it, don't forget to get a C-cell battery.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner

text_fidelity_a: CGE Czech Games Edition Codenames Boardgame This game is best played with 4 people (two teams of two).  Your partner tries to prompt you to pick the correct cards on the table between you by giving you a single word clue and telling you how many cards on the table it relates to.  You need to decipher the hint by figuring out which of the cards they means, but don't pick the wrong one!  It could end up giving a point to the other team or if you pick the one "black card" on the table it ends the game and you instantly lose.  This game is endlessly creative and challenging as the word cards on the table and which cards correspond to your team will always be different each game.  The creative part is figuring out new ways to bundle the most cards together with a single word so you can find all your teams cards before the other team finds theirs. text_fidelity_a:
MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries Big & fast are the best ways to describe this RC racer!

At 1:10 scale, the unit ships with everything you need to run EXCEPT batteries for the RC transmitter. You will need to provide some AA batteries here. Also, make sure to charge your running batteries first.

Unfortunately, you will only get about 10-15 minutes of run time per charge. So having the 2 included battery packs is nice. Although, if you swap them out back-to-back, the one charging will not be ready to go before your second battery depletes. And charge time is roughly 4 hours EACH. So, you actually need A LOT of spare batteries if you want to run your car without any downtime.

Outside of this concern, the car is a lot like a hobby RC vehicle that you would assemble from scratch. But at a fraction of the cost. However, the parts are probably not hobby grade, but good enough for the intended audience of this vehicle.

In the mid-eighties, I was really into RC racing (A Tamiya Frog for those who remember), but even back then this was an expensive hobby (I was around 14, so everything was expensive!) as you always wanted to upgrade something - motor, servos, shocks, tires, etc... And I wasn't even running anywhere near top of the line stuff.

In contrast, this unit ships complete for right around $110.00. So, if you're just getting into the hobby (or re-entering), then this car will make a fun introduction/re-introduction without breaking the bank.

Lastly, this thing is FAST. It's rated right around 30-32MPH. That may seem slow when the only comparison you may have is driving in a car at that speed. However, seeing one of the RC cars rocket down the street at 30+ miles per hour will quickly alter your perspective!

Overall, this is a great out of the box setup that's a ton of fun for a kid, an adult or the kid in every adult!
text_fidelity_b: MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries

LEGO Disney Frozen Elsa's Magical Ice Palace 43172 Toy Castle Building Kit with Mini Dolls, Castle Playset with Popular Frozen Characters Including Elsa, Olaf, Anna and More (701 Pieces) This LEGO DISNEY PRINCESS ELSA’S MAGICAL ICE PALACE 43172 TOY CASTLE BUILDING SET (New 2019; 701 Pieces) is a reissue of the previously discontinued 41148 set of the same name that was originally released in 2017 (also at a retail price of $79.99). Some of the ad pages in the 43172 building instructions are different, but the models are the same.

The Elsa’s Magical Castle model isn’t large, but it has loads of sparkle and detail; and tons of play potential in the many accessories (e,g., castle furniture, Olaf’s train) and moving parts (e,g., swirling staircase, snow slide). It’s one of my all-time favorite LEGO buildings--one that I have on permanent display (alongside my big Disney castle model).

What I love most about Elsa’s castle is that it incorporates a lot of transparent “Frozen blue” bricks, many of which have embedded silver sparkles. I love shiny stuff, and Elsa’s shimmering cape is something to behold. I also love trains, so Olaf’s train is another plus. The little snowmen’s teeter-totter (near the snow fort) is fun. I don’t really care for the scary snow monster, but it helps in reenacting scenes from the movie.

Some of the model’s sparkle is added with stickers, but there aren’t a lot of stickers, and they’re easy to apply. There is a moving slide that opens and closes the tall castle front doors. There is a spiral staircase that swirls open when you turn a knob. The figures of Elsa and Anna are true to the cartoon figures in the Frozen film. This is truly a great, classic LEGO set, based on a great, classic Disney movie.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Frozen Elsa's Magical Ice Palace 43172 Toy Castle Building Kit with Mini Dolls, Castle Playset with Popular Frozen Characters Including Elsa, Olaf, Anna and More (701 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

Meredith is absolutely beautiful and my daughters love her glamorous clothing and hairstyle. An affordable 18" doll option that doesn't make me cringe to give to impulsive young girls for play.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith

The set up and instructions are easy to follow but, I would definitely recommend an adult be involved with the process. The two batches we made we done per the instructions and it seems like a day later, they are different and have different consistencies. The first batch came out perfect. There is a lot of stirring and kneading that has to be done to get all of the clumps out for a smoother slime. The slime came out doughy and fun. The second batch, done at the same time, feels more wet and sticky than the first despite having mixed and kneaded more than the first batch. The color and glitter add ins are fun but aren’t as eye catching as I thought they’d be.

The thing I was absolutely disappointed in was that there wasn’t a container to put the slime in once the fun was over. We ended up putting them in sandwich bags until I can grab something from the store to hold them in. Overall, fun was had but, turned out a little frustrating that the results were so clearly different from one another.

Overall, I would still recommend.

Classic Mancala Game - Features A Full-Sized, Solid Wooden Board with Exquisite Detail Stones by Pressman For 2 Players I do not play Mancala regularly but it is something I do enjoy, and I looked to this set as one I could take to the office to enjoy with coworkers. It’s a decent set up it lacks some fit and finish that would make it better.

Included in the set is the Mancala board and a plastic bag with multiple colored stones. There is also a concise rulebook on how to play one variant of the game - overall, a decent starter set.

There are several things about this set that make it less than ideal. The most serious problem is the board which has multiple issues. First, it feels unfinished with several very rough spots that are actually visibly rough. This doesn’t make the game unplayable but it does take away. My board is not routed properly and it looks like the design was routed by hand and wasn’t cleaned up properly with wood shavings wedged in the grooves. The reservoirs are shallow and it is easy to spill the stones while playing.

The stones are another matter. There are enough stones to play. However, there are no extras at all and if one or more are lost the game cannot be played correctly without replacements. And, there’s no container beyond a cheap plastic zipper bag for the stones; a cup with a snap-on lid, or a cloth pouch, would be so much better.

This is a playable and functional set, lacking in finishing touches that differentiate it from a good one.
text_fidelity_b: Classic Mancala Game - Features A Full-Sized, Solid Wooden Board with Exquisite Detail Stones by Pressman For 2 Players

To refill the brush pen, twist it open in the opposite direction than you may anticipate. It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.

So many refill kits only include 2-prong or Y-looms, even refill kits from Rainbow Loom. They call their 2-prong looms Happy Looms, and this kit does have two of those, plus the two big teal Rainbow Looms. The Rainbow Looms can be connected to each other, so that you can have a very long loom or a very wide loom.

The kit includes some instructions, but they aren’t the clearest. Videos are the place to learn the coolest techniques. I started making bracelets to keep my hands busy, and learned so much from YouTube.

In my opinion, the band colors are subpar. They are supposed to be from the JEWEL collection: green, purple, gold, black, white, baby pink, pink, blue, teal, and yellow. The white bands are actually clear. The baby pink bands are so pale they’re nearly clear too. The yellow bands are more like a yellow glow-in-the-dark, very very light yellow. The teal bands are flat teal, they don’t have any pearly or translucent sheen.

The storage box is nice, it has compartments for everything, including the pony beads and C-Clips. There are even slots for the crochet hooks. The box latches shut, so if the box gets knocked over, you shouldn’t have a mess to clean up. But the box is delicate -- mine arrived with several cracks in it, and a piece broken off the lid. So that’s something to be aware of if you take the box on the go.

text_fidelity_a:
HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 I am a solid intermediate (I hesitate to call myself advanced). Put a plane in my hands and I can probably fly it pretty well.

I have had a Night Vapor that I absolutely love to fly when I am too lazy to carry all the gear out to a park. I can fly the Night Vapor around the yard. I wanted something just a little bigger to fly in the small field behind my house. After seeing some videos on YT I could tell this plane can fly nice and slow. I made the mistake of thinking this was a 4 channel airplane when I bought it. I got it home and was a little disappointed when I pulled it out and realized there where no ailerons...until I flew it.

I have to say, this little plane is an excellent little flyer. It literally flies itself. Ultra stable in fast and slow flight. Docile stall tendencies and if you just stop touching the sticks it will roll itself over and be flying straight and level within a second or two. Take off roll is only about 5 or 6 feet if you jump of the power. Landings can be done in about 10-15 feet of concrete if you are good at spot landing. Just remember THIS IS NOT A PLANE FOR WINDY DAYS. As much as it sucks to get a RTF home and not fly it, be patient and wait. Even 5 mph is probably a bit much for this featherweight little plane. Experienced flyers will be able to handle this plane up to 5-8 mph but new guys should wait for calm winds. Since this plane is so light it doesn't really break easy, it just bounces off things. Being inherently dumb I like to do things I probably shouldn't. The result of this is my Champ being bounced off roofs, trees, rocks and pretty much any other object I just can't resist buzzing as close as I can. So far only little scuffs on the foam are the evidence of my wild flying. This little bugger is hard to break!

My Dad is new to RC and as soon as they get another Champ in at the hobby store I am buying him one to learn to fly.

As an experienced flyer I would HIGHLY recommend this for a new flyer or an experienced flyer that wants to have fun in a very big back yard or a small field.

By the way, I still wanted a 4 channel so I went straight back to the hobby store and got a Parkzone T-28 (the ultra micro version that is roughly the same size as the Champ). It is fun and the ailerons allow for more aerobatics but I have to admit the Champ is much more fun in a small field because it is so easy to fly.

I have a lot of airplanes and helis. I can't think of a better plane to learn to fly with. The Night Vapor I mentioned is also super easy to fly but the Champ flies more like the bigger planes so it will make a much better trainer.
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

text_fidelity_a: Educational Insights Panda Rollers I work in a high school special ed classroom. The students are considered to be moderate-intellect. I took this game in to play with some of them. The game can be played with 2, 3 or 4 players. Each player gets a set of 12 "eye" cards. There are two cards of each eye color, but one is a left side of the face and the other is the right side. You have to physically pick up the panda board to shake the dice. At first I thought it was like the old classic game Trouble where you press on the dome to get the dice to move, but that's not how it works. After the dice are rolled, you find the two cards in your pile the match what shows up on the panda board. It took one of my students a while before she started "getting" that the left/ride side mattered, but my other student picked up on it fairly quickly. I ended up with a set of cards, too, and I would position it correctly and model it for the one student to copy. The first person to have the correct eye match, wins a tile. We ended up playing three full games. Both kids liked it a lot. Although they are in high school, it was very appropriate for their academic levels. There's no reading, so we weren't slowed down by that. I would definitely recommend this to other special ed teachers or people with preschoolers.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Panda Rollers

text_fidelity_a:
Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions Well first I have to admit, I do not have an internet saavy family. And this game is very much tied into internet memes from "I can haz cheezburgers?" to "Erhmahgerd." Luckily, I have spent a healthy amount of my life researching internet culture, but I ended up having to explain a lot of the cards to my kids.

But the reason I love this game is because of how engaged it kept the kids, and the amount of laughs that it produced. The selfies were ridiculous and caused laughter in itself and the cards played were even better. The game is pretty simple, pick a card from your hand to recreate in a selfie, then others play cards with scenarios that best fit your selfie. There are a lot of "Trying not to poop" type of cards so the humor is a little juvenile but perfect for keeping kids engaged.

Everyone willingly took their turns on the cell phone and everyone seemed to really enjoy the game. Scoring was pretty meaningless which was good. I was thinking that since the person taking the photo got to be the judge of who gets the point for the best caption that there would be hurt feelings and poorly awarded points, but the fun of the selfies and reading the cards trumped any controversy. Actually we ended without caring who scored points.

All in all this is a great ice breaking game.
text_fidelity_b: Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions

text_fidelity_a:
da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People Gave this as a gift to a recipient out of state- Due to that fact, I never felt capable of reviewing the product. Craziest thing… almost a year later, when we went On vacation and met up for dinner at the house I sent this too..(can you follow that..?!) to my happy surprise- they were all playing awkward turtles!! Yep, the game I had sent to them almost a year prior!! (could have been contrived Sure-but, from the wear and tear on the game… I knew they had been using it all along.)

Of course, we went to have Dinner with the adults at the house.. But, their group of teen/20+ yr olds were laughing hysterically in the other room having “game night“ and I promise, they were having way more fun than we were!!

I peaked in on the gameplaying and the concept looked pretty straightforward. Basically, divided into two teams… One member has an awkward word and tries to describe it to their team- if guessed correctly they get points! And the game sort of back-and-forths from there… Funny, quirky, annoying, cringe worthy, racy words all make up the options.. These kids were playing the game when we arrived- 2hr. Later we left... And they were still playing! (No! Not the same round but, plenty of rounds and all entertained long enough to still be having fun hours later.)

To me, this is the best type of endorsement one can have… Seeing a game in action and hearing the laughter as it was being played. This told me all I needed to know… The game was a hit for the crowd at hand- it kept them happily playing for hours. Combined it with the ease of which it takes to “learn” the game.. And you’ve got a winner in my book!
text_fidelity_b: da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People

It's still the first toy she heads for when she visits. One kid can play on each side, so they can play at the same time. They didn't seem bothered that things didn't work quite right. Cons: The kitchen is basically held together by the parts having been firmly pressed into place. Thus, even lifting it by the roof can cause parts to come off. We've moved the kitchen around several times with no problem as long as you use the handles on the purple side panels. The oven and cupboard doors were initially hard to open, but luckily use has loosened this up some. There is some assembly required, and the instructions are simply line drawings. Keep the box since looking at the two sides in the pictures is of more help in assembly than the instructions. Keep in mind that you will not fully tighten the joints until done with the first couple steps. The barbecue sign is a thin sheet of cardboard, so I assume that the thicker board is supposed to be put in the slot along with it. I don't know why they didn't just print the sign on the thicker board or even just past it on. As it is, you're trying to fit two separate sheets into a slot seemingly meant only for the thicker one. I had someone try to help me get it into the slot, but it was too tight to get in very far. I ended up cutting off some of the top just to make it fit (though it turns out I didn't need to do this. You use three AA batteries to power the sound. Once you hook up the spigot, you can put water in the sink and then pump it out through the spigot. Since it is merely pressure that fastens the joints together, this could come apart under especially hard play, but it's unlikely a two-year-old will cause any problems with it. Overall, I'm pleased and my niece is extremely happy to play with it when visiting my house.

UPDATE: The stickers are coming off after about a week, and not just because of use. They just didn't stick well to the water bottle and utensils. The handles on the cupboard about the oven is difficult to open because there's nothing to really get a grip on the handle. It's the perfect height for a 2-year-old, but my 4.5-year-old niece has to kneel to use it. Crayola Glow Book I never really thought I would be calling any toy a godsend, but the Crayola Glow Book has done something for my ten-year-old son that none of his school teachers (and certainly not his art teacher) has been able to do. I've tried, too. I've tried asking, showing, cajoling, ordering, limiting privileges, exaggerated sighing, and using his full name, but my child's penmanship is abysmal and his art skills mostly stink.

The reason for this is relatively straightforward: in my family, kids develop their fine motor skills later than most kids do. My parents and teachers made me work at it, but I at least was getting a lot of practice all the time. My child goes to a school where he gets to type a lot of his assignments. He's learned a lot in art about color and perspective and design, but he gets extremely frustrated trying to execute what's in his head, so he stopped enjoying drawing and painting pretty much as soon as he hit kindergarten.

When I ordered this, I thought it was going to turn out to be just a gimmicky gadgety thing he'd use once and then I'd get to use it to leave notes my husband would have to work to ignore, but my son loves it. He can write, draw, erase, illuminate, and animate without having to commit anything to paper or to critical eyes (except his own). Because the illustration plates are layered, if he's happy with one part but not another, he can re-do the one without having to worry about smudging or wrecking the other. As a result, he is spending time using his fine motor skills, they are improving, and he is much happier with the work he is doing.

I gave this five stars for fun, based on his recommendation. I rate it five stars for educational value and five stars overall for how much help it has been in an area in which my child needed some help. I gave it four stars for durability. It feels a little flimsy, but it's holding up well so far.

UPDATE: When you exhaust the markers that come with this, you can use dry erase markers on it. They're actually a little bit easier to see and work with, they come in tons of colors, and they clean right up.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

Cat Construction 15" Toy Excavator , Yellow Note: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the CAT excavator.

When I received this item I was a bit surprised at how large it is, bigger than I expected. I was thinking this would be approximately the size of a bread loaf pan (a testament to how terrible my sense of measure is), so when the box arrived I was surprised when I opened it to find this large plastic truck.

This truck is all plastic which has some pluses and minuses about it. It’s not all that expensive, which would not be the case if it was metal or had metal parts in it. It’s completely waterproof, and it is made well enough to handle some limited abuse. It is not made of heavy-grade plastic, though, so if it is thrown or stood upon it could break.

There are moving parts but everything is manual. No levers, no buttons, no wheels other than the tires, so play isn’t as automated. This may or may not frustrate a young child, though that depends on the child and not the toy. It’s not a toy for the impatient.

This is a decent toy though there are some trade-offs. For the price it is a good unit that will keep a patient child busy. It is not the sturdiest nor is it the most technologically advanced, so it can be broken if handled very roughly and it may prove frustrating for a child who expects some automation.
text_fidelity_b: Cat Construction 15" Toy Excavator , Yellow

text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do-Art Dot a Design Animals For ages 6 and up. The set comes with 6 "design sheets" for kids to paint, but there are only 3 designs (koala, turtle, or dolphin). You get one sheet with only black-and-white lines for an older child to paint and dot. You also get that same design with the main colors pre-printed and you only need to add dots of paint to the white dots in the design. The kit also comes with: 8 acrylic paints (light blue, dark blue, green, yellow-green, yellow, orange, red, purple), 2 fine tip dotters, 1 medium tip dotter, 1 brush, sticky tac (keeps paper flat while painting), 2 cardboard frames with hangers, and instructions. Acrylic paints can dry out quickly, so you may need to add water to the paints to keep them from drying out. Acrylic paints can quickly dry onto clothing and not come out, so you'll want to wear a painting smock. Wash dotters, brush (and work surface) before the paint dries if you intend to reuse them. The "dotters" are foam rounds on the end of a handle, and they create somewhat raised paint dots on the design sheets. It's a fun idea with colorful paints, but it is kind of simple so probably for younger kids rather than teenagers or older.

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do activities, and then the parent will secretly leave another activity in the fairy house. This is suppose to make the child believe the fairies left them a gift. (For example: The child is to craft 3 fairy bells and hang them around their room. Inside the fairy house, they'll place a stick, pebbles, and a leaf. They'll then spin the house and ring each bell to summon a fairy visit.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids. In my opinion, there's more in the wizard kit. There is the same amount of activities in both, but there's just not as much to do in this fairy kit. (It seems more stickers and easy crafts.) It's not high quality, but it's still nice enough. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there'd the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though the wizard kit that is similar to this one could work for boys and girls(and this one still could, if desired), this fairy kit is definitely targeted to girls. At the end, I couldn't help but feel sorry for all the little children doing these activities, hoping to see a fairy. While gifts are left, which are supposed to let the child know a fairy visited them, they'll never actually see one, unless the parent does something extra. We just did the crafts, since we don't do imaginary things as real. Without the added magical element, though, this kit just doesn't hold near as much value. If you're like us and don't do Santa and all, I'd recommend another kind of kit. If you do love the idea of pretending fairies are leaving gifts, this might be a blast for you and your child, as long as you don't think they'll be too disappointed that they never actually see a fairy. Overall, I found it a little disappointing, particularly considering the current price(which changes constantly).
text_fidelity_b: Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House

It has a guard with a swiveled gold spinner at then end of the plastic and is attached with a screw, which could be removed. When fished for larger saltwater fish, it is a little bit bulkier than the usual spoon, in that is made with a rattling cavity "throat" at the eye end of the body up front to give it a hefty weight forward look. The rattling heard when holding the hook and swivel to keep them from moving is a low pitched clicking rattle. The size of this specific hook is comparable to a 5/0 Strike King hook and it weighed 0.84 ounce on my digital scale. The sound and wobbling, clicking and spinner flash may intimidate a finicky feeding smaller fish, but this luer will only make a big Bull Red Drum hungrier. Big Specs also should not be scared of this spoon and the shiny gold spoon is a proven offering for both redfish and trout. Bomber has offered a uniquely designed product with the Who Dat Rattling Spinner Spoon and the later reviews from buyers will determine if it will catch fish. Good luck with it and enjoy your next day fishing.

I took pictures with my phone and have tried to add them to the product pictures, haven't seen them yet.

Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit) The Klutz kits are hit and miss for us, but this one was a hit. Now, that said, like a lot of the Klutz kits, this is a difficult one for children, and will require a very hands on adult helper.

The designs are very nice, and the instructions are good throughout if you have Google or sewing knowledge. It's not that it's going to be terribly difficult to figure out how to sew necessarily, but some of the designs are reasonably complex. I'm not a sewer, but I could figure it out, and instruct my little ones. There are a lot of steps to some of them, and the dexterity needed means that this is going to be one for the older children almost exclusively - they'll need some "advanced" skills like maintaining an even stitch pattern that is not too widely spaced or narrow, figuring out what "whip-stitching" is without it being explained thoroughly, and so forth. Because the designs are all fairly small, you can make one, then save the rest for later, and the kit will see use for many crafting sessions.

I'm very impressed by the finished product as well. Overall, a fun and educational experience for the little ones and for myself as well.
text_fidelity_b: Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit)

text_fidelity_a:
Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary [[VIDEOID:e1253051a67b2634f9e78ac021248ab6]] I will be the first person to admit that I purchased these because I always wanted Sea Monkeys as a kid but for some reason I never got them.

The video was shot on day 5 after I put the eggs in. There are quite a few little guys swimming around it the water and they are doing fantastic. I used spring water in their tank, kept my hands and fingers OUT of the tank and placed them in a sunny window during the day and I don't move the tank around much at all. I also aerate them for about 20 seconds every other day with a small air pump and stone that is made for fishbowls, the smallest one you can find.

Mine hatched the day after I put the eggs in.

When the kit arrived, I rinsed it out with the spring water after taking everything out of it. Then I filled it to the fill line with spring water, put the lid on it and let it sit for 24 hours.

The next day, I poured the water purifier in. I didn't stir it, I didn't mess with it at all. I poured the pack in and then put the lid back on the tank.

Next day I aerated the water then poured in the eggs. Again, no stirring or anything. I left it alone, put the lid back on and walked away.

The next day, low and behold I had teeny tiny babies swimming around.

Fed them on the 5th day after they hatched, which was a few hours before I took that video footage.

I'll update again when they are larger but so far I'm really getting a kick out of this. It would appear that the secret is less is more, spring water, don't move the tank around and a lot of patience.
text_fidelity_b: Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary

Diamond Painting Stickers Kits for Kids, Paint by Numbers Diamonds for Adult Beginners,DIY 5D Diamond Art Mosaic Stickers I have the “28PCS POKEMON” option in this pack of diamond painting stickers from BLYNN. This option is really a multipack of different themes: Pokemon (12 stickers), Star Wars (8 stickers), and Princesses (8 stickers).

This is a great way to try diamond painting since the images are small. They vary in size, but are roughly 3 inches by 3 inches. An image this size takes about 30 minutes for a beginner. When you are finished putting the diamond drills on the image, you can peel off the back and it’s a sticker.

The pack includes two toolkits, so you can have two kids working on their chosen sticker at the same time. The diamond paintings can be cut apart -- I recommend an adult do this part, since the edges are close together -- and then worked on separately. That way you don’t have to remove the protective plastic from the whole sheet.

The pack also includes the drills for every sticker. Some of the colors are really off. Snorlax should be dark teal, but the drills are dark green. Eevee should be brown, but the drills are yellow-orange. The drills come in tear-open plastic baggies; I recommend having some small resealable baggies or containers ready if you aren’t going to do all of the stickers at once, since they often share colors (like yellow-orange for Eevee and Charmander).
text_fidelity_b: Diamond Painting Stickers Kits for Kids, Paint by Numbers Diamonds for Adult Beginners,DIY 5D Diamond Art Mosaic Stickers

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. I was afraid to force it to completely connect and potentially breaking the plastic connector. It is listed to be for 12-36 months, and up to 40 pounds. Personally, I think 12 months is a little young to be riding this, especially if your child is on the small side and not completely steady on their feet when walking. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad

The project went well, though her father managed to break two of the needles during the trial-and-error phase, so I'll have to replace those. GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'
text_fidelity_b: GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa

Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab These days with many kids doing home schooling due to lockdowns, this would be a great home schoolilng science project or lesson.

The age recommendation is for children six and up, however since most of these experiments require the use of a pot of boiling water, I think the manufacturer should increase the age requirement. Parental supervision is of course a great idea. The booklet is easy to understand, however it might be more difficult for younger children to read and understand the instructions.

I only tried the first experiment in the kit and it worked as expected, and it was the easiest, fastest experiment to get results. The instructions were easy to follow. (I also lacked any distilled water which many of the experiment recipes call for). It was fun for me as an adult to try.

I am not sure if this is an option or not, but it would be nice if refills on the "magic water, colors, (maybe even some not available in this kit) and paper cones) were made available so kids (or adults) can continue to keep playing and making different crystals. (Alum powder and food coloring are both readily available at any grocer.)

The box is attractively marked and would make a great gift for any adult or child who likes science or educational toys. This kit is compatible with other chemistry sets available from the same company.

All in all, it's a fun, educational kit that anyone can enjoy. The only true down side is that it may try the patience of kids who like instant results. Some of these experiments take two or three days to have decent crystals develop. I liked the kit and found it fascinating. I can't wait to try the other experiments in the kit.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab

SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is just one of dozens and dozens of slime toys intended to fascinate the young scientist in your home. The way most of these labs works is similar: Combine the included slime mix, if any exists, with a few household items like baking soda, vinegar, cornstarch, etc., and let the fun begin.

This slime toy works like the others in terms of the mixing, but it is also different than others, and I mean that in a good way. With this slime lab, the mixture is placed atop a motor that vibrates for greater effect. Kids can watch the colors and textures swirl around as the vibrations create some fun and very visual patterns. The instructions include 20 different recipes for slime and each can be made using items found in most kitchens.

What I probably like best about this slime lab is the lack of mess! Okay, there is some mess but in relative terms, the messiness is kept under control very well. The key difference is that, with most other slime labs my kids have used, messiness is encouraged. These other labs involve sticking hands in the slime, spreading it with your hands, and so on. This is messy and gross, and if multiple kids are involved, they often end up smearing it on each other, splattering it on the floors and more. There is no problem like that with SmartLab. The slime, for the most part, stays in the bowl, out of your way.

Educational toys are nice and SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is a toy that does get kids thinking and asking questions. My girls like it and have returned to it more than once, creating more slime and learning about household chemicals and how they react. It’s a good choice of toy that will keep kids entertained as they learn.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab

All five of my grand kids have some kind of sound machine in their bedroom, ranging from the $26 sheep to a $100 Ecotones Sound + Sleep Machine (I've bought five of those for adult family members).

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset There's a lot to love about sets like this that can be combined with other sets and used in creative ways. However, I'll say right up front that the whole point of getting this one is that you get the power booster, and the power booster, in my view, could use a big overhaul in the design.

Is it fun? Yes, without a doubt, the power booster is pretty fun. The problem? First of all, it takes 4 D batteries. Who uses D batteries nowadays? I'm lucky that we had just the right number of D battery adapters that allow us to use AA batteries instead, because otherwise I would have been in for a trip to the grocery store and I don't think it would've come cheap. What a power hog!

Second, the battery area needs to be taken apart with a screwdriver. This is fine for toys meant for the under three crowd, but for kids old enough to use a hot wheels set, it seems a little excessive and pretty irritating that every time a new set of batteries I need to become Mr. fix it and get out a screwdriver.

Third, when you actually go to play with it, the power booster is either on or off. So when the kid forgets about the hot wheels set and wanders off to go do something else, it's still sitting there using up your expensive D cell batteries. It's also noisy. I would've much preferred a button on the top that is easy for children to press that makes it work for a short period of time, such as 30 seconds. I'm guessing it is too much to ask to have a motion sensor turn it on or off or anything like that, so a limited time button that the child can find easily and press in the midst of gameplay without turning the power booster upside down would have been ideal.

That said, I think my primary criteria for evaluating hot wheels set is whether it is fun. Not fun for me, but fun for my kids. With only a little bit of help getting things set up, my three-year-old has been playing with this vigorously for two days and shows no signs of getting bored with it. We actually have a manual hot wheels ejecter to where you pull the lever back and press a button to make the car go really fast, and instead of using the power booster, we set that up for him to play with it on his own. The power booster is fun for when you make a big elaborate set up and are playing with a group of kids or with a parent for an extended period of time but to be honest I think when the batteries run down we may not replace them until there is a compelling reason to do so. It's just too noisy, and requires too much intervention from the parent to turn it on and off when it is needed and not just leave it noisily running and eating up our batteries.

The loop the loop works great with either the power booster or the manual ejection thing we already owned, and the tracks of course work with all of our other hot wheels sets.

I would probably recommend this most for people who have multiple children who will be playing with large and extended sets of hot wheels for 30 minutes or longer at a stretch. Otherwise, the power booster seems silly and kind of a waste.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

text_fidelity_a: Schleich Horse Club, 15-Piece Playset, Horse Toys for Girls and Boys 5-12 years old Pick Up with Horse Box This is a really cute set good sized set (roughly 18 inches long and 4 inches high) made of rugged plastic and with real rubber tires.  The truck looks realistic with nice details inside the cab with a center console, two bucket seats, a dashboard and a steering wheel.  It is molded in 4 colors plus a clear plastic windshield, sunroof and back window.  The side doors have no windows.  The steering wheel turns, but is not functional for turning the wheels.  The two front doors of the truck both open.  The hood of the truck opens to reveal an engine.  Nice detail including non-functioning headlights, parking lights, front grill, side mirrors, gas cap and a rear tailgate that also opens.  The only assembly required on the truck is putting on the 4 tires, which should be easy for just about any kid.  The horse trailer also requires putting on 4 tires and a special wheel in the front; also there are 6 trailer pieces that have to be snapped in place. An illustrated book shows how to install the pieces.  Pretty easy, but a younger child might have a little trouble figuring it out.  The pictures on the side of the trailer and the license plates on the truck and trailer are provided in a sheet of stickers, which a child can place where they like.  Includes a completely black horse with a blanket, 2 figures (a driver for the truck and a handler for the horse) and several accessories for the horse including a bridle, halter, saddle, a couple brushes, a bale of hay and a bunch of carrots.  Suitable for both boys or girls, especially those who like horses.  Probably this toy would be preferred by girls since the truck is pink and the horse handler is female. Even some adult collectors might like this set as it is colorful, detailed and well made. The real downside that I see to this set is that if you have very young children who will be around this, they could easily put one of the small pieces in their mouth and choke.  There is no instructions on showing how to use the horse accessories; most are obvious, but a couple are not.  The most important thing to know is that this is more of an "old school" type of toy; no batteries, no motors, no remotes.  A lot of kids today want the latest electronic devices and radio controlled toys, but this toy allows them to use their imaginations a little. I think that's a plus, but if you buy this for the kid who wants a cell phone instead, there will be a level of disappointment, I'm sure.  Note that this is made by a German company, with components from Germany, China, Romania and Tunisia. It's not that important to me where it is made, but it might be to you.  Note too that you can also buy other items in this series, such as a barn type structure, a corral and other horses.  If your child insists on other components, it could get expensive, if you give in.  As a kid at heart, I like this toy a lot myself and would keep it if I didn't have so many other things.  It will probably go to a grandson.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Horse Club, 15-Piece Playset, Horse Toys for Girls and Boys 5-12 years old Pick Up with Horse Box

text_fidelity_a:
Lulu Jr. My Comic Book - Create Your Own Comic This kit made my daughter so excited she literally ran out to the delivery man to get it squealing. She loves ANYTHING art related.

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
The kit comes in a nice box which is not too big, so it is easy to store while working on the comic.

The kit has a decent booklet inside which covers the following:
-Characters (ideas for who to draw)
-Settings (locations)
-Panels (how to draw and use them)
-Words (balloons, types of words and sounds)
-Styles of topics (flavor of the book)
-Art Style (realistic, cartoony, stick figures, etc)
-Character personality (giving depth to the character by quirks)
-Props to make the story interesting
-Panels and perspective
-Dialogue and sound effects
-Icons that are used to translate ideas, heat, etc
-Idea starters (great boxes with beginning sentences to motivate and inspire)
-Practice pages

There is a sheet which gives the specs for how the book will be printed and what not to use and what to use on the comic for printing. There is a series of design sheets that will be submitted to the publisher. A postage paid envelope is included for submitting the finished comic.

The kit also comes with markers, pencil, eraser, sharpener and a pen.

OVERALL COMMENTS
I think that this kit is a great inspiration for anyone who wants to make a comic. The instructional manual has great ideas to springboard from. My daughter is having some difficulty narrowing down her final ideas, but she has spent a lot of time considering and thinking of what to make her final comic like. This is a great gift and also a great addition to homeschool or art classes if you have a child who loves to draw and who especially likes comic books.

I am under a time constraint to publish this review, so I will update it when my daughter finishes her final product, submits it to the company, and receives the final comic back. At the time of this review, I am giving it five stars, but will adjust if I find that the final submission process warrants it.
text_fidelity_b: Lulu Jr. My Comic Book - Create Your Own Comic

The video editing software was easy to install and use, and we found it easy to edit the wobbly bits of video at the beginning and end of each good shot.

I also LOVED the feature where you can strap it to a bike helmet, scooter, etc. The fact that there were four little attachments meant that we could stick it to four different surfaces. Very cool!

Overall, this would be a great toy for anyone in the 5-9 range. I like the fact that it encourages outdoor play as well as indoor, which is a nice change from a lot of techy toys.

text_fidelity_a:
Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ I'm a fan of Faber-Castell colored pencils, and I've been meaning to try some sketching pencils as opposed to the mechanical pencils I've been using, so I grabbed this set.

The pencils give a good selection of hardnesses from the soft 6B to the very hard 2H, and I've had fun using the different pencils for sketching and drawing. I didn't expect much from the little plastic sharpener, but I should have kept in mind that this is a Faber-Castell set. That little sharpener not only sharpened the pencils to sharp points, it sharpened some of my colored pencils to long, sharp points - better than my more expensive art sharpener does.

The last two pieces of the set are the little how to sketch pamphlet, which is an overview, but has a few handy tips if you're new to sketching, and a small pad of paper. Even though I sketch on pretty smooth paper, this pad was too smooth for me to use. It might be the smoothest paper I've seen in all my life.

These are good pencils ranging from soft and easy to smudge to hard for details and fine lines plus two pencils that fall between the two. I like the pencils a lot, and the cheap-looking little sharpener is excellent. I'll be using the pencils frequently as I sketch and draw a lot, and I won't hesitate to buy more of these when I need them - but then, if you've used Faber-Castell pencils before, that probably won't surprise you.
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+

text_fidelity_a:
HOT WHEELS MONSTER TRUCKS MECHA SHARK FACE-OFF Play Set Once we unboxed the Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Mecha Shark Face-off Playset my 6 year old has been launching cars and trucks for about two hours now.

Hot Wheels is often hit or miss. They sometimes have a great idea and an awesomely executed toy. Sometimes the toy created nothing but frustration. So, this playset has captured my son's imagination and interest for a couple hours now.

The idea is that this is a Monster Truck Arena and you are to launch your Monster Truck into another Truck that is placed in a trophy. When you do so, there is a shark that spins and it spins to catch/eat/collect the Truck kicked out the trophy while your truck has landed in the trophy. I think.

Set-up as far as Hot Wheels goes was pretty easy. It took me a total of about 20 minutes to put it together plus the stickers (ugh!). This part of the instructions has no words so you have to guess. Be extra careful to peel the stickers off and put them on! (Any parents know that the worst part are the stickers!!) But once you have the base and the stickers on the base, the rest goes pretty fast and your kid is ready to launch. This comes with two Monster Trucks. One of the Trucks "falls apart" as if it's been actually in a crash. There are two spaces to put extra cars or Monster Trucks. You can play with just one person or with two people vying to try to land inside the trophy.

This is stand alone playset. It does not attach to any other Hot Wheel set. In other words there are no tracks to go with this set. And I'm ok with that. The reason for 3 stars instead of 4 is that I'm scared for the shark mechanism. I have a feeling that it will someone stop spinning or that my son will push in the wrong direction too many times and it will break. Actually, based on my experience, I know that will happen, it's just a matter of how soon that will occur. On the first day or in a couple days time. I would say that the instructions on how to play were confusing and didn't really make any sense. So, my description on what to do is based on what my son said and my interpretation of what the toy looks like.

Overall, my son spent hours launching cars into the air. He couldn't be happier and that makes me happy.

UPDATE:
As predicted (within 24 hours) something was bound to break. One of the Monster Truck launchers stopped retracting back so its ability to launch a truck as high or fast is greatly diminished. Therefore, playing with this playset isn't as fun as it used to be.
text_fidelity_b: HOT WHEELS MONSTER TRUCKS MECHA SHARK FACE-OFF Play Set

The track segments are made of small individual pieces, which is why the box says it comes with 220 pieces of track.

The track is flexible and can be arranged in many different ways, and each segment can be used as a straight or curved part of the track. The car worked well and stayed on the track. A small pamphlet with quick trips is included with ideas on making the track more fun. I used the cardboard pieces used to package the car to create a small ramp and tunnel which worked better than I expected. After the track pieces were exposed to bright light, they did slightly glow in the dark. However, the box shows a picture of a looped track. I tried both a couple types of loops and none of them worked because the flexible track wouldn't support the weight of the car. In spite of this, this is a fun racetrack set that allows for a lot of different track formations to keep kids interested.

One should just be careful to have plenty of clearance from hard objects when learning/practicing.. hitting into a solid item could potentially cause these to break! Definitely an item for older kids/adults.. Otherwise these may be a bit too fragile!! Priced at $35- it does seem a bit excessive for the actual materials used.. however, if enjoyed- it may end up $ well spent.

Not an easy feat to begin learning how to use- I suggest googling a few videos.. we found this is the easiest place to start and helped far more than any written instruction!! Springbok Puzzles - Eiffel Magic - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle - Large 30 Inches by 24 Inches Puzzle - Made in USA - Unique Cut Interlocking Pieces At 1000 pieces, this SPRINGBOK EIFFEL MAGIC JIGSAW PUZZLE (1000 Pieces) is definitely an “expert” puzzle. However, it goes together very quickly, because it has large blocks of unique colors--if you color-sort your pieces at the beginning, the jigsaw morphs into a series of much smaller jigsaws.

My puzzle, received in March 2019, had ALL of the pieces. No surprise, because I’ve assembled many, many Springbok jigsaws in my lifetime, and have never found one to be less than perfect. (The negative reviews suggest that Springbok temporarily had a quality control problem with this puzzle design. I sympathize with the people who received defective puzzles--even though Springbok will replace a defective puzzle, any guarantee is cold comfort when you finish a jigsaw and discover pieces missing.)

Though I wasn’t crazy about the picture, I ended up loving this jigsaw, and am saving it to put together a second time. It’s really fun to assemble, because the crazy-shaped pieces let you find fits by overall shapes as well as by design colors and patterns. There are very few dark or ambiguous pieces that are hard to place in a particular area of the design.

The only thing that I didn’t like about the puzzle is that two pieces frequently slide together side-by-side to make holes for the tabs of other pieces. This means that when you assemble a small area (e.g., the pink automobile in the middle), you can’t easily pick it up to move it to the correct location. You have to slide the assembly across your tabletop, or slide a sheet of paper under the assembly to support it as it’s moved.

Note that this is a very large (30” x 24”) jigsaw. Check to make sure that it will fit on your tabletop.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Forces & Interactions: Middle School Classroom Kit | NGSS-Aligned for Physics & Engineering Classes| Teacher Guide & Lesson Plans | Durable, Timed for Classroom Use, Includes Storage I generally love Thames and Kosovo’s products. This is a classroom physics kit. There are enough pieces to build several cars at once, but some experiments can only be done one at a time. For me that is fine since I am using this with homeschooling several kids, but for a small classroom, I can see students wanting to make their own. I am also not sure there are enough pieces to build more than one ramp. The snap pieces can be hard to remove especially for smaller finger, there is one connector puller included. For bigger groups of students I would have liked more of the pullers (looks a bit like the Lego splitter tool) You will need to provide weights for one experiment and batteries for the power module. I used slightly stronger nylon cord for my bucket pulls. It comes with magnets, wires, cord, nails, a cheep compass, and paper clips. Most of the odds and ends I just used my own and left the nails etc in the bucket.
There is a nice top divided tray to store the tinier pieces, and the bottom bin I left filled with the large pieces. The top of the storage box is dimpled to allow connecting the (not Lego) plastic building blocks to it. My kids had fun and easily figured out how to build onto any experiment we tried.
My one and biggest complaint with the kit is the magnet and iron filing board. None of the magnets work. They appear to have either been super heated or smacked around enough to unalign or weaken the magnet. I have a collection of bar magnets and rare earth magnets so I replaced the included magnets with my own. Most science teachers I know have collections of magnets so overall not a big issue. The clear iron filing board designed to show magnetic fields was a bust though. It’s not that the filings didn’t align, but that there were so few filings inside to show anything to begin with. I have a board I bought from a science teaching supply store and it has enough filings to demonstrate the magnetic field. This one was meh at best.
Because it does allow for multiple fun interactive classroom experiments I am rating this four stars. The spiral teaching book was great with Detailed instructions for building, and alignment guides (this assumes a knowledge of the material on the teacher’s part). The plastic technic like pieces were easy to use and fun for the kids. It was in the magnetism and wires and accessories that fell short of expectation. My Dad was a physicist (and MD) and I have a background in Physics as well, I had no trouble explaining what was going on to my kids, but this does not have answers to the questions because it assumes teacher knows answers, and how to relate NGSS Standards. Booklet includes lesson plan with target student age, time to teach, and any any materials needed. It is a great classroom kit, or group science instruction kit. Just keep in mind it’s target is classroom supplementary instruction, not home so kit is not designed to be a done by a kid on their own following a visually interesting book. (The spiral is pretty standard for teacher lesson books)
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Forces & Interactions: Middle School Classroom Kit | NGSS-Aligned for Physics & Engineering Classes| Teacher Guide & Lesson Plans | Durable, Timed for Classroom Use, Includes Storage

Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle Monster High toys and accessories are a huge hit with their fan base and the Travel Scaris Convertible vehicle is bound to be a big hit with kids who love Monster High. It is a stylish and attractive toy vehicle with a design that sets it apart from the average kid's toy vehicle.

I'm not usually very impressed with toy vehicles because I have seen so many of them and because most of them look very similar. But this toy vehicle grabbed my attention. The cool, eye- catching, all- around design pattern is one that is bound to warrant a second look and both adults and kids alike will find that it easily stands out against other toy vehicles.

Aside from the exterior, this Monster High vehicle does have other features that make it cool. The stylish wheels glide smoothly across a tile floor or a table without any problem and the vehicle seats up to four Monster High dolls. Rather than have all four dolls face forward, this convertible is a two- seat model with a pair of seats that are actually on top of the trunk, where the dolls face backward. Again, it's something unique that you don't find with other toy vehicles.

The Monster High Travel Scaris Vehicle doesn't have any lights or sounds. This may bother some youngsters, but it is better from an adult perspective because it means no batteries to buy and more imagination required. Most kids will not mind anyway- they will find the vehicle so cool and fun that they will not even notice that it doesn't make noise or have any lights. And another advantage is that boys and girls both seem to like this toy. Girls like it because its Monster High and boys like it because, well, it's a vehicle, which is a toy normally associated with boys.

This Monster High vehicle doesn't have opening side doors, and this is one quality that I wish was different because it would not only look cool, but it would also make it easier to place the dolls into the seats. But other than that, this is a fun, nice- looking toy that belongs in the home of every Monster High fan.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle

Mega Construx Pokemon Detective Pikachu Hi-hat Café Construction Set with character figures, Building Toys for Kids (328 Pieces) The Mega Construx Pokemon Detective Pikachu Hi-Hat Café set is recommended for ages 6+. I’d say the average 6-year-old will have difficulty with this set. I’m in my thirties and had trouble deciphering some of the instructions and assembling Ludicolo. And I’m used to doing UCS Lego sets!

Ludicolo is difficult to put together. When trying to fit the big beige rubbery pieces that cover the inner structure of his body, I broke off his arms several times. The rubber has to be smashed down and precisely fitted in order for the block pieces to fit and hold them in place. Then getting the lily pad head to line up properly took a few attempts, while holding the upper body piece in place.

Some of the bags of pieces are numbered and some aren’t, which I found odd. I appreciate that Mega Construx did attempt to organize them, as I’ve mentioned that in the past when assembling their sets. Having to open every bag at once and then spend time finding the pieces I need usually takes longer than the actual build.

The café is much easier to assemble, and I appreciated the cute, printed pieces, such as the cartons of milk. But beware that the pieces can take some finger strength to snap together; they definitely don’t click as easily as Lego does. Kids might have trouble with some of the steps, too; the instructions aren’t always clear.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Construx Pokemon Detective Pikachu Hi-hat Café Construction Set with character figures, Building Toys for Kids (328 Pieces)

Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

DWD INA Hatching Dragon GEN [[VIDEOID:86cf3e64e0b55c3de87641f5762af581]] I couldn't wait for Toothless to arrive! I've been collecting animatronic robotic toys since they were first introduced by Hasbro. I would have been over the moon of these were available when I was a kid and I adore him.

I've decided to post the video of Toothless hatching since you only get to enjoy that once and I preserved all the pieces, but you have to remove some internal part in order to place him back in his half shell where he sleeps,

I collect them so I saved everything. If you set him on a flat surface he rocks so it's best to keep him in his shell for extra stability and cuteness factor.😍

HATCHING::
The process takes about 20 minutes and you get to encourage him on his journey. He responds with adorable sounds to show you he is trying his hardest to meet you. His eyes flash and he makes grunting and light struggling sounds. 😍

A DRAGON IS BORN: 🐣
Toothless greets you with cooing with flapping wings, head tilts, and happy sounds.🐥

PLAYING:
He has 7 settings and play modes with 4 touch sensors and responds with different actions and sounds depending upon which sensor is activated by touch. Toothless is equipped with a mic and reacts to voice. Place his fish near his mouth and he makes eating sounds, but his mouth doesn't open or close. In blast mode, there are two blue LED lights on each side of his mouth that flash and he makes a photon blast power-up sound. He makes several sounds (I haven't counted them all yet) with affectionate noises to encourage interaction. ❤️

Overall Toothless is a MUST HAVE for anyone who enjoys robotic toys. I would have been over the moon💗🌙 if this were available when I was growing up and I don't know of any child who would not enjoy him. I certainly do. I would rate him at 4 1/2 stars due to the price. This is a well thought out and high-quality toy. I absolutely adore him 😍, but he lacks some of the more sophisticated programming and functionality of my other animatronic robotic pets. I still highly recommend him because he is cute and unique. If you saw the movie you'll love and enjoy him all the more.

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces) This is a great quality play set with hundreds of pieces that will keep your kids occupied for hours. The box says 569 pieces, which is enough to build a lot of different objects.

As a parent, it's not hard to see the advantage of Lego sets. Although I think it's a little ridiculous to assume that your kid will grow up to be an engineer if they play with Legos, it's easy to see the benefit of a toy that makes children follow rigorous and complex instructions.

The build diagrams are a lot like you will encounter on any number of products in your lifetime, for everything from maintaining your vacuum cleaner, to the owner's manual of your vehicle, to how to put on a compression valve. The early you learn how to sit down and interpret an instructional diagram, the better equipped you are to deal with life.

The most amazing thing about Lego sets is that even though they are a rigorous mental exercise, kids love digging into them each and every time. This set is triple the fun as it contains the instructions for three different builds. My kids are 7 and 9 and they put together the boat in a couple hours. The boat even has a mechanism that allows you to spin a handle on the top and it makes the propeller spin (although we couldn't quite get the piece to set in place properly). Still, this is a complex build that gives a little bit of insight into gearing.

The best part is, once they're done building all the suggestions, they break the whole thing down and start constructing fortresses and whatnot. I have never seen a kid disappointed to receive a Lego set ever. Great toy.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces)
