Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz. One of our kids has been on a slime kick of late, so we got this glue to add some dimension to the experience.

WHAT IS THIS GLUE LIKE?
This glue is a bit different on the label from the other color changing glue that we have used. It states that as you play, it will change in color from darker to lighter green. There is no odor and it is pretty standard type glue.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM WITH SLIME?
We used this with the Elmer's slime maker solution and got a nice slime. It makes a good consistency, and the slime is fun to play with if it is mixed at the right ratio.

DOES IT CHANGE COLOR?
That is where we have some issues. Perhaps because it is winter where we are testing this, but the slime does not want to change color unless it is really warm, something that only happens in sunlight after a while. Perhaps when it is warmer weather, or a really well heated room this will change more easily. For now, to get it to change to light green, we have to make it get REALLY warm in the sunlight in the window for a while.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a pretty green slime. It will change color if it gets really warm, but not as easily as we expected.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This does not change color that easily, so for that I have removed 1 star. It is still fun to play with as green slime, with the added bonus of changing color once in a great while when the conditions are just right, an added bonus.
text_fidelity_b: Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz.

text_fidelity_a: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+ This card game can be played solo or with up to five players. It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+

I spend most of my time flying drones these days. But, this little helicopter, purchased as a gift for a friend, proves to be a fun little bird. I wasn't sure if it was IR controlled or RF. But, that's okay too. Seeing that there aren't many changes you can make other than trim adjustment. So, all in all, this is a good toy heli. I know my friend will have a lot of fun with it.

So you can build upon or modify your robot with standard Legos if you wish. It is especially a great opportunity for parent/child bonding time. We already put together a similar robot that is half the cost of this one. So if you wanna give this a try, but weary of its quality. App and packaging logo looks the same, so it's by the same manufacture. But these are white label items from China. Meaning different sellers will sell them under different brand names. But they all seem to use the same MOULD KING app. If you own several of these robots, you can access all their controls under this Mould King app. I made a screen recording to demonstrate. However, this app is NOT available in the Google Play store. You'll need to use a QR scanner to scan their code, and it'll take you to a link to download. But it is available in the Apple Store.

Overall, we like these toys a lot. The only thing that keeps it from being 5-Stars, is the lack of Google Play certification.

The cement mixer is AWFUL. It is infuriating that they make a cement mixer with no opening to put stuff! It has this tiny little grate that lets out small amounts of dry sand or very teeny tiny pebbles. I guess you are supposed to cram it in through the tiny grate that is supposed to let stuff out? God forbid you get dirt in there and water, and it clumps up, as has happened with many other trucks in a similar vein. I had no issue turning the drum smoothly and appreciate that the drum can be angled downward to dump out, but this was pretty much the most disappointing disaster of a cement mixer I could imagine given there is no mechanism for getting stuff IN, or cleaning it. I am a grownup, so it is hard to imagine that this was truly vetted for use by toddlers if it needs that much force. Then the angling mechanism also requires a lot of oomph. Overall the packaging of having this set of three harmonizing full size trucks is great. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games I'm a wolf lover as well as a game nerd and couldn't pass this one up! It is absolutely beautiful out of the box. I'm impressed they kept it to a $50 price point with the level of detail here, I've seen similar games priced closer to $80!

I haven't had a chance to play yet because I need to get folks together but I did watch a video playthrough about the rules after reading the guide so that I'd be prepared. They are complex but once I watched the video it made a lot more sense. It's definitely tactic-heavy in that you need to change strategy based on what your opponent is doing or what phase of the moon it is on. I love many of the creative points in the design, and I love a game with a very clear endpoint because I hate games that go on forever! 75 minutes is perfect for a game night.

I especially love the design of the wolf cards. They are extremely clear where the tiles and meeples go etc. It's not only attractive but it also includes reminder text which is really helpful for absent-minded players like myself. I love how the rules for your items level up as you get more pieces on the board.

My favorite part about games like this is that it's possible to lose a battle here and there and not feel discouraged halfway through. Since a lot of scoring can happen later, it keeps players invested until the end. This generation of games is so different from the ones before!

My only complaint is that with a game like this it is so easy to lose a meeple because they are so small and so many. This can make it hard to trust strangers with at board-game meetups.

Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+ If you, like me, are looking for games to play with a high energy, lack of focus little boy, then this is the game for you. For my four year old, games with a lot of rules and that require skills he's still learning with clear winners and losers are not the best choice games for us. He doesn't have the patience, skill, or temperament. I needed games to slowly introduce him into those skills and Pop Up Pirate is that game! The only rule, everyone takes turns to place a sword into a slot. The person who makes the pirate pop-up out of the barrel wins. We don't play winner/loser, but you can if you choose to do so.

The game comes with 20 swords, four colors with five each, a barrel, and said pirate. It's for 2 to 4 players, my son and I just pick up a sword no matter the color, but if you have more kids or players, then you can choose colors. You stick the pirate in the barrel where there is a trap/spring mechanism that is only triggered when someone sticks a sword in the right slot. Each player takes a color and everyone takes turns sticking a sword into a slot. When the right sword pokes the pirate, he pops high up into the air. The pirate is fairly light weight so if he were to really go flying he would not break anything or hurt anyone. The pirate jumps at most 2 feet into the air, probably less. The only caveat is to make kids aren't sticking their face near the barrel with the pirate in the hole for obvious reasons. This game comes in fairly big box as the barrel is about as wide as a clothes iron, but not nearly as tall.

If you need a game for toddlers/preschoolers that is guaranteed to teach taking turns and highly giggle inducing, then Pop up Pirate is your game!
text_fidelity_b: Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+

Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit I’m a big fan of the Thames & Kosmos building kits--especially the ones that teach STEM principles. However, this THAMES & KOSMOS PEPPER MINT IN THE FANTASTIC UNDERWATER SCIENCE VOYAGE EXPERIMENT KIT is definitely NOT one of my favorites. The experiments do teach about the physical properties of water (e.g., siphoning, hydraulics), but they are boring--mostly they require operating a syringe to push water through tubing.

The boat is easy to build. The parts are stamped onto thin sheets of wood. You punch the parts out of the sheets, and the edges come out smooth and clean. The parts then lock together without requiring glue or other fasteners. The assembly instructions are included in a booklet that contains a silly adventure/discovery story that features the girl character Pepper Mint.

The story is interrupted from time to time with instructions for science experiments. Each experiment has a good, easy-to-understand explanation of “what’s happening” (e.g., water can move things because, unlike air, it cannot be compressed).

The kit is apparently aimed at 11-year-old girls (Pepper Mint’s age), but the story and the experiments seem rather simplistic for that age group. I do wish that Thames & Kosmos had chosen a more serious name than “Pepper Mint” for their girl scientist. This kit has some teaching value, but it trivializes science for girls.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit

text_fidelity_a: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle T. S. Shure had a temporary design lapse with this product; probably, the worst coming out of this brand.  Excellent idea coupled with poor execution only increases the frustration one would feel about the product.  The idea of 'magnetic' pieces to help discover countries and continents is great; so is the use of some cutesy imagery that often is often ascribed to a particular country (the dragon shaped like the Great Wall of China is a clear standout).  But trying to cramp all kinds of information in a tiny board proved disastrous.  The pieces are cut with no logic - the sub-continent looks from another planet; the font size for the capitals is so tiny, the target audience will barely notice it;  there are random airplanes and ships distracting the overall map and adding no value.  The tiny pieces are clearly not to be allowed anywhere near babies (it is rated for 6-15 years, to be fair; though it will be a miracle if anyone in that age group will use this for more than a day).  On the positive, with the weak magnetic pull and cardboard-feeling tiny pieces are bound to be lost sooner or later. And then you could create a new game - "which country is missing?".  That may be a better use of this playboard;

Cosmic Encounter 42nd Anniversary Edition Board Game - Classic Strategy Game of Intergalactic Conquest for Kids and Adults, Ages 14+, 3-5 Players, 1-2 Hour Playtime, Made by Fantasy Flight Games Ok, so every 4th of July my rather decent sized family (~30 people) gets together and has a great time. A few of us in the younger age range (<30) love to play board games and stuff like that. We had played the same games for several years and I was getting board with the same stuff. I was looking for a new challenge!

I searched for weeks, looking for a game that I thought would suffice, and I kept coming back to cosmic encounters. I finally decided to buy it. When it came in the mail I ripped everything open and started discovering the game. I was so excited and hopeful. It looked pretty complicated, ever after watching How-To's online.

I tried to get a couple of my friends to play it, but after watching me setup the game (still barely having a clue how to play) they gave up and wanted to play 3's (a simple card game).

So there my expensive new game sat for weeks... months... a year! I finally got one of my cousins to play it with me, but we had to switch off playing a third person. We hardly had a clue how to play, but it sparked his interest.

The few times we got together after that, we just didn't get the time to play the game but his interest stayed.

Finally, a friend of mine and I went up to my cabin, and my cousin happened to be there.

I had brought the game, so we decided to finally play it the with the right number of players! After each of us read through the manual, we started playing. There was a fair amount of confusion with the rules, and how the game actually played out, but we managed to finish the game. We then played another, and another after that. The game was a blast! We discovered a new rule or something we hadn't been doing right practically every game. We actually played 3 or 4 whole games before we learned we were supposed to be able to get 2 encounters per turn!

Every game we played we got more and more accustomed to the game, and we enjoyed it a little more. I now cant wait to play it again, and I am getting more people involved with it. I am planning on buying the expansions as well!

Long story short, it is a somewhat difficult game to learn, but once you do it is a blast! Each game took about 30 minutes to an hour with three people.

I definitely recommend it if your looking for a good board game!
text_fidelity_b: Cosmic Encounter 42nd Anniversary Edition Board Game - Classic Strategy Game of Intergalactic Conquest for Kids and Adults, Ages 14+, 3-5 Players, 1-2 Hour Playtime, Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin My family has really enjoyed playing this updated version of an old favorite. The basic rules are the same as in the original Sorry! Each player has four pawns to move around the board from Start to Home. You draw a card to find out how many spaces you can move your game piece. Landing on another player's pawn sends them back to start as does the Sorry! card, just as in the classic version.

What's different about Sorry Spin is the spinning board. The center circle is the main board, with connecting circles for each color's home which fit together like gears. The challenge of the spinning board is your home is contantly changing position in relation to the main board. You may be just a few spaces away from reaching your home track when the board will spin and you will end up all the way across the board from your home.

It took about 5 minutes to assemble the game board, which seems very sturdy. We had some trouble spinning the board on a slick surface (wood table, counter top), but when we placed it on a placemat, it worked fine. A nice addition is a box that can be assembled and used to store the cards.

This is a great family game which is faster paced than the original version of the game due to the spinning board and a shorter path between start and home. Also any number gets a pawn out of start. (unlike the original which requires a 1 or 2). Older kids and adults will enjoy the suggested variation of the two-player game in which each person selects two different colors instead of only one.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin

The object of the game is to be the first player to move all 4 of your men around the board to get back home. You choose from 4 different colors of your men and your home- blue, green, yellow or red. There is a deck of cards that tell you how many spaces to move your man, and of course it isn't as easy as just moving your man as quickly as you can around the board to get home before anyone and win the game. There are obstacles along the way, should a player get to slide, he slides everyone in his way back to start, and no two men can occupy the same space, so someone has to go back to start- Sorry!

I remember when we played with 2 players, the game took about 15-20 minutes, but with 4 players, it took close to half an hour. It's very fast moving and even faster when hardly any players are sent back to start. I really love the look of this classic 1939 Sorry Game- it's a little different from the one we played on in the 60's. Regardless of the look you like, Sorry is a fast and fun game that brings back so many fun memories of when we had 15 minutes to kill before we went bike riding to a picnic on a lovely summer day in 1962. This early version of the game is really a nice one to own and it also comes with other game versions you can play including a Sorry For One, in case you have a few minutes to kill by yourself! Some Classic games never wear out their fast fun and this 5 Star Classic Sorry Board Game is one of them!
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

The brush has real hair bristles and is medium sized, which is good for administering a base coat, but not so great for detail work. The rocks photographed for this kit clearly are made with the help of paint pens or fine detail brushes. What is most valuable in this kit is the book.
The book has a lot of valuable information for painting in general and for rocks in particular. Some things might seem obvious to an adult but not so obvious to a child, such as, "To make a pastel, mix a tiny bit of color into a blob of white." The advice to let paint dry between colors is repeated several times, and in my experience, kids need to hear that more than once! There are tons of cool ideas for painting. Flowers, food, pirates, animals, names, and more are featured.
This klutz kit is a good starting point for young rock painters. I would present it as a gift along with some fine point brushes or fine point paint pens, smooth rocks, and perhaps a few Apple Barrel acrylics.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height

Mixed in are some specialty pieces (e.g., Unikitty’s cloud stole, the golden scallop shell, the piano keyboards) that require considerable creativity to be used in other projects.

If you download the Lego Life app (available for both iOS and Android), you can scan the maze code on the front of the printed instructions and get building instructions for an “Intergalactic Drum Set” (see photo). This uses parts from the basic build, and extends the building fun. The Lego Microfighters are mini vehicles you build, which you can use to either expand your Lego-verse or play with separately. These come with instructions on how to build the microfighter. They are simple to put together, but I would not advise this for a child younger than 6 unless you know your 4 or 5 year old is really good at Lego instructions (which are in picture form). These are not ideal for children who are still primarily freebuilders or just learning about Legos. You should get the creative set for that. However, if your child loves to freebuild, but can also follow instructions this is a great gift! My son built all of the microfighters as designed, played with them for a bit, and then rearranged them to his freebuilding heart's desire. I cut the instructions apart and rearrange them in plastic sleeves so that if he wants to build according to the instructions they are neat and organized. Also do not let the "Micro" fool you, they are regular sized Legos, they will work with other Legos, it's just that they are really small scaled models. Also, the Lego people (Chewbacca) that come the sets are regular sized Lego people. So, their body parts can be mixed and matched with others you have in your collection.

One Caveat: For some odd reason, these sets as well as some of the smaller Lego City sets always have their boxes just crushed and in horrible shape. So, if you are looking for these are gift, I usually purchase from a store like Target, Walmart, or the Lego store itself to pick out the very best box. I'm not sure why Lego does this. I used to blame Target, but then I realized this was a Lego issue and not a store issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Millennium Falcon Microfighter 75193 Building Kit (92 Pieces)

CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver) This is my first lightsaber in about a decade. The last one I owned what a Force FX by Hasbro; my, how technology has evolved.

This lightsaber is cheaper than the one I purchase, yet has a lot more to offer. While it doesn't have the "expanding" lights (it's sort of like a flashlight), the features it has make up for it. There's only one button, yet it does so much. Initial long press wakes it up or puts it to sleep. While it's on standby, there are button sequences that control music, volume, and sound font.

With the light emitted, the lightsaber has clash functionality, and the ability to change colors. What I love about changing colors is that the colors cycle in a rainbow fashion; there is no predetermined number of colors. See a color you like between cycles? Stop on it and it stays. Pretty nice.

The smooth swing works effectively, but the sound doesn't fade away; instead, there's an abrupt stop. So if you turn the lightsaber one way, the sound follows in synchronization, but immediately stops. It sort of takes away from the effect, but I imagine lightsabers with better smooth-swing functionality have better accuracy.

One day, while charging the lightsaber after a month, the charging sound came on and kept announcing the charging state. I was a little concerned, but left it. Suddenly, the sound was rapid, then silence. I checked the lightsaber and the charging light wasn't on. I tried different outlets, but no fix. Thankfully, the lightsaber is easy to disassemble, so I checked out the battery. It seems fine, but I am awaiting a new one to make sure it's just the battery that was fried.

From the moment I unboxed it it felt great in my hands it didn't feel cheap most of the construction was plastic but with that said it is very consistent with some of the quality that I've become accustomed to with the hs700 the hs190 and a hs720. Nerf N-Strike Elite Rapidstrike CS-18 Blaster (Colors may vary) My kids have had an absolute blast with this nerf firearm. I am amazed at the speed that it empties an 18 dart clip with startling accuracy. I am also impressed at the decent but manageable sting that the darts give you when your tween son unloads on you.

The construction seems very solid. It is amazing that it has sensors that will not allow firing when the chamber is open or the clip is missing. There are lock release buttons on everything from stock extension to a safety for firing (well maybe more just a button to engage the fly wheel more than a safety.) Also there are rails for accessories and clip loops for attaching a carrying strap. Perhaps the most superfluous feature is the fold down sight. I have never seen my boys aim. It seems to favor firing from the hip.

Pros
+ Absolute blast to fire
+ Satisfying click when slamming the clip home
+ Impressive accuracy
+ Well Constructed

Cons
- It does Jam, especially when trying to use the clips from other guns in the series.
- Bullets seem to burrow to freedom after shooting them, or turn invisible because they just disappear.
- Needs 4 C batteries
- Having just one causes sibling bickering

I do find it funny that they rate this for educational purposes. But I guess it is a great introduction into our gun culture. The false sense of strength and self confidence it provides is very self evident as you fire down on someone with only a pump action nerf gun, or better yet, an unarmed victim. We have lost a lot of darts in a short time, but that's what supplemental dart packs are for.

I feel like I'm putting in too many cons, because In the words of my boys, "This thing is awesome." I wish they had these when I was their age. Either that or I wish the office had a more lax view on noon-time Nerf battles.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Rapidstrike CS-18 Blaster (Colors may vary)

text_fidelity_a:
BRIO World - 33833 Central Fire Station | 12 Piece Toy for Kids with Fire Truck and Accessories for Kids Ages 3 and Up If you are not expecting a Brio wooden toy set, you may like this fire station set. Unfortunately, I was expecting wood, and I am disappointed. I assumed, wrongly, that this would be an old-fashioned, high-quality, Brio, wooden toy set. It is not! This fire station is almost entirely plastic, except for one small area. Yes, it is apparently a high-quality plastic, but it is still plastic. Wooden toys are sturdy and made to last across multiple generations. Plastic is not.

I personally think that, since this toy set is made of plastic, it is quite overpriced and not a good value. It is priced as if it were made of wood. Further, I wonder why on earth a company that is famed for its high-quality, wooden toys would opt to convert to plastic toys? It makes no sense.

However, if you are not looking for wooden toys for your child or grandchild, the fact that this is just another plastic toy set, in a world already over-filled with plastic, the plastic construction may not bother you. This toy set, on the positive side, does have very attractive, bright colors, and it does inspire creative play, as the older, wooden sets did. It's just not wood!

This set is for children age 3 and up because of small parts and a choking hazard.
text_fidelity_b: BRIO World - 33833 Central Fire Station | 12 Piece Toy for Kids with Fire Truck and Accessories for Kids Ages 3 and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Avengers Marvel Legends Iron Man Electronic Helmet - Multicolor There are a few ways to evaluate this. I'll to approach it methodically.

Appearance
Nails it. Tony Stark could wear this. While it isn't metal, they got the color and the shape so spot-on. If you are looking for a piece to display in your home or office, this is it.

Size
This will fit all but the largest heads. M.O.D.O.K and The Watcher might not fit this, but almost everyone else will.

Weight
Not too heavy, but it weighs enough to feel real. It is comfortable.

Sounds
A weak spot. They sound much like greeting card special effects.

Lights
When the lights are on, it is hard to see. Cool, but nearly blinding. That means taking this to a con might be difficult.

Taking It On/Off
It is hard to explain, but it is tricky to get right. You can, so don't worry but be aware that undoing the back is a pain in the neck.

Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set We hold a monthly “Game Night” at our house and felt this was the perfect opportunity to introduce the Pathfinder Card game to our friends. Unfortunately, it took at least two hours to explain the rules of the game and our crowd is mostly people over 40, so keeping track of each character’s journey, remembering what powers they do or do not have, and explaining strategy was somewhat difficult, especially as everyone was a first time player. I think this game is best suited to a younger crowd (under 40) but it’s still fun for those who really stick with it.

A few of us played Dungeons & Dragons years ago, so this playing this felt very familiar. Every player is given the opportunity to "customize" their game play, in that they can choose to be a particular character. The characters are individually possessed of different powers, spells, weapons, and capabilities. You choose a specific character and a “scenerio” (a.k.a storyline) and draw cards that determine the path of your journey. Your objective is to maximize your advantage, using the cards and dice to advance or retreat. The objective, of course, is to win the game by overcoming monsters and capturing the bad guys for points. It’s like a video game in that they are different levels and you can move on to different stages. The game shifts scenes as you advance, so it feels like a continual maze. The game can technically go on forever as the company encourages you to buy “expansion sets” that give you additional cards and new adventures to go on.

Two people in our group are big science fiction and fantasy buffs, and they absolutely loved it. For the rest of us, it was challenging, and after playing this for two hours, a little tedious, since it requires so much thinking. This is not a game to be played when you’ve had a few cocktails! But for devoted game geeks, I can see this being a big hit.
text_fidelity_b: Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set

text_fidelity_a:
Rodzon Remote RC Car，Control Truck with 2.4Ghz Controlled Toy Car for Kids & Adults，Double Sided 360° Flips. (No Battery Included) Green What I thought would be a fun holiday toy for my kids turned out to be a huge pain and battery guzzler. While packaged nicely, it was evident that you get a product that, in my opinion, isn't even worth the relatively low price point. The controller is made of thin plastic and has unnecessary triggers that make me wonder whether it's a generic mold that's been used for game controllers of some sort.
The body of the car is a bit sturdier, at least. With the fat tires, the body hardly ever touches surfaces.

When I first took the parts out of the box the first thing I did was open up the back of the controller to put in batteries. The battery cover also has a screw to keep it in place, but I soon realized that the plastic screw (or else very cheap metal) was broken so that no matter how much I turned it it would not loosen. I didn't strip the top; the screw itself was broken. Thus, I had to bend and crack the battery cover open to get the batteries in. "Okay," I thought. "At least that'll probably be the worst of it."
Nope.

I did the same for the car. Thankfully, that screw wasn't broken so it came off without any manipulation. The instructions state that a rechargeable battery is inside, but that's not the case. Instead, there's a compartment that requires four AAA batteries. I stock up on plenty of AA batteries, but as AAA batteries are becoming less common I had to order some. Not a big deal; I've been meaning to stock up on some anyway. And I actually prefer batteries over internal rechargeable ones as that means better longevity. (I have this twenty-year-old RC car that is useless now because the rechargeable battery is impossible to find a replacement for.)

So I got the batteries all set and I started to play with it. As it was late at night my kids were asleep, so I figured what better way to test it before they had a chance!
The car moved fine. It detected all my presses. However, two big problems I noticed were: 1) to push the car forward, you have to push both triggers forward (or backward if the car's on its flip side), but every time I did the car would make a slight turn left before continuing forward. I tried countless times to see if it was me but it would not go straight before turning a slight left.
2) Because the underside of the car is mirrored from the top I sometimes forget that I'm supposed to reverse the controls. I wish they made the mold of the car so that they wouldn't be facing the same direction.

Anyway, I figured my kids would have fun with it and wouldn't bother with these gripes. They woke up and noticed the car immediately on the table, and I let them have at it. For a while, they had a lot of fun, but not too long did they complain that the car wouldn't go straight. When the car would stop and they'd try to get it to go just straight, sure enough it would turn slightly left before going straight. Despite their complaints, however, they used it the entire day.
By the end of the day, the batteries inside the car already needed replacing. Mind you, they didn't use it every second of the day, but I was still surprised to find that the batteries needed replacing already. I changed them and thought nothing of it.

Two days later was Thanksgiving and my kids wanted to bring it while visiting family. When we got there the car needed battery replacements yet again. In those two days prior to the holiday they used it probably a max of about half an hour. There's a switch on the car that turns it off and on, but then I realized that if it's not turned off then the batteries still are being drained. I thought we'd be fine to leave the car switched on and the batteries would be in a sort of idle state, but that was not the case. As the family we visited didn't have AAA batteries, my kids weren't able to use it. It wasn't a total loss as we had plenty of other activities to do, but even I was looking forward to using the car with a couple of pets brought by family.

So when we got back home I replaced the batteries. When my kids went to bed I remembered to turn the car off. The next day they played with it and forgot to turn it off that night. The next day it needed replacements again. I told my kids I'm not replacing the batteries again and then I showed them this RC helicopter I had. They've forgotten about the car.
text_fidelity_b: Rodzon Remote RC Car，Control Truck with 2.4Ghz Controlled Toy Car for Kids & Adults，Double Sided 360° Flips. (No Battery Included) Green

Play-Doh Kitchen Creations Sprinkle Cookie Surprise Play Food Set with 5 Non-Toxic Colors We do a lot with play-doh in our house, and thus have a big collection of fun kitchen items for it. What I have noticed over the years is that sometimes the simpler items are best. It is really hard to store items that are big and bulky and have a flashy plastic presentation, and even though we have a substantial area dedicated to Play-Doh, items like this which have a big piece but only perform a couple of small functions end up not being are very favorites.

This was quite fun and my children really enjoyed it. We do a lot of sprinkle cookie decorating with real cookies and sprinkles, so being able to make a thrilling series of decorated cookies was really fun for the kids, and they very much enjoyed the action of this set and getting to play with it together. They set up a fun little cookie shop making cookies and decorating them and lining up their fancy creations.

Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds This recycling truck is awesome. It takes two AA batteries (included for demonstration purposes only—meaning they may have to be replaced using a Phillips screwdriver shortly after use). The biggest difficulty I had is in removing this truck from the box because it arrives in the ON condition and started working immediately as I was trying to unpack it. That was a bit annoying.

The on / off button is located underneath the truck under the cab. There are two levels of sound and lights to choose from when turning on.

Once the truck is on, the button in the center of the CAB turns on the ignition sounds and the lights come on.

The lights also come on when pressing down on the tires and moving forward and backward. When moving backward, the backup warning sounds activate.

The recycling truck container opens in back and can store Legos or other small toys. It also tilts back to the rear.

All the sounds of dumping, loading, and idling are realistic. Pressing down on the horns on either side of the cab also generates realistic sounds.

The recycling bucket has a slot that allows for placement into the hitch. Once in place, move the lever handle down to dump (or pretend dump) what is in the pail. The pail can also be stored in the top of the truck’s container.

The instructions are useless as it only talks about the batteries. Therefore, it is important to pay attention to the pictures on the box or read the description on Amazon to learn how to fully operate this vehicle. Another option is to learn via trial and error.

To me this is an extremely impressive toy for a reasonable price of $29.99.
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds

Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers) I wanted to LOVE this set.
I really like it. But I don’t love it.

1st - I don’t know why companies create toys for kids 3+ that include markers that aren’t washable!!

2nd - the main (black) dry erase maker is the only one that is a complete handled marker with an eraser lid. The other 4 markers have a 1.5” handle area to hold onto. The markers work and erase well.
The markers are hard to get back into their elastic straps. It’s difficult to do as an adult- let alone a 3+yo. An additional 1/4” of elastic would have been helpful.

3rd - the activity pages have a spiral binding. The way it is set up the last page is attached to the back of the kit - I like this. But the spiral is too small to allow the pages to tuck behind the kit and the top of the pages lift up from the back of the bottom.
The pages are sometimes used together for a project but not always.

4th - there isn’t a bag or something to store the magnets that aren’t being used.
The magnets are all on 2 sheets and are very strong. You can easily layer these magnets to get different looks. There are 54 magnets so it would be nice if there was an area built in to store the magnets while they aren’t being used.

5th - This activity pad takes a lot of space and is larger than a child’s lap - it’s 23” wide. It would be nice if the pad could be opened and folded in half.

6th - the velcro closure is nice and strong but the cardboard tab is weaker than it needs to be. I worry that after much use this tab will be ripped off.

All that being said - this activity pad is nice.
It’s a good quiet time activity that has a lot of fun included.
My daughter takes this to restaurants and plane rides to keep her busy!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers)

So I think I can give you a balance opinion.

Artificial Intelligence... Vector wins.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Vector is like Pinocchio trying to be a real boy. Miko is a smart device that moves on command. Imagine if Alexa, Siri or Google was given a Robot body in the shape of an egg, that's Miko! If you're looking for a robot that's more independent and feels more real, Vector is what you want. Vector truly feels like a pet with the convenience of never having to feed it or take it for a walk. LOL! When you physically touch or nudge Vector, it reacts. If you tap the floor in front of him, his eyes will look down, if you waive your hand over his head, his head will look up. You can tell it gets excited to see you. It is happy when you stroke it, and gets mad when you lift him in the air for too long. Miko is not like that, nor does Miko move around autonomously like Vector. You have to to initiate "AUTOPILOT" in order for Miko to move around herself. And when she's on autopilot, some default music is playing, basically the theme music you hear in their Miko ads. When she bumps into something, she has a few phrases, one of which is "Not again!" But it all feels programmed, it does not feel like a pet roaming around with independent thinking. It can bump into the same spot over and over. Whereas with Vector, when you put him in a new environment, he will scan the room, and take 360 degree snapshots of his environment so he can roam around more intelligently. When you interrupt him, he'll react, when you pick him up, he gets mad, he wants you to put him down. When you interrupt Miko on Autopilot, nothing happens. You can put your hands in front of her, and she'll move in another direction because of her sensors, but that's about it. If you use the wake word, "Hello Miko," she will respond, but she will no longer be on autopilot, and you'll need to manually start it again. They should at least put an update where you can tell Miko to go on autopilot using voice. It's basically like a Roomba that you set on autopilot. Vector feels like a living thing because you can interrupt him, and interact with him, then when you leave him alone, he goes about his business moving around again. You can tell Vector to come to you, and he will like a real pet. Miko does not come to you like that. She may move forward, but she does not come to your direction. Vector knows where the direction of the command is coming from and he will move towards that direction. You can make a loud banging noise and Vector will react like a nosy human, his head will move as if asking, "What was that noise?" Meanwhile, Miko will stand motionless, there is no reaction to the environment. When Vector's battery is drained, he knows how to find his charging dock and dock himself. Meaning you could be away for awhile, come back and find Vector on his charging dock, but that doesn't mean he hasn't been snooping around. LOL! With Miko, there is no charging dock. She'll let you know she needs more juice, and you'll have to charge her. Lastly, as is, Miko only recognizes one face, whereas Vector can recognize multiple faces and call your correct name. I think Miko actually doesn't even recognize any faces, for that matter. This is how I know... When you introduce yourself and tell her your name, JACK, you become the default profile. Then when you ask Miko "who am I," she'll say JACK correctly. Now if you have someone else introduce herself as JILL, she now becomes the new default. So if Jack comes back and ask, "Who am I?" Miko will say JILL. She basically just calls you by the name of the last person introduced. So currently, there is no intelligent facial recognition like Vector.

Which one has more games and learning apps? Miko wins.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
I guess this would be the bread and butter of Miko. Vector has a tiny interface to show his facial emotions and a few games like black jack, but there's not a lot to do with Vector in terms of apps. He is not app-centric, Miko is app-centric. Both robots have the usual general knowledge AI. You can ask both robots questions like who's the president, what time is it, math, definitions, etc. Basically all the types of general knowledge you would ask Alexa, Siri or Hey Google. But on top of the general knowledge, Miko has a big colorful screen with lots of learning apps. The games will require the child to interact and press buttons to give or to get answers. This is the main advantage Miko has over Vectors. So that's why I say Miko feels like a tablet that moves on command. I guess the plan is for Miko to continue to develop and add to their app store, which is called the TALENT HOUSE. I've seen a coding app that they are asking $30 for. But most apps are free. This would be equivalent to the Skills section of the Alexa app. The more you add, the more things your Miko will do. Again, you want Vector if you want something that feels more life like, something to play with. He has a cube that he likes to play with, so you can ask him to flip his cube, pick up his cube, etc. Like a dog with tricks. Miko has no moving arms, and does not interact physically with you.

Miko has a neat Video calling feature.
--------------------------------------------
Because it has the advantage of the big screen, one neat feature of the Miko is that you can call it from your smartphone, but within the Miko app. I assume this will work from anywhere. It's basically wifi calling with video. So you'll be able to see your kids when they answer, and they'll be able to see you. Can't do that with Vector! You can also move Miko during this video call using directional buttons in the app.

Wake word.. Miko wins.
---------------------------
How is this even a category for competition? LOL! But you see, with Vector, the wake word is "Hey Vector," but you have to wait for him to turn blue, then you have to say "I have a question.." Then wait for Vector to say, "Ready!" Then you can ask your question. This is probably the #1 complaint of Vector. It doesn't feel like a natural conversation like it does with Alexa, Siri or Google. Miko wins here because asking her general questions is just like Alexa. You say, "Hello Miko," when she turns green, you proceed with your question. Not convoluted like Vector. I will say this.. Vector has Alexa built in. So you can actually bypass Vector for general knowledge and just say, "Alexa!" This way, you won't need to say "I have a question." But it's just weird to hear Alexa's voice in Vector's body.

The VOICE.. Vector wins.
----------------------------
Vector sounds like a cute robot. Miko sounds like your very dull and boring Auntie. LOL! There are 4 voices to choose from in Miko's app, one of which is a man's voice, but they don't sound all that much better. For such a cute and colorful device, it's strange to have such dull choices for the voices.

Availability.. Miko wins.
---------------------------
Why am I talking so much about Vector, a robot who's creator company Anki, is out of business? LOL! Well, that's because Digital Dreams Lab has continued on with Vector. They bought the rights, and they were on Kickstarter to provide new life to Vector for a fee, including an escape pod feature that supposedly will allow Vector to be fully functional forever even if Digital Dreams Lab goes out of business. But now, I think Vector cost a little more in the secondary market.

Conclusion:
--------------
There is potential here. Ultimately, I might be comparing apples to oranges. I have no idea about what goes on behind the scenes in AI, programming, coding, etc. The path in development for these two could be so different that asking one to be more like the other could be unreasonable. You can't ask Vector to have more apps and games, right? It wasn't develop with a big screen. Likewise, you probably can't ask Miko to be more like vector since it wasn't built with any arms. I would sum it up as Miko being App-Centric, and Vector is Movement-Centric. If you're interested in something more like a smart device/tablet that could move, get Miko. If you're more interested in the physical interaction with a robot, that's more on the side of a real learning AI, then get Vector.

Reasonable improvements I'd like Miko to make:

-Ability to turn off music in auto pilot.
-Ability to turn on apps, including auto pilot by voice.
-Ability to turn off apps by voice as well. Right now, if Miko is dancing or playing music, you cannot voice her to stop. You have to grab her and push the stop button.

I hope this company sticks around and improves on Miko!

text_fidelity_a:
Mainstreet Classics 18-Inch Backgammon Board Game Set The nicest part of this Main Street Classic Backgammon Set is the white topstitching on the black leatherette case which gives it a high quality look. Unfortunately, the set I received has a couple of creases in the fabric interior lining which continually attract my eyes and I always want to play the side without the creases. Because I'm a good sport, I always ask that my opponent select sides and I therefore always wind up with the creases to call my own. The set is not heavy and I appreciate the absence of a weighty and cumbersome handle, but if a handle is important to you for carrying, then this is not the set for you. The "stones" or round pieces have a nice weight to them and I also like the look and feel of all five dice. The cups are just fine in appearance and heft as long as you don't look at the workmanship closely, especially on the bottom where I fear the glue will not be effective for too long. The "manual" is extremely difficult to read because the imprint is faint and some of the words/diagrams are not legible, but as a plus, it does include a paragraph on the history of the game. With a better manual, I think I would have been more impressed with this set, but the included sheet of paper gives a very cheap and careless impression of the manufacturer. One can find resources for the game rules online or in game books and these are easier to read, so I'd suggest that if Main Street is not interested in providing worthwhile instructions, they'd be better off leaving this weak attempt out of the set.

All in all, the workmanship in stitching is excellent but the glue is lacking in the construction of the game I received. I enjoy playing the game, like the look of it, appreciate that it's far superior to the heavy pleather set I had many years ago, but I'm not excited about the retail cost.
text_fidelity_b: Mainstreet Classics 18-Inch Backgammon Board Game Set

This box is more complicated that either of my other puzzle boxes mentioned here, but one thing they all share in common is the veneer work.  This box features very geometric veneering and it is quite pretty.  The complexity of the puzzle to open the box is a lot more fun and interesting for this box - it's really neat! text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

text_fidelity_a:
Bendy and the Ink Machine - Boris Buildable Figure (202 pieces), 60 months to 180 months Ok, I do not "lego". I find it equal parts boring and frustrating, that said because I'm a parent I've had to pitch in enough times that I'm "unwilling" but competent. Which is what quickly happened with this set. Granted my kid's only 7, and this is for 14+ (which at this point I agree 100% with). I'm not going to knock a star for that, mine is young and it was a risk he wanted to take. He often does the 14+ lego sets so I figured we'd be fine. NOPE. NO SIR. NOT TODAY.

There were so many tiny pieces, like unnecessarily tiny. He made it to step 2 and couldn't make heads or tails of the instructions. I took a look and also struggled which meant he felt vindicated and took off. So, I spent the next 2 hours debating life choices and contemplating day drinking. Ugh parenting is hard sometimes.

Be very aware: This is not a lego set. The pieces do not snap together as well, or stay together as well, there are no extra pieces, and the instructions are frustrating. I'm keeping my language clean here, but imagine a much more colorful word than frustrating. "Frustrating" really doesn't do the whole experience justice.

However, Boris is built. It can be done. PERSEVERANCE PEOPLE. Kiddo however is not allowed to touch it. It will go up on his bookshelf, like super high and when ever anyone walks in he is to loudly proclaim MY MOM BUILT THAT!

....on the upside it's priced pretty cheap, so if you have any kids in your life whose parents you want to torture, send this to them as a gift. So in the end I'm giving this 3 stars. One star off for the less then stellar pieces, and another star off for the horrendous instructions.
text_fidelity_b: Bendy and the Ink Machine - Boris Buildable Figure (202 pieces), 60 months to 180 months

LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces) I hope they don't overdo it, but this new LEGO Augmented Reality system is quite cool.

There is an app that you download to your phone, and using that app, you can view your LEGO set, and watch it move and change a little bit. If you've seen someone playing Pokemon Go or using a filter on their camera phone, you'll get the idea. It works surprisingly well given that it's easy to slightly alter the design. The app itself is downloadable on iTunes and Android, and works well on the Android system, although you really likely want to use a phone because of the size of the tablet. It will work, but it gets in the way of play.

Like all parents, I'm not entirely thrilled about yet another excuse to hand over my phone, but I think that the augmented reality piece is really more of a gimmick that my daughter will tire of sooner rather than later. The building of the set must come first in order for this to work, and that's mildly educational, and we get to play with the LEGO set without the phone as well.

And did I mention how cool this set is, even without the augmented reality? The ghost theme makes for some cool pieces, and I like how this one looks when it's done. It's a winner.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces)

The DUPLO elements (NOT compatible with the elements in standard LEGO sets) are very large, designed for toddlers who are still developing their fine motor skills.

The DUPLO truck holds 26 alphabet blocks--each block is printed with a single letter on one side. This gives you and your child a complete set of alphabet blocks for teaching/learning ABCs.

The set includes three doll-like play figures: a girl, a boy, and a teddy bear. The set also includes a flat sheet with the alphabet blocks printed full-size, in A-Z order, for learning the order of the letters.

Twenty-six of the thirty-six pieces are used for the alphabet blocks. (There isn’t much assembly required in this set.) I wish that this delightful, versatile set had been available when I was learning my own ABCs!

Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

I have been over some friend's houses that had an oversized version of the standard game and it was a ton of fun to play in the backyard. This set is not as big as I have seen in the past, but it also makes it a bit more manageable to store.

We played as a family and decided to try out the custom rules. It took us some time to get creative to come up with some rules, but once we did, it was a lot of fun. So, basically, there is a small board where you can write down custom rules, which mean you have to do a certain task depending on the number you pull. This is a great game to play as a family or with some friends.

text_fidelity_a: Pokemon TCG: Shining Fates Mini Tin, Multi I don’t know what every pack had in it because we bought a boost box for a school fundraiser. I’m an art teacher for an elementary school and I was trying to think of a fundraiser that was different and that all the students would like. I talked my principal into a Pokémon fundraiser. He bought one of these Brilliant Stars booster boxes. I did open about 7 packs to sell cards individually. Of those 7 packs we got 2 V’s. One of them was a Galatians Moltres V (photo attached) secret rare 183/172. I know of at least 3 more V’s one being a Charizard V Star. I know this because a student that had bought a pack decided to open it at recess while I was doing recess duty. A group of boys took off running and hollering. Then I seen the one boy (that had bought a pack) tuck something into his hoodie pocket. I called him over and asked if he had his cards out. Though we sell the cards at the fundraiser they’re not allowed to have them out. They’re supposed to take them home and not bring them back to school. I had him show me what he had. It was a Charizard V Star! Now I’m not Pokémon expert but I’ve learned a little from the students and from researching for the fundraiser. I know this was an awesome card! I was told if I see a student have them out that was supposed to confiscate it. I couldn’t do that to this kid. We had a good talk and I had another student go to my room and get a hard sleeve card case (which we were also selling at the fundraiser) for him to put it in to protect it. I can see him putting it in his pocket and bending it and couldn’t stand the thought. He promised to take it home and not bring it back. I told him I know he would want to show his friends the card and now that he’s not allowed to bring it to school they may not believe him so I told him if anybody questioned him to come see me and I can let them know I seen it in person. It’s been the best fundraiser. It was supposed to last 2 week and we sold out of almost of everything in 2 days!
text_fidelity_b: Pokemon TCG: Shining Fates Mini Tin, Multi

Radio Flyer 4-In-1 Stroll 'N Trike, Red Radio Flyer Tricycle, Toddler Bike When I saw the opportunity to review this Radio Flyer four-in-one tricycle, I was eager to accept: My cousin and his wife, who live a couple doors down the street, have a three-year-old, and they have just learned that they are expecting another baby in June. So I knew that this toy would be used in all four of its "incarnations" at one point or another.

The toy arrived within three days, even though I did not request any special shipping status.

The directions for putting the tricycle together are excellent and detailed. They are entirely pictorial, with no words at all, which is a godsend for those of us who labor for hours trying to read badly translated written instructions. Laura (the mom) put the entire tricycle together with only minimal help from Brian (the dad). Brian did have to help with Instruction #13, and also with tightening screws and bolts here and there. I was delighted to hear that one does not need an engineering degree to put this toy together.

The tricycle went together very easily for the most part. The handlebars are the hardest part of the construction. Laura recommends that anyone putting this tricycle together pull up on the handlebars after attaching the bars and the clamp to be sure that the clamp has tightened properly. She pulled up on the handlebars at least four times and was able to remove them despite that clamp being on. You just have to tighten the clamp as much as possible.

This tricycle seems very durable, though I will add to this review after Brandon (the three-year-old) has used the toy more. The canopy is very nice, and the straps on the seat will be great for the new baby when he or she can use it (at nine months or so). The cupholder that surrounds the infant in the seat will be great for the baby as well. My only wish is that the tricycle had rubber tires instead of plastic tires. We live in a somewhat rural area with no sidewalks, and the plastic tires may not hold up as well as rubber tires. The push handle, to be used for infants, adjusts to the height of the adult pushing the tricycle, which is a wonderful feature.

Now to the acid test: Does the child like the toy? Brandon has been off this tricycle only to eat and sleep ever since it was put together. He even attempted to get on it several times while his mom was putting it together, saying, "I should try it!" With winter coming on he will probably use it only in the house at first, but Brian and Laura have a huge basement, and riding his tricycle there will give him hours of play time.

I highly recommend this tricycle, especially if your child or children are young enough to take advantage of it in all its formations. The product description says it can be used from nine months to five years, and that sounds about right.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer 4-In-1 Stroll 'N Trike, Red Radio Flyer Tricycle, Toddler Bike

There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This summer was the year of Jurassic World! My 5 turning 6 year old is too young to watch any of the Jurassic Park movies, but that didn't stop the advertisements and displays in stores from reaching audiences far and wide including my son. He already loves Legos AND dinosaurs so this was the perfect mashup for him! We already have other Lego Juniors sets (I honestly wish they would make more).

Lego Juniors are designed for 4-7 year olds. Basically, they are the same as the other Lego kits, but the instructions are more simplistic than the other kits for older children. The Legos designs are also more simple than the Lego kits for older children. The Legos are still the same size as regular Legos, so these are not an in between Duplos and Legos. If you step on them they will hurt. In addition, the pieces are tiny enough to get lost forever.

My son is a free form builder, he does not care about the actual instructions, what he cares about is the potential for creating what is shown on the package. His Lego bin is filled with Lego kits all mixed together and he has a blast creating his own world, which is limitless. So, if you are insistent on your child following the directions to a T, then I would not recommend these for a younger child. Most boys under 6 just do not have the patience for this. Frustration sets in quick and the desire to just play take over. Stick to Duplos or just plain free build sets until about age 6 or 7 if you want to stick to the instructions. However, if you don't mind the kits getting mixed up for creative play and you child loves Legos and Dinos, then this is the set for you.

As usual, the Legos are of the same quality we had when we were kids. I would recommend getting several of the Lego tools because some of this pieces are tiny and get stuck. The only way to get them out is via the Lego Tool!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.

text_fidelity_a:
Kid Galaxy RC Off Road Car. Claw Climber Tiger 4x4 Remote Control Vehicle, 2.4 GHz Wow! My toddler had been in a terrible mood all day, the sort of no good mood in which nothing satisfies and none of the toys or projects he was working on seem to come out right. Even a nap didn't cure it, but I'll tell you what did: this vehicle arriving in the mail. The presentation is awesome. You can see the face of the vehicle and the cool claws on the tires right from the get-go, and he immediately got excited. Though he is totally into trucks, construction vehicles, and things that go of all kinds, this got a higher level of excitement out of him because of how it was personified – it looks a little like Bowser from Super Mario Brothers, or has that same kind of appeal.

But, for a not quite three-year-old in a terrible mood, would he be able to work it? Though I've tested about 15 RC vehicles in the last year trying to find just the right one that he will be able to enjoy controlling, without going too fast, too slow, bottoming out on small obstacles, tipping over when driven over slopes, or being generally too complicated to run in some respect, only a few have passed the "I can do it myself" test. This is one of them.

The remote control is simple to understand and use, fits in small hands, and is lightweight and chunky to hold. Perfect for a toddler. There also isn't any pokey wire or metal antennae sticking out. I always wonder how companies justify giving that to a kid, given that they're going to be sprinting across the lawn not looking where they are going and liable to poke somebody's eye out, or their own if they fall.

I also really liked the speed level of this. I would've been happy if it were also a little slower to allow for better reaction time, but the speed was fast enough to be fun but not so fast that it's hard to control with childlike reflexes.

But the very best thing about it is those clawlike tires and the suspension. The claws are made of a softer rubberized plastic material, and the claws flap out with the centrifugal force of the tires movements, and retract in as needed. It's not something you can really control, they just do it themselves. Mine seem to have an error where one of the tires has the claws stuck inside for the most part and trying to pull them out on my own didn't work that well, they just retracted again and stayed retracted as soon as I started the vehicle again. No matter, it almost seems to help the car have better traction to have one back wheel that is essentially without claws.

The claws grip onto pretty much any surface, carpet, blankets, toys, rocks, lawn and woodchips, and thrust them out of the way so the car can off-road just about anywhere. We, perhaps unwisely, began our testing in the living room, where it climbed over a wide array of baby and toddler toys, turning upside down, then catching on a blanket and turning itself right back up before getting stuck in a ridiculously large mashup of garbage truck and Duplo bricks. It was exciting, impressive how it righted itself and went over such a wide variety of huge objects, and loads and loads of fun.

I also love the high suspension. Many other trucks, even ones with big monster tires such as from John Deere, ruin things by having a small plastic box on the underside of the vehicle which hangs downward and makes the vehicles bottom out on anything it hits. I don't know why this is such a "thing", but at least half of the RC vehicles we've gotten have this exact problem, even the off-road ones. This little truck does not suffer from that issue, and thus was able to go through a wide variety of terrains, and nothing seemed to stop it. It was going sideways on a pile of landscape trimmings, went upside down, righted itself, clawed its way all the way through the backyard and house with no issues.

The one complaint I have is not really a complaint, just a minor caution. It looks as though there is not really any way for sand and dirt and mud to work itself out of the holes in the tires were it to get truly filthy. We solve this problem by not taking it to the sand dunes or running it through sand or mud. We brought it to the playground that has woodchips and lawn, in the backyard that has woodchips and lawn, and discouraged our toddler from using it in the dusty vegetable beds in the backyard. No problem. However, if your vision is to bring it someplace truly dirty, I have no idea what the longevity would be and how nice the vehicle would look and work after prolonged running through such materials. It is off-road, but not necessarily all-terrain.

Overall, this is probably my favorite RC vehicle we've gotten yet. It is just so much fun, has great personality and really made an impression on our toddler, is easy to control, and doesn't have many of the issues that previous RC vehicles have suffered from. A thoughtfully designed toy all around, and fun for the whole family. I definitely don't feel too old for this, and my almost 3-year-old toddler isn't too young, so that's quite a range.
text_fidelity_b: Kid Galaxy RC Off Road Car. Claw Climber Tiger 4x4 Remote Control Vehicle, 2.4 GHz

text_fidelity_a:
NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Aurora Light Projector - Perfect Night Light, Star Projector for Kids & Adults, Room Decor for Any Room, 6 Light Patterns & 5 Nature Sounds, Remote Control, Micro SD Card, Aux Cord [[VIDEOID:be0356b78014df3072ccf28ee48026f8]] I actually purchase this for my 60 year old husband. He has always wanted to go see the Northern Lights, but now in the Covid climate, I do not think that kind of travel will happen any time soon. I did not tell him I was getting this for him and when it arrived, I actually saw glee on his face. Mind you, this is not an emotion I see a hint of very often. I have given him gifts before, but truly, I saw something different on his face. I figured if he didn't like this we could pass this on to some friend's smaller kids, but I do not think this unit is going anywhere.

When we first got it, he opened it immediately and we set it in the living room and ran through all that the unit does. It pretty much does the same things just in different color patterns. It has 5 loops, which a few of the loops you can hear the definite stop and repeat. NG's creation crew should have spent more time selecting better clips here. Somebody dropped the ball. For that I was a wee disappointed.

The light pattern is pretty neat. We soon moved it from the living room to the bedroom. This item didn't just get set aside, he scooped it up and found a place for it on his bedroom dresser. Before bed, he set it up and we fell asleep to a light show and crashing waves. It was set on the 1 hour mode and turned off as it should have.

The unit is smaller than I expected and is probably best if set on the floor and displayed, you get a wider spectrum of the swirling colors. The multi colors are very soothing.

Plugs in via mini USB. The cord has some length, but not enough to get it good and centered in a room. Comes with a remote that takes a couple of AAs that are not included. Wish the unit did not have to be tethered to the wall. Would have been nice to be rechargeable and been able to set it in the middle of the room.

Overall, this was worth it. In hindsight, I would still purchase. Could easily recommend. Great gift.
text_fidelity_b: NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Aurora Light Projector - Perfect Night Light, Star Projector for Kids & Adults, Room Decor for Any Room, 6 Light Patterns & 5 Nature Sounds, Remote Control, Micro SD Card, Aux Cord

Home Run Games 8-Bit 2600 Playing Cards I have collected many different types of cards for playing and tricks. The design on these struck my interest, but aside from that design I feel like these could be better for the price.

text_fidelity_a:
BlueFit German Tiger I Panzer Tank with Remote Control, Battery, Light, Sound, Rotating Turret and Recoil Action When Cannon Artillery Shoots, Mini 1:72 Scale, Assorted Color This this is awesome. For something that easily sits on the palm of your hand the detail is pretty sharp. It honestly looks like a World War ][ Tiger tank with tons of details. I received the standard, mostly green, camouflage there's also a darker camouflage and a blue tank available. Colors appear to ship randomly. Remote control device coloring also seem to match the tank you get.
This little thing really zips around. I was surprised at how quick it gets up and goes. There's also a super speed button on the controller that adds fifty percent to the speed of the tank. There's also engine noises and what I'm guessing are 'track' sounds are this races around. The turret will turn 360° in one direction, I found going one way the barrel would hang up on the antenna but the turret rotation switches back and forth as you rotate. The barrel also raises and lowers as the turret turns. When you press the fire button there's the sound of a cannon firing and the entire tank body recoils backwards.
The remote control takes four double A batteries and the tank itself charges from a cable attached to the side of the remote. Charging time is fairly quick and I've already gotten several hours of fun out of the tank and it's still going strong. The only reason I can't give it four stars is the tank just won't drive in a straight line. You can someone adjust for the tendency to turn by steering left or right as you go but it would have been just that much cooler if it had driven in a straight line. Still, I'm a fully grown adult and this is one of my favorite things. It's just such a gas to play with.
I received this item in exchange for my review.
text_fidelity_b: BlueFit German Tiger I Panzer Tank with Remote Control, Battery, Light, Sound, Rotating Turret and Recoil Action When Cannon Artillery Shoots, Mini 1:72 Scale, Assorted Color
