text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

Passnag Light Saber with 3 Mode Sound, Force Heavy Dueling, FX Real RGB 12 Colors Changeable Light Saber with Blaster Sound, Metal Hilt with 1' Blade--Black SN227B [[VIDEOID:70401b9086e08489b8471006d9a7ceb7]] March 2, 2021 UPDATE:
--------------------------
This was adult owned and taken care of. Mainly used for display, and sparingly demo'ed in the 6 months that I've owned it. I hadn't turned it on for a long while, probably several months. I decided to test it out again, and it wouldn't turn on. I've charged it for over 5 hours. There is a red light to indicate it's charging, but still won't turn on. No longevity for this item. Reducing review to 1-star.

Original Review:
------------------
Very fun light saber! Has a good heft to it and feels high quality. The handle is some sort of aluminum or metal. This looks much better than those plasticky toys. But as usual, with all these sabers on the market, the worst looking part is the the plastic tube. Our tech isn't there yet, but hopefully one day, we can get rid of that plastic tube and have a real solid light beam out! In any case, here are the controls:

-Single click button once to turn on.
-Single click button again to hear effect.
-While it's on, Double click for a blasting sound which the manual calls "lockup mode." It will stay at this sound until you Double Click again to get out of it.
-While it's on, triple click to change colors (this is finicky though)
-Press & hold button to turn off.
-To change the sound "theme," while it's off, hold the button, you will hear a sound theme. Hold the button again to hear the next sound theme, hold it again to hear the next, etc. There is a total of 4 themes, one of which is actually mute.
-To use any of these themes, once you like what you hear, just single click the button to turn on and play. Remember clicking once turns it on, but holding the button would cause it to cycle through the themes. But once on, to get back to cycling through the themes, you need to press & hold to turn off first, then press & hold to cycle through the themes.

My kids have a few sabers from the out of business toy store. This one belongs to daddy. LOL! I'm knocking 1 star for the finicky controls and instructions that were a little hard to figure out. 4 stars.

Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb We have had a few other Treasure X sets in the past and my son really enjoyed them, with the sets keeping him busy for hours at a time carving and opening little slime filled packages with interesting toys inside. He has a castle "dollhouse" that he uses a lot of these toys in to create stories.

This treasure tomb was completely different in the sense that we work carving the toys out of chunks of sand this time, rather discovering each element and kind of figuring out everything as a puzzle.

The one criticism I have is that while I would've loved to have set this down and let my son just figure it out, the texture of a few of the things that you were supposed to just pick apart and peel away were not necessarily obvious that they were disposable elements of the toy, so the instruction manual was necessary, and because the instruction manual was not made big and pictorial, I had to sit there while they figured the whole thing out. My six-year-old figured out and understood most of it, but again, the parts that were not obvious that he was allowed to just tear into them really did need my reading the instructions and giving encouragement.

Aside from that minor quibble, this thing kept both my six-year-old and my three and half-year-old busy for a really long time. Hours. I sat them outside on the patio with a big pan to hold any messy elements, and they carved and drove swords into holes and put the keys in and popped everything out and overall had a ridiculously fun time.

The weird textural blue rock like slime in two of the tombs was particularly compelling to my son, who played with this stuff for about 45 minutes. I would've appreciated if the two tombs had had different types of slime or even just different colors, but my son had no such complaint and played for a long time.

While the tomb itself has not continued to hold their interest after about a week of play, some of the parts have been incorporated into frequent play with their castle dollhouse, and so overall even though part of it feels somewhat disposable, the other parts of it feel really fun for incorporating into our normal imaginative play.

This would make a fantastic birthday gift, because it is extremely flashy, tons of fun, lots of excited commentary and wowed children, and then lots of little toys that feel very fun and abundant.

Would I buy a set like this again? Very possibly, for a holiday or other occasion that I really want to feel super special and fancy. If there was a holiday where we were unable to have family and friends visit us or something like that, this set would bridge the gap to make the day feel sparkly and exciting for the kids.
text_fidelity_b: Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb

There are still some little blue clippy things that came in the boxes that we never did figure out how to use, and I couldn't find the information anywhere on their website or google searches. 6' Giant Teepee Play House of Pine Wood with Carry Case by Trademark Innovations (White) purchased for my grandsons to use when visiting..... it is large.... large enough for an an adult to get into. The material is a cotton canvas... not terribly thick, but not too thin in my opinion. It was relatively easy to put together... I like that this is a bottom floor attached. It is quite popular to stay grandma's and camp out.... I added some "nap pads" which are perfect for the 5 and 2 year old. I also added a stuffed bear and alligator and a camp lantern that is a lantern or a star map night light. Honestly, I keep it up in the corner of my living room so it is ready for any visit. It does come with a handy bag that has a handle if you'd like to store it when not in use. The poles are wood... a pine I believe... very sturdy. I would recommend this teepee... I always update if there are any issues that may be helpful.
3/25/2016 UPDATE: ...so I just finished deconstructing the teepee and felt an undate with tips might be helpful... first... you will never get the canvas teepee back into the canvas bag provided... it's like folding/rolling a really thick fitted sheet and trying to get into a tube sock.... BUT the wooden poles fit nicely into the canvas bag along with the plastic connector pieces... it would have been nice if the connectors gripped the poles better and stayed connected during the deconstruct phase... however... I just removed all the holed top pieces and then turned the teepee upside down and shook it sort of like a pillow case... the lower pieces eventually come out... I just rolled the teepee up, put all the poles and connector pieces in the bag and set in a large drawer I have. I would have lowered my rating one star for the deconstruct hassle, but honestly, my grandsons love it so much I just can't. The quality is such that this is going to last for many years if we take care of it. It's just a matter of learning how to use it in an efficient manner. Also... I have hard wood floors, so I went to a local carpet store and purchased some carpet padding. I cut into a circle and place it under the teepee when I have it set up... I worry less about bonked heads that way - grandsons 5 years and 2 years. Ok! Hope this is indeed helpful info!

text_fidelity_a:
KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+ I bought this for my 2 year old son for Christmas, I mean Santa dropped this off for my son for Christmas because he loves to come into my kitchen and pull out all the pots and pans and grab every utensil in the drawers to, "mix, mix, mix" as he says. So, why not a kitchen. The world's greatest chefs are men so why can't my son get a head start. My concern is that he is so tall I needed a kitchen that he could grow into. I also wanted something basic that he would pretend to cook instead of pushing pushing buttons on gadgets that whirred, chirp, and buzz. So, a wooden kitchen was the way to go, not plastic. I settled on this one because it's not pink and the dimensions seemed to be appropriate.

Pros:
If you have a tall two year old, this is the kitchen for you. My son is in the 95% for height. I am 5'10" and everyone else in my family is tall, so you have an idea of how tall he is. It will be at least a year before the counter is at a counter height that adults would expect a counter to be. Currently, it stands at his bottom of his breast bone. He's currently about 36* tall.

Once you put it together, it's sturdy and it comes lots of extra screws and parts just in case, which I needed.

The pot holder and the spatula and spoon you see in the picture also come with it.

The instructions were no more difficult that an Ikea set of a directions.

The hours of playtime during the Christmas break and the look on his face and level of excitement was priceless.

Cons:

You will need two sized Phillips head screwdrivers, a wrench or a set of pliers, and at least FOUR hours to put this together. So, slow down on the egg nog.

It's made of particle board and the overlay is paper not painted so it chips off easily.

It's HEAVY! Over 70 pounds!

OFF GASSING! This is the biggest downfall, which I should have known, but just didn't think of. This product offgasses something terrible! Because the box is extremely heavy and because it was delivered to my front door I just couldn't get this down to the basement or to the garage. (I live in an older, well-established neighborhood where most of the houses are pre-1950, so if your house has a garage in the front of the house unlike mine, which is down a driveway and to the back, try to get the UPS man to take it there!) I could only open the box in the house on Christmas Eve, and thus, the offgassing of the kitchen was really terrible and made me nauseous. I would highly recommend airing it out for at least a week in your garage before you put it together and bring it into your house.

Therefore, the toxic chemicals we no doubt inhaled because of my inability to air this product out is a big reason why this only a three not a four star rating.

Overall, I'm satisfied because my son is happy and loves it. If I had the money or space, I would have just purchased the Pottery Barn kitchen set or if I had the time, I would have just made one inspired from Pinterest, but it was a good $150.00 spent, and I'm sure we'll have it for a long time.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes I started playing Settlers of Catan when it first came out, many years ago. It has a special place as a gateway game. It brought people who wouldn't normally play anything exotic out of the world of Chutes and Ladders, and into the realm of strategy board games. It's easier to learn than Monopoly, but without the very lengthy period of regret between knowing who will win and actually reaching the foregone conclusion. I largely stopped playing the game about 20 years ago because thanks to Catan, the world of board games exploded into a great variety of games that I consider to be much better. Seeing this fancy set made me want to give it a try again, see what might have changed, and teach the kids.

Unboxing:
The components are visible in the packaging, which is unusual. The outer box is a throwaway, but there is a good sturdy box inside. Everything is packed well enough to avoid shifting and scuffing in transit. There are a few too many components for my taste. It takes quite a while to get everything taken out and put away. I'm fine with that if a game really needs that level of complexity, but I think this one is pushing it. The new three dimensional components make it even more of a chore. I like that the water border clips together securely. In the original, the water spaces tended to slide around, and since the game is about building roads and houses on the cracks, it was destabilizing for everything. Now the board stays together securely, even on carpet.

The new three dimensional tiles are a fun idea, but poorly implemented. Each one needs a convex, translucent, slippery disc on top, but few allowances were made for this in design. They just teeter there and slip around, or sit way off center. I can't support making the number circles translucent. I can't see any positive purpose for it, and it reduces the ability to play with variants that start with some of them face down. After assembling the sea sections, I see that the game board is smaller than I expected. I really like the addition of harbor shapes on the seas to show where the ports should go. The ports themselves are a bit hard to see compared to the old cardboard ones.

The colors chosen for each player are questionable. The parts themselves have a dark wash over them to make the details stand out, but it makes them all dingy. Beige, orange, red, and blue. I guess the blue player can find their pieces, but in dim lighting, the rest look too similar. There's an odd mix of unique things, like the shape of each player's houses, and having things repeat that could have been unique, like all of the forest hexes being identical.

If the instruction book is hard to open, it's because it isn't a book, it's a foldout that folds counterintuitively. There is a quick reference startup guide and another small book with more in-depth details.

It's nice that it comes with card holders, and while it's a chore to get everything back in the box right, at least there's a secure place for everything. The gameplay is as I remember. Simple and engaging enough for most people to be willing to play, and strategic enough to be satisfying. There are games that are both simpler and more strategic out there. Quite a lot of them. In a four player game, anyone who ends up hemmed in by players who chose after them can end up stuck without anywhere to expand. This leads to occasional games like Monopoly, where someone isn't going to be having much fun for an hour. Luck can play a bit too heavily. This was one of the early games that added the excellent mechanic of randomizing the playing field, but the dice too often just end up rolling the same number over and over, which tends to give some players a lot to do and others nothing for several critical turns.

It's strange, but I think I may actually stick with my old plain set. This one feels more fancy and less functional.
text_fidelity_b: CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes

Paw Patrol Marshall's Transforming Fire Truck with Pop-Out Water Cannons, for Ages 3 and Up I felt like I needed a Paw Patrol car lesson while shopping for cars to fit in the Lookout Tower. Let me tell you there are three main lines I found on Amazon, Spin Masters website, and in Target/Walmart:
- Basic Vehicles
- Transforming Vehicles
- Ultimate Rescue Vehicles

I wanted cars that would fit the Lookout Tower, and finally figured out that although some people may say that the Ultimate Rescue line fits in the tower, they are the biggest of the three lines and some reviews say those are too big.
The Basic Vehicles are the original vehicles (the Basic Chase car comes with the Lookout Tower) and those were originally intended to be the cars for the tower. The Basic Marshall car is simply called “Marshall’s Fire Fightin Truck”. However, the Basic line is hardest to find, and they are currently either marked up by third party sellers on Amazon or I could only find one or two Basic cars at each Target I visited.

Enter this Transforming line. They are a bit smaller than the Ultimate Rescue, and I was able to find them for $12.99 each on Amazon. They all have a little button that pops out the pups gear. My kids like popping out Marshall’s water cannons and they can reset them themselves (ages 2.5 and 4).

Long story short, this will work in the Lookout Tower. Best of luck finding them all for your kid.

The other big downside is that you don't get to do the bags in order like you do with LEGO. You kind of have to open them all at once and work from one gigantic pile in the center of the table. It's messy and can lead to quitting, but that's all part of the experience.

They will fit somewhat within the tractor component, which is the largest piece of this set, and by far the most interesting. There are a number of playable aspects to this that give you a lot more bang for your buck than the more model-focused kits we've tried from Wishalife previously.

Fisher-Price Imaginext DC Super Friends Batman Playset Super Surround Batcave with Lights Sounds & Phrases for Ages 3+ Years, 33 x 42 Inches We've been huge Imaginext fans for years! Their toys have always been high quality and very durable. They're on the pricey side, but I happily buy them because I believe the value is there. And this new massive Batcave is no exception!
I can not tell you how excited my kids were when I pulled this out the Amazon box! They've had it for a couple of weeks now and have played with it nearly every day. It comes with a lot of extra figures and accessories that help keep the imaginary play going for hours. Not to mention the lights and sounds are awesome! It needs four C batteries (which we didn't have when on hand when it arrived) and took us about 20 minutes to take it out of the box and put the whole thing together. I'd highly recommend setting it up before you show your kids it or they just linger around behind you whining every 30 seconds about why you're taking so long to put it together, lol! But beyond that, any kid would be thrilled to have this. It really is one of the coolest playsets (if not the absolute best one) that I have ever seen! Thank you so much Imaginext.... it will bring our kids years and years of happiness!!!

Puzzle 1000 Pieces Adult - Puzzle 1000 Puzzle for Adults - De Haar Castle, Netherlands - Jigsaw Puzzles 1000 Pieces for Adults This GLISTELLO 1000-PIECE JIGSAW PUZZLE FOR ADULTS - DE HAAR CASTLE, NETHERLANDS (27.5 x 19.7 inches) is a good quality puzzle, highly appropriate for jigsaw puzzle experts. It has many similar cloud and tulip pieces that present a challenge to assembly, because the pieces need to be placed by shape as well as by color. Of course, jigsaw puzzle experts love these difficult jigsaws!

The puzzle pieces are small, which makes the 1000-piece puzzle fit easily on a worktable. The fully interlocking pieces are thick enough to be handled easily, and the interlocking tabs don’t bend if the pieces are handled with ordinary care. The pieces don’t click together like Ravensburger puzzle pieces, but they fit together unmistakably by feel when properly joined.

Unfortunately, the pieces don’t fit tightly enough to allow joined sections to be picked up and moved without falling apart. Completed sections need to be picked up on a sheet of paper, or pushed along the tabletop, to reach their proper locations in the puzzle.

The puzzle picture looks exactly like the photograph on the product page. The picture is nicely printed on the puzzle itself, and on a big sheet packed inside the box for reference during assembly. The price (about $19 on Amazon) is very reasonable for a jigsaw puzzle of this size and quality.

I wouldn’t recommend this puzzle for group assembly, because of the many pieces that are visually similar in color and shape. Puzzles like this one require a lot of sorting of pieces in advance by color and shape if the actual assembly is to proceed quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Puzzle 1000 Pieces Adult - Puzzle 1000 Puzzle for Adults - De Haar Castle, Netherlands - Jigsaw Puzzles 1000 Pieces for Adults

I would say the age range can be up to age 9 actually. Everything you need to make three instruments is in the kit with instructions on how to make 4. The water xylophone doesn't have any materials to make it, so you'll need your own same sized glass jars/cups and food coloring to do that exercise. I wish the explanations were a bit more simplistic for 5-6 years olds. I feel like this is better geared toward older kids 7-9 to understand the science behind sound. My almost 8-year-old kind of got it, but not really.

In the kit, there's a book that has a story. The beginning of the story doesn't really make sense or tie in at all to the ultimate situation at hand. However, the gist eventually becomes a classroom of kids with their music teacher making instruments for a performance. Once he walks you through the 4 different instruments (only three have materials to make an instrument) then you'll start building your instrument and experimenting with them. I feel like the materials are ok sturdy; however, I have instructed my son to not play with them unless we are doing the experiments (until we are finished with all of them). Simply because I do not want them to become damaged before we get to finish. So far we have completed the box guitar, which was easy enough. We did it together with me mainly explaining the instructions and my son completing the tasks. The only thing I had to help with was folding the box. After that, we went through 3 of the 4 experiments. We'll complete the 4th experiment and then move on to the next instrument at a later date. With COVID, it's been nice and important to stretch science kits like this one out over multiple days. I'm glad I saved this for a rainy day because now we've had something nice and fun to do all while responsibly quarantining.

This zip case is made just for the Karaoke microphone. It has a cutout to place the actual mic. itself and a pocket for smaller parts!
All buttons are easily marked on the mic. and easy to see and use. Bonus… You can purchase an SD chip separately, to record your masterpiece and future Justin Bieber duet!! We however have not taken this toy/device to that next level… (i would consider us still at the novice side of things!)

Overall, the price point of $30 is spot on and a very reasonable good deal for the product you will receive. My youngest is High School and male… So a little too cool to admit this is fun- my 2 college age girls are fighting who gets to take it back to the dorms with them after Xmas break!?!! I’m telling you- singing is fun, and this.. Just makes you want to sing! I won’t break out into a Neil diamond song right now… If you’re looking for a fun add-on to family/friend game night.. text_fidelity_a:
Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+ Flash is a simple yet fun dice game for the entire family. It consists of six sets of six dice, each distinguished by a different color, six numbered chips for scoring, a score pad with eight challenges and a small pencil, and a storage bag and instructions.

Flash is a fast game and this is one of the reasons busy parents and others will enjoy playing it so much. The object of the game is to complete each of the eight challenges faster than your opponents and what makes it move so quickly is that everyone plays at the same time, racing against each other to see who can complete the challenge the most quickly. Unlike Yahtzee and other dice games where each person plays solo while the others wait, this game offers all- out action through each challenge.

What are the challenges in Flash? Well, they are basic numbering combinations such as six of a kind, a straight, etc. It sounds like it might be difficult, but it really isn't because each individual die has a flash (lightning bolt) on one side that counts as a wildcard. All you do is throw your dice, keep the ones that you need, then pick up the other dice and throw them again and again until you meet the challenge. Whoever completes it first yells "Flash" and picks up the highest scoring chip. Everyone else keeps throwing the dice until they get the challenge correct, but they get a lower scoring chip, all the way down to the number 1 chip. Play continues through all of the challenges and the highest scoring player wins.

The simplicity of this game is one of its strongest points and kids seem to like it more than a game such as Yahtzee for several reasons. First, the speed- it's an all- out battle to see who can meet the challenge before anyone else. Second, every challenge is certain to be met, in contrast with Yahtzee where you may or may not be able to complete each of the items on the score sheet. The scoring is simpler, too, and I like that the manufacturer included a small bag in which to place the dice, chips, pencil, and scoring pad because they would eventually get lost without it.

If I had to look for something to criticize with this dice game, it would be the fact that the challenges are really not that challenging. No matter how bad your luck may be, you will be able to complete each and every challenge- usually in two minutes max. It is only a matter of time until you roll the right numbers on the dice and the wildcard flash makes each challenge that much easier to achieve.

Family game night is part of growing up and Flash is a good game to have around on those nights when you want some family entertainment and only have about 20 minutes or less to spare. It's a fun little game that most anyone will find worthwhile and worth playing.
text_fidelity_b: Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+

It also uses infrared to follow lines in front of it, to avoid things in front of it, and also to follow objects. It's a really fun car.
I think almost anyone that enjoys cars and building things and all that stuff will really have fun with this. The kit is filled with the tools all the tools you need and there is no welding or anything required. It's fun, semi-easy, and so worth it when you get to play with the finished product!

LEGO Marvel Spider-Man Far from Home: Molten Man Battle 76128 Building Kit (294 Pieces) This LEGO MARVEL SPIDER-MAN FAR FROM HOME MOLTEN MAN BATTLE 76128 BUILDING KIT (294 Pieces) is probably most appreciated by kids and adults who’ve watched the “Spider-Man Far From Home” movie that features Molten Man. However, the kit produces a great monster figure that is fun to build even if you haven’t seen the movie.

The kit is compatible with standard LEGO sets, and has some elements that can be used very creatively in other models. For example, the two gold chains that hang from the figure’s shoulders are unusual for the color. Another element that I really love is the fast-action stud shooter hand. (It shoots 6 studs in rapid succession as you turn the rotary gear part.) The gripper claw hand is also pretty cool.

The minifigs and their accessories are especially good. You get Spidey with an assortment of web weapons; a fireman with a buildable fire extinguisher; and a purple-caped Mysterio.

Vziimo Titanic Ship in a Bottle Building Set with LED Lighting and Display Case, Collectible Architecture Sunken Ship Micro Blocks Kits for Adults Age 12+ Gift, Compatible with Nano (1040 Pieces) Nano bricks are tiny! This isn’t a set for young kids, unless they are closely supervised while building. I’d say adults and older teens, due to the small size of the pieces and complexity of the instructions.

Unlike most building sets where the pieces for each step are shown next to that step, these instructions show a bunch of pieces for several steps at once. So you might have a pile of 50 or 60 pieces for the next 3 or 4 steps (or more).

The instructions themselves require attention to detail, you really have to pay attention to how the pieces are laid out. A single step might involve 20 pieces or more.

Instructions aside, the pieces don’t snap together very well. I was building the ship on a desk, but even with the hard surface, the pieces aren’t straight. The bottom of my Titanic is curling upwards even before I get to the part that’s supposed to be bent from the iceberg. I pressed so hard my fingers hurt but I still couldn’t get all the pieces to fit together as they should.

I wish the stand for the bottle was made from bricks instead of faux wood. The stand looks clunky and is flimsy.

T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle Well, this was kind of educational, and it was kind of a frenetic, fun 15 minutes trying to put things back together, but the end comments were "This is ridiculous" and "Well they could have made that better." The ridiculous part was how they made decisions to cut the pieces. They do not follow international borders very faithfully and randomly cut larger countries into random parts. Pieces that include only one country do not resemble the country at all. the eastern united states is a irregular rectangle that appears to miss New England and average out Florida. France is a strange amporphous shape. Canada and Russia are random blotches of non interconnecting shapes.

I like the story that the first puzzle was a US map cut into pieces in a classroom to teach geography. This could have been similar except that the countries are so crudely hacked in shapes. But it does give an idea of location and cultural icons like the great wall of china, russian dolls, local animals are located on the map. I was very impressed that the Great Barrier Reef made the map as an entity. But it could have been so much better in the way it was handled.

As for how it was made, the pieces are small and found to be easy to misplace. The magnetism is weak but sufficient to keep the pieces loosely on the board. The backing is very flexible and all in all it does not seem to be a super well built product.
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
BIBIELF Bat Decor I cannot begin to tell you how much fun our entire family is having with this robot! (Well, almost the entire family...the cats hate it but the dog LOVES it!) I am truly impressed as to how well this toy works and all of the features it includes. I usually mention at the end of a review my opinion as to whether an item is worth the price but I feel the need to start with that in this review. I cannot believe how low the price of Rock Robot is. I would expected it to cost FAR more than it does!

Other than needing place 2 AA batteries (NOT included) in the controller, there is no assembly required. The robot has an on/off button on the front and rather than using batteries, it is charged using a USB cord (included). Charging does take a few hours but then Rock takes off, moves, dances, sings, plays, etc for a good 30-45 minutes straight before needing to be charged again.

As soon as its turned on, Rock giggles and introduces himself. He lights up as well. The remote controller has a SO many different functions and works well. We have experienced a few times when we had to turn the robot off and back on again after using a lot of the controller functions in a short time. (The robot will stay lit but not perform the controller functions. Its truly NOT a big deal. Turning off and back on again is all it takes and he's back in action) Rock can walk or slide; frontwards or backwards, fast/slow-pretty much whatever you want him to do. If he's gliding and comes to a stop, he doesn't tip over! I keep thinking he's going to tip but he has not fallen over even one time! He dances, sings and even moonwalks. He has a bunch of stories to tell as well with the simple press of a button. The volume as well as the voice is easily controlled with the controller.

The gesture sensing function is pretty neat. A simple command using your hand will make Rock move backward or forward/left or right.

Rock appears to be well-made. As mentioned, he hasn't fallen over once. It glides/walks/dances, etc VERY easily on flooring. (Rock does not work well on thick carpet) The controller is easy to use as well. I feel the need to mention my husband has a hearing impairment and cannot always understand what the robot is saying-he has trouble making out the words. However, the rest of us can understand it perfectly fine.

We truly are having a blast playing with this robot. I cannot recommend it enough. Its fun and entertaining and WOW, is the price ever incredibly LOW!
text_fidelity_b: BIBIELF Bat Decor

Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog Sometimes when I get a box of Bloks, I chuck the instructions, dump them in with the rest of my collection, and make something cool with some of my favorite new pieces. I really liked the look of this one though, and I haven't followed the instructions for a while, so I actually built it to spec. I wasn't sure if there was any logic to all the separate and nested baggies, but half way through I concluded that the answer was "very little". I dumped them all in a dark colored jewelry display tray and things went much more smoothly. I definitely learned a few things about how some of the pieces can work together, and the end result came out looking nicer than most of the pre-built toys out there these days, but fully customizable. Melissa & Doug Children's Book - Poke-a-Dot: An Alphabet Eye Spy (Board Book with Buttons to Pop) - Alphabet Pop It Book, Push Pop Book For Toddlers And Kids Ages 3+ The Pop-a-Dots are a novel tactile experience for any little kid. The initial excitement is lots of fun. The color pallet is bright. The layout of the book is excellent:
1. The beginning of the book contains 14 pages showing 2 letters of the alphabet, per page, with a “Look for:” list of words at the bottom of the page. There are Pop-a-Dots for 1, 2 or 3 objects, per page.

2. Next, there are 5 pages of upper case letters of the alphabet. Each letter has the head of an animal beginning with that letter and a Pop-a-Dot. There is a “Can you find” word list of the animals at the bottom of each page.

3. The final page is an alphabet grid. Each block of the grid shows both the upper and lower case letter as well as an object. The full upper case alphabet and lower case alphabet run across the top and bottom of the page, respectively.

I give 5 stars for the font, punctuation and correct relative sizing of upper and lower case used throughout the book. Excellent!

There are some challenges for the intended age group, in my opinion, that I would like to share.

Potential Challenges (imho):
1. When this arrived, the first thing that struck me is the weight of this book. It is too heavy for me to hold while reading alone or with a toddler. Book is recommended for ages 3-6 yrs. and those little ones could not hold this book. The only comfortable way to read it is opened flat on a table or the floor.

2. The structure of the binding prevents the pages from laying flat when the book is open on a table. The binding will be damaged/tear if a child presses down on the book trying to make the pages lay flat, specifically the pages in the middle of the book. You can see in my pics the stress creases already showing at the inner binding edge of the first and last pages just from me flipping thru the pages for 15 minutes, or so.

3. I am on the fence about the artwork (perhaps just a personal aesthetic) and choice of some items used to represent the letters. For example, I had no idea what a Xolo was. I had to google it to find out it is a rare breed of hairless dog. I dont find the artwork for Quail, Iguana, Vulture, Ice or Gorilla to be easily recognizable to a child. Yoyo, Nail, Wig are not common objects for this age group. ( I checked the copyright date to ensure this was not an older book where a yoyo would be a known object. Copyright is 2019)

All in all, the Pop-a-Dots are THE selling feature of this book. Kids love to pop them and the sound they make. If you are looking for a novel gift, this would be a great choice. As far as a learning tool, this would not be among my top choices.

I hope the pics below will clarify my thoughts on this book. Thanks!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Children's Book - Poke-a-Dot: An Alphabet Eye Spy (Board Book with Buttons to Pop) - Alphabet Pop It Book, Push Pop Book For Toddlers And Kids Ages 3+

Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers - Educational Wooden Pattern Blocks Playset in Vehicle Transportation Shapes with Vibrant Colors, 5 Brain-Building Peg Puzzles Youngsters have special educational needs. They love to play and as parents, we want to give them things to play with that also exercise their young, curious, developing minds. A good toy for this purpose is this Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle set from Lemostaar.

Packaged in a box, this set contains 6 different dinosaur puzzles and each of the puzzles has just 6 pieces. The puzzles are each assembled on a small board measuring about 7 by 6 inches. With only 6 pieces, toddlers are the age group most likely to benefit from these puzzles. Kids have a chance to show their skill as they put each of the pieces into place. Depending on a child’s interest and skill level, some may take longer than others, but most preschool age kids will be determined to assemble and show off their completed puzzle to supportive parents.

With all these pieces, there could be a tendency to lose them, but fortunately, the manufacturer includes a storage bag. You could place them back into the box, but the storage bag is better. It’s cool that the manufacturer thought to add this because it’s practical and better ensures that pieces don’t get lost.

Teaching problem- solving skills to young people can be accomplished in many ways and a toy like the Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle set from Lemostaar is useful for this purpose. With 6 puzzles and just 6 pieces each, a young person can complete each with relative ease and improve coordination and other skills in the process.

My First Sewing Kit by Alex Crafts, Perfect for Beginners, Arts and Crafts Colorful and Fun Sewing Projects to Learn the Basic Skills of Sewing (Ages 7+) This possibly isn't the best starter kit for a child who has never sewn before. The instructions aren't that good. If the child has done any other sewing, or has anyone who can help (can be another kid) then this will provide a great deal of practice, which is where this really shines.

There are quite a few projects here. There is a draw string bag, a stuffed cat, a stuffed dog, a stuffed elephant, and a book cover with pencil holder wrapper.

For supplies, it has everything - scissor, tape measure, pins, pin cushion, button, even some extra stuff, like pop poms, that you won't need for any of the projects. There definitely is not even close to enough stuffing. It did not quite fill the cat, which is the first, and smallest, of the stuffed animal projects. You'll want to pick up something like [[ASIN:B000YZ7G44 Fairfield Poly-Fil Premium Polyester Fiber, White, 1 Bag, 12-Ounce]]. Any fiberfill will do, but this is a good one, similar to what is in the kit. While on the topic of stuffing, a double pointed knitting needle, or better http://www.amazon.com/Little-Foot-That-Purple-Thang-/dp/B001ELBCFG/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1464647654&sr=8-1&keywords=purple+thang will help get the stuffing into the tight areas, like the tails. Both the fiberfill and the thang will be useful items in a variety of sewing projects.

For the embroidery floss, it says to cut the skein on one side to make lengths. That works, no issue, but it might be better to make a little yarn butterfly (really simple; instructions are online) so that you can pull the length you need for each section and the leftovers, and there will be plenty, can be used to make friendship bracelets. There is an excess of embroidery floss here.
text_fidelity_b: My First Sewing Kit by Alex Crafts, Perfect for Beginners, Arts and Crafts Colorful and Fun Sewing Projects to Learn the Basic Skills of Sewing (Ages 7+)

text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy This is very cute! Elmo is soft red plush, with big "googly" eyes, a big orange "squeezable" fabric nose, and a bright yellow shirt with a white, plastic-coated star, outlined in blue, with white surround sound waves.

The white star on the shirt shows the spot where you must press a button to "tickle Elmo's tummy" (to activate each sequence) but it is placed just a bit high. To press the center of the button, I have to place my thumb below the star, on the yellow shirt fabric.

My favorite feature is how Elmo's mouth opens and closes while the talking and singing sounds are playing. Incredible engineering and technology went into this toy!

This toy is targeted to ages "2-4 Years." A child has to put one of Elmo's 3 hats on his head for each different play mode. Some 2-year-olds will no doubt have hands large enough to accommodate holding the hats and pushing the plastic tab down into the slot between Elmo's eyes, but some will need assistance.

The toy is packaged in "try me" mode. You can reach through a hole in the front of the box and "tickle Elmo's tummy." When you bring Elmo home, pull the fabric on the bottom to the side, move the switch from "try me" to "on." Then pull the fabric back up and attach with the Velcro strip. Batteries are held firmly in this bottom compartment with a tightly screwed on lid. Requires 4 AA batteries.

4 INTERACTIVE PLAY MODES:

HAT-FREE. I think Elmo is saying, "Hi, hello! Elmo likes to imagine with you, what should we imagine today?" "Place a hat on Elmo's head so we can imagine together." "Let's play together, tickle Elmo's tummy." "Let's play together, squeeze Elmo's nose."
Squeezing Elmo's nose gives different responses, sometimes it's two honks, and sometimes it's a long squeak.

PRINCE ELMO
"Greetings loyal friend, Elmo loves wearing a crown." "Prince Elmo says, bounce Elmo." Elmo has to be "bounced" fairly hard and there is a "boing, boing, boing" sound, followed by, "Squeeze Elmo's nose." After his nose is squeezed, he says, "You did it! Tickle Elmo's tummy." After button on tummy is pushed, he says, "You did it! "Now, first, squeeze Elmo's nose, then bounce Elmo."

If you don't do it right, there's a sound, followed by, "That's not right. First squeeze Elmo's nose, then bounce Elmo."

Elmo asks for three correct actions in a row (squeeze his nose, tickle his tummy, or bounce him). After three correct actions in a row, he'll up the challenge to a two-action sequence.

It's repetitive, with immediate positive or negative feedback.

CAPTAIN COWBOY
"Well howdy partner, hello to Captain Cowboy, yee haa!"
"How many times can you squeeze Elmo's nose?" "Let's bounce together."
Squeeze Elmo's nose and he counts to 20.
Elmo sings a song.

CAPTAIN ELMO
"Squeeze Elmo's tummy to hear a song." Elmo sings a song ("Sailing, sailing over the ocean blue, Captain Elmo loves to listen to all of the sounds, don't you?") and plays a game with sea sounds: a horn, seagull, bell or dolphin. "Squeeze Elmo's tummy when you hear a horn," (or seagull, bell, or dolphin). When Elmo's tummy is squeezed, there is immediate positive feedback: the sound of a xylophone.

This is fun and interactive. Parents can model patience when they show children how to put Elmo's hats on him. Parents can watch their children learn, or play and sing along. Parents can learn about their child's temperament (easy, difficult, slow-to-warm-up) when they see their child's response to Elmo. Some children will be able to play with Elmo by themselves. For some adults, the pitch of his voice and the repetitive sounds could begin to chafe after awhile.

Through 3/31/2015, there is an insert included in the box, advertising, "Elmo the Musical," and a web address for parents and children to watch an episode online.
text_fidelity_b: Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy

ZILINTOYS Orchid Plant Building Set Creative DIY Orchid Building Blocks Home and Office Decoration Birthday Aniversary Gift for Her Women Girlfriends(564PCS) I always wanted an orchid, but I’m not very good with plants. This set allows me to have an orchid *and* build it, which is even better in my eyes. The set includes yellow and pink parts, so you can pick what color the orchid flowers are, and even change the colors if you want.

The set has numbered bags: three #1 bags for the pot, two #2 bags for the flower stems, and one #3 bag for the flower pieces. The instructions say “the numbered bags have no bearing on order of build” but that’s not actually true, as you do use the bags in order.

The pot is nice, it has pearly gold and slate blue pieces. It’s solid, easily supporting the big orchid plant. The plant itself is sturdy, the stems are connected together for extra reinforcement. The pieces stay together reasonably well. There are some loose parts, but not very many for an off-brand set.

The instructions are mostly clear. Some of the colors are hard to see, like the dark green pieces used for the plant stems. For the most part, the instructions point out confusing bits, one step even has an overhead view so you can make sure the pieces are in the right spot. But the very last step has me stumped: adding brown pieces to the pot to mimic dirt. I *think* the pieces just sit in the pot and aren’t snapped to any others, but if so, I don’t like that.

Overall, this is a fun set to build and the finished plant is a nice display piece.
text_fidelity_b: ZILINTOYS Orchid Plant Building Set Creative DIY Orchid Building Blocks Home and Office Decoration Birthday Aniversary Gift for Her Women Girlfriends(564PCS)

Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball Most puzzle balls come with the last five pieces pre-assembled. You have to sort of ease them/roll them into place--putting the last piece in by itself is close to impossible--and it can be quite a pain. Not this one.

This one has tiny holes on the top and bottom for stoppers that allow the puzzle to sit in the stand and turn (the thing spins smoothly, just like any good globe should). For some reason that makes putting the last piece, as a singleton piece, in easily. I just popped it in, with no more difficulty than putting in any other piece. That makes this a top choice for anyone just starting out with puzzle balls. You can assemble by image or by number. The pieces interlock smoothly and easily and hold together substantially better than most puzzle balls. It didn't fall apart a single time as I was working on it, even when adding a piece into a hole that has been built up around substantially. As a puzzle, this is orders of magnitude better than any puzzle ball I have ever assembled. It took just under two hours from start to finish, making it the fastest assembly for me, and I think I picked up a little geography as I went (my worst subject when I was in school).

The detailing on the countries is excellent. The print is clear. This can serve an an excelling globe after the puzzle is done. The stand is very nice too.

Highly, highly, highly recommend, especially for kids.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

Fisher-Price Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Battle at Shipwreck Falls This toy serves up plenty of pirate fun for your little matey. Swashbuckling Jack takes on the evil mummy in an epic battle upon a ship impaled on "Shipwreck Falls". Operated by the included battery, the falls are contained in the large head of a skeleton with eyes that light up while playing funny, fairly melodramatic music and spouting pirate sayings. The two figures affix to pegs at different locations on the ship. Both the crow's nest and the waterfall rotate and there is a trap door. This toy is sure to amuse most youngsters. The figures are cartoonish and neither they nor the skull are frightening. text_fidelity_a:
Harrisville Designs Lap Loom Kit, Hand Weaving for Kids and Adults (Style B) I used to make wall hangings as a child with homemade looms. I recently met someone who weaves huge items and after seeing photos of her work my interest in weaving was renewed. I like the simplicity of these looms but do have some comments. Firstly, the frame is wood with plastic pegs. A screw in each corner holds the frame together but mine is a bit loose. I may need to tighten later. Instruction booklet is well written, read all the way through before starting because there are tips later on in the booklet. Parents please note that every other row you must insert a second flat shed stick into the loom. It's not complicated, just takes time so be aware if your child may not have patience to do this.
My only complaint is I ordered the bigger size B loom and in the photo on Amazon it showed yarn in orange, yellow and reds so I bought a refill yarn kit called Sierra because it was black and red and I thought it would be nice to have both but when my loom arrived I see the size B comes with the black and red yarn and the smaller sized A has the oranges. So now I'll have two black and red items :( I don't know where the photo came from but it should be corrected!
The manufacturers website shows the correct colors but I didn't go there until after I got my loom. I would also recommend spending $10 more to get the Wonderloom. It helps push the yarn down evenly.
This loom is a good size for making place mats.
text_fidelity_b: Harrisville Designs Lap Loom Kit, Hand Weaving for Kids and Adults (Style B)

Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder This version adds difficulty without making it more interesting. In this game, there are both railways and ship routes to build, which means you have to collect cards for each route in the correct color and mode of transportation. Effectively, this game adds twice the number of colors you have to collect to build things. In the original game, you always end up with a bunch of cards in your hand that aren't useful to you because they're not the colors you need to finish your tickets. This game is twice as bad in that regard. Furthermore, there are fewer ship cards, even though you're expected to build more ship routes than train routes. Many of the ship cards are actually worth 2 of that color, which theoretically allows you to collect fewer cards of that color before building, but what actually happens is that you can go through the entire stack of ship cards without getting what you need because the other players are unintentionally hoarding the few cards in the color and type you need.

I didn't hate this game, but I wouldn't play it again.
text_fidelity_b: Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder

Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Easy-Bake Ultimate Oven Baking Star Edition When i was a kid, i had one of these. LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces) This LEGO CITY RACE BOAT TRANSPORTER BUILDING SET ((60254) New 2020, 238 Pieces) is fairly easy to build--the difficulty is what I’d call “normal” for a City-themed set. City sets are among my favorites, because they include fire trucks, police stations, buses, trains, beachgoer minifigs, space stations, and all the rest of the things that a bustling city (or the airspace above it) needs. This particular set is aimed at ages 5 and up.

The set contains all the pieces required to build three separate items: a semi-trailer truck (for towing the race boat), a trailer for hauling the race boat, and a race boat. (You can use the truck’s trailer hitch to tow other things that you build, of course.)

The “Xtreme” graphics are NOT printed on the pieces, but are applied with stickers. (I hate stickers, too.) Applying stickers is made easier if you first stick a corner to something long and thin (e.g., a spudger or a plastic knife) so that you can better control the placement on the element. A good thing about LEGO stickers is that they can be removed and replaced (like Post-Its) if you get them misaligned.

The LEGO elements are compatible with other City sets and with all regular LEGO sets (but not with DUPLO sets, which have extra-large pieces for very young builders). The Race Boat Transporter set is another fine addition to the extensive collection of City sets.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces)

Black+Decker Kids Workbench - Power Tools Workshop - Build Your Own Toy Tool Box – 75 Realistic Toy Tools and Accessories [Amazon Exclusive] I'm disappointed in this workbench. Knowing I would eventually want to get our boy a tool bench, I started shopping for one when he was just when he was a newborn. After carefully reviewing every bench on the market, this seemed like the best one, based on the reviews on several sites.

But here are some of the reasons why I am disappointed:
- The vice (vise) grip no longer opens and closes like in the previous version.
- the nails and screws don't stay up on their own, you put them in the holes and they sink immediately (which completely defeats the purpose of pounding them down with a hammer).
- the batteries are already drained in the saw and drill press, and it hasn't even been out of the box for a month.
- the drill press lights are too bright and flash rapidly... seizure anyone???
- as you'll notice from the other uploaded pictures, the hooks that hang on the tools (like the screw driver, hammer, etc) fall out immediately.
- the storage shelf underneath is incredibly shallow; you really can't store anything of the extra pieces down there. And even the slightest play motion from your toddler will knock everything off of the lower shelf.

So with all that said, it still gets 3 stars because our 24 month old plays with it several times a day.

And another FYI: The last two years, the mega chain store with the bulls-eye logo has put this toy on sale during Black Friday weekend for $40 dollars, so Amazon drops their price too. For $40, it was an ok buy.... but for the $60 dollars it is listed for now (or for the $80 it was listed for in the weeks on Amazon prior to black Friday), I feel like this was completely over-priced. You'd be better off watching craig's list or finding it at a re-sale shop for the equally-as-good used version for around $25-30. In fact, the older used version (where the vice grip is in the front, not on the side) would give you a working vice/vise grip; which I remember playing with a real version in my dad's workshop as a kid and it was a blast!!! (while he supervised of course) :-)
text_fidelity_b: Black+Decker Kids Workbench - Power Tools Workshop - Build Your Own Toy Tool Box – 75 Realistic Toy Tools and Accessories [Amazon Exclusive]

Nature Bound Bug Catcher Toy, Eco-Friendly Bug Vacuum, Catch and Release Indoor/Outdoor Play, Ages 6+ This is such a clever and useful tool.

When I read the description of this product I had an "I should have thought of this first" moment. We live in a drafty, old house and unfortunately we have more than our fair share of spiders, tree beetles, silverfish and centipede freeloaders wandering around. Our son is fascinated with bugs and no matter how many he finds or how creepy the insect, he always wants to save it.

The bug vacuum arrives already assembled with batteries. So right off we were ready to use it. We've had the vacuum for just a few days and we have already liberated a giant furry legged spider that tried to Little Miss Muffet my husband as he was washing dishes. A slightly smaller relative was captured in the shower and a trapezoidal shaped stink bug was on the window in the living room causing our cat to make strange barking distressed noises. Kitty hates insects.

Each captured insect was studied from all angles, the clear plastic reservoir chamber is perfect for this, and then released into the wilds of our overgrown yard. Several insects were ones we were able to identify because we were able to study them. So this vacuum is not only useful it is hella educational.

Even storage is taken care of; the vacuum has a clip on the end perfect for hanging from a wall hook, we keep ours on a hook near the kitchen. I can't believe how ingenious this product is. I wish I'd known about it sooner.
text_fidelity_b: Nature Bound Bug Catcher Toy, Eco-Friendly Bug Vacuum, Catch and Release Indoor/Outdoor Play, Ages 6+

Hurray for nerf for attaching these to the packaging with easy to cut twine, rather than the usual zipties.  The included darts work in all blasters but are easily lost (especially when this blaster shoots them so far) so be sure to pick up extras (I use the Elite dart in all my blasters so I get the 75 pack to replace all the lost ones). BOMENNE Build-on Brick Mug,Funny Novelty Coffee Mug Compatible with Lego,Creative DIY Building Blocks Cup,Birthday Party Cups For Kids,Unique Gifts For Christmas,Black I should have read some of the reviews before wasting money on these mugs.

I have spent the last 90 minutes trying to decorate this mug. The parts sent with the mug do not attach; you can place them but they immediately fall off. Those parts fit to one another very well, but they decline to play nicely (or at all) with their mug.

I tried LEGO pieces and they do not want to be pressed onto the mug. I really cannot blame them.

The only block pieces that do fit onto the mug are ones I had purchased from Dollar Tree. They meld easily with the mug and hold beautifully. Unfortunately, the only surface that will accept them is the front of the mug. As you can see from the pictures they are holding well, but the rest of the mug surfaces are...well, I am trying so hard not to be all negative and everything, but the mug is so poorly designed and sloppily made that nohting will attach at all, not LEGO, not the mug company's blocks and not even the pieces of white bread that I smushed together and tried to mold to the pegs and holes. It stuck whilst still moist and them fell off when it dried and I picked up the mug to check.

We are a totally dedicated LEGO family. We have even indoctrinated...coerced...um...lovingly brought my son-in-law into the LEGO Love. We give and share those precious bricks at every gifting opportunity. There have been times when my grandchildren are out playing with their friends and my daughter and I are still inside playing. I recently learned that the one set she would love to have is the Friend's Heartlake Hotel, but by that time it was already hovering around $400.00. I am thinking that I will make provisions in my will for her to have one.

Sadly, I bought two of these. Double the heartbreak. Do not buy this unless you are planning to do what I intend to do with them. I have a tiny ton of old costume jewelry that I use for crafting and I am going to use Gorilla Glue to cover the mug with some cool bits and bobs of jewelry. That will be a totally huge and groovy improvement to the really quite pathetic red C that is now on the mug. I am an old granny and am surprised how disappointed I am with this mug.

Please protect your loved ones and buy something else. You can buy some nice real LEGO packs for the $26.00 I wasted on this crap, or a very large amount of blocks and accessories of the blocks sold at Dollar Tree. Tell them I sent you.

Love,
Granny
text_fidelity_b: BOMENNE Build-on Brick Mug,Funny Novelty Coffee Mug Compatible with Lego,Creative DIY Building Blocks Cup,Birthday Party Cups For Kids,Unique Gifts For Christmas,Black

The erasable highlighters are especially cool and something I haven't seen before. The washable gel pens are nice, comfortable grip, vibrant ink and quick drying so great for left handers. The permanent markers and dry-erase markers offer good performance but nothing really special or noteworthy about them. I do like the felt tip pens, they offer performance similar to the conte felt tip pens with a more comfortable shape.

The only thing I don't like about this set is the silly names applied to the colors. I get that it is supposed to be cute but does the black color really need to be called 'little black dress' and 'twilight sky' instead of blue. I totally get why crayola does this for their crayons where there are hundreds of colors with similar shades that need unique names.. but it makes no sense to apply silly names to basic black and blue colors, and especially to use several different names for the same color (ie the black shade is 'little black dress' for dry-erase markers but the black permanent marker is 'always onyx').

My 6 year old daughter was reading the dry-erase marker and was quite confused why it said 'little black dress' when it is a marker and not a dress.. I didn't feel like going into a long explanation about what a 'little black dress' is so I just told her its because the people who made these markers are silly.

SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories We had so much fun with this. While we did not do the whole party element with people watching us unbox, we had a great time just on a normal day when the kids had done a great job, having a special treat of opening up each of the flaps to see what was inside.

A glow-in-the-dark boo, another boo, both with movable arms, a skeleton for around the plant and a dry bones were the highlights for us in this set. The Princess peach, also was detailed to an extent I have never seen on any of our other Princess peach figures. Usually they just fill in and under her skirt with solid plastic, and this one they gave her legs, undershorts, and high-heeled shoes underneath her dress so it is much more of a realistic figure than usual. I think either Mario or Luigi, needed a little plastic stand to be able to stand up and not just topple over. I would've appreciated a little more design on those guys so that they could be played with without an additional little clear plastic stand.

The flap opening and unveiling of the characters was a lot of fun. The characters were almost impossible in some cases to get out of the container without completely destroying the entire packaging, so my kids had to be flexible to wait until we were done opening all the flaps, then tear open the packaging to be able to push from the back and get some of those characters out. However, they were definitely firmly and securely packaged in there and were not going anywhere or getting damaged with those vacuum formed spots to sit.

Overall this was a lot of fun, and with the excellent quality of the figures, made for a very special and memorable gifting event to the kids.
text_fidelity_b: SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win Amazon was temporarily out of stock so I grabbed this from another source. We are an avid Hot Wheels family and always like to check out the newer sets. I love the idea of running a car around a course continuously, without relying on batteries. This set comes with a big launcher, that features a unique track with protruding tabs that catch the cars from behind as you blast them around the track. The whole idea is to catch the car(s) at the right time when it reenters the launcher, so you can have it racing around the course non-stop. Unfortunately, the course is too small and uninteresting, yet, if the layout was much larger, that launcher wouldn't have enough force without some kind of midway helper (like an automatic loop launcher). This would make a world of a difference in fun, so you you're not pounding the launcher every half second to keep the car circulating around a tiny oval which gets old fast.

Big annoyance: The launcher is very tall, so it comes in packed in two pieces which easily lock together, however, once locked, you're unable to seperate them. This is now the second set we have with this annoying problem. We like storing our hot wheels in their boxes, but once opened, there's no way to get this giant launcher back inside. Even if storing out of the box, with other toys, it's a big jalopy that could have been dismantled, taking up less space.

And finally, kids need laser-sharp hand/eye coordination to catch the car on time, so this may frustrate the impatient type. When you do manage to catch the car to keep it going, it does feel rewarding, even if it's only 2 laps. We haven't tried more than one car at a time, but I imagine on a large course, it must be fun, but on this small circuit, it's probably near impossible to work with.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win

Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game The only bad thing about this game is the fact that my 2 year thinks it's a radio. We've had it for about a month now, and as I write this, it's "playing" in the background. It's playing in the background almost every night, if not during the day, too. It's super annoying! :P It's supposed to sound like ducks, I guess, but it's just lots of squeaking.

Otherwise, it's super cute, and my boys love playing it. I think 2-4 year old children will enjoy it the most, but it's labeled 3 and up. I imagine this is due to the stickers that must go on the ducks, and game board(which is a motorized pond). You do need batteries! There are 4 colors of stickers, 4 each. 3 of each will go on ducks and 1 on the game board. I wasn't paying attention enough to realize one of each color went on the game board. I ended up having to peel some stickers off of ducks.

You put the ducks on the game board, assign a color to each child(up to 4 players), and then press the center button. The ducks will then circle around the pond. Taking turns the child picks up a duck and turns it over. If it matches their assigned color, they keep it. If not, they put it back on the pond. While all the ducks are on the pond, it's a little crowded, so it was tough for my 2 year old to get the duck placed back on there without knocking over another duck, or several. It's easier to turn the pond off while your child is looking at the color and placing it back on the pond.

Overall, this is a fun game to teach a few colors, along with the art of taking turns and patience. My children had so much fun with it, they were impatient for their turn.

VELIYAKA Flowers Building Blocks Set, 12 Kits Mini Bonsai Tree Building Toys , Simulation Succulent Flower Building Bricks for Home Decoration,Kids Girls Women Birthday Gifts This is a set of 12 little succulents. The description says 12 and 6, but really, you get 12 sets.

THE GOOD:
🌵 The sets are individually packaged, with their own directions, pieces, and coffee cup container. The box has a picture of the set inside, so if you wanted, you could give a set as a gift. Or if there’s a certain succulent you want to build, you can easily find it.

🌵 The box identifies the succulent. I like knowing the name of what I’m building!

🌵 The sets are quick builds. It took me about 75 minutes to do all 12.

🌵 The instructions are simple, there are a few confusing steps but since these are plants, I was okay with them not being perfect.

🌵 The finished succulents do make cool display pieces, and are a perfect size for desks, bookshelves, or even windowsills. They are small: about 2 inches at the widest point and 5 inches for the tallest.

THE BAD:
🌵 The pieces don’t stay together very well. Some do and some do not. I had several construction accidents while building because some pieces clicked and some did not. Some pieces are very loose, one of the succulents (February, Plum Blossom) fell apart while I was building another.

🌵 I was unable to build one of the succulents because the thing would just not stay together. That was the December set, Antirrhinum majus. The main body of the plant is two pieces that will not snap together.

🌵 My sunflower is missing a petal because the necessary piece was malformed.

🌵 The coffee cup lids are a cute idea, but they did not stay connected to the cups. The lids are intended as the base for each cup, but no matter how hard I tried, the cups popped right off the lids. Fortunately, the cups are stable without needing to sit on the lids.

Overall, while this box of 12 succulents is a good value, I was somewhat disappointed that the succulents didn’t always stay together. A finished set shouldn’t fall apart while it’s sitting on the table because the pieces are loose.

Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up This MOONLITE STORYBOOK PROJECTOR (Special Edition Disney Gift Pack, for Ages 1 and Up) is a flawed concept. The projector is difficult to position over the flashlight on my Galaxy S10 phone, unless I turn the phone over and look through the lens at the light. This burns an image into my retina, and is clearly not good for my eyes!

The projector clips onto the phone, and exerts moderate pressure on the screen. I don’t like this, because I worry about cracking the screen.

The projector works with the free “Moonlite” app (available from the App Store or Google Play). You will have to register for an account to use the app. After that, you must activate each set of story reels by entering an activation code--the code is on a small card packed in the box. You tap the “unlock” icon at the top left of the app, and enter the code.

Once you’ve activated the story reel set, you click on the story you want. The app will then display a story for you to read to your child. As you read each page, you advance the reel in the Moonlite projector, to get a new illustration for each page of the story.

The projector shows a focused illustration (focus is adjustable), as long as you are no more than a yard or so away from the surface you are projecting to. You cannot project the picture across a room, or for any great distance, because the phone’s flashlight isn’t bright enough to project for long distances.

The photos that accompany the stories in the Disney set are boring, as are the stories. Kids will no doubt love the Disney characters in the pictures (e.g., Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy), but the story illustrations are repetitious. Also the detail in the illustrations gets lost because the projected images are fairly small.
text_fidelity_b: Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up

Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink Let’s just say. . . I’m not “squealing with laughter” as it shows on the listing in several places.

First of all. . . This is NOT a pretty pig. It’s kind of “odd” because the color is different in the pictures (the picture of the girl holding it makes it look white with a little tan and black splotches. . . which it is not). The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.

The Resistance I picked up The Resistance to play at family gatherings where mafia and werewolf didn't go over so well. People didn't like getting eliminated and didn't like someone needing to moderate/narrate the game. The resistance is best played with more people. The more the merrier definitely is true here. Some people will play as the resistance and some as spies. The spies are trying to sabotage the missions while the resistance is trying to complete the missions. The game has a mission leader who will pick which players are going to go on the mission. The game then opens discussion to all players to decide if that is the best choice of players for the mission.

Overall, We enjoyed the game, but when playing with only 5 players, it's a bit too easy and people don't really get into the discussion. When playing with 8-10 players, the game is a lot more fun as people really get into the accusations and deciding who should go on the different missions. Since people aren't eliminated like mafia and werewolf, people tend to enjoy this game more.
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance

I am tired of hearing the "What time is it?" song. You think hearing the cartoon is bad, wait until they can bring the song to life on command. Oy!

The kids like the toy. It is very closed ended. They don't use their imaginations much. But the kids laugh and have some fun. If your kid just loves Bubble Guppies, and you love electronic toys- go right ahead.

Grandma- let me give you some advice. Your daughter-in-law will love you if you buy quiet plush Bubble Guppies instead. She'll love you even more if you spring for a nice set of blocks. Unless this toy was specifically asked for, avoid it!
