text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Friends Roller Disco Arcade Set 41708, Toy Bowling Game, Andrea Mini-Doll Included, Birthday Present Idea for Kids, Girls and Boys 7+, Fun Playset for Creative Play I’m actually old enough to remember disco night at the roller skating rink, so the Lego Friends Roller Disco Arcade set was a fun trip into nostalgia for me. The set is packed with cute details, bright colors, and play features. It might be the best Friends set I’ve ever built.

The disco arcade has 3 areas: the roller disco, the bowling lane (6 pins), and the arcade. The different areas are connected with hinges, so the set opens and closes. When it’s closed, the translucent green windows let you see inside the arcade. When it’s open, you can utilize all the different play areas without being cramped.

I really like how the building is designed to open and close! It looks cool either way. And if I compare this to a set that has an open back to access the play features, the roller rink just looks more complete.

I don’t love all the stickers, but for once I’m not going to ding the set. It would be impossible to print so many tiles. I do recommend adults help with sticker application, but the rest of the set is easily doable by a kid (6+). The instructions are clear as always with Lego. Pieces are separated into numbered bags to help with assembly (less time searching for the needed piece for a step) and to cut down slightly on mess while building.

Overall, I was really impressed by this set. It’s fun to build, fun to play with, and fun to have on display.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Friends Roller Disco Arcade Set 41708, Toy Bowling Game, Andrea Mini-Doll Included, Birthday Present Idea for Kids, Girls and Boys 7+, Fun Playset for Creative Play

Buffalo Games - Vintage America - 2000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:70993f24c2cce65d6b7aea10ebd6a5fc]] This is an awesome puzzle! It was so much fun to put together. It's actually pretty easy for a 2000 piece puzzle, because of all of the different colors and patterns. I'm not saying it's super easy, because any 2000 piece puzzle is an intense challenge. But, it has lots of clear detail, and with most of the pieces, you're able to get a pretty good idea of where it actually goes by looking at the picture. That makes a puzzle fun and not frustrating. The hardest part to do was actually the "America" part, because it had a lot of solid red. But overall, all of the parts of the puzzle went at a pretty good pace.

They include a poster print out with an enlarged full picture of the puzzle, which I really like, especially because the box picture has some of the picture obscured. They fully exclude Hawaii and Alaska, so you might get a little upset if you're from either of those fine states. But, aesthetically I think it was a good choice.

The pieces are medium sized and above medium quality. It's a good solid puzzle, probably about Ravensburger quality, which is mid-range for puzzles.

text_fidelity_a:
Kiddieland Lights 'N' Sounds Space Blaster,Multi Perfect item for toddlers who are stuck in that quirky place.. between infant toys not peaking or holding their interest yet, toddler toys are a bit cognitively too hard!! At 18mo. This is the perfect size being its lower profile.. for a little to play without your help! They can climb on/off and scoot a few feet.. if they tumble or bump off, no worry of injury with adult supervision and used on carpet.

Ours is entertained by anything he can load and unload on his own.. Ohh, and pushable buttons seem just too much for him!! This space blaster delivers in spades.. he’ll mount up scoot a few ft. all just to get up and meticulously load in items around the house into the seat! Then, repeat the process stop- and time to unload his haul! Before each scoot.. he moves through a button sequence with the gadgets provided on the dash… he even removes spaceman and puts into the seat- filling up the “under the hood” as well.. This $38 item has provided us our longest entertainment yet at this awkward stage.

Downside components noticed: this does not have a mute button!!! If turned on you get both lights ans sounds- Would love ability without sound when using dash controls- as the sounds get daunting!! I recommend indoor use only and although this can in theory function outdoors.. I find it’s not made for outside elements! Concrete rips up plastic tires fast and any water sprinkler, rain, etc will bring it to an early demise..!! (If used outdoors place on grass + bring inside after use!)

A quirky toy for that awkward phase and one I’d recommend.. it’s not the element of riding that entertains- but, rather what can be done while maneuvering!! Hoping this info can help your decision- stay safe.
text_fidelity_b: Kiddieland Lights 'N' Sounds Space Blaster,Multi

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players Ok hear me out for a minute before I explain why I didn't give it a better rating. My wife and I love The Office. We consider ourselves huge fans-- buuut maybe not quite to the point of super fans because we can be forgetful on certain things about the show occasionally. But we are those people that, if you tell us a story, we'll likely have an Office reference to match it. So we were excited about getting to try this out.

This is where I might be a little too picky about it…well, I'm just going to say a little passionate about it lol. But if it's a classic game with a different theme (such as this one)-- it's usually directed toward people who are big fans of that specific theme...that likely will be expecting certain details. Otherwise, if they aren't fans, or real into that theme, they will probably just get the classic/original version...or go for a different theme that they are fans of. So if you're leaving big parts out, you're likely going to have some disappointed fans.

I also realize that there's so much great things about the show and so I'm sure it's hard to narrow it all down to a select amount of cards. So I give some credit to that.

My reasons for rating it lower:

Nearly all of the cards are of Michael, Dwight, Jim and Pam. Then there's randomly one of Kelly and the special rule/twist card with Kevin....but no one else is part of the game?! And yes, the ones included are amazing actors/characters and all...but many of the other regulars are, too- and all together they made The Office.

There are cards for numbers 0-9 (they each have the different colors) and 6 action cards. So that's 16 different pictures they could utilize. Which means there are enough to feature the regular characters…I'll list/count out the ones that come to my mind 1-Michael, 2-Dwight, 3-Jim, 4-Pam, 5-Angela, 6.Kevin, 7-Oscar, 8-Creed, 9-Meredith, 10-Stanley, 11-Phyllis, 12-Kelly, 13-Ryan, 14-Toby, 15-Darryl.

I also felt like some of the photos could have been better selected. I won't rant on too much about that, and spare you, but a quick example-- Kevin's chili twist card isn't of that actual scene just him at his desk. And why not put Toby as the draw 4 card, instead 😄

I do like the picture of the back-side of the cards, the wild card with Michael dancing in the Diwali episode and *some* of the other pics they chose.

The card and photo quality is really good. My box container was torn a little at the top.

It is still fun to play, I do like the special rule/twist for Kevin's chili, and like the idea of The Office theme but I do think it could be improved upon by including more characters.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit Holy Crap Yes! We are a family of Lego Maniacs and this set is wonderful. I have a fifteen year old and we recently got the newest Millenium Falcon and I had a realization that his abilities were quite beyond that set, and most sets out there, so I started looking at the expert and Technic sets. This set was perfect, it is a step up in challenge and scope from the standard sets. It was great to watch him to tear into the bags and deliberately build. Not only was it a little more challenging, but the scope if far more impressive. The set itself is huge, and the architectural elements are involved although somewhat repetitive.

We worked on this over several days and we are quite happy with the results. The build is detailed and has some very interesting pieces. Especially nice are the clock faces that are beautiful. The back printing on the clear disk gives them a gem like quality, they are sharp clean and wonderfully graphic. Absolutely beautiful. Also impressive are the scores of micro figures (usually found in Lego games.) Long term, I'm not sure that we will ever need this many tan microfigures on any build, but interesting piece. Also nice are the literally hundreds of architectural detail pieces from the little teeth pieces to the spires.

We actually looked up photos of Big Ben and we are astounded at the details. It is a wonderful representation of the end of the building. If I had anything negative to say about the build it would be that it is a bit of a façade for that end of Westminster. Which is forgivable given all the detail and how many pieces (and space) it would take to make the whole building.

All in all, this was an incredible build. I'll try to get the time lapse up when I can get it edited.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

TitanShield Solid Gold Polyhedral Dungeons and Dragons D&D Metal 7-Dice Set These are really beautiful and well packaged. They come in a small, foam-lined tin. The tin is slightly larger than a standard deck of playing cards, but it fits easily into a pocket. These really are the most beautiful dice I have ever seen and photos really do not do them justice.

The dice are slightly smaller than my other standard sized, acrylic polyhedral dice sets. They roll well, but I'm sticking to a dice box or tower to avoid denting surfaces. I think the dice themselves can likely withstand denting, as they are solid metal.

These would be great for a wealthy and/or greedy character. The only real downside is that though most of the dice have a smooth edge, the 4-sided dice is awfully sharp. This could do some damage if squeezed too tightly, carried unprotected in a pocket or stepped upon. So, use some caution.

These are really pretty and would make a nice gift for any table top gamer in your life or for yourself.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it informative and helpful.

The barn opens into two separate unattached halves that slide together at right angles like a puzzle. There are latches on either short side of the barn that can be unlatched to display each half. The barn can be left open or closed. When closed it is easy to carry. A cow, chicken, donkey, lamb, hay bale, basket, red and green vegetables, and a pitch fork and broom are the accessories included. The barn doors on the long side of the barn open in both front and back. The color is vibrant and the farm animals are very realistic.

The only negative I found is that the entire barn is held together with clips that come apart. The clips are not its strongest point. The four clips on either side of the barn roof on mine would not hold up the roof and the boards keep falling off. I tried for over 30 minutes to get two of the clips seated correctly but neither side would snap in place. My boyfriend also looked at this barn and he could not get the clips to seat firmly in place either. He did say, however, that this is a well-made toy. According to the side of the box below the Germany label, it says this is made in Slovakia.

The clips and vegetable pieces that come with the barn can present a choking hazard to a small child. If the child is of that age where items are frequently "tasted," then I recommend adult supervision while the child is playing with this barn. The box indicates that this is not for children under 3 years of age and does state that the small parts present a choking hazard. This is typical of many toys with small parts, however.

Other than this, I got this for my friend's son to play with and he's going to love it. However, he'll have to play with the two roof slats off since they will fall off in its current condition. If the unit I received did not have this problem, I would have rated this 5 stars. Since mine does have this problem, I'm rating it 3. Had I purchased this unit and not received it for review, I would have returned it for a replacement. Since the three other reviewers have not complained about this issue, I suspect it is either a new issue introduced in recent manufacturing design or the unit I received is slightly defective. If there are no other recent reviews that complain about the clips and barn roof, then I would consider this a 5-star toy where I was the one exception. Nevertheless, this defect will not detract from my friend's son enjoyment as young children rarely notice those things.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

-$10 for 20 cards is a little steep
-no pronunciation guides
-no usable vocabulary (phrases are better than words. We don't speak in individual words)

This is a cool novelty gift that is also educational, but it is not really helpful in learning a language unless you already know the letters, where applicable, and the pronunciation. It is not useful, for example, if you are traveling or trying to have even the most basic conversation.

As for the pronunciation, some might say "but in what language do you explain the pronunciation, since there is no specific target language or assumed language for the learner?" The answer is to use the International Phonetic Alphabet, which is a standardized system of pronunciation.

Cool toy, if I had to categorize it!

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set We have almost the entire Thomas and friends Fisher-Price wood set of the new type of connectors, and we do not have any of the old style tracks from any brands. Overall the new tracks stay together very well and are easy to put together, but in all honesty my three-year-old sometimes has to bring these new style wood tracks to me to get them apart, which she never has to do with the tiny set of traditional tracks that grandma has at her house. What is nice is that you can attach the tracks from either direction, since both sides connect identically.

We have the busy island set, the farm set, cranky at the docks, the train station, and the huge Tidwell sheds station. All of these sets fit together beautifully and provide a lot of different play options for the kids. However, the main complaint I have had is that most of these sets have not come with enough tracks. Even the huge sets, come with just enough tracks to barely get it together if you are very careful and mindful with how you put things together.

The main advantage of a set like this animal park one, is that you get a whole lot of tracks and every piece in it can be used to connect all of the big and exciting things in those huge sets. My daughter also really loved the simplicity of this set, that she doesn't really have to think too hard about how it goes together, she can just wind and turn and connect things up without too much planning ahead.

text_fidelity_a: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on My toddler is really into Mickey right now so I just had to get him this trike. It’s adorable and super well made. I really appreciate the design of this trike since it’s made to grow with your child. It starts out with safety straps, bars that lock in as a secondary way to keep your child in the seat and a handle so you can push and steer. There’s a switch on the front wheel that you slide so it will move without the pedals. Once your child gets big enough to ride alone, move the switch back and the front wheel is controlled by the pedals. The handle is removable as are the safety bars and canopy. I always love finding toys that will get a lot of use since there are so many things that are really only made for short time periods or specific developmental stages then they’re quickly outgrown. This is a wonderful toy and I’m looking forward to helping my son learn to ride it as he grows.

text_fidelity_a:
Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+ I have very mixed feelings about this game. First, it is REALLY FUN, and my kids and I were laughing really hard playing it. The drone taking off is really a lot of fun and cool to see, and even our little 3 year old who is too young to play was enamored by it and shrieking when it would lift off with little playing pieces inside! Really a lot of fun.
That being said, there are 3 caveats to be aware of:
1)I don't feel comfortable letting the kids play this alone. The drone comes crashing down sometimes and I want an adult or kid old enough to be able to catch it to avoid hurting anyone / furniture, or crashing so hard it cracks the plastic (a part of the drone siding already popped out, but I was able to push it back into place).

2) I feel like this game won't last very long. The pieces are VERY easily lost, as they end up being flung around the room as you play. Also, the drone lifting off bumps into the ceiling easily (thankfully we have cathedral ceilings in our living and had to move the game over to there, otherwise it would hit and come crashing down fast). It's only a matter of time before the plastic breaks or pieces get lost forever.

3) I dove to catch it on the way down after a particular round, and it hurt my finger. Nothing major, didn't hurt more than stubbing your toe on furniture or stepping on a lego- it has a safety to shut the propeller if it detects something in the way, but I was still surprised. I was fine, but one of my kids would have been crying if it happened to them.

My daughter actually suggested we try playing it outside next time, which might solve some of the issues- can't do damage to the house and everyone can duck for cover until it crashes into the grass. Wind might make it less fun though. HOWEVER- this was a TON OF FUN TO PLAY, so even with all those caveats, and even considering it might not last more than a few months in my household, I'd still consider it worth playing even for those few times. The look on their faces when the drone takes off is PRICELESS, and worth it even if you only get to play it once.
text_fidelity_b: Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+

text_fidelity_a: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+ The toy is well-designed and promises many hours of creative play for my fire-fighter enthusiast grandson. It was easy to put together, with excellent instructions. The construction seems sturdy. I didn't give it five stars because of several factors. I deducted one star for poor paint quality. There were scratches in the paint finish, and the worst were on the header with "Fire Station" painted on it, just where it will be the most visible. The paint seems very thin, and flaked areas look like they'll easily spread with use. In many places, the paint came off when I peeled the part-number stickers off. I deducted the second star because the accessories were not as advertised in the listing or the video. Missing were the doghouse; one of the basketball standards (two were shown; only one was included); the bathroom sink; and one firefighter (two were included; the description promises three). The firefighter's helmet makes it nearly impossible for him to fit through the holes to slide down the pole. The Dalmatian dog pictured was replaced by a brown dog, with a dog bed that he does not fit into, instead of the doghouse. The TV/bookcase console was replaced by a freestanding TV on a pole that is very unrealistic looking. The included accessories match the parts-list in the instruction booklet, so I know the omissions were not accidental.

The included instructions give steps for a small house, a castle, an igloo, a windmill, a family home, and a lighthouse. You can build all of these at the same time, without having to deconstruct anything.

This set reminded me of when I was a kid, taking out my bucket of Legos and just building whatever came to mind, instead of following the instructions to a specific set.

This set includes a good assortment of colors and pieces, and hopefully the different building techniques and different house styles will inspire kids to try out their own house, or whatever else they want to build. That’s the aim of the Lego Classic line, to inspire kids to make their own creations, and I think the pieces here are good for that.

It could make a good gift for the beginning Lego builder, especially if you’re unsure of what theme they might prefer, or be a good complement to other Lego Classic sets.

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.
text_fidelity_b: Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover

Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

Pass the Stache Board Game This is definitely not a cerebral or strategizing game. It is pure reaction, action, and laughter. We played a number of rounds as a way to break the ice between to families of children who had not met yet, and it was perfect. The rules are as simple as you can get, flip a card up, if it matches the color or shape of your mustache, hit it with your suction cupped mustache and claim the card. It you suction cup up one that doesn't match, you pay a two card penalty and he who ends with the most cards wins. Ok there are a couple more rules, but that is the gyst. There are also an all smash card and a none smash cards. But seriously, that is the rules right there.

The mustaches themselves are great. They are a blast in themselves as our kids giggled continually at the look of the mustaches touch to everyone's upper lip. They are made strong with decent suction cups below them. It is fairly easy to strike a card and pull it up with the suction cup. And the cards are well made to take the abuse.

As for game play, the rounds are short and exciting. Some feelings got hurt, but for the most part it was an uproarious game which put smiles on everyone's face. Scoring is easy...just count up the cards you won. Personally, I don't think this will be a classic game, but it willl be pulled out in our house many times.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

LEGO Star Wars Episode VIII Resistance Transport Pod 75176 Building Kit (294 Piece) There are some LEGO kits that really shine, and this LEGO STAR WARS RESISTANCE TRANSPORT POD BUILDING KIT (75176; 294 Pieces) is one of them. It’s an interesting build, with some elements attached underneath (studs not on top), many added to the sides, and several specialized parts (e.g., canopy, bolt launchers). The finished build is solid, and provides a toy that’s fun to play with (even for adults).

The pod has room inside for all three minifigs (Rose, Finn, BB8). The pod canopy, rear compartment roof, and side storage compartment door lift off and go back on easily. The cockpit has holders for Finn’s and Rose’s weapons. The storage compartment has extra weapons.

The pod has a side turret gun that swivels for aiming when you turn the big knob at the back. The turret gun has a trigger that launches single rounds. The pod shoots long red bolts (rounded tips, not pointed) from underneath the cockpit. (Two special-to-the-kit bricks have springs inside that work as launchers). The pod feels good in your hand.

The kit takes two hours or less to build; it uses some Technic connectors in addition to standard bricks and plates. The instructions are crystal clear. There are quite a few stickers to add to the bricks, but the graphics are nice when all the stickers are in place.

This is a great small LEGO kit, one that I’ll be keeping for display and play.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Episode VIII Resistance Transport Pod 75176 Building Kit (294 Piece)

So for my 70th birthday, pizza and a game were an obvious choice. Two of my sisters, a nephew, and I played Lost Galaxy for the first time and except for the fact that the birthday boy came in third place we had a great time doing it.

The instructions say you don't need any instructions, just download the app and get started. We did that and the first round of three was a bit of a mess. We had to stop the app frequently, going back and forth, checking the help tab and so on trying to understand what we were doing. That didn't take too long though. By the second round people were catching on nicely and the game started getting competitive as folks began developing some strategy. By the third round, the game play was positively cutthroat, with one sibling loudly announcing "No more Ms Nice Sister!" The poor birthday boy - me - lost several turns due to enemy action and to cosmic upheavals, which every one else greatly enjoyed. I greatly enjoyed all the moaning and groaning I got to do. 🙂

The age range at the table was 13, 54, 60, and 70 with everyone unanimously agreeing that this was a great game that would immediately join our stash of family games. It was a sweet way to celebrate turning 70 and Lost Galaxy will always be a part of my memories of that night.

His last Halloween costume was Dr. Alan Grant, if that tells you anything. It's all we hear from his mouth 95% of the time. His mind lives in the world of the movies. It was his pleasure to try out these toys and then tell me his favorite things about them.

He likes how this vehicle is remote controlled, but it's a little hard to control in our driveway. It won't move on the grass. It does work well on the trampoline and hardwood floor, though. That's true of most remote control vehicles, but some have done better in our driveway than others. You'll need 6 AA batteries(total) to go in the vehicle and the remote. They're not included. Figurines can fit inside the vehicle, but none are included with this one. The doors don't open, but they'll fit through the top. (My son wanted me to mention that the Owen figurine that comes with the Jurassic World Gyrosphere vehicle won't fit inside this one. He also discovered that another of his Jurassic World figurines can hold onto the outside of the vehicle and ride that way.)

He's very much enjoyed playing with this vehicle, even if it's not very fast.
text_fidelity_b: Jurassic World Toys Textron Tiger RC Vehicle

LEGO City Service Station 60257 Pretend Play Toy, Building Sets for Kids, New 2020 (354 Pieces) This LEGO CITY SERVICE STATION 60257 BUILDING SET (New 2020; 354 Pieces) is intended for kids aged 5 years and up, so it’s simple to build. Of course, that means there isn’t a lot of fine detail in the vehicles and buildings, despite the high piece count. Many of the 354 pieces are small ones, like single round studs for headlights, or a puppy figure, or a hot dog.

Still, this is a rather cool service station, because it includes a charging station for an electric SUV, in addition to gas pumps for a more traditional van. The set includes a mini-convenience store/pay station. The van opens up to show a spacious interior. Both vehicles can accommodate a minifig in the driver’s seat. There are 4 minifigs, including a station attendant.

I love all of the City sets, because they illustrate the ordinary jobs, workers, buildings, and vehicles that make up modern cities. The City sets are easy to build, their standard LEGO elements are interchangeable with other LEGO sets (not just the City sets), and they’re relatively inexpensive.

Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+ All of the fossils were in a single spot, and it took only a second to find them. I soaked the block in water, as I didn't want to take hours to dig them out, and after a little bit, I was able to pull the fossils out of the block with ease. I got this kit specifically for the trilobite, as I have always wanted one and didn't have one yet. So imagine my dismay when my new trilobite is crumbling to pieces in front of me. It couldn't have been damaged by my not digging correctly, as I didn't even dig at all.

I looked it over and I was upset to find spots that had been glued together. That tells me they knew it was coming apart when they included it. I guess they thought it was going to go to a kid who would just assume they broke it by being careless and would just throw it out and not care, but I personally don't like that they included a piece that was crumbling. There are other reviews that have the same problem with their trilobite crumbling and there are also others with pictures of the same.

The other fossils are all fine, and if you don't care at all about the trilobite, then I guess this kit is still ok to get. But I can't bring myself to recommend it to anyone because they knowingly included a broken and glued back together fossil.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+

text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32"

text_fidelity_a:
Dimension - A 3D Fast-Paced Puzzle Game from Kosmos | Up to 4 Players, for Fans of Strategy, Quick-Thinking & Logic | Parents' Choice Silver Honor & Oppenheim Toy Portfolio Platinum Award Winner Though it can at times feel a bit simple, overall Dimension is a fun game that plays quickly and makes for fast, easy to learn family fun.

Packaging and materials: everything in its place, easily held in place, all in good shape, no excessive packaging, easy to open and easy to store back in the box. The balls have a good sense of heft to them, stack easily in their spots, and are well-made. Our son dropped a good number of them the first few times playing and after the first few, our nervousness about the balls breaking or chipping disappeared (though we still wished he’d control their rolls a bit better . . . ) Cards are also well-made, as our the playing boards--heavy stock that come with stick-on feet to hold them slightly off the table surface so the balls don’t move around too easily. All in all, construction is a plus.

Directions: For the most part, directions are quite clear and are pretty minimal. The directions also offer up a few variant forms of the game for making things easier or more challenging, though to be honest, anyone could have come up with those pretty easily and quickly (for instance, upping the number of challenges one has to meet)

Game play.
You each take some point markers to start, and place your 15 spheres--five trios of different colors-- in your game board (again, the balls rest solidly in their holes).

The center of the game board is where you will build patterns with the balls depending on the card challenges. There are seven spaces in the building area, and you can build upward from those spaces, employing up to three layers and up to 11 spheres (7 in your bottom layer, three in the middle layer, and one on top).

You lay out six cards, each one detailing a particular challenge you must meet when you build your patterns. Some examples:
Two specific colors must touch (i.e. somewhere in your pattern, a blue sphere must contact a white sphere
Two specific colors must not touch
You must use a specific number of a particular color
One color must outnumber another (i.e. you must have more green spheres than white spheres)
Two colors must total a specific number (i.e. between blue and white spheres, you must total 4: 1 blue and 3 white, 2 and 2, 1 white and 3 blue)
A particular color cannot be laid atop any of the other colors
A particular color cannot have any of the other colors put on top of it (i.e. your green spheres must be the topmost layer)

once the cards are laid out, you turn over a one-minute timer and try and create a 3-dimensional pattern/pyramid that will meet as many of the challenges as possible.

You get one point for each challenge you meet and lose two points for each one you miss. There is a bonus for meeting all six and/or using all the colors. You also get more points the more spheres you use, though you’ll have to weigh quickly whether adding more spheres to get more points might break a rule and thus lose more than you gain (for instance, adding another blue sphere would get you a point, but if in doing so you broke a rule by having it touch a green sphere, you would lose two points).

As you can see, sometimes the rules may conflict (you might, for instance, get a card that says blue and white must touch and another that says blue and white cannot touch). In those cases, each player decides for him/herself which challenge they choose to ignore.

An entire game is six rounds and most points wins.

It goes very quickly and as you might guess, the speed and difficulty of each round is determined by the combination of cards. Sometimes all three of us were done well before the timer, other times we were all caught with spheres still in our hands trying to figure out where to add or remove a color. And sometimes you’d smoothly and confidently total up your six points for meeting all the challenges and other times as you were oh so cockily adding another challenge to your list you’d suddenly realize, “Doh--how did I end up with a green touching a blue?!”

Mostly the game moves along quickly and the combinations are decently challenging, though we all thought we’d probably move on to doing 8 challenges soon to up the difficulty even more. The only other point I’d make is an electronic timer would be nice as you’re all concentrating so hard on your pyramid that we’d often miss the time running out, or you’d just pluck off a ball to replace with another when someone noticed it was done and you were stuck. We’ve therefore actually taken to using one of our iPhones as a timer to give us a 10-second beep before the full time runs out.

The other nice thing about the game is it is pretty easily modified for playing to younger levels--dump the timer, drop a color, uses only three or four cards. The game can grow with your kids. Certainly even 5-8 year olds can play simpler versions and then grow into more difficult challenges. Fun to play, a bit different, uses some different skills. Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Dimension - A 3D Fast-Paced Puzzle Game from Kosmos | Up to 4 Players, for Fans of Strategy, Quick-Thinking & Logic | Parents' Choice Silver Honor & Oppenheim Toy Portfolio Platinum Award Winner

dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks The theme for my five-year old's birthday party was Lego Batman. Therefore, I needed a bunch of Lego bricks to make decorations, but I did not want to pay an expensive Lego price and I also just needed basic bricks and colors. Enter the Dreambuilder Toy Building Bricks with 1000 bricks! Not only did I get exactly what I wanted, but I also got a superior toy. I was able to "build" all the decorations I needed (a napkin and silverware holder) with lots of bricks to spare, but when the party was over, I gave my son all the bricks and he was none the wiser that these were not "real" Legos. Some of the older boys at the party inspected the decorations and were able to come to a conclusion that these were in fact not real Legos, but that does not matter because they function exactly like real Legos.

Within the bag you get basic bricks in various sizes, 1x1, 2x2, 2x6, 2x8, etc. There is also one small, green building plate. The set also comes with various bricks for roofs, doors, fences, and windows. The colors are Roy G. Biv with black, white, and grey added. There are equal amounts of each color. We do have a real Lego 1000 piece "creative" bucket and here are the differences. There is no idea booklet with this. However, I do believe you can check their website for building ideas. Therefore, if free form building is not for your child like it is for mine, then this set is not for you. There is no brick separator, and the really flat bricks that drove us adults insane when we were kids are back to haunt to us. You will need to purchase one separately unlike the Lego creative sets. The Lego creative sets have more unique bricks, which take away from having more basic bricks to build bigger and better things as you would with this set. Dreambuilder bricks do not come with a storage bucket. You will receive a plastic bag with all of the bricks contained within that bag. So, you will need your own storage box.

Overall, I find the Dreambuilder bricks to be vastly superior to Lego if you are into simple, old school, free building without instructions. I will be purchasing additional sets.
text_fidelity_b: dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks

Don't eat my cookies. Blam! Don't make fun of my shoes. Blam! I'm a girl, you don't get to snicker about my lip balm collection. Blam!

I'd say the age guideline is just about right, I don't think I'd give this to anyone under eight, if only for my own sanity.

Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue) I love the old console games and I looked to this handheld to revisit some of the older games I remember enjoying several years ago. For the price this is a decent little console and I like it, though there is some room for improvement.

In the past, playing the older games required downloading a ROM and putting it into an emulator, and if you knew where to look for ROMs you could find hundreds of them, many familiar and even more that were very unfamiliar. I expected this little console to be something silimar to the old emulator, preloaded with old ROMs, and it seems to be fairly close to that. There are many games I recognize that are a lot fo fun to revisit, and there are a lot of games that are unfamiliar.

This console comes preloaded with several hundred games of varying types and quality. As mentioned there are quite a few that are familiar, but many that I never saw in an arcade. Some appear to be Asian releases that never were released here.

Navigation is a minor pain. If you want to play a game that is far down the list, you have to navigate there every time. There doesn't appear to be any memory for last games played.

Another minor disappointment is that several titles are listed more than once in the menu. This suggests to me that there are different versions, even if I can't tell what the differences are.

I'm thinking this is the same thing as the old emulators that can be found online and it just packaged in a handheld and preloaded with ROMs. That's fine by me, I like those old games. It would have been nice to provide better navigation, though, and maybe reduce the versions of each game to the latest or most bug-free? For the cost, it's a worthwhile system if you love those old games.
text_fidelity_b: Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue)

Predators Top Trumps Card Game This card game is played in the United Kingdom. It isn't difficult to play. This is how you play:
2-6 Players
30 Predator cards including the Great White Shark, the Lion, Leopard and the American Alligator
Learn about the world's most dangerous Predators from the Great White Shark to the Lion
Simple to play - difficult to master!
1. Shuffle and deal the cards face down.
2. Players pick up their cards and look at their top cards only.
3. Player 1 (left of dealer) chooses and calls out their best stat (e.g. 'Speed - 20').
4. The other players see if they can beat this stat (Highest number wins).
5. The card with the highest stat wins all of the top cards and adds them to the base of their pile.
6. The winner of the round chooses the stat for the next round.
7. The first player to get all of the cards wins!
The game is recommended for ages 6 an up. Each card gives information about the predator. The company makes a number of card decks for different subjects.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.

Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+) Luvabella is quite an incredible doll, as the more your child plays with her, the more she learns and does. At first glance, she's quite plain, hard- not cuddly soft and has huge eyes with real eyelashes. The minute you put her 4 "C" batteries in (Doll does not come with batteries, you have to buy them), she comes to life with the cutest expressions, movements and baby babble speech. And incredibly, she speaks either English or French. (Coming from Canada, it's only natural- but of course she's made in China.)

Luvabella has a cute dress and hairbow, bottle, spoon, pacifier and lamb toy. When you give her the baby bottle, she easily goes to sleep, especially if you sing to her. When you feed her with the spoon, she chews and if you didn't feed her enough, she'll let you know. When she cries and gets fussy, waving her arms, her pacifier soothes her. Her lamb toy makes her make babble and animal sounds and the more she plays with the lamb, the more she learns more animal sounds and more animal names.

As the child plays with Luvabella, she does more and more. Touch her chest and hear her heart beat. Touch her feet, and she talks and calls you Mama. The baby babble will grow into words and eventually phrases. She even kisses her little Lamby toy and makes cute animal sounds. When you tickle her, she giggles and waves her arms. She plays peek-a-boo and laughs while you play with her, and eventually you'll hear her say "I see you". To have a conversation, hold her feet while speaking, she will answer back first in babble, then in words, then in phrases. As you speak and play with her, you never know what she'll do- either smile, cry, giggle or laugh. She constantly changes her responses and learns more vocabulary, and if your child gets tired of English, you can also hear her in French. This is a doll that gets cuter as she comes to life and keeps learning more, and your child will find her a wonderful challenge that never gets boring! A big 5 Stars for 2017.
text_fidelity_b: Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+)

LEGO Jurassic World Jurassic Park: T. rex Rampage 75936 Building Kit (3120 Pieces) At first glance, the Lego Jurassic World T. Rex Rampage is an impressive set. It’s geared towards older builders (16+), but I would say anyone could handle it.

The set has a lot of bags and 2 thick instruction books. The first book builds the T. Rex, the second book builds the Jurassic Park gate/scenes. There’s also a sticker sheet, which I was quite disappointed to see. In a set this pricey, Lego really should have printed a Jurassic Park tile. The sticker is the main focal point on the front of the gate, so if it’s not applied perfectly, it just doesn’t look great. Lego printed a similar size tile for an Ideas set, so I don’t think it’s too crazy to suggest they should have done it for Jurassic Park!

I also wish Lego had considered how the set would be displayed. Yes, you can play with this set, but I am sure most older builders like me are building it to show it off. I personally think the scene vignettes on the *back* of the gate are cooler than the front of the gate. At least they did think of the buildable stand for the minifigs, that’s a nice touch.

By the way, the minifigures are amazing. Great detail and major thumbs up on them.

The T. Rex was my favorite part of building the set. I knew how big he was going to be since measurements are included, but knowing versus seeing are two different things. Many of his joints are ball and socket, so he can be posed in a variety of ways. But at the same time, due to the weight of his various parts, he doesn’t always stay in those poses. For example, his head often falls forward. Small parts like his toe claws fall off easily, so watch if he’s played with. I had his head and tail come off multiple times when I was trying to pose him for display. He’s delicate.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Jurassic World Jurassic Park: T. rex Rampage 75936 Building Kit (3120 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a toy made with greenness in mind. It is manufactured with recycled materials and is great for environmentally- conscious parents who wants their kids to have some creative fun while also minimizing environmental impact. Designed for children between the ages of three and six, it is one of the few building toys that doesn't involve blocks or other interlocking rectangular pieces.

This toy involves building arrangements of flowers on a green, branch like base and there is no end to the different number of creative arrangements that kids can make. The pieces consist of leaves and three different flowers and they can be stacked and arranged in any number of ways. The combinations are endless and every time my girls play, it turns into a new adventure. My girls love creative toys, flowers, and art, so a toy like this is very likeable and enjoyable to them.

I like that this toy is made using recycled materials and I like the small, cube- shaped box included for storage. Most manufacturers do not even think about including a small storage box, and this often forces parents to use plastic bags or plastic containers to store the pieces. With an included box, there is no need to reach for these environmentally- unfriendly storage receptacles that may one day wind up in a landfill. Instead, you just use the included box, which is also made from recycled material, and the pieces will be safe to use for the next adventure.

With its lack of batteries, green composition, and creative encouragement, this toy is certainly a nice change from most others, but does it have any possible flaws or potential issues? I can think of only a few. One is the small pieces. They can easily become misplaced, so parents need to watch closely to make sure that kids place all of the pieces back into the box. Of course, the nice fact here is that you can afford to lose a few because, since they are all interchangeable, it won't prevent the toy from being used again and again. Another issue is that this toy could become boring after a while. There are those youngsters who crave action, lights, and sounds in their toys and if yours is one of them, then they may grow tired of the toy in a short time.

Recycling is certainly a good idea and creative toys that require imagination and not so much of the lights and sounds so common with kids' toys today are definitely a nice change of pace. Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a very nice little toy from Green Toys and it makes a great choice for these reasons. The possible building combinations are endless and while some kids may tire of it in a short time, it still has enough positive qualities and creative entertainment value to make it worth a purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games

Pantasy Saint Seiya Building Kit, Sagittarius Aiolos Action Figure Level Building Sets for Adults, Creative Art Collectible Model for Home or Office, Soul of Gold - Saint Cloth Myth EX Building Blocks Pantasy makes amazing building sets, with pieces that usually stay together and super clear instructions. There are some untranslated dialogue boxes here and there, but the diagrams are so clear that I was never confused.

This set of Saint Seiya is something of a mix between a figure and a building set. The base is a traditional building set, and then Saint Seiya is a somewhat poseable figure. The neck, shoulders, knees, ankles, and wings have ball and socket joints for articulation. The elbows have gears that limit movement somewhat. The hips can move forward and backward only. The hands have small ball and socket connectors, but they don’t always hold the positions I set.

I usually really like sets from Pantasy, but this one fell a little short for me in the figure itself. It keeps breaking when I try to put it on the stand, or if I try to pose it too much. This is a set you build and then put on display, somewhere it won’t be bumped. I’ve tried several times to get the feet attached to the base, but end up relying on the clear support on the back of the base, which has a rod to attach to a hole on the figure’s back.

I’ve had the wings fall off, the hands fall off, armor pieces fall off, you name it, it’s fallen off. One of the wings has a loose connection and continually falls off. I have built several sets from Pantasy, none with this problem.

I think the armor is actually fantastic, all metallic gold pieces that match in color. Many of the bigger pieces are wrapped in extra plastic to prevent scratches. The bow and arrow are nestled in foam in a separate box; the packaging is impressive, on par with a UCS set.

There are two face options, and an extra hand if you don’t want to use the bow. There are some great building techniques like SNOT, and as I said, the instructions are very clear. This is an 18+ set, but I think anyone could handle it.
text_fidelity_b: Pantasy Saint Seiya Building Kit, Sagittarius Aiolos Action Figure Level Building Sets for Adults, Creative Art Collectible Model for Home or Office, Soul of Gold - Saint Cloth Myth EX Building Blocks

Polly Pocket Playset, Travel Toy with 2 Micro Dolls, Toy Boat & Surprise Accessories, Pocket World Owlnite Campsite Compact This is a really cute little doll set with very tiny dolls and accessories. You definitely would not want to give this toy to a child under the age of three due to a choking hazard. However, for an older child who loves tiny things, they will really enjoy this set.

On the downside, which perhaps is not surprising given the miniscule size of the pieces in this set, and that everything is made of plastic, the carrying case is rather fragile. It is difficult for a coordinated adult, let alone a small child who is not yet very coordinated, to store all the pieces safely inside the carrying case and avoid breaking the catch on the case. There's definitely also going to be a risk that within a short period of time the child you give this toy to will scatter and lose many of the pieces in this toy set.

There is also a potential choking hazard for pets, particularly small cats and dogs, if they try to chew on or eat the tiny parts in this toy set.

Monster High Monster Maker In my opinion, kids are born these days innately knowing how to handle technology with their little hands. We first used the [[ASIN:B00IVFCD0Q Monster High Monster Maker]] with an eight year old who guided me through each step. I had already downloaded the software for using on my computer, had installed the included AA batteries, and connected the printer cable. His approach was very different than mine because he wanted to print his design on all the legs, then the arms, then the heads. I wanted to do each of the three dolls as a single being. By inserting the pens which actually can be used to draw freehand, the design is drawn directly onto the doll parts and if you don't like the outcome or grow tired of it, they are erasable. My only complaint about this kit is that two wig caps are included and a single rooted wig whereas the rooted wigs are far superior. The shoes are pretty cute and the dresses are very simple. When I have time, I'll put together some more of the little dresses with fabric scraps.

Keeping all the small parts together is well contained with this set and the [[ASIN:B00LOR4Z3Q Monster High Monster Maker Primary Extension Pack]] is an affordable addition. Because the ink is fairly light when applied to the dolls, there has not been residual color remaining after we've used the eraser to clean them up for refreshed designs. This is a very smart "toy" that is capable of entertaining small groups of children as well as a single designer. By having more dolls on hand, it's a great tool for a birthday party, especially when each child can leave with a doll of their own that they have designed.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Monster Maker

I think I have every Grandpa Becks game, starting with Cover Your Assets and this and Cover Your Assets is one of my favorite games to play. Birds and Bees is a pretty quick game to learn and you can play a complete game in twenty to thirty minutes.

I think it's fun to match the colors and patterns . I'm slightly color blind - ok- a lot color blind, and my family loves to tease me as I have a hard time telling the difference between the red and purple colors on the cards. So it's become a standing joke, if I put a card down that is red or purple the family makes sure I'm not "cheating". I just laugh, Darn when my color doesn't work!

The other great thing about this card game is that anyone can play it. We have a family member that has autism and he is actually really good at this game, has figured out the strategy, what cards to get rid of immediately, aka the Bear and the flowers and he regularly beats us. I highly recommend this game. A lot of fun for your family.

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game If the classic game of Monopoly seemed to take too long, then you will appreciate this newer, shorter version. Instead of B&O Railroad, it is updated with businesses and brands like Spotify, ebay, Intel, Xbox, McDonalds and Coke. Instead of zipping around the board with an iron or a dog, you have a choice of a gold token like a coke bottle, game control, French fries, and motorcycle among others.

You choose your token, roll the dice and start buying brands, add brands to your tower, and buy and trade and take over brands with empire cards. First to the top of the tower wins. The game board reminds me of Times Square in appearance a bit.

Contents include: 4 towers for up to four players, 6 tokens, 30 billboard tiles, 6 office tiles, 14 chance cards, 14 empire cards, money pack, 2 dice and the game guide. I like this shorter, express version. I used to call the classic version Monotony, partially because my brother always beat me at it because I virtuously would save all of my $$$ and he would spend his buying up all of the real estate in the first half of the game. In the second half, I would just go around the board and pay him rent for hours on end until I ran out of $$$. Not a good strategy on my part.

I think this new version will be a hit for families who want a quick, fun game for family game night. It has current, relevant brands which is fun. And not all of the brands are about material consumption: there's ebay which is great for selling and recycling, and spotify which is about listening to good music for free - although they may charge a nominal price down the road.

While it involves luck more than strategy, some of my favorite games as a child involved luck: Chutes and Ladders, Candyland, Parcheesi etc. This is just a fun, light game for families to enjoy. When my son comes home for the weekend - he was a board game designer and now video game designer - will get his opinion and let you know what he thinks.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma Just like I had thought before actually receiving this, you are probably thinking that this is a hefty pricetag for a doll that doesn't even have the American Girl logo attached to it... well, move over Pleasant Company (yeah, I said it), because Adora is a new generation of dolls that are not only kid approved (my girls, ages ranging from 6-10, all love their Adora dolls) but it is also parent/caregiver/teacher approved (I would know, as I'm technically all 3, haha). My girls love this doll because she's so cuddly and lifelike, and I love her because I have spent some time actually researching the Adora company... and let me just say THANK YOU for finally coming out with a line of dolls that are crafted from SAFE and nontoxic materials! No more feeling that tiny pang of worry ("mom guilt" lol) whenever my daughter is snuggled up with her doll. I love the peace of mind that comes from knowing the dolls arms, legs, and face are made of vinyl and are BPA free. Finally, a toy company with ethics!

Many of Adoras dolls are machine washable (this particular one has electronics and therefore is not, so care must be taken when wiping the vinyl parts and perhaps spraying a safe vinegar solution on the dolls plush core to keep clean and fresh). Honestly, I can't really comment on the electronic aspect of this doll, as I turned off that feature pretty early (i think it encourages better open-ended imaginative play that way... not to mention less annoying for cranky mommies lol). So you'll have to check other reviews for better details on that function.

All in all, yes, this is not a cheap doll. But in my humble opinion, you are getting a lot of value for your money with this doll. The brand has less expensive plush options too that are just as adorable, less expensive, and even machine washable (we have one and I'll be doing a review soon). The Adora line has a wide selection of dolls and accessories too by the way. I'm actually excited to buy some accessories because I feel like they are very competitively priced and plus it feels good to support such an ethical company that brings so much joy to children.

Grandparents, this is a gift that will not only make you the favorite grandparent, but will also please even the pickiest of health-conscious daughter-in-laws lol.

Two thumbs up for Adora!!
text_fidelity_b: Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma

B. Toys by Battat Marble Run Toy Set – 62 Piece Educational Building Toy with Lights & Sound – STEM Learning Toy Marble Track for Kids 3 Years + This version of the classic marble run is just ok. The pieces are interesting, especially the light up one, and they are made of nice, sturdy plastic. But there are a few issues that make this toy frustrating for my kids to play with.

The biggest problem is that the pieces do not have consistent tolerances for the connecting portions. Sometimes they snap together easily while other times it takes a lot of force. My 2 and 4 year olds cannot do this without help. They always end up knocking the sections over when trying to put the pieces together. This hasn’t been the issue when they played with another brands’ marble run.

Another issue is that there are not enough base pieces compared to the number of “action” pieces (like the ramps, slides, etc). This results in having to build tall, unstable designs that are easily knocked over, which makes the first problem even worse.

Also, the piece that shoots the marbles up is difficult for my fairly coordinated 4 year old to use. It requires a quick tap that is firm but not too hard. It would be nice if it was easier to use. Both of my kids like the idea of this piece, but I end up having to do it for them. And I can’t always get this piece to shoot the marble properly every time.

Last, it would have been nice to have a couple of example layouts included in the instructions. This is not too big of a deal, but the pieces are difficult to connect and take apart, so for my kids’ sake, knowing some layouts that use the different sections properly would be nice.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat Marble Run Toy Set – 62 Piece Educational Building Toy with Lights & Sound – STEM Learning Toy Marble Track for Kids 3 Years +

Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game

But, they ended up sticking pretty well. I guess you don't want them to stick so well that a 3-year-old can't pull them off. In my video, I show how they stick to a piece of metal, and they also stuck to my fridge, and all other metallic surfaces.

The construction of the pieces was good. The box was just okay. I had a hard time pealing all of the stickers off the box, which I needed to do to open the box. Also, once I took all of the magnets out, it took a long time to cram them back in so that the box would re-close. Forget having a toddler do this on their own, but if you lose about four pieces, then you should be able to easily fit the remaining pieces. But, I'd recommend throwing the box away, and finding your own box.

They have the numbers 1-20, with the corresponding number of things on the piece. For example, piece number 17 has seventeen butterflies.

Pros:
+Really sticks to a fridge or other surface
+Has the numbers 1-20, with a corresponding illustration
+Teaches new words like clownfish, cardinal, construction worker, flamingo
+The pieces are good quality

Cons:
-The pictures with larger numbers have too many things that are too small for a young child to easily count
-In order for a toddler to clean these up, you'll need to find a replacement box
-The magnets aren't super strong
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Numbers Wooden Magnets 20 Piece MagnaFun Set

text_fidelity_a:
Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange This is a simple "flick-and-write" game with good production values, a questionable rulebook, simple and fast gameplay, and a box that is just ridiculously large for what it is.

Gameplay is fast and straightforward, involving a Crokinole style mechanism for shooting your disc into a recessed game board with a central hole in the middle. This board has a plastic shelf with corner sections for "shooting" pieces, and they'll fall into a central area divided into four main sections. My central board easily comes loose from the shelving piece, and needs to be adjusted prior to gameplay almost all the time. Once you shoot, you'll be making marks onto your player board with the included markers, which are of average quality for a game like this. The boards are easily erasable - a major plus to the production aspect of the game.

The rules are not that hard, but they are explained in a way that makes learning the game quite a bit more difficult than it needs to be. Few examples are covered, and there will be a number of times that you run into situations where you aren't sure how to interpret the rule as written. Once you get it though, play is not too hard, and Sonora is something you can play with the kids after you've worked out the kinks. And they'll want to play this - it's colorful, with kid-friendly artwork, and the gameplay looks like a kid's game, but has enough meat to interest an adult for at least a little while. I don't know that I'd play this game too often, but it is certainly different and a good family game that will keep kids interested. You can play a few games back to back, as they'll run 20 minutes or so once you know the general flow of the game. For a family game night, this will be a good alternative to a more traditional strategy or roll-and-move board game.

The biggest downfall of this one is that the box is so large. As a gamer with a large collection, it's disappointing to see a 12x12 "Ticket to Ride" sized box for a game that could have opted for a foldable game board and fit into a very small game box. They would have lost nothing in doing this, and in fact, they might have fixed the issue I have with the main board. Even if they must have a one-piece board, dropping the molded plastic insert that holds a handful of discs and pens could have reduced the size by a few inches in depth. In reality, there's not much here in the box, and the components can be entirely stored in the recessed game board area alone. That would be about 3/4" in depth, not 3".

All in all, it's OK.
text_fidelity_b: Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange

Snap Circuits Classic SC-300 Electronics Exploration Kit | Over 300 Projects | Full Color Manual Parts | STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8+ 2.3 x 13.6 x 19.3 inches I got this kit for my 10 year old. We had been experimenting with kit electric motors, magnets and radios and everything ended up mixed in a box that he liked to play with, so there was interest in this type of toy.

The parts of this kit snap together on a clear plastic grid. The instruction book is a black and white center stapled pamphlet that can be challenging to decipher for builds that are more complex. My son liked building the simple circuit that included the motor with the fan. Many of the advanced plans are very similar.

The kit seems durable but not indestructable. My kids can be pretty rough on things so they have been using this kit with my supervision.

For most kids under 10, this is not the type of toy that they can play with on their own. I have my son use this toy at the dining room table. We check to make sure that all of the parts get back in their place when we are done.

This is an educational toy. My experience is that early exposure to learning experiences like this can shape interests later on in life.

I would have liked to have seen a description of what the various modules do to the electricity to make the magic happen.

If you have any specific questions please leave a comment and I'll try to get back to you as soon as I can.

Be aware that the dividers holding all of the different markers in separate containers is not actually attached to the bottom in any way, so your order will almost certainly arrive with the markers disorganized, as mine did. However, a bit of tape and a jellybean bounty to the children soon put that right.

The line is a good clean line and the tips seem resistant to fraying when mushed a little too hard by small hands. The color saturation is very rich and worked well on the notebooks that we keep for coloring.

The highlight of this set is that the markers are advertised as not drying out when exposed to the air when children leave the lids off. If you have small children, you'll know that "put the cap on it" is a constant and tiresome refrain, so for families or teachers, this is a huge and thoughtful benefit. While I didn't test keeping the lids off for 90 days, a couple of overnights assured me that for more normal, temporary times of the lids being off, the markers are not prone to drying out.

Overall this is a fantastic set for teachers or homeschoolers who go through more than the usual amount of art supplies. It would also be great for a party where coloring a themed item is part of the event.

text_fidelity_a: Pokemon Trainer Guess: Hoenn Edition Electronic Game My 21 year old son is still a Pokemon fan. I thought he might enjoy this. He played a round or two, but then grew bored with it. It's a lot like the 20-Q game where you answer a series of yes and no questions then it guess what you're thinking. Most of the time when she played it, it guessed the correct answer. Since my daughter doesn't know a lot about the Pokemon subject, she found that she wasn't able to keep going after a while. We then shared this with my 8 year old nephew. text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster The recon has always been a pretty good blaster.  Somewhat prone to jamming, and on the short side for range, but accurate as all get out, and good for modding.  Then enter the Retaliator!  This is not your typical Recon with a face lift!  The shell is still recon- but with a new name badge and the digital camo effect.  The GUTS are all new- direct plunger powerhouse.  This blaster will pop the elite darts out to 75 feet (angled shots) and will put darts out to 50 feet level shot.  The accuracy is still there too!  It will take the old Streamlines too(with a noticable loss of range and accuracy)  This blaster will jam- but if your careful to pull the cocking slide back fully (not just till it clicks, but fully back, usually a couple mm beyond the point of the trigger latch engagment) jams are minimal (we actully shot 50 or so shots without a jam!).  I'm not a huge fan of barrel and stock attachments, but these are pretty good on this blaster.  The barrel does reduce range (about 8 to 10 foot lose), but does increase accuracy (we use cardboard standups aprox 2" wide by 4" high and can hit them 8 out of 10 time without the barrel and 9 out of 10 with- at 25 feet).  The new 12 shot clip (mag) is very cool and makes a nice transition between the 6 shot (way to small) and the 18 (nice capacity- but kinda gets in the way).  My daughter uses this blaster to sniper me all the time.  All she needs to see is a foot or a hand sticking out from behind the couch and I'm toast!  All in all a worthy upgrade to the recon.  Great for a primary or secondary carry.  I did take 1 star off because nerf still hasn't made this jam proof- close, but not perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice
