text_fidelity_a:
UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid This horse is striking in appearance. It looks wild and spirited. It is quite a conversation piece on its looks alone. I would give it five stars alone for that. Movement is not as spectacular, but it does move. There’s a winding key and start/stop control levers. The horse is not able to take more than 5 steps without halting or simply falling over. It looks like the last motions of a horse before succumbing to the effects of a trank dart. The kit is a real bear to assemble. The instructions must be heeded. You may find you have to flip ahead a few pages at times to see just what this subassembly is that you are working on and where it is supposed to go. I knew at the start that I would need to sand the pieces and use the provided wax. Ther's not a whole lot of wax. It’s a 1 inch slice of a candle but the important thing is that it enough for the horse. The wax is somewhat soft, like beeswax. I had no problem with missing pieces. There are six boards with laser cut parts. If you don't see anything missing, you have all the parts. Assembly is a bit tedious and somewhat painful. As the model continues to take shape and become more horse-like there is the adrenalin surge all model builders feel when they are nearing the end. Once assembly is completed the key is wound and switch is moved. My model just sat there. C’mon little horsy, let’s go. Well, back-winding the key overcomes the initial friction and horse begins to haltingly show movement. Lots of going back and forth with the key helps to distribute the wax and the horse becomes more limber. After lots of massaging like this you can get the horse to take 4 or maybe 5 steps. Max is 9 and only rarely achieved. It will usually fall over to announce it is finished walking. Well and good. It is still a cool model and I would build one again. I’m giving it 5 stars but 4 would be reasonable too. I wish it walked a bit better and that the instructions had a bit of expository text. This is a worthwhile model that will occupy 8 hours of your life in assembly. It is ingenious.

I have a few hints on this horse:
Mine locked up once while fully wound up. I could not get it to operate at all. I tried moving the legs and rapping the body with my knuckles. Nothing! My horse was dead. It was not until I grasped the horses neck and moved it forward and back that the gears unlocked. This only happened once, but it was super frustrating as I was contemplating opening up the entire model to fix it.

Understand at the outset that this horse can’t walk for long. If you watch the clever videos the horse appears to leave its stall and seems to be on a journey to a pasture or whatever. If you look closely the horse only takes a few steps in each scene. Clever editing makes it look like the horse can go on a pastoral journey. Not really complaining because all the ad copy and literature says the horse can’t go far. This is only a problem if your expectations are too high and unrealistic. It is what it is, a model of mechanical horse. So enjoy that as I do I.

My rubber band broke. I suppose it had a nick in it that grew over time. I was able to cut out the broken piece and retie the rubber band but it is not easy working in the body of the assembled model. So do examine the length of the rubber band before assembly.

Update on the rubber band issue 5 days later:
The rubber band broke again. No, I haven’t over wound it. I’ll have to see if I can get a replacement from somewhere.

The rubber bands for the horse’s mane and tail are genius. Looks great and the bands lie perfectly when cut. I was worried I’d need hair styling skills to make the horse look good. It was no problem.

Seriously, sand everything. Knock down the edges of the large pieces as well so they lose their painful sharpness. If you have to reach into the interior of the model later you will be glad you did.

Some parts are seeming impossible to press together with human hands. I finally resorted to a small furniture clamp with soft jaws to supplement my finger strength. I think pliers or small c-clamp would work, as well.

A cushiony work surface was helpful in supporting a board while I was breaking a part loose from the board. I used towel I use for assembly projects.

It really takes 8 uninterrupted hours to assemble this model no matter how skilled you think you are. If you leave out trying to be extra careful and the extra sanding I guess you could do it in about five.

On page 13 of the instructions I was confused. The diagram seems to suggest that the rubber band should be folded upon itself in thirds. After puzzling on this I covinced myself that doubling the band was correct and it turned out to be right choice.

Check for proper operation of parts during assembly. In some steps you are "told" to operate the key and check that the parts move freely. This is very important. Once the horse is fully assembled getting back inside it is a difficult task since gear timing must be maintained.

There is a down side to using the wax. Your hands will get a coating of wax and when that is transferred to the horse there will be discolored spots. Try to keep the wax from where you don't want the wood to darken. I washed my hands frequently and still ended up with a horse that is more pinto than wood white.

There are no troubleshooting hints in the instructions. If you can't find help on the website you are on your own. I do have a vibe from Ugears that they are helpful and I think you can correspond with them and get help if you have a bad problem.
text_fidelity_b: UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid

text_fidelity_a:
B. toys – Water Doodler Portable Drawing Board – Kids Painting Writing Doodle Board Toy – Perfect Travel Toys for Toddlers Non-Toxic – Color Doodle Drawing Game & Magic Water Pens The main thing that this toy reminds me of is invisible ink, though in reverse. Invisible ink made with lemon juice (see recipe below) starts out invisible, and can be made to "magically" appear. It's the opposite with this toy. When a child draws on this board, the drawing is initially visible, but it starts to fade within seconds, and it is completely gone within half a minute. Most children like to be able to see what they have drawn, as a complete drawing. Experiencing one's drawing disappear before one can even fully finish it is an exercise in sobbing futility for most young children.

Another comparison I'd make, and not to the favor of this toy, is that it is a poorly conceived remake of the classic toy, the [[ASIN:B00000J0HG Etch A Sketch]], which is a much better choice for no-mess drawing because, with that toy, the child's drawing does not go away until the child shakes the Etch A Sketch.

In my humble opinion, this toy is more geared toward caregivers than children because of its low mess-making potential. The pens don't leak, though it wouldn't matter if they did, because they are filled with water. It is also easy to tidy up this toy because it comes in a sturdy storage case with convenient handles.

Unfortunately, this is supposed to be a toy for children. Though it is certainly possible that some children will like this toy, I believe that many more will be frustrated. For that reason, I can't recommend it.

For those who are interested in an old-fashioned, inexpensive game of disappearing ink where children are less frustrated because they can make it reappear, here is a recipe:

1. Squeeze 1 tbsp. or so of lemon juice (either bottled juice, or juice of half a lemon) into a bowl and thin it with 1 tsp. of water.
2. Dip a Q-tip into the lemon juice mixture and use it to write a message onto a sheet of white paper.
3. Wait for the juice to dry completely, and watch it become invisible.
4. Show your secret message to a friend by heating the paper (safely!) by holding it close to an incandescent lightbulb. (Do NOT hold it near an open flame!)
text_fidelity_b: B. toys – Water Doodler Portable Drawing Board – Kids Painting Writing Doodle Board Toy – Perfect Travel Toys for Toddlers Non-Toxic – Color Doodle Drawing Game & Magic Water Pens

Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs) We like the Lego brand, but sometimes we need a lot of bricks without paying an exorbitant amount of money. The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.

LEGO Speed Champions Formula E Panasonic Jaguar Racing Gen2 car and Jaguar I-PACE eTROPHY 76898 Building Kit (564 Pieces),Multicolor,Standard I really like these new redesigned speed champions models that are 8 studs wide. The previous generation was 6 studs wide and while that worked great for a few car shapes, many of the models just looked weird in my opinion because the length was out of proportion to the width.

With the new wider chassis design there is a lot more room for the designers to keep the proportions more realistic and also add lots more detail to the models. My only complaint is that they are still using the same size wheel/tire molds from the previous generation which means the wheels are now out of proportion to the larger chassis.. It doesn't look too bad though and I still think its a big improvement over the previous generation. Hopefully next year they will come out with new molds for the wheel area to make them even better.

This set offers a fun build with a lot of neat pieces and advanced building techniques.. and the price per piece of only 6.2 cents for a licensed set is pretty great! Its pretty rare to find larger sets significantly under 10cents per piece, so this one offers a pretty good value compared to most others even at full MSRP. Definitely recommended for any LEGO fan.

It was a little disappointing to see what was in the box because with the mirror on the front, we expected to find goodies other than the cards and paper frame. I like smaller boxes for smaller products to reduce disappointment and save storage space. Anyway, since we'd decided that we would go the route of using a smartphone for selfies instead of relying on our aging memories to retain a live animated face inside a frame, I pulled out an old one and connected it to wifi so we could share the images later if we wanted to. We didn't but at least we had the option. After we were warmed up, we decided that I would be the judge right away because it's my game and my home and I was supplying the refreshments. While playing, we agreed that some of the cards could be eliminate, that we could replace them with some of our own captions. We acknowledged that this game is reminiscent of other games which we've played, but we had a lot of fun with this one nonetheless because we had photos.

I think this would be a much appreciated game by teens who are in the getting to know you stage and would love to be a fly on the wall watching them play. Since the judge decides which card wins, anything goes when hormones are stirring.

text_fidelity_a:
HUBSAN X4 H107C HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter Red/White (PH-H107C) At first I received the SD version instead of the HD version from one seller on Amazon. I returned it.The Little One's Choice got it right and sent me the HD version for which I had paid. Make sure you get what you paid for. It should say "HD Camera" in big letters on the Hubsan box. Unfortunately, the correct one they sent had horrible very dark lines in the video in all types of lighting conditions. I had to return it. The replacement was fine.

My "review" is going to be a bit rambling from an experienced guy to those who are tying to get started in this hobby. My hope is that I might have something to say that the old-timers might find useful as well.

My short review in this paragraph is that this quad is awesome (overused word, I know, but it fits here) for the price and simply amazing. I've had hours of fun with mine and I own 2 other non-camera Hubsans, one Proto-X and a Blade Quad Nano. This Hubsan quad is the most bang for the buck. I've also got big copters that are gathering dust while I have fun with these small ones. Strangely, I'm not missing them. Did I mention these little things are fun?

It is refreshing to the point of joyfulness to be able to fly this quad around since it is so relatively inexpensive and nimble. I bought several bags of props out of an abundance of caution and have not used one yet. Still, I don't crash much, so if you are new at this, you might need more propellers than the one set provided. I bought some spare batteries (they are blue, sold in a set of 5) and a couple of the Traxxas 2-port chargers. These work fine and let you have more charged batteries handy.

I want to say this quad is easy to fly. For me it is very easy, but it is also fun. I understand that for those who have never flown any type of RC rotor craft that you will have to be serious about learning to use and fly this little thing properly.

Don't be frustrated if you crash a lot at first. Fly in an open area outdoors if possible. If you fly indoors, which I know is a very attractive prospect at first, you will crash into walls and ceiling often and perhaps lose some propellers. At first you may even forget which hand "does what" and crash pretty hard. The body of this quad is tough, but I have seen some photos of broken ones. All of those slammed hard onto concrete walls or slabs.

If a crash is imminent, learn to cut the power immediately. Throttle off completely. You do not want the motors stalling against an obstruction. They will burn out if you abuse them that way. Also, never try to bump the throttle to kick the motors on in an attempt to flip the copter upright if it sets down at an angle. Motivate your body to the quad, pick it up and set it down straight. It will last longer that way.

The rotor guard is taped to the bottom of the tray. Use it if you are unsure of your skills. By the way, when removing the props to put this on, do be sure to hold down the motor body. If it comes up too far the motor wires will snap off. It is only held in place with friction. Use a pinching grasp to pull the prop off. There's a little wrench to help with pulling the props. Use that if one came with your quad. Some people don't get one, I don't know why.

This same type of grasp is also the correct way to disconnect the battery. If you pull by the wires, you will soon have a broken connection. Try to grasp both sides of the connector with your thumbs while you squeeze to persuade the connector away from its mate. Try to make contact with as much connector, not wire, as possible.

There are many videos on YouTube which are instructive for newbies. Especially helpful even for an experienced guy like me was one video that showed how to restore a stuck motor to working condition with a pair of pliers. Especially learn how to reset the gyros with the transmitter and how to zero-out the transmitter itself. Read the instructions carefully and you'll see that you can adjust the sensitivity of the transmitter relative to control input. Learn and understand how to use the trim buttons. There is a lot of info in that little manual. It's not the greatest manual I've seen, but it is a good effort at one and most of the hazy parts are cleared up on YouTube.

I've found that when the lights flash during flight to signal a low battery (time to land!) that the voltage is about 3.7 volts. This is a pretty safe voltage for storing a LiPo so if you are not going to fly again soon don't bother to charge it. Letting a fully charged LiPo sit for more than a week can be hard on it. Take good care of the battery by never flying it to the point where it is dead. In fact, as soon as you get the flashing warning - land! If you are flying outside where you can't see the warning well in daylight, I'd recommend setting a kitchen timer set to 5-1/2 minutes and timing your flights. Better safe than sorry. Once you run a LiPo down too far it's gone or soon will be.

If you have spare batteries all charged up during a flying session, avoid the temptation of replacing an exhausted battery with a fresh one and getting right back up into the air. My opinion is you should let the motors cool down for a few minutes first. They will be very hot after you complete a full flight so give them a chance to cool a bit before you take to the skies again.

They sell higher capacity batteries here on Amazon. I believe they are 500 mAh. I would not recommend them. Any longer flight time potential will be offset by the extra battery weight. Also the motors will have to work harder at higher RPM to keep the quad airborne. I think the stock capacity battery size is well-suited to this quad.

The instructions encourage you to stuff the battery leads up into the copter body so they don't hang out. I just let them hang out. Stuffing them up in there just stresses all the connections and solder joints and the wires don't stay up in there very will anyway. Just my opinion on that one, folks.

The motors are amazing on these little quads. They are good for about 70 hours of actual flying time. That's really pretty good. Still, if you are going to use the quad a lot and put about 100 flights on it, you will eventually have a motor go bad. It is a good idea to have a spaare motor kit. The motors on the 107C are 8.5mm wide. The motors from the 107L will NOT fit. So get the correct ones.

If you have to replace a motor, you'll have to be able to solder or know somebody who can do it for you. It's a simple soldering task for an experienced RC hobbyist so members of that ilk will have no problem. If you are just leaping into RC with this quad and don't have those skills because you haven't had to suffer the school of hard knocks like we old-timers did, you just have to learn soldering or lean on somebody who can do it for you. Some solder and a basic pencil soldering iron can be obtained for less that 20 bucks if you want to learn a new, useful skill.

As for the HD camera, it is quite sufficient. This little camera will never be super stable outdoors in wind but the video is still quite good. In windy conditions, you MUST press down the right stick to get into expert mode. If you don't you will not have sufficient control movement to fight the wind. You will watch helplessly as your copter drifts away from you if you can't bring it down immediately. Incidentally, while in expert mode if you are afraid of flipping the copter because of the unlimited control movement it provides, just click the left stick down to enter "no-flip" mode.

Also regarding the camera, you must follow the correct procedure to obtain video. Turn on your transmitter with the throttle completely off. Insert the SD card. Connect the battery. Wait for the red light to turn off in the SD card slot. All you should see is a tiny blue light (NO red light). Now you can press the little switch on the side to start recording. You'll see the tiny red light flashing. When you finish your video flight, you must press the little switch again to stop the video. Wait for the red light to go out (indicating the video file has been saved. Now you may unplug the battery. If desired you may also unplug the SD card now.

If you don't use the switch to stop the video, or if you unplug the battery while the red light is flashing, you will save no video.

Always plug/unplug the SD card with the battery disconnected! Also, the SD card socket is not like those on many mobile phones with which you may be familiar. There is no "spring action". You just slide the card in until it bottoms in the slot. If you keep pushing it when you feel resistance thinking you are going to push against the locking spring, don't do it. Push too hard and you could harm the card socket. So go easy on it!

It is amazing that we can now buy a gyro-stabilized copter and get it hovering with so little "learning". It was not unusual for people to spend weeks just learning the touch to get a single rotor copter off the ground in one piece and into a hover. Now it is so much cheaper and simpler. I won't say easy, because as I have said if you are absolute noob you have to learn the controls and develop your skills. Still, you should be able to get it off the ground and hover without too much agony.

If you are interested in flying RC, I don't think you can go wrong with giving this quad a try. I feel it is a bargain price and rewarding and fun to learn to fly.
text_fidelity_b: HUBSAN X4 H107C HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter Red/White (PH-H107C)

Insect Lore - Butterfly Growing Kit - Butterfly Habitat Kit with Voucher to Redeem 5 Caterpillars, STEM Journal, Butterfly Feeder & More – Life Science & STEM Education – Butterfly Science Kit The Live Butterfly Garden by Insect Lore is a fun, hands- on educational experience that is certain to appeal to even the most stubborn, disinterested child. With the Live Butterfly Garden, children get to observe the process of metamorphosis, right before their eyes. Starting with caterpillars, children watch the little critters eat food, create a cocoon, and then transform into fully grown adult butterflies. The butterflies can then be observed in their habitat for a while before setting free.

This butterfly garden is great for dozens of reasons, the most obvious of which is the educational value. Reading about insects and metamorphosis is one thing, but seeing the process live is another thing entirely. Kids get to learn how caterpillars/butterflies live, eat, and thrive; how to care for them; etc. They get to observe the caterpillars and butterflies at play and watch the butterflies eat their food, which is provided in the package. The caterpillars that come with the Live Butterfly Garden are painted ladies, which are not very common and will not be recognized by most children. However, most kids won't care- the fun of watching these small caterpillars transform into butterflies will have many kids gazing in awe, and prompt them to ask many questions.

This educational toy is a huge hit and my kids loved it, but there were a few small issues. One was waiting for the caterpillars to arrive in the mail. To get the caterpillars, you have to mail in an included certificate, along with a check, and then wait. It seems like an eternity, especially from the perspective of young children, and it took longer than expected. Anther problem was parting with the butterflies. Once you have the caterpillars and they have transformed into adult butterflies, the next problem will be setting them free. Kids will grow attached to their small, winged friends and will not want to let them go. Another minor issue is with the transferring of the caterpillars from their small container- the one you receive in the mail- into the actual habitat. The container that the caterpillars arrive in has a paper area at the top, where the caterpillars will hang as they spin their cocoons. This paper section is fairly easy to remove, but the problem is that the cocoons are very delicately attached, and that means that some will fall off when the transfer is made. You will need to pin this piece of paper to the inside of the butterfly garden, but the kit doesn't include any pins. Safety pins or straight pins work, and it would have been nice if these were included in the kit.

Still, when all factors are considered, the Live Butterfly Garden is worth the purchase and young children will enjoy the educational experience. Sure, it could be improved a little bit by making a few minor changes, but this is still a very good toy and considering my kid's fascination with the process, along with the educational value, it earns an easy recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Insect Lore - Butterfly Growing Kit - Butterfly Habitat Kit with Voucher to Redeem 5 Caterpillars, STEM Journal, Butterfly Feeder & More – Life Science & STEM Education – Butterfly Science Kit

Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome My almost four year-old boy loves the Fisher-Price Power Wheels Dune Racer Chrome Ride-On. This means it passed the most important reviewing test. Overall, I also like it, but some things could be improved.

Pro
* It looks cool with its sky blue and chrome features, with black seats and slick black wheels. He's the first kid in preschool with a rad set of wheels.
* It goes forward 2.5 and 5.0 mph, and backward 2.5 mph.
* Steering is actual. The driver could parallel park if needed.
* It auto breaks when the pedal is let go. Nice safety feature.

Con
* Chrome and other parts scratch easily, and even arrived scratched a little
* It took over 90 minutes to put together, and some parts had to muscled in.
* Not everything lines up easily. This isn't just aesthetic, but includes the front wheels. We are still trying to get them properly aligned.
* Seat doesn't move. My boy can barely reach the pedals despite being almost four (the stated age is 4-7). Moving forward, we'll include a back cushion.
* While it too early to be sure, the tires (hollow hard plastic) look like they'll wear quickly.
* I weigh too much. I want to ride in it!

Lots of fun, and a great way to bring your child along on long walks.

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up Chess has been my favorite board game since I was a child and I have collected chess sets as a hobby over the years. When I selected this one I expected it to be on par with typical portable wooden sets which are usually cheaply made. This one was a pleasant surprise in that it is a step up from most portable wooden sets I have seen and used.

This is a fairly straightforward set. The case is a clamshell design that folds open into the board. There are magnets in the rim of the underside of the board to hold it closed when the set is not in use, ands the manufacturer did a decent job of concealing the contacts (though they are visible if you look for them). The squares on the board are smooth and while the seams between the squares can be felt when you run your hand along the board, the seams are smooth and are less pronounced that what I have seen on some other boards.

The pieces are decently made though are nothing special. They are machine cut pieces and have been smoothed, sanded and varnished. They are weighted nicely and have felt on the bottom to avoid scratching the board. They’re a fairly average design but they look good and are very recognizable.

The main feature of this set is that it is larger than most fold-out boards I have seen and used. While this might not be the best for packing and portability, I really like the size. I am less likely to knock over pieces accidentally and I can see what’s going on a little better.

This is not just a chess set but includes wood chips for playing checkers as well. The chips are small and are nothing of note but they are sufficient.

I really like this chess set and will use it as my main travel set moving forward. I like the size of the board, the feel of the pieces and the overall quality. There are better sets out there but they cost more. There are less expensive sets too, and the chances of finding one that is of the same quality as this one for less is small.
text_fidelity_b: Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up

Hot Wheels T-Rex Rampage Track Set, Works City Sets, Toys for Boys Ages 5 to 10 My son has several sets of Hot Wheels toys. Hot Wheels is often hit or miss. They sometimes have a great idea and an awesomely executed toy. Sometimes the toys create nothing but frustration. However, with this playset my really had nothing but fear. Therefore, the Mattel Hot Wheels City T-Rex Rampage has done it's job. It strikes fear in all those who come upon it. My 7 year old is afraid of this toy. He was ok with it until he found out that the T-Rex moved, and it's no dice. He doesn't even want it just sitting in his room.

After you figure out how to put it together. The T-Rex part was tricky, but don't worry the part can come apart so if you mess up the alignment, you're ok. You get 1 angry T-Rex who needs a snack and a nap, 2 buildings, a launchpad, and a piece of track and a car. I'm not sure what the name of the game is. I am not entirely sure what you are supposed to do. My son comes up with different ideas every 5 minutes. However, the scary part comes in when you turn it on. The toy comes with batteries and when you turn it on and push the blue button on the circle track, the T-Rex will start to thrash around and knock over buildings etc. He roars and all of this action is what scares my son. The launcher is of course his favorite part. If you launch the car just right, the car will hit a button to "defeat" the dinosaur.

The ultimate issue with Hot Wheels is that except for the cars themselves, most sets get broken fairly quickly. I cannot say the same for this because it's not getting much play. As with all Hot Wheel sets you can connect them to each other if you have enough track to do so. So, that is the best part about Hot Wheels. However, tracks are hard to come by and they are usually long and flimsy. So, you can't really link up the sets and the tracks get all bent out of shape. So, this will connect to the other sets we have. However, that is only great thing about it. I don't really get the whole dinosaurs or mutant alligators are taking over the city. Neither does my son. I'm all for imagination, but this whole concept seems to have been created in a vacuum. There is no background story, nothing. My son asked why is the T-Rex in the city. I had nothing.

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Bubble Guppies, Check-Up Center My 2 oldest boys(5 and 3) are obsessed with all things "hospital" right now. They pretend they are firefighters/paramedics/doctors constantly, and LOVE watching the old show "Emergency". They also enjoy Bubble Guppies occasionally, so when I saw this check-up center, I guessed that they would enjoy it.

I guessed correctly! They fell in love with it.

Unfortunately, they caught sight of the "Clambulance" on the back of the box(and all the other items that *didn't* come in this set, and it took a moment to curb their disappointment. Once they did, though, they've greatly enjoyed playing with it. Thankfully, there are several ambulances already at our house, and they gladly used those.

Another disappointment is the fact that this set ONLY comes with the dog, and none of the other "guppies". Again, though, my boys made do with other toys, like a small spiderman and a couple of miniature piglets for the baby cart. The wheelchair and cart are specifically made for the toys in this set, though. The toys have a thick plastic covering on the bottom in the shape of a half oval. This shape is also in the wheelchair/cart.

Overall, if you get this check-up center, I do recommend getting at least a couple of the other characters to go with it, along with at least the "clambulance" or helicopter. I think your little one will have more fun with it. We intend on adding to the set, possibly for a birthday present. You CAN make do with just this one, though.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Bubble Guppies, Check-Up Center

BIV plus brown, black, white and pink. There are 15 laminated cards with activities on them and there is an activity guide as well to help you through activities.

The cubes themselves are plastic, but they feel soft to the touch and almost rubber-like. They are pretty easy to snap apart, but they require some strength to put them back together. I think with time and use, the plastic will wear down and snapping them together will become easier. You can use a dry erase marker on the cards to come up with your own activity or to expand upon the ones suggested.

Learning Resources actually has other Mathlink Cubes about $8 cheaper. You don't get the cards with it, but they are something similar to these cubes. So, I am sure a really crafty person could figure out their own activities and save a bit of money. I am ultimately happy with them because my son's Kindergarten teacher suggested that he work on counting to 100 over the summer. So, that is what we are doing with these, but I will probably have to look into other resources to expand on the lessons from these cards. I just feel like we'll get through them really fast and after a couples times they will get boring.

I typically like Learning Resources products. They are good quality and have helped my son thru various stages of his academic life. I'm just not wild about these. I know I will use them for a while, but I'm just not over the moon pleased with them.

The one thing that's a little bit confusing to me as it seems like a few of these animals have a shinier, slicker finish that looks a lot cheaper, while some of the animals have a more matte or hashed texture like for, that looks a lot more like a higher end product. It feels inconsistent and kind of confusing, and had you laid all of these out for me and not told me they were in a set, I would not have guessed that the lion and tiger, for example, went in the same set as the gorilla. text_fidelity_a: Hot Wheels id Smart Track Starter Kit with 3 Exclusive Cars, Track Pieces and Hot Wheels Race Portal for Physical & Digital Play, Gift for Kids Ages 8 Years Old & Up This is okay. If not for Vine, I'm not sure I would spend this type of money though. The one good thing is that there is some hand/eye coordination in play, so your children well get some development. You see they have to view an app, which shows a speedometer. They need to keep the needle at a certain speed. Speedometer graphics is broken down into 2 colors, blue and red. If you go to the red, chances are good your car will fly off the tracks. How do you control the speed? By pumping the booster. The faster you pump, the needle will move towards the red. So you need to time yourself and not pump too slow, or too fast to keep the needle in the blue at all times. My kids seem to think it's fun, so that's all that matters. But if you're an adult or an older child, I think you might get bored. Just pumping and watching the car go round and round. All the hardware is top notch. I won't subtract a star for thinking it's boring, since that's subjective.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels id Smart Track Starter Kit with 3 Exclusive Cars, Track Pieces and Hot Wheels Race Portal for Physical & Digital Play, Gift for Kids Ages 8 Years Old & Up

text_fidelity_a: Pass the Stache Board Game Watching a group of 13 year olds play Moustache Smash is like watching a Black Friday sale with everyone fighting for the same discounted towels. I couldn't help but laugh hysterically as each girl held the mustache up to her face then frantically tried to be the first to smash the card that either matched the color or the shape of their mustache. (Mind you they had to remember which mustache they chose and what it looked like because they have to keep it up on their face at all times when the game is in play - until it's time to snatch a card). The game comes with 6 mustaches on very solid plastic sticks. There is a suction cup at the end of the mustache that allows the playing card to be snatched up quite easily. It's best to play on a solid surface to make sure the card stays put. There are 32 mustache cards of various colors and shapes. Each player takes a turn being the dealer. The dealer flips the card over for all to see - but can't cheat by flipping the card facing them first. IF a player accidentally snatches up the wrong mustache, they have to return it plus two more mustaches (if they have them) from their stash. It goes into a pot for the next player who correctly snatches up a mustache to claim. When all 32 cards are dealt, the game is over. The player left standing with the most 'stashes wins. The cards are in perfect squares - keeping the field even for all players. The mustaches feel rubbery so are less likely to cause harm if accidentally smacked into another players hand. The one thing I suggest is you have the camera at the ready! I have some great video and excellent pictures that I was able to share with the players' parents. Unfortunately, without the parents' permissions, I cannot display any of the videos or photos. They weren't comfortable with their children being seen. The recommended age is 7 and up, but I can easily see a 5 year old handling this well. I would also be willing to play with a group of adults. For $15.99 with free prime shipping, it is a great birthday or Christmas gift without breaking the budget. Plus, there are no tiny pieces to lose or step on. (BONUS!)  Keep in mind, though, that there are only 6 mustaches... so a max of 6 players can play at one time.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde Baby Alive is an iconic doll. She was one of the first dolls that not only took a bottle, but also ate food, mixed and served to her from premade packets. She has been available in many different versions, each with the same eat/drink concept with a slightly different variation. My Baby All Gone is one of the latest Baby Alive dolls and she will easily keep your little one serving, feeding, changing, and burping her baby for hours.

What sets this Baby Alive doll apart from most of the others in the series is her ability to say so many different things. She still takes a bottle, eats food, pees, and poops just like the other Baby Alive dolls, but for a more realistic twist, she makes periodic statements from her wee little mouth. She will say that she wants to cuddle, that she just went pee, and so on. Her baby- ish voice and cute sayings will appeal strongly to young girls still going through their mommy phase.

My girls are both in their early years of elementary school, but they still like dolls and they like Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll just as much if not more than the others in the series, of which they have quite a few dolls. What they like best is the feature that sets this doll apart: The sayings, mentioned above. They like that she says so many different things- more than 30 sayings in all- because it makes her seem more real. I agree that the multitude of sayings is a vast improvement on other dolls that, while they might speak, say only three or four different things. My girls like playing the role of mommy, changing diapers, giving Baby Alive a nap, and everything else that goes with being a mom.

The one disadvantage of this Baby Alive doll is the same disadvantage with the others- you have to constantly purchase refill packs. Trust me, the few packs of food and the small number of diapers will not last long at all! In a matter of a day or two out of the package, your girls will be asking for replacement food and diapers. We have had this doll in our household for only about 10 days and have already ordered a refill pack.

Little girls often like to play the role of a mommy and Baby Alive is one of the best dolls for interactive mommy play. My girls like her very much and I like that they are happy. The cost of the refill packs can add up, so try to improvise when you can or create your own cloth diapers that can be washed and reused. There is the pending "live-action" Sonic movie, but that has been pushed back from November to Winter/Spring of 2020 so any tie-in toys will also probably be pushed back. So, this RC car was the only thing I could really find that wasn't exorbitantly priced.

This currently priced at $27, but I would say it's really not worth more than $20. It's really light weight and does not come with batteries. So, keep that in mind when you are giving this as a gift. The car and the remote both need batteries. AA and AAA. Sonic is part of the car. He does not come out. And this operates just like any other R/C car. There's nothing special about it other than it is Sonic. The headlights turn on when going forward and turn off when in reverse. My so has launched this off the porch and into the front yard several times. It's only about 6 inches down from the porch to the ground, so I doubt there's any real damage, but I would caution against doing that from any heights above that. However, I would say that he has played with this for a couple minutes and then moved onto something else. Without any other bells and whistles, the hold factor for this toys wasn't very long. Keep in mind while my son loves Sonic, he doesn't play the video games or do much on electronic devices. So, he actually plays with toys most of his day.

So, I think this is a nice, cute gift, but I think it is a bit over priced.

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark and the DJI Tello, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for 35 dollars. Compared to other drones, I would say that there are certain improvements that could be made but those drones are much, much more expensive.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is quite small, which is nice because it lends itself to indoor flight and easy travel. It is about 4.5 inches by 4.5 inches for a length and width, and the diagonal rotor distance is about 5 inches, while to entire copter stands at about 1.25 inches. This, as I said, is nice for indoor flight and you don't have to worry too much about hitting someone. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards proved themselves quite useful, as I bumped it into walls several times, and the guards did their job. The copter simply bounced off the wall and continued flying. Additionally, when I was testing it, the drone died while flying. I knew this was coming, as I could feel the responsiveness beginning to slow and the flip function would no longer work. The drone fell from about 12 feet in the air onto the blacktop. I didn't notice and dings, dents, or scar=tches, and once it was charged, it flew fine.

Quiet - The drone has a shrill high pitched sound as it flies. It isn't too loud, and I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. Executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward of backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button a the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Cons:
Disproportionate flight to charge time ratio - According to the user manual, this charge time is about 70 minutes, while the flight time is around 5 minutes while hovering. I, however, found that it took about 35 minutes (charging for a wall outlet) for a full charge from dropping out of the sky dead. The flight time that I got was about 6 minutes, doing maneuvers, flips, climbing, falling, accelerating and decelerating. Still, I think this could be improved, and, as there are no removable batteries you can plug in once another is dead, I make using the drone for more than 10 minutes hard.
Poor wind resistance - This thing blows outside with the slightest breeze. Inside, the flight trim is hard to adjust, and outside, it is not worth it. I found myself constantly adjusting to compensate for any wind.
Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as find things within the manual. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
Joysticks don't articulate much - This is actually somewhat annoying. there isn't much height to the sticks, and they don't move around much, making any more precise movements difficult. Additionally, the other buttons on the controller are somewhat difficult to press.

I liked this drone, especially for the price. This would be great for any kid, or even as a starting copter for someone who wants to see if they are interested in them. I like the size, durability, and flip function, but the battery life and wind resistance are something to consider.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. I had almost forgotten about this little loom -- I first learned how to make these potholders in the 1950s even before I started school (I was probably 5 yrs old). My brother and I spent many summers working on these and selling them around the neighborhood to augment our $0.25/week allowance. My mother taught us how to make them and kept us supplied with the loops while we came up with our own designs.

One thing I remember very clearly -- she avoided nylon loops, preferring instead cotton loops. Why? Because the nylon loops could melt at the temperatures commonly encountered when using cast iron pans and metal baking dishes in hot ovens. I retained that memory, so when I saw this kit available with cotton loops, I knew I needed to try it one more time.

The major difference I see is in the length of the "prongs" in the loom -- I recall them being a little longer. Also, the metal weaving hook was a bit longer. But other than that, the design and construction are close to what I used as a child.

The package from Amazon arrived earlier today, and I quickly put together the potholder in the photo. It took probably an hour -- perhaps a bit longer, but not much. There are enough loops for a couple of pot holders and enough colors to mix and match. Follow the directions, especially the part about finishing -- pulling one of the loops on each finished edge back over a loom peg to keep the rest of the loops on the adjacent and opposite sides from popping off the loom. Take your time with this part -- it's easy to want to hurry to finish it, but it can be a bit "fiddly."

Very happy with this -- I've already ordered additional loops in specific colors to coordinate with my kitchen colors so I can make several of these to use as potholders as well as hot pads/trivets.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

---------------------------

The firing part is even cooler- you pull back the spring loaded mechanism to load it, then mime a cat slash (flick wrist downward) and it gives a satisfying firing sound that jettisons two darts across the room. The only thing I don't like about it however is that there are 3 darts included and two fire at a time. You could load one at a time if you want, but it feels like they should have included an even number of them. Also, there is no place to store the additional darts. The Iron Man version of this set also comes with 3 darts, but has a place to store all of them on the glove as you lead them one at a time. Firing two with this and then awkwardly holding the third seems like they didn't think it through all the way. But, it's still fun, especially if you love the Black Panther character.

text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed.

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into 4 separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost. It kind of made me wonder what the point of 4 bags were.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers ache after working with Mega Bloks, just because of the pressure I have to use to get them attached.

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cute! (I just found it a pain. Literally. To be fair, though, I probably would have enjoyed the whole experience more, minus the finger pain, if I wasn't so spoiled from better. It really is cute enough!)
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills This is not up to the typical quality of Melissa and Doug products in my opinion. There are 12 mini-projects in this "book"(it's an scruffy bubble envelope with other envelopes inside), and each has some very basic scissor projects. The first one, for instance, has your child cutting in straight lines to create a simple memory game. The second one builds on this, adding some cross-cutting, and so forth.

Each kit is good enough, and the variety is greatly appreciated by the kiddos. In some instances, the instructions needed a little work, while in others, they were perfect. In each case, they're language independent and entirely taught through pictures, which is great for helping the kiddos follow along and do the projects somewhat independently.

There are two pairs of scissors included in this package - a straight pair, and a "scrapbooking" scissor that cuts "teeth" - but these safety scissors are entirely too "safety" for me. The straight one works well enough at first, while the teeth scissors barely worked at all. Their entirely plastic frame wears out with minimal use. There are no metal parts on them, outside of the screws. We had trouble making clean cuts as we approached the middle of the kits, and by the end, we just switched to metal scissors as we were mangling the paper more than doing actual cutting.

The problem with the scissors, as well as the complete lack of a storage solution for these projects as they're in progress is enough for me to rate this kit lower than I normally do. My kit arrived mispacked, so I received two #4 projects, and no #3 project. Good projects can be had here, but bring some of your own materials.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills

text_fidelity_a:
Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This game hits that sweet spot where the complexity is enough for adults but not so high that kids struggle. And it’s FUN! It says 9 and up but my 7-year-old caught on pretty quickly and was delighted when we talked about it in terms of executing a program. My family loves this game. My husband and I can see playing it with just adults too.

The gameplay involves drafting cards and then using them to create a plan for how the mole will move on the grid, which is essentially a simple program much like one would write on a computer. It takes some strategy, but you can only predict other people so much and this is where the game shines.

I was worried it would be too complex or long when we read the rules, but it plays very smoothly! We felt comfortable within 2 rounds, and it was a lot of fun seeing how the plans we made would be thwarted as other players move. We also enjoyed how the turn order changed. There are many levels of subtle strategy, I feel like we will be learning new things each time we play. There is a random element of dice when placing a rock on the board, simple but genius game design. It keeps it from feeling unfair, and adds an element of luck to using it.

Even when you are losing, it’s so interesting to see the programs unfold as each card flips that it didn’t feel upsetting, and most of the points are earned in the later rounds as the mounds get higher so you can easily catch back up to an early lead or after a bad round. This means you don’t feel too discouraged if you have a poor start.

I like that it has a defined timeline, there are 6 rounds and you know what they will look like. Overall a great choice for a family game night as it is not likely to overrun an hour.

The double-layer boards and gameplay are unique and the story of the moles is full of flavor. The art is charming and the explanation of the rules such as “moles are too polite so they don’t move when they hit another” is a really sweet touch. The printing is great quality, the game is just beautiful to look at. The box is well-organized making setup and takedown easy, and it looks pretty on the shelf. Plus, we love the moles! The standees make great pieces. This game shows a lot of care in the details, and we love games with a lot of artistic flavor.

We play a lot of games as a family, but when we finished this one kiddo said this was their new favorite! The only downside is the limit of 2-4 players–it keeps it moving but means we can’t invite more friends to play at a time!

Bonus, the box art is beautiful so this also would make a lovely gift to open.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

Immediately out of the box, her head popped off. She has a huge head for her body (which is cute) but it makes it easy for her head to pop off. (It easily pops back on.) If the kids fight over her, her head pops off. It is easy enough to put back on that they don't need my help with it, but I foresee a day when we have a head with no body or a body with no head floating around the toy box.
I loaded the CribLife.com website up. They were minutely interested in the website. You can create your own room and pick your doll. It really seemed like more of a marketing strategy to get you to buy more of the dolls, because it shows all the dolls and prompts you to "get to know them" which translated into the kids pouring over the computer to determine which one they wanted next. Once that was determined (the result- all of them), they went on about their business and wanted nothing more from the website. I tried to see if they were interested in creating a room for Makayla, but they wanted to create a place in their room for Makayla. They weren't too interested in the virtual aspect of the toy.
I also wanted to add that she is pretty small. I thought she'd be regular Baby Alive size, but she isn't. Her head is the size of a softball and her body is tiny compared to that. It is almost a mini-doll, though slightly larger than most of the mini-dolls on the market.

Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show is a fun way for your little fashion diva to spend some free time. All you do is download the application on your smartphone, tablet, or iPod touch, draw some fashion designs, and then scan them. Your fashion will then show up on an actual fashion model, in 3D, to your child’s delight.

My girls are fashion designers in the making so I knew they would love playing with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show. It takes little effort to get going. You just add the application to your smartphone or tablet, and then have your child start drawing. Once scanned through the application, kids will be able to see their own fashion design on an actual model. This caused squeals of satisfaction from my girls who loved seeing their fashion on screen.

From my children’s perspectives, there is little that isn’t perfect with a toy like this, but as an adult, I can see a few issues. One has already been stated by others who have used the device, but bears repeating: The phone or tablet you use will make a difference. Not all smartphones or tablets are created equally and the colors may look a little off. If you have more than one device and it doesn’t look good on one, then you might want to consider downloading the application to another device. It could make a difference and it’s simple enough to do.

The included accessories with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show are a little limited. The small colored pencils are also somewhat of an obstacle, as they are not good for larger hands. But overall, this is a fun fashion design kit and I cannot imagine a fashion- loving child who wouldn’t fall in love with it.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show

Alex Art Wooden Dough Tools Set Kids Art and Craft Activity What you see is what you get! This fun set of clay manipulation tools would make a perfect gift alongside either play doh or one of the more sophisticated and fluffier types of modeling clay such as[[ASIN:B011TRQ3TO Sago Brothers 36 Colors Ultra Light Modeling Magic Air Dry Clay Crafts Kit]].

I think my favorites are the three rolling wheels, which are suited to small hands and fun to use. The wood has a light coating of some manner of varnish or slightly slick treatment, so it doesn't stick to the clay too badly, and keeps things fun to use. I like the bright primary colors in the natural wood tone, and the diverse shapes are a lot of fun. The only thing you should know is that a few of these are not entirely safe for extremely active toddlers, so this is a toy that you will supervise and make sure that nobody is sprinting down the hall with a small pointed spear. When used as directed and not as a weapon (mothers of small boys will understand my caveat), this is such a fun set!

I actually held one of them back, the rolling wheel that has little squares stamped into it, so my son can help me make peanut butter cookies by gently pushing the cookie with his roller. This one will remain food safe only, and the rest will be played with with modeling clays and play dough. I don't think these would be as fun and successful with more grown-up clays such as Fimo just because the surface area is so large and usually you are creating giant rough sculptures with an expensive material like Fimo or Sculpey. This is definitely the sort of thing you would use with children's modeling clay. A great starter set that would make a great auxiliary to a simple modeling dough gift.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Art Wooden Dough Tools Set Kids Art and Craft Activity

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I like the size of the pieces because I have kids in my home who like legos and with those it can be hard to find pieces because they are so small and they end up all over the place. I also like the color combination that was provided. The instructions have to be accessed through a website, which is okay, but I would have liked to have paper directions (but that's just a personal preference).

What I like: 1) within the app it provides step by step directions to build the characters. You have to press play through each step therefore you move along at your own pace. You can also flip the image around so you can see the sides, front, and bottom of the chracter (how it should be) so you can make sure everything is in the right spot. 2) the pieces are very sturdy. I don't forsee myself having a problem with them breaking unless its intentional. 3) it charges really quickly. The block that is the main piece of the entire item is rechargeable. After playing with it for sometime the battery indicated it was on 17% (through the app) and it only took about 20 minutes to fully charge.

What I didn't like: 1) the app is a pain. The description states the item is optimized for android devices with android 7.0 or more, but this is not true. I have three tablets and a samsung chromebook with android 7.0 or more, but when I go to the appstore, it says the app is not optimized for my device or I cannot find the app at all. I had to download the app on my Galaxy S9. Which I would rather the kids be able to play with it on their own devices instead of my phone. I also added it to an iphone XR and it worked. 2) the app isn't the best functionally. It would shut off on me randomly or freeze up. It even caused my phone to go black for about five minutes and after plugging it into the charger and waiting, it finally popped up on camera mode. 3) it is not always easy or fast getting the phone and the item to connect. You have to have your location and bluetooth on and even when the device is powered on, the app will tell you to power it on. Then half the time, it takes 3-5 minutes to finally connect. 4) I like to coding part, because you can do an order of functions, but when you want to just play with it, you can only go back and forth or right and left, depending on the character you built. We built an alligator and it just opened and closed its mouth and not with the same force each time.

Pressman Tri-Ominos - Deluxe Edition Triangular Tiles with Brass Spinners, 5" I’ve always wanted Tri-Ominos because it is a twist on Dominos but uses triangular instead of rectangular tiles and it's lots of fun.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX:
56 triangular tiles
4 plastic tile holders (or racks)
1 instruction sheet

The object of the game is to be the first player to score 400 points with each game consisting of several rounds of play.

For example, with two players, nine tiles are given to each player. The tiles should be face down so that the other player or players don’t see them. Each player adds up the numbers on each of their tiles. If a player has a tile with three of the same numbers on the tile, then the player with the highest combination goes first. For example , a player with three 5’s (which is equal to 15) would go before a player with three 4’s (which is 12) and score the bonus points explained in the instruction card. If no player has a Tri-Omino tile, then the player with the highest numbered tiled goes first but no bonus points would be given.

The idea is for a player to match his or her tile to a tile on the board that has two of the same numbers. They basically get connected the way that it is done with Dominos. The score gets added up for each tile placed. Those that can’t make a match pick from the “well” or remaining face down tiles. Each pick from the well cost the player 5 points from their score. If you can’t match any Tri-Omino in your hand and the well is empty, ten points are deducted from your score and the play continues.

The first player to play all of his Tri-Ominos wins the round and receives a 25-point bonus plus the total points of all the Tri-Ominos left in the other players’ hands. If the game is blocked, then the player with the least amount of tiles wins and gets to add all the points from the left over tiles to their score but there are no bonus points given. This player must also deduct the total number of points that were left in his hand from his score. This method of play gets repeated until a player reaches 400 points to win the game. There are a few other ways to get bonus points in a game as well.

Scoring is done after every play, so from this perspective the game can be tedious. However, it is a lot of fun and for young children, the process of adding up the numbers on the tiles is an education in math. My boyfriend and I really love this game. Playing a full game with two people takes a couple of hours.
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Tri-Ominos - Deluxe Edition Triangular Tiles with Brass Spinners, 5"

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll As a longtime Barbie collector, I'm always curious when a new Barbie doll uses a gimmick that was popular years ago. In this case, the Barbie Hairtastic Color Styling doll offers the same "color magic" idea that made a 1966 Barbie doll a best-seller. The concept is similar - wet the doll's hair and you can change her hair color using a simple brush and a "foil clip".

This doll comes with a chair, water brush, comb, water bowl (for rinsing the brush), eight "foil" cards (purple, orange and pink), a set of three Barbie hairties, and a styling "foil clip".

The box makes the color transfer seem easy, but actually it takes a bit of work. The instructions say "wet the hair generously" so if you do this with a child, be sure to have a newspaper or towel around so that the doll's hair and the dyes don't stain your table. The foil clip comes already loaded with an orange card, so I tried that first.

The results were mixed. I had to run the clip up and down the hair a few times before the color started to show. I also had to reapply the wet brush several times even though the hair seemed wet enough. Finally, the orange color streak came out bright and strong. Then I tried the purple dye, and the color was faint and weak. I added more water and tried again, but the purple dye failed to transfer a rich color. Not sure why this is.

Contrary to the box claims, the foils can't be reused. It's low-tech - a swatch of watercolor paint on the back of a foil card. When some of the dye from the purple card failed to transfer, I simply took the card out of the clip and rubbed the card itself into the hair. This was sloppy but it did the job better.

The chair has a suction cup, which is a wonderful and long-needed feature. Barbie sat snugly in her chair and it remained firmly anchored while styling. I wish all Barbie chairs had something like this.

Lastly, the instructions don't mention how long the dye will last, only that it comes off with water. Good, but I found that the dye stained my hands and clothing. If a child does this, be prepared. The clip idea is good, but it doesn't fully prevent the process from getting messy.

Overall, it's a decent toy but once the dyes run out, you'd be left with an ordinary Barbie doll.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Words with Friends Luxe I love word games and I particularly like Scrabble. I have seen Words with Friends online and though I have not played it online I suspected this game would be a lot like Scrabble. It definitely is. It's a good game and can be a great addition to family game night.

Words with Friends is a crossword game where the goal is to create words and score points by strategically placing the words on the game board. The board has a number of bonus squares where extra points can be had - double word, triple word, double letter and triple letter. The player with the highest score at the end of the game wins. Each player gets 7 letter tiles (with point counts printed directly on the tiles) with which to make words. Play continues until all the tiles are used and all of the scoring opportunities are expended.

Game play as described above is just like Scrabble, but there are some differences. The score assigned to individual letters varies is little bit. The bonus squares are laid out differently too. Using all 7 letters in one turn results in a 35-point bonus, not 50.

The tiles are a glassy-looking orange color and are very aesthetically pleasing, even though they are simply plastic. The board itself is a two-piece creation and it clips together into one larger board. Assembly is simple.

I noticed a couple of flaws in this game, though these are not enough to lower my opinion of the game enough to matter. First, the board does clip together and turns nicely - on hard, flat surfaces. On carpet, the board can be a little uncooperative and can come apart. My second complaint is that the rules are so general that there is a little room for interpretation. People who have played Scrabble have a slight advantage - the unspecified rules are easy to fill in.

I especially like something printed on the box: "Your Smart Phone Unlocks Digital Features (phone not included)" Sorry, this made me laugh - I hope it's clear to everyone that there's no phone in the box...

Other than a touchy board and some slightly incomplete rules, this is a very fun game and is sure to be a hit on game night. My teenager and I have been playing and he's learning that I know more than he thought I did...
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Words with Friends Luxe

Adora Amazing Girls 18 Doll, Sienna (Amazon Exclusive) This is a beautiful girl and of really nice quality. I really like the face sculpt so much more than the Target Our Generation dolls and the soft body makes her a pleasure to hold. We do not have any American girl dolls in our home, but based on my memory of holding a friends, these seem a little more comparable in quality level to American girl than the cheaper our generation and 14 inch glitter girls which is what we have had in our home until now.

Her styling is beautiful, much more so in person than in the images. The longsleeve shirt is sparkly gold and kind of fits like a tunic top, and the black leggings are soft, shiny, and have some wonderful sparkle to them. The jacket and boots are a lovely soft fabric that is not loud and wrinkly, but rather smooth and pliable and lovely to the touch. The fur details are quite nice and do not seem to be depositing over much fuzz on the rest of her outfit. The boots are fabric and are relatively easy to get on, with a Velcro closure. Her little bag has an open top and is easy to set a few things inside of, though it is on the smaller side.

Curls are absolutely gorgeous! I did a little finger combing and gentle fluffing and she just looks so beautiful. Her skin tone is more of an olive skin tone than a cocoa color. I am white with blonde hair and blue eyes, and you can see my hand in some of the images next to the girls skin tone so that you can get a feeling of what her skin tone really looks like. To me she definitely reads as an African-American girl, but with a lighter skin tone.

I'm not a huge fan of the pale pink box that this line of dolls comes in because it doesn't seem modern, and seems more suited to a baby doll than something for an older girl, but the doll itself once you remove her from the box is lovely. If you are giving this doll as a special gift, consider taking her out of the box before giving, unclip her from the things holding her in, put on her shoes, and remove the hair net that is knotted quite tightly into her beautiful hair. The hairnet is protective of her hair in travel, but they tied it in with the thick piece of thread right at her forehead and even without an excited child sitting right there, I found it took me a number of minutes to carefully cut that off of her hair to free her gorgeous curls.

One other thing that I really like is that we have a boy doll from our generation, and I really appreciate whenever the clothes from girl dolls have parts that can be unisex enough for the dolls to share among themselves. This is really nice because these are just like regular clothes the real girl would wear, only a little bit fancy and dressed up. And our boy doll could certainly wear some of these pieces as well. She fits the other 18 inch doll clothing that we have from our generation and other brands and seems to be the standard 18 inch doll size.

Overall this is a high quality doll who is beautifully detailed, has lovely eyes which close when she lays down, and beautiful hair and clothing.

text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit
