text_fidelity_a:
Money Savvy Pig - Pink Money Savvy Pig offers a fun and effective way to teach kids about money and its many important uses. Parents devote very little time to the concept of financial management, in spite of its critical nature, often because they are not sure how best to approach the subject. Money Savvy Pig makes it easy to introduce youngsters to these important concepts.

How does Money Savvy Pig work as an educational device? The answer is simple. By including four different chambers with different labels- one for spend, one for save, one for donate, and one for invest- kids gain a sense of financial management and money allocation. They learn that money has uses that go far beyond ordinary spending. Kids under the age of seven are not ready to learn the specifics of these different concepts, but early exposure is a good idea and the Money Savvy Bank Pig certainly succeeds in this respect.

The Money Savvy Bank is made from plastic and mine has held up fine thus far. Others have pointed out that this bank can break if dropped on a hard surface. Considering its lightweight design, it isn't difficult to imagine the bank breaking apart if mishandled, which is why parents need to exercise caution and make sure their kids handle the bank with extra care when moving from one place to the next.

I like that this bank separates money into four different sections and I like that it gets kids thinking about money and its uses. One limitation, however, is that this bank isn't very good for storing paper money. The reason is because the pieces of paper are difficult to remove. The openings on the bottom of the bank are small- too small to stick your hand inside the bank to remove paper. Place a folded dollar bill inside this bank and it will take some shaking and maneuvering to remove it from the bottom. Thus, this bank should be avoided for storing paper currency. It is intended for use with coins.

Financial literacy is important and kids need to learn about money at the youngest age possible. The Money Savvy Pig is a very good piggy bank for youngsters and its benefits go far beyond the encouragement of savings. It encourages kids to ask questions and think about money in different ways, making it a great choice for a child's early financial education.
text_fidelity_b: Money Savvy Pig - Pink

If you roll a six it is an all-play, and each team also has three steal cards which they can use to jump in when their opponents are playing. Each time you guess a clue, you win the card. The first team to ten cards wins.

I liked that there is no game board. The game comes in a small box that is easy to transport. It's great for family vacations or game night.

All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

Trying to remove them with a cup and piece of paper is perilous at best (what if it GETS OUT and gets on my hand?? I would flail in terror and then who knows where it would land?). I knew my time had come when my cats were staring at the floor. It was my nemesis, a spider. I tore the catcher out of the packaging and - with only a little shrieking - successfully subdued the spider! It was caught in the bristles, unable to escape! And I was at a safe distance, unlike the cup method where I'd be practically touching the spider. I darted outside and released it. I told the spider he was evicted and to eat bugs outside, never inside. If it ever does venture inside aagin, I know my cat sentries would alert me to its presence and - with minimal shrieking - I could safely evict it again.

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game I have two teenagers who spend a lot of time in their rooms. We have the occasional game night once or twice a month for some quality family time. This game has become my 16 year old daughter's absolute favorite game. She has even started having her friends over for game night. You roll the dice and whatever letter comes up is the letter that each word that you write has to start with for that round. You are given a card that tells you what to write. For example, the card may say "a color" for number 1. The die was rolled and it landed on the letter G for that round. So you have to write down a color that starts with G on your list. Now if you and anyone else write the same G word, neither of you get a point. You are trying to come up with the most original and creative word that fits the letter and the subject. It's usually hard to come up with all twelve words in a round when the timer is set! We all enjoy this game!

text_fidelity_a: HSP Nature Toys Root-Vue Farm Multicolor, 16 Inch Loved the idea of this - who doesn't want to get their kids excited about veggies? But this has been a disaster since it arrived. I also wasn't aware that it's an expensive piece of styrofoam.  Also, you need to keep a cover over the viewing area to help the veggies grow, so none of the roots are visible without an adult carefully removing and replacing the cover (which is a thin piece of plastic).  Our veggies sprouted quickly and well, and then promptly fizzled out.  You place 3 ropes through the dirt extending into the tray of water on the bottom, and these are supposed to wick all the needed water to the plants. At least here in Colorado, it is too dry and the plants couldn't get enough water.  They could however mold a little and then die.  The bottom holding tank of water turns into this muddy cistern that supports fruit flies amazingly well, and is easily knocked by an eager kid trying to see the plants.  The roots weren't particularly visible. This toy has been very disappointing overall, and now I have a hunk of styrofoam that I will have to pay to bring to our special recycling center.  Hoping that our garden reignites some excitement for growing things and the wonder of nature!
text_fidelity_b: HSP Nature Toys Root-Vue Farm Multicolor, 16 Inch

Disney Sorcerer's Arena: Epic Alliances Core Set | Strategy Board Game for 2 or 4 Players Ages 13 & Up | Featuring Disney and Pixar Characters & Villains | Officially-Licensed Family Game If there was one company I can confidently say I wouldn't have expected a skirmish miniature battle game to come from, it would be a Disney mashup. Ariel and Aladdin get out there and trade punches with Gaston? I wouldn't have thought.

But that's exactly what you have here. The character mashup is novel, and the board, pieces and cards are pretty good quality, although I am not a fan of the poorly implemented version of the "Heroclix" format you see on these acrylic minis. They look good, they're just a bit difficult to fiddle with.

The game is broken into chapters, and you can really start exploring the entire set starting with Chapter 2 rules, which are a good starting point for experienced gamers and older children as well.

I'm excited to see what could come from the expansions for this game and which characters they choose to add. I don't think there are going to be a lot of people who gravitate towards Dr. Facilier, for example, so some more fan favorites would be nice to see.

Generally speaking, I really like this game and I think it will make for a fun tactical combat game for people of any age to enjoy.

Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition A nice update to an old game. I threw this in my shopping cart while out Christmas shopping. So I did not buy it on Amazon, but I am an Amazon Prime member. Cars 3 Monopoly Jr. is played just like regular Monopoly Jr. Only the pieces, property names, and chance cards have a Cars 3 theme. The rules are exactly the same. For those of you who do not know, Monopoly Jr. is a simplified version of Monopoly. You don't build houses or hotels. Mortgages on property is not a thing. The money is also way more simple. You still go to "jail." You will collect $2. However, there is literally no strategy involved. Just be the one to have the most money once one person goes bankrupt and you win. Monopoly Jr. does not end in arguments or tears (so long as your child can handle the issue of losing, which I will explain later.) Monopoly Jr. will not be the source of a deep rift through the family. You will find that you're still friends with people after the game is over. Game play is fast, you will not be playing into the wee hours of the morning trying to negotiate a loan because you landed on Park Place.

I like board games because it gets me and my son together and playing together. Screens are not involved. However, do understand that teaching 3-5 year olds how to play board games is a long process. At the end of the day, the point of playing games like this with kids this young is to get them using various skills. Skills such as paying attention, following multiple steps, counting, and taking turns. I would recommend holding off on competitive board games until after you have played a few cooperative board games. Such as [[ASIN:B006S9MUPU Peaceable Kingdom / Race to the Treasure! Cooperative Board Game]] or [[ASIN:B002V3RCE6 Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It]] Why? Because I found it helpful to play cooperative style games after playing competitive games ended in broken pieces and a broken spirit. Now at 5, it's still tough, but he's more capable of receiving the lesson that there are winners and there are losers. If your child gets really heartbroken when they lose, definitely get cooperative games before you get this one.

I would recommend this only for children starting at 5 years of age if you have spent time playing other board games, especially cooperative style board games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition

text_fidelity_a:
NERF Rebelle Slingback Blaster We are a nerf gun fighting family, so we were very happy to try out a new nerf gun. Unfortunately, it seems to have broken rather quickly. It is still usable, but there is a little stop pin that pops up into the action lever and stops you from being able to draw the sling shot back. My guess is that there was something that retracted that piece on the draw back, but now we need to push the pin down while drawing back the slingshot so you need two hands and a lot of concentration to get the blaster to fire.

Had that part been working, we are happy with the distance and accuracy of the darts. They are propelled well by the slingshot action and if it was not such a pain to get the device to fire, we would probably like it a lot. However it does not have a high rate of fire, even if it was working and requires a lot of manual loading per shot.

The other feature of this set is the secret message dart which turned out to be a little gimmicky. The dart works on a red dot filter that camoflauges the message. In our case there was a message preprinted on the dart and when you slip the dart into a red transparent tube, the red dots disappear and you get a simple one word message. We imagined the nerf equivalent to carrier pigeons to send messages covertly during battles, instead it is kind of a gimmick.

It will go into the arsenal, but we were not overwhelmed with this device. Especially since ours seems to have broken some how.

Pro
+ Good power for long shots
+ Nice Accuracy
+ Easy assembly

Cons
- Ours kind of broke
- low rate of fire
- Message dart is a low use gimmick
text_fidelity_b: NERF Rebelle Slingback Blaster

text_fidelity_a: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney This game is harder than you might think. I thought my Disney knowledge was pretty good, but I was stumped on maybe 1/3 of the questions during the two games I played. My younger Disneyphiles did about the same as me. You might remember that the caterpillar in Alice in Wonderland is blue, but can you recall the color of the flags that sit atop the hats of the Tweedles? There are some questions that require you to come up with as many as five different colors, all of which must be correct for you to gain a point. What color is Celia's dress from Monsters Inc? What three colors are seen in Go Go Tomago's superhero suit from Big Hero 6?  You need to answer quickly, by putting down your selected color cards in front of you. This is actually pretty fun and interesting. Minor characters can be especially tricky. There were a few cards with answers that we disagreed with, such as the one that said Joy from Inside Out wore a yellow dress, when we all see it as green. The answer cards all have pictures from the animated films, and sometimes the photo is not great quality. My family enjoyed this game despite these issues and found it a more challenging activity than we had anticipated. It takes almost no time to learn how to set up and play. You can fill ten minutes or half an hour easily.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney

text_fidelity_a:
Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games From the first time I saw Fallout the board game on the shelf I knew I wanted it. I have been a fan of the Fallout line since the first game. I have play almost every Fallout video game to come out and it was time to get the board game. After watching a couple videos on how to play, I was very intimidated. There seemed to be a lot of moving parts, card decks and miniatures. My fiancé and I play a most of our games together and I was thinking this would be one that would be a little out of her comfort zone.

I played through the single player game mode and enjoyed the game from the start. After the first game I knew the game was not as complicated as I thought. The game was so fun I stayed up till 3 am playing the game another 2 times. The next day I set it up for my fiancé and I, and I wasn’t disappointed. My favorite part of the game is the questing. The flavor and the ways you go about completing the quest feel like playing a video game. This is the closet I have come, in a board game, to a video game RPG. With hundreds of quest cards, the game replay is awesome. We both enjoyed the game and can’t wait to introduce it to our play group.

I play a lot of tabletop games with miniature and the piece in Fallout are top quality. Before long they will be painted and looking great on the great design of the game tiles. It really feels like you are in the wastelands. For those of you that have played the games, look forward to the quest for the Wasteland Survival Guide! All of the cards are well designed and I really like the decks are different physical sizes. There wasn’t enough room in the box for the insert and all the cards/game pieces. And there was not enough bags for all the game pieces, packaging could have been thought out a little more. Other than that, the game is great and I am looking forward to the expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Elmer’s Slime Kit Slime Supplies Include Elmer’s Metallic Glue, Elmer’s Magical Liquid Slime Activator, 4 Piece Kit [[VIDEOID:bdfa1de61b851debc9ef1be1e95922ec]] I won't lie ... I didn't buy this for the kids or the grandkids. I bought this for my 47 year old self. I had been in a funk all day and broke out this kit to get my mind reshifted. As I was sitting there popping my slime bubbles and squishing it in my hands, my husband asked if I felt better, and to a large degree, I did. This is what keeps us young.

I almost used one whole bottle of activator with the glitter glue and actually did not get all the glitter glue out of the bottle. When it finally fully turned into slime, it seemed to do so instantly. I then used my slime ball and picked up all the residue on the glass bowl and my silicone spatula. I wasn't sure what material utensils to use. But those worked well and they are not all sticky with glue. I was able to clean fully.

I put the slime in a ziplock bag and then inside a rubbermaid container and put all the fridge. The next morning it was still pliable and as I warmed it in my hands it seemed to work better.

Overall ... this was worth the price of admission. My granddaughter is small right now but when she gets bigger, this would be a fun project for her. First time making slime and it was easy and a winner. Could easily recommend this kit.

text_fidelity_a: Be Amazing! Toys Just Add Water Science Kit I really wasn't impressed. I got this to amuse myself but I think giving it to a kid would be somewhat mean.  Even the shortest experiment takes quite a while to complete and while the box says 'Just Add Water' you need more than just water. Do you have clear, 16 oz. disposable plastic cups laying around? I don't, and you need them to do several of the experiments. The kit comes with three small cups and aa plastic cap to do certain experiments in. I think Just Add Water should be just that and come with everything necessary to do all the experiments and a larger warning that every experiment requires adult supervision. It would help to mention on the box that not everything necessary is included and some take quite time which might annoy some younger, impatient, children. In the end it's okay but I didn't go crazy over it and honestly wouldn't recommend the kit to any but the most science interested children who have adults who can be around to supervise as some of the chemicals included can be harmful.

text_fidelity_a:
Tech Will Save Us Synth Wave Kit | Educational Music Toy, Ages 8 & Up What a great idea, and what poor execution. What you get here is a little music kit that looks like a kid's version of a soundboard from a recording studio. Your child does a little basic assembly, and then experiments with making sounds. And those sounds are...interesting. Not exactly a kid's first Vivaldi kit, but I don't really think that's quite the point. I'm sure it's possible to make some decent music with this - although I'm sure that it would only appeal to the youngsters.

My biggest problem is that the entire thing is made out of cardboard, and it won't last long enough for your child to actually practice with. Ours was in the trash after two days of very light use. As another reviewer mentioned, mine shipped with batteries, but those were dead.

As an idea, this is excellent. As a kit, you can pass.

text_fidelity_a: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack There are 24 different Halloween themed pieces in the box, ranging from pumpkins, to ghosts, to pirate ships, to spiders, to skulls.  The necklaces have a simple snap clasp at the end, and the bracelets have two different size settings.  The lights have three different colors including red, green, and blue.  There are three different setting to the lights with how they flash.  When first turned on, all three of the colors work great.  All the red, green and blue lights work at first.  But after about 10 minutes, the blue light starts to fade, then the green light starts to fade, until only the red light is working.  If turned off and left to sit and rest for a while, then all three light begin to light up and work again, but eventually again only the red light will remain lit.  This happened with all of the necklaces and bracelets in the box.  So as long as the lights are not needed to stay on for long periods of time, they are nice.  If needed for longer periods, two bracelets or necklaces or one of each could be used to alternate between them to give each one a rest by turning it off to refresh the colors.  So if handing these out for Halloween treats, I would recommend giving kids two in order to compensate for the lights not working all the time.
text_fidelity_b: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack

NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case I didn't expect this drone to be so tiny but no matter. It was a good introduction to drone flying for me. I had planned on attaching a camera and expanding on my photography using this.

I will definitely need a bigger drone before I can do that but at least I was able to learn how to fly a drone since this is the first time I have ever had an experience with flying one.

What I enjoy about this is that it is easy to fly and the instruction manual was fairly easy to understand. It is small and lightweight so won't really injure somebody if it happens to crash land on somebody.

The drone itself has an extra set of blades in case the blades that are already on it get broken, as well as extra batteries for the drone itself. It even comes with a screw driver so you can open the battery compartments. This way no hunting down your own tools.

The remote used to fly the drone however requires some AAA batteries, which did not come with it but you can get those just about anywhere. The control looks much like a video game controller so kids and teens who are already adept with holding a video game pad will be able to master this in no time.

The drone performed well on its intitial flight for me, and I even got it to do a few flips and rolls as well.

This is a decent little starter drone.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case

text_fidelity_a:
CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question Excellent party game from the makers of Codenames. If you've played Codenames, then you know that is a fantastic party game, but that it requires the right group - a slow or domineering player can often mean that everyone is standing around staring at the board for an hour while they dole out perfectly configured clues. It's a fun game, but it requires the right group. That's a Question is a party game that can be played by absolutely anyone, and that, in my opinion, makes it almost a superior game.

In That's a Question!, players use cards to ask A/B style "would you rather" questions in which players attempt to guess the outcome. Based on the results, you move your pawn along the track.

The rulebook is well-written and funny, and is aware that this game is a little bit weird - attempting to give a theme to a basic Q&A style game, but it works. Of course, the game is not perfect. You are limited to only asking three different main questions, although the game does provide a wide variation of answers. There are also point modification questions which allow you to muddy up the scoring in your favor. Ultimately, the scoring was the part of the game that we found most cumbersome, and the modifiers didn't help that, simply adding a little more chaos. Scoring is also modified based on how many players are playing; as this was clearly designed as a 5-6 player game, a 4-player game has a few modifications, and the 3-player game has a fairly substantial number of scoring modifications to make it more challenging. It's nothing you can't figure out, but it is not very clean.

Overall, a good party game for 5-6. The box indicates that this is a game for ages 15+, and nothing in the content of the cards makes me think that anyone from age 7 and up can't handle.
text_fidelity_b: CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question

text_fidelity_a:
Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift Wow, is this a toy? Because it is full of problems and inaccuracies. I’d like to start with my side-by-side photo showing some of the most egregious problems.
On the right hand with a black background is how it is supposed to look, and on the left is how it actually looks.
*Spinal alignment: any human with this type of alignment has a serious medical condition. The spine is supposed to have curvature in order to support the weight properly. As you can see by the Sideview of this toy, there is minimal curvature, and what little there is would lead the person to fall backwards. This is particularly problematic along the cervical and lumbar vertebrae (neck and lower back)
*The ribcage on this silly toy flares out at the bottom in a bizzarre way that doesn’t represent normal anatomy. Likewise, there is no attempt to indicate where the bone ends and the cartilaginous attachment points begin. Our ribs are not solid bone all the way from the vertebral column to the sternum. There’s supposed to be cartilage toward the midline as the ribs approach the sternum. Even if this model can’t indicate that, there should at least have been some sort of scoring or line or something.
The radius and ulna are ridiculous. Their thickness and size are not in correct proportion with the rest of the body. Also, why is this not in anatomical position?
Then there’s the attachment from the humerus to the glenoid fossa of the scapula, which cannot be seen in the poster or in this model. That’s just not how our arms are attached at all. Like the hip joint, the shoulder is a ball and socket joint, albeit a much shallower one than the hips. The way this is attached is so misleading and terrible. I can’t even deal with it. And circling back once again to the alignment of the spine, the pelvic bowl is completely wrong. It’s supposed to tilt downward much more.
So basically this is garbage. It’s not good for art, and it’s not really good for teaching either. What a shame. It did have some things going for it, but the issues I pointed out are too significant to ignore.

text_fidelity_a: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi What kid doesn't like dinosaurs?  This is perfert for your boy or girl who is into dinosaurs.  I suppose it could be considered an educational toy, but probably only marginally so.  Who says educational toys can't be fun too?  This is especially nice for a kid interested in archeology.  Contains a block of plaster that has embedded into it "DNA" stickers and a glow in the dark dinosaur.  After the fun of digging out the dinosaur and stickers with the included digging tools and brush, they are left with a dinosaur model, so even though the digging fun is over after one time (if they do it all at once), there is something to show for it.  There are also two "augmented reality" (AR) play mats that are completed with the DNA stickers that have been "excavated".  The mats when used with a cell phone and an application from the App Store (for Apple phones) or the Google Play Store (for Androids) produces a 3D dinosaur, visible on the phone.  One problem with this is that it might not work with all cell phones.  It is supposed to work with MOST Apple devices (8.0 and above).  On Android phones the only devices tested are Google Nexus Series, Samsung Galaxy S5 and Samsung Galaxy Tab.  I didn't have a cell phone to test this on, but it seems like it still might be fun even if that part doesn't work.  It's just that you might not be able to use the full capability of the kit if your phone doesn't work with the application.  Also if you give this to a child of only 8 (the lower age limit on this), they may not yet have a cell and you may not want them to have one at that age.  Since this contains many small parts, it needs to be kept away from small children, as there is a choking hazard (box says no one under 3).  I would have loved a toy like this when I was a kid.  Just remember to put down a newspaper when they are working on the plaster block in order to collect all the plaster pieces that are chipped off as they excavate.  Pricing of the kit is very reasonable.  Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set Ok first let me say, we are a "it's Lego or its crap" family. My kids evangelize on the evils of Megablocks and other brands they consider knock offs. But this is such a well engineered and detailed set that my fifteen year old wasn't even grudging when he said, this is a really good set.

And he's right, the detail on this set is super impressive. My son loves it for what seems like very authentic design from a war historian rather than a gamer, so maybe a fan of COD would like it even more.

This is a very challenging build, filled with small parts and unlike Lego that pre bags parts so you can open a single bag to do the first couple pages of instructions, mega blocks has you open 80% of the bags for the first few pages. You end up with an impressive pile of pieces out there. Also unlike Lego, mega blocks will create molded pieces specific to a model so realism can be pushed farther than Lego does. In this set, the body is filled with parts that are not just molded to shape but also in color to seem camouflaged or dirty from use. This truly lends a wonderful realism to the model. We also appreciated that markings are screen printed onto pieces rather than using stickers. Kudos for doing that it makes it feel like a quality set.

I do notice a bit more brittleness in the blocks and brick for brick the quality does not seem to match lego, but I can do little but rave over this set. It is beautiful, it took my son and I working together to get this done in several hours. And once done, this is a beautiful set for display.

Well done Mega Block, you are doing what I thought was impossible, you are winning us over from Lego.

*** additional

My son wanted me to mention that the instructions were hard, I would use challenging. But one thing I did forget, I am partially colorblind and often found it hard to distinguish colors in the instructions if it was not daylight.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set

Hot Wheels Track Builder Spiral Stack-Up Track Set This HOT WHEELS TRACK BUILDER SPIRAL STACK-UP set is a terrific choice for expanding an existing Hot Wheels track layout, as long as you have a fair amount of floor or table space. It's a really large stunt that's about five feet long when it's assembled according to the boxed instructions (though the launcher ramps can be rearranged, using two towers instead of one, to use less space).

The way this set works, is that the first car launched from the top of the tower launches two more cars (not included with the set) as it speeds down the ramp, then triggers a release that dumps a car off the second level of the "box" located at the end of the double ramp, until it finally exits the stunt through the lower level of the "box". The second car that is launched (by the first car) speeds down a long ramp that is connected near the top of the tower, and exits the stunt. The third car that is launched travels down a short ramp and stops on the second level of the exit "box", waiting to for the first car to dump it.

There's a lot of action that makes me smile in this track builder set. Also, the two cars that actually exit the setup have a lot of momentum left that will carry them elsewhere in a well-designed layout. One of the best things about this setup is that all three cars usually complete the entire run flawlessly, without jumping the track or losing momentum or stopping too soon. The "Nitrium" car that comes with the set is a fairly heavy one, because the set works best with a weighty car starting in the top position.

For me, this Hot Wheels playset was a little more challenging to assemble than others that I've set up. As always, the key thing is to identify your parts correctly, and to keep looking until you find the right place to make a connection if you don't understand the instructions right away. The color-coding of the plastic parts helped me with one confusing part--the set has two red launcher arms that attach to a yellow base, and one gray launcher lever that attaches to a gray base. In my customer photos, there are three cars loaded into the set--the orange/white car at the very top is the included Nitrium car.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Spiral Stack-Up Track Set

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored Excellent game for toddlers and preschoolers! This collaborative game (everyone works as a team) is so easy to learn and play. For two to four players, the game board is three piece, six foot long puzzle. After you set up the board, everyone has a marker. There are about ten magnifying glasses, a cardboard boat, six cardboard pieces of food, cards, a spinner, and a timer. The goal? Everyone has to make it to the boat and the boat has to make it to Picnic Island before the pigs eat all the food. The youngest person goes first.

Each player spins the spinner. The arrow lands on either a Move, a Bug, or a Pig. If you spin to a Move, you move your marker that many spaces and the next player goes. If you spin to a Pig, the Pigs "eat" one picnic food item and you take one food items away and spin again. If you spin to a bug, you pull a card. When you pull the card, you have to look throughout the game board for those items (almost Where's Waldo style). For example, if you pull a card with pictures of "balloons", you set the timer and look all around the game board for balloons. You use the magnifying glasses to mark that you've found one. When the timer is up you count how many "balloons" you found and all players move that many spaces. So if you found three balloons, everyone moves three spaces. Once everyone lands on the boat, everyone takes turns to spin to move the boat to Picnic Island. So long as the pigs haven't eaten all the food, everyone wins!

This game is a great concept for kids who have issues with winning and losing. Especially at 3 and 4 years of age when other skills like patience, taking turns, and working together are my main focus for my son rather than learning to be a gracious loser (I hope to teach him this later). Focusing and patience are the skills that this game builds as my son loves being a helper and the idea that he is helping for everyone to win actually helps him to focus and be a little more patient. The game also helps with counting and memory. I am pleasantly surprised by this game and I highly recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage I have been a Barbie fan since I was a child, many years ago. My now 16 year old daughter was a huge fan when she was young. I even have several "in the box" collector Barbies. The Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage just doesn't seem as high quality as the many Barbie products I have purchased over the years. It's definitely not a collector's item. The price is decent and you get a complete set of a doll, unicorn, and carriage. The plastic carriage flexes when you apply pressure. It doesn't feel like it's going to easily break, but it's not as rigid as other Barbie products. The carriage door opens and closes.  The wheels rotate easily and give a pretty smooth ride. The details on the carriage are nice. There are lots of textures to make it more realistic.  The unicorn is a sturdier plastic piece. The doll has the rigid, no bend legs. Her facial details are what you expect on Barbies. She has a removable crown. Her top is molded plastic and not removable. Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. Overall, it's an attractive looking set, but the quality is disappointing. With all that said, I think young Barbie fans would probably still enjoy it.

text_fidelity_a:
Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.
text_fidelity_b: Asmodee Hit Z Road

Party Charades Game – Contains 550 charades – Great Family Game for 2 or More Players Ages 10 and up by Outset Media TOTAL CLASSIC...!!! No matter what type of spin you put on charades… It will always be a solid go to/staple for any group- no matter ones talents- young or, old! My group includes a player with a disability.. and I love the fact, this can be played in teams and eliminates the worry if, one must be left out if they can read or not- this game can be easily tweaked not to exclude anyone! (with teams we pair up 2-3 players per group.. sprinkling those who need extra help amongst all teams and we take turns acting. Then, when an adult adds input/guidance, it’s done without ever appearing like “help” to those who can’t.. instead, it appears like a natural collaborative decision!) with party charades we actually found it to be quite helpful for adults as well to play in teams!! Some of us adults were a bit clueless to the “pop culture references!“ So, it was great to have a younger kiddos be knowledgeable on the team.. The help flows both ways with this style of set up... it’s perfect!!

Note: you can tweak the rules OR.. follow included instructions.. OR, Control the time by playing “best out of five rounds” etc. charades is a must-have for any game covered.. One more perk- Party charades definitely can help keep the mid adolescent teen group entertained as well- (this is big when playing family game night- anyone with a 17yr. old boy with coolness attitude can attest! The Party charades version actually keeps the teens entertained..!!)

One last note/hack: we do allow for a set # of “cell phone sneaks” if no one knows the person or, catchphrase reference on the card- I recommend this just to keep the game rolling.. definitely must limit the “sneak peek” to 15sec. just enough to know Who/what but, better we found it’s better then skipping multiple cards.
Loved party charades so much- I bought 2nd copy for my daughter to take back to her dorm room… During Covid quarantine this will bring endless fun in the dorm room, I’m certain of it..!! Hands-down recommend for sure. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!

It's not like you can play with the erase pad in your hands or anything, so it shouldn't matter, but I just wanted to mention that because in previous bundles Osmo used to include a high quality dry erase board. You should also know that any dry erase board will work. You can buy the biggest board you can find at an office store, and put this Osmo base on it and it will work.

As I've mentioned in my other Osmo reviews, what type of case you have for your iPad will determine how often you play Osmo games. Some of us have very rugged kid cases for our children that are hard to remove. We have those colorful big rubber rugged cases for our kids and it is a chore to remove, put back, remove, put back. So I don't think we play Osmo games as much as we should. If you want your children to get the most out of Osmo, you first need to get an easier case for your iPad, so that the case doesn't become a deterrent. .

Lastly, the compatibility should be emphasized... "All iPads except Generation 1, iPad Pro 11-inch and iPad Pro 12.9-inch. The minimum iOS version needed is iOS 9."

As for the games itself, they are top notch, and there are plenty of YT videos to learn more about them. 5 stars!

Winning Moves Games Classic Twister Ah, the memories I have from playing Twister when I was 16 and drove a red Firebird. Paul, who I wished was my boyfriend was interested in me only as a friend, so the best way I had to get close to him was to invite friends over for a game of Twister. Memories are interesting because I recall exactly what he and I were both wearing -- he in a light blue oxford Gant shirt and me in my self designed and sewn striped wide legged hip-hugger slacks, solid shirt and matching striped vest. I can't tell you who else was there, but we had a full house and we had a blast with my little sister calling our moves and tattling when we were having TOO much fun.

[[ASIN:B00HVTH2MC Classic Twister]] can be played by most ages, provided the bodies are somewhat agile and the individuals are not really shy. The vinyl mat allows for between 2 and 4 people, no more. A game lasts less than 15 minutes usually with the winner being the person who remains on the mat without falling over. A designated person who is not on the mat spins the little plastic on cardboard wheel and those playing place the appropriate limb on a designated spot. For color blind people, your friends will let you know where to put that foot or hand, I guarantee. It is a really fun physical game that stimulates conversation and breaks the ice. I noticed that there are several versions of the game available as of today but cannot tell you what the differences are or why the prices vary. What I can tell you is that this is a really amusing game for all ages, even those who can't actually do the moving but can participate from the peanut gallery.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Classic Twister

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain My boys(3, 5, and 7) had fun with this kit, overall, but there's really not much to it.

Basically, you mix up cornstarch, gelatin(both provided), and water, through various steps, and then pour it into the provided molds. This project has to be done in several steps, with waiting periods in between. With my children being so young, the wait was annoying. Thankfully, we did the project on a day that it was beautiful outside, and there was plenty of play in between, so it could have been worse.

After the brain/eye has set up in the mold, you'll dump it out, and paint it. You get paint(food coloring) in the kit, and can mix it up to what colors you want. My children were disappointed that they couldn't get the colors to look as bright as they do in the pictures. I even helped with this attempt. The colors were just very dull, and our brain didn't look anywhere near how bright it was shown to be. I'd recommend using real paint, as opposed to food coloring. I think the results will be better.

The molds are reusable, so as long as you don't mind buying more gelatin and cornstarch, you can make as many brains and eye balls as you'd like.

Overall, this is a fun little experiment if you're studying brains or eyes. It's very simple, though, despite the several steps, which make it time consuming.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Nanotechnology Science Experiment Kit Do your kids enjoy science? Mine certainly do and they love anything that is interactive and involves more than simply reading a book. This is why they love science kits the way they do and one kit they really enjoy is the Thames and Kosmos Nanotechnology Kit.

I have purchased countless science kits over the years for my youngsters and my kids have played with each, often with varying degrees of interest. The problem with many science kits is that the package doesn’t really contain enough to conduct the experiments- you are required to supply almost all of the materials, measuring devices, etc. yourself. Another problem is that many of science kits contain experiments that are too simple and don’t really challenge any child beyond the age of six. But with Thames and Kosmos Nanotechnology Kit, my children and I quickly discovered that a store purchased science kit can be fun, challenging, and complete. You know the moment you open the box that this science kit is different and the uniqueness only serves to encourage children to open the manual and start conducting experiments. Just looking at the contents reminded me of the science from high school.

The science experiments in this kit revolve around the world of nanotechnology and they serve to educate children on this tiny, micro world. The experiments deliver on their promises and kids really do learn a great deal. Some of the experiments are actually more complex than expected so if your kids are younger, you may need to step in and offer your assistance. I didn’t mind at all, in part because, as I completed the experiments with my kids, I found that I enjoyed the experience just about as much as they did.

Another added touch I like with this kit is the included game board. This is a great idea, because the board helps to further educate children by showing how different experiments relate to each other. Everything is diagrammed and once kids see the visual representation, they will better understand how each experiment works and how things tie together.

Educational toys are great and make for an important diversion from the mindless drabble so common to most forms of child amusement. Thames and Kosmos Nanotechnology is one of the best science kits I have ever encountered and while the price is a little higher than that of other kits, it is certainly money well invested and it will help develop a child’s understanding and interest in science to levels you never would have thought possible.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Nanotechnology Science Experiment Kit

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys My Giant Busy Box Craft Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity I'm not the best at doing any kind of organized crafts with my children. My style is more along the lines of giving them art supplies and letting them create what they want, and honestly, that's what I'll always prefer for them. They really enjoy projects that have a somewhat defined end result sometimes, though, and so it's kits like this that come to my rescue. Thankfully, they still get to be a bit creative with these projects, and while end results might look similar for many children, they probably won't look just alike.

There are 16 projects within this box, with lots and lots of little pieces. There are only instructions for 5 of the projects, but really, with those instructions, you can easily figure out the rest of them. I would have preferred for each of the projects to have been individually packaged to make things easier. I have had kits like that, and they make things a breeze for this disorganized mama. This kit does need a bit more organization on my part, but it's really not that bad. The supplies are all separated into different bags, and there are even extra bags for me to divide out some of the supplies. I could turn my children loose with everything and see what they come up with, but I prefer separating each project(at least for the most part), so that my children can choose which one they want to do, and not worry about running out of supplies before all the project are finished. Between my 3 children, I'll get 5 rainy days out of this box, with one extra. (I can't beat that!) ;) Plus, the included finger crayons can be used after all the projects are finished.

This is a really nice box of crafts. Especially if you're like me, and don't do so well with organized crafts, this is an excellent way to give your children some fun with crafts.

3Doodler Start Emoji & Symbols Doodleblock Kit with 2 Pack of Refill Filaments (3D Pen Not Included) First things first: There are two different popular 3Doodler pens: 3Doodler Start and 3Doodler Create. Each uses different filaments and they are NOT interchangeable. The two 3Doodler pen models use different melting temperatures: Start is cooler; Create is hot. This pack is for the 3Doodler START -- it will NOT work with 3Doodler Create! Be sure you know which 3Doodler you have.

That said -- this is a nice addition to the 3Doodler Start collection. I've been using my 3Doodler to create embellishments for paper crafts -- primarily hand-crafted greeting cards and a little scrapbooking. The emojis and symbols in this set work well in terms of size -- perfect for my cards. I use the heart and star most often, as well as the asterisk, pound sign, and ampersand. There are two packs of filaments: blue, red, green, gray and white, mint/aqua, yellow and orange. Good colors that work with a variety of color schemes.

Overall, a good refill set with the addition of the emoji/symbol DoodleBlocks. I like it!

text_fidelity_a: Disney Minnie Mouse Walk & Dance Unicorn Feature Plush, Multi-Color, Ages 3+ (13616) This is a cute but limited combo. It arrived in a plain box with a gift type label printed on. Both Minnie and the unicorn are hard plastic covered with soft material. They are not soft like plush toys. They are not huggable. Minnie and the unicorn can communicate if within a short distance. For Minnie to "walk" the prong on her finger gets inserted into the hole in the unicorn's back. The unicorn drags her along. Minnie doesn't walk: she rolls. There are wheels in her feet. She does sing, not as annoying as Frozen but is does get tiring fast. The unicorns makes horse like sounds. Her dancing consists of moving a leg and shaking her head. Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset Out of all the newer 2016 Track Builder Releases, this in my opinion, is the best! There are multiple ways of setting up various layouts which the manual suggests, and good variety of pieces, though straight track are lacking as usual. The star of this show is no doubt, the duel booster! It's very "next gen-ish", as it looks nothing like boosters that have been around forever. What makes it unique is the way it is set up. There's your usual battery-eating power brick (this uses 4 D cells), but both boosters are independent from the power source. They simply plug in to the battery block, so you can place them away from each other, giving your layout twice the power to shoot your cars around. You don't have to use both boosters, but why wouldn't you? What's more interesting is, the booster's rollers are now vertical, instead of horizontal. When a HW car enters, a single rubber roller grips it from above and launches it out, and both boosters pack a punch! I only wish the connecting cords could have been longer, as you can't place the boosters too far way from each other.

The white support towers are one of the newer pieces found in this series, as they can be placed horizontally or vertically to support tracks. Each tower offers a number of node connections, so tracks can be connected at various heights using the pivot points. The pivot points are brilliant little button-like gizmos that slide easily slide into any track. Now when you snap your track into any of the towers, you can actually rotate and angle your track with much freedom. All in all, it's a very roller coaster-style approach to track building, and a good one at that.

As far as the layouts go, there are a few duel shoot outs as in...gravity drop to booster, through loop, then off to space (hopefully, a carpeted one). These are short lived, 2 second runs but kids will have fun launching their cars simultaneously (this set only comes with one car of course). One interest layout features a continuous run where both boosters work together to continuously shoot your cars through a figure 8 course. Cars zoom around and eventually crash, so it becomes a survivor game. The sample courses won't hold a child's attention for long periods, but they can experiment on their own, and combine the pieces with other sets.

And finally, the box. The new, thicker cardboard box also doubles up as an extra stunt accessory. Perforated cut outs allow tracks to be integrated for even more variety. If your kid rather keep the box, then get ready for a shock: You can actually fit all the pieces back in the box for storage. I know, right?

Overall, this is example of Mattel heading in the right direction.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.

Simba Steffi Love - Hawaii Camper, Multicolor I am overall satisfied with my order of the Simba Steffi Love Camper Set. This arrived very well packaged for shipping. It was not overly difficult to remove from the box as most of the securing straps simply untied. There were several pieces of clear tape that needed to be removed. I do like that this set included a Steffi Love doll. It's an overall nice doll with articulated ankles and knees. I do wish that the elbows were also articulated, but they are not. She has shoes, a simple dress and sunglasses. She has underpants imprinted on her plastic pelvis. I do not advise to remove the elastic on her hair as the plugged hair will show the widely spaced hair plugs and be less than attractive.

The first impression of the playset inside the packaging is that it's very cute and attractive. The camper itself is not as durable as I had hoped. This will not stand up to rough play. I would not at all advise this to be accessible to toddlers or careless children because if one tried to use it as a seat or step-stool, it would break easily. The wheels are held in place with a metal rod, this would be a safety hazard if it came out of place. The many small accessories are also not appropriate for very small children as they could pose a choking hazard. There is not enough leg room in the two front seats for the doll's legs, they must be bent to the side or the doll has to sit sideways. Not all of the doors are well-molded to close completely. Some stickers are included, which is nice as one side of the camper already is decorated with stickers, leaving the opposite side blank. Several packets of accessories are included so the dolls can use props for various activities such as cooking, lounging and even showering. The small accessories are the best point of this playset.

I personally do not find this camper set to be a good value at it's current price point. There are too many issues that will lead to frustration in play. Primarily, the type of plastic material used to mold the camper is prone to failure as it's not at all durable. The play patterns of most small children will prove to be the source of frustration or failure of the toy. This type of plastic is prone to shattering and can produce sharp edges if broken. For many children, this will be a short-lived disposable toy. This would be most ideal for children that play gently and are able to keep small toys well organized and enjoy playing with fashion dolls. The camper itself measures about 22" long, 11" wide and 9 1/2" tall. This will need a significant amount of storage space, and would not easily withstand being stored stacked with other toys in a toybox. This would be best 'parked' under a bed, in a closet or on a shelf between play sessions to avoid a tripping hazard. I hope that my experience with this camper set is helpful as you kindly click the button below.
text_fidelity_b: Simba Steffi Love - Hawaii Camper, Multicolor

Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor [[VIDEOID:c9ed210fcea7bd15ff238268da66c6e5]] I really liked this classic game of Sorry. I hadn't played this game in over 25 years, so this is a fun blast from the past.

The game isn't as silly or as random as I remember it. For a random move your pawn game, there is actually a decent amount of strategy involved.

The rules were a bit confusing, since they used the old 1959 rules. Here's my summary of the rules: You can only move your pawns out of start if you pick a 1, 2, or sometimes a Sorry card. If you get a 1 or a 2, then you only move out to the first circle. You only slide when you get on the first part of the slide. If you can't move, you don't move, and you need an exact count to get into the Home square. Follow the rest of the instructions on the cards.

Pros:
+It's possible to win no matter how far behind a player is
+Great rendition of a classic game
+A lot of fun
+Great for any ages

Cons:
-The rules are a bit confusing. I had to clarify some of the rules on the internet.
-The game starts out very slowly
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

text_fidelity_a:
Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists. This kit was made to help families like ours. I am a stay at home mom to four kids (11yo and younger). Prior, I was an artist and earned a Special Ed and a Rehabilitation degree. My background has been useful because we ended up a household full of ADHD, severe anxiety, learning and speech disabilities, plus more. We have been using this set for three weeks now and it has proven invaluable. It truly was an excellent find.

We do not own the original set (with the Dove on the box), but I suspect this new version is probably an upgraded improvement of the first box set. It looks very similar, except now there appears have some new (maybe better) ideas and slightly more guidance in this new version. I don't mean to imply this set is a duplicate of the first set, nor am I trying to discourage you from buying both. I simply don't know. I came to the conclusion that these were similar after reading the reviews for the first one. Had I been given the option to chose between the two sets, I would have chosen to start with the newer set I am reviewing here today. Simply because of the changes that were made.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT:

- Most of the cards appear to have between 200 to 300 words. Each activity lasts about 5 minutes per card, give or take. Of course each could be longer or shorter because you get decide how much time you want to spend.

- This newer set has a total of 24 meditation activity cards. 18 of the 24 are guided scenarios. The 18 cards are "story like, short guided imaginary meditation with different scenes that people can imagine themselves taking a part of.” Meaning they ask you to concentrate and imagine yourself in a particular story line (like "walking through the woods" or "stargazing on a warm summer night", for example).
- 6 of those 18 cards mentioned above focus on our senses (touch, taste, etc).
- In addition to the above 18, there are 6 more "positive affirmation" cards. These affirmations address different times of day (morning or bedtime) -or- feelings (anger, stress, etc).

OTHER COMPARISON NOTES:
- From what I can tell, the original set only appears to have 23 guided imaginary "walk through the woods" type scenarios. It does not specifically explore common human experiences that center around feeling or our body.
- The Legend Card is unique to this set. The Legend is more of a guide chart that will help you quickly find the most useful card, depending on the your feelings/needs at the moment­.
- Both sets have the same breathing exercise card.

MY POSITIVES:

- This set is excellent quality. The cards are very nice and are made of a thick paperboard. They are technically laminated, though it wouldn't consider it a plastic waterproof type of covering. It feels more like a wax coating that is water resistant. But it is a sturdy material.
-This truly is an activity for all ages. Kids 6 and younger will probably need guidance. Around 6 or 7, this could probably be an independent activity for most kids. But this mediation set is NOT just for kids. I think pre-teens, teens, and even adults can still benefit from these cards. I wish I made more time to use them myself, tbh.
- These have been excellent in helping everyone in our house decompress and cope with our daily stressors.
- I think this encourages and even teaches how to use our imaginations better (an essential skill!!!).
- It has increases our awareness of self worth. And in a sense, these also teach us to take responsibility for some of our thoughts and feelings too. These activities seem to encourage future motivation and action too.
-This kit is secular and inclusive. Meaning it is not religions in any way. And Many people are represented in the images. The language the cards use, and the activities are age and gender neutral. The suggested scenarios are something anyone can envision.
- And the art is beautiful.

THE NEGATIVES:
- The box is terrible. It's too small. It's impossible to find the one card the Ledged Guide tells you to grab without taking out the entire stack. And it's a pain putting the cards away. I'm going to have to come up with a better storage system.
- There are spelling mistakes, improper punctuation, and unnecessary capitalization. If it had been here or there, I wouldn't have said anything. Nor am I in a position to judge. But it's really bad and does not feel educational.
- The price feels a bit steep initially. However, I think if you make it a goal to give this set a real try and use it for a little while, I think you'll see the $30 price tag actually feels like a good deal.

Overall, I definitely recommend trying this. It is unique and I wish I had know about the original set years ago. But I think this newer set was an even better find. We couldn't be happier. Thank you for reading this ridiculously long review and I hope it helped make your decision easier.
text_fidelity_b: Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists.

MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS This is a set of 3 succulent planter pots, each mini set is bagged separately with its pieces and instructions.

The bags for each mini set are unnumbered, you’ll need to open all at the start. All of them except the bags of round 1x1 plates. The studs are meant to simulate dirt, and you don’t attach them to anything, simply pour them in the pots. I didn’t use the studs, the pots are really full and I couldn’t see the bases anyway.

The pieces mostly stay together on the succulents themselves. But some of the pieces are loose, especially the connections between succulent and pot. To build the sets, you assemble the various succulents and then attach them inside the pot. Most of the succulents clip into the base with bar pieces. Imagine a piece that looks like: —C. Sometimes those clips didn’t hold very well, so sticking a second succulent in was enough to dislodge the first.

Getting all the succulents inside each pot takes some finessing and patience. The finished sets are display pieces, not for play -- they are a bit delicate.

The instructions are usually easy to understand, though sometimes I did have to go back or flip forward to understand where a piece went. Some of the colors are off. For example, dark pink in the instructions are really orange pieces. The color differences made some of the sets harder than others, since I couldn’t always tell which piece to use.

I did like that the set include extra stamen options. Getting to choose my own flower colors among the options, or even mix them, was fun.

Arm & Hammer Baking Soda Color Creations, Island Green, 1 Lb I love to have the ability to bring out different ingredients to make either natural body care, or crafts. Having colored baking soda seemed like a great idea, but there is a problem..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a pound of baking soda which is colored up to what I would call a shamrock green. it is housed in a thin plastic bag which is supposed to be able to be cut and reseal. The green color itself is not overbearing. There is a recipe for clay on the package along with tips on how to use this.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This would have been a more pleasant experience, but the plastic bag this comes in is very fragile. This came to me exuding green powder all over me and the mail delivery person. Upon examination, the bag itself is very easily punctured and cracked. That means that storing the baking soda back in the bag is a BAD idea. If you drop it, it will break.

As for what we made, I did a very small batch of bath bomb and it was fun. I used the white swirled with the green and it worked out okay. The green did not stain the tub badly and seemed to rinse out pretty well. As for making baking soda clay ornaments, I tried a sample of that and it was not bad either- the green is great to use in Christmas decorations from the clay/dough.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a pretty good idea, but the packaging is awful. Even if it does not come broken, it is hard to reseal due to the soda getting in the plastic reseal slide. I would like it better if it came in a tub- with a window that is clear- somewhat bendable and not fragile.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. This needs to come in a tub that has a bit of resilience to it and is see through too. It just is not practical to use or ship with such fragile plastic packaging. The product itself is okay, and worth three stars, but the way they market it needs to be better.
text_fidelity_b: Arm & Hammer Baking Soda Color Creations, Island Green, 1 Lb

LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.

Crayola Crayon Maker with Story Studio Kids love to color, so a toy like the Crayola Crayon Maker would seem like an ideal addition to any home with children under the age of eight. Coloring with your child's own crayons he/she just made would seem like a great creative addition to an already fun activity.

Unfortunately, the fun with this toy stops at the concept itself. Making crayons is a great idea, but this device has several issues that prevent it from living up to its potential. The way it works is simple enough- you place the crayon material on a tray and set a timer. The heat from the lightbulb melts the crayons, which are then poured into a mold. You then wait for them to cool and they are ready to use. This sounds simple, but there are all sorts of problems along the way, and many of them seem to stem from Crayola's desire to apparently make the crayon maker as safe as possible.

One issue is with the locking mechanism. As you move from one step to the next, the device locks itself and you cannot unlock until the cycle is completed. For example, when the crayons are transferred to the molds, there is no way to unlock at this point. You are forced to wait for the crayons to cool before you can open. Issues with the timer are similarly frustrating- if your child accidentally sets the timer prematurely, you have no choice but to wait until it is finished. You cannot move the timer forward. You have to wait for it to complete its cycle.

Another issue I have is with the melting phase. There is no buzzer or anything to tell you that the crayons are ready to transfer to the molds. Thus, you have to pay close attention and make sure you are there, when the light bulb goes off, ready to transfer. If you don't act promptly, the crayons will cool off and solidify in the tray.

These frustrations might be tolerable enough for more patient types, but there is one ultimate frustration is enough to make you want to give up and ask for a refund. I am referring to the amount of crayons included in each package. You get only enough to make two crayons! You heard me correctly- two small crayons! When you consider what you have to go through just to get a pair of crayons and when you consider how inexpensive crayons are, it makes you wonder why you even bothered to obtain this device in the first place.

Making crayons can be fun and there are many ways to make them using ordinary household heat sources, utensils, etc. I recommend making crayons the old fashioned way and skipping the Crayola Crayon Maker completely. It is a good idea gone bad and I can only hope that Crayola has a new and improved version in the making.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Crayon Maker with Story Studio

There’s not a ton to build here, compared to other sets in this price point. There’s only 40 pieces in the set, many of which are small vet tools. The cube is the big draw.

My favorite part for this set, and actually for all the play cubes, is that the surprise is always the same animal. For example, Mia always comes with a rabbit. It’s the color of the animal that is the surprise. The colors are pink, purple, blue, or gold.

The box includes a mini poster that shows all the play cubes and the pets they come with. The poster also indicates there will be a Series 2 of the play cubes.

Learn the basics in 5 minutes and average game play is about an hour (maybe an hour and a half with 5 or more people).
