Jurassic World Bite 'n Fight Tyrannosaurus Rex in Larger Size with Realistic Sculpting, Articulation and Dual-Button Activation for Tail Strike and Head Strikes, Ages 4 and Older Wow! Wow wow wow!

That's pretty much what you're going to hear when you present this gift to a small person. A bunch of wows, and then a bunch of roaring after you get it out of the package and they start playing with it. There are two buttons in the middle of the T Rex, one of which works the tail and the other of which works the head and snapping jaws. The buttons are a little hard to press effectively to make the action occur, so small T Rex fans might have a little more trouble activating things than one might like, but there's a next to it, which bigger guys will soon figure out.

I picked this up because I have a Jurassic world toys truck, which is supposed to hold the dinosaur in the back. There's like this included shell that comes up over the top and is supposed to have the dinosaur's head sticking up out of the shell, and I thought that this T Rex, being from the same line, would fit gracefully in the back of that truck. Nope, this thing is huge. Huge huge. Check the measurements before expecting this to dovetail with any other toys because T Rex is a big dude.

The size and the snapping jaws action really contributes to the awesome gift presentation this makes. Does it have a lot of long-term play potential? I'm not really sure that it does, frankly. I think in our house, once I get tired of tripping over it, I'm going to relegate it to being a backyard toy and just allow it to slowly stop working. However, right now the kids are having a blast creating scenes for T Rex to come in and stomp. He is particularly good it crashing through block towers.
text_fidelity_b: Jurassic World Bite 'n Fight Tyrannosaurus Rex in Larger Size with Realistic Sculpting, Articulation and Dual-Button Activation for Tail Strike and Head Strikes, Ages 4 and Older

text_fidelity_a:
Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ At the time of this review, this set is under $10. If it were over $10, I would probably subtract a star. This is definitely beginner, student quality.
But if you have a child, or maybe you are just looking for something reasonably priced to see if you enjoy sketching, even though it's geared for children, this set can't be beat.

The main reason it gets five stars, is that you get four different hardness levels of graphite pencils. Perfect for experimenting with your creativity and making a sketch come alive. And it's less messy than charcoal sticks, so once again, it's the perfect introduction to nurture a child's creativity and talent.
To make it even better, there's a little pamphlet to encourage and explain how to get your feet wet. I really like that the emphasis is on the fact that there are no mistakes, that each line is is just fine. So important for children that might be discouraged that they aren't instantly a great artist, forgetting or not understanding that being an artist is only 10% talent and 90% learning and desire.
It might be only a folded over page, but it covers various techniques. All is written in a way that kids and young adults can easily follow. This set is cured for ages 7 and up.
And once again, a 7-year-old doesn't need professional quality pencil sharpeners or paper. You can see in the photograph how thin the paper pages are, and how cheesy the little pencil sharpener is. Cheesy, but perfect for the purpose.

This well thought out set is just what I would expect from Farber-Castell. Their supplies are favored by the students and professionals worldwide.

I hope that this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not this set is right for you or a special child. Kids seem to be passionate about something one minute, and totally change the next. This little set is a very small investment, but of course, little investments add up.

xxoo
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+

text_fidelity_a:
Battat - Deluxe Wooden Train – Classic Toy Train Set with Magnetic Trains, Tracks, Vehicles, Buildings & Accessories for Kids Aged 3 & Up (102Pc), Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington Trains are a classic toy. Most of them are electronic, high- tech in nature, and can be made to look and sound like an authentic train, in small scale of course. But there is also something to be said for a train that isn’t electronic and requires imagination more than anything. This is what you get with the Battat Deluxe Wooden Train.

This train set comes with track, train, and a large number of accessories. It’s easy to assemble the track because it interlocks with almost no effort. Setting up the accessories takes time, but this is perfect for the more imaginative child and parents will enjoy just sitting back and letting their youngster take over.

The quality level of this set is good and the pieces are made from wood. Once assembled, it covers about four feet by three feet of space, so it will fit on most tables. If you don’t have available table space to spare, just set it up on the floor instead. A smooth surface is best, of course, but a flat carpet may work, too.

With the train cars, they are held together by magnets and this is good enough for this type of train. One issue some people may have is with the track. The interlocking isn’t very secure and that means the track is easy to bump out of place. Metal tracks hold together better, but this isn’t a huge issue, really. Most kids won’t mind this aspect of the set up.

There are some really cool electronic trains on the market, but trains that require manual movements and that lack sound and other automated features can be just as fun. The Battat Deluxe Wooden Train is good for this purpose. It’s made with a good deal of quality in mind and it’s great for stimulating a child’s imagination.

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

Mancala Board Game Classics Stones Game Wooden Folding Strategy Game Travel Game for Adult 18 Inch Set I love mancala. It is a fun game to play. Well, except with my very competitive husband. But still it is nice to have handy. I decided to get this set so we can bring it with us and then fold it up to put it away. Let's take a look.

BOARD
The board is nice. It is a good folding board. There are decent sized wells in it, and the end collection spots are good sized too. The finish is rough. It really is not nearly as smooth as it could be. However, it has a thin coating on it that helps a bit.

CLASP
The clasp on mine works well.

GLASS PIECES
This has a carrying case with plenty of glass pieces in it. We play the 6 pieces per well version so having these pieces is helpful. There are many colors and finishes so you can have fun using it. There are more pieces than we use so if any break, there are plenty to replace them with.

INSTRUCTIONS
The instructions are basic, but doable. I suggest looking online for more details if you prefer to learn different ways to play.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you like mancala, this is a fun game. The board is a bit rough in finish, but this is still decent for a quick game. There are plenty of pieces.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I wish there was a way to store the pieces with the board instead of a separate bag. I will have to get a case of some sort to store this in for easy carrying and to keep these together. I also wish the sanding was a bit better on this and finish too.

3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold First off, with the START, the main thing to know is it is safe. The temperature of the plastic and the pen tip is low enough, if you accidentally touch it, you won't get hurt. This is great for anyone who isn't fireproof.

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. With this, I wiped it off and continued along. That ability, to learn and not worry that much about a beginner mistake, is exactly what attracted me to this. Think of it as training wheels.

The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. They have additional kits over here [[ASIN:B01CL1FCEY 3Doodler Start Rocket & Robot DoodleBlock Kit]] not just the robot, but a page full of them, if you get tired of hexbugs.

text_fidelity_a:
ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls 3 stars

This stroller is very cute, and it is nice that it is in gender-neutral colors, so that boy children as well as girl children can enjoy this stroller. It can be used not just to hold baby dolls, but also stuffed animals.

This toy stroller resembles a typical human-baby, umbrella stroller in design and functionality. The difference between this and a real stroller, though, other than the miniature sizing, is that it is not sturdy. Therefore, there is a safety element in that your child may easily push or lean harder on its handles than it is built to withstand, and end up tripping and falling on top of or tumbling headfirst over it. If you have stairs in your house, this in particular could lead to a dangerous injury.

A major factor contributing to this flimsiness issue is the fact that the wheels are not at all strong and, overall, this toy is very cheaply made. It is certainly not constructed to stand up to the rather rugged treatment a toddler or preschooler would give to a toy like this.

In short, this doll stroller is certainly not a case of, "You get what you pay for." Because of the expensive price of this and all other Adora doll accessories, you'd think you'd be getting something really sturdy and long-lasting. Unfortunately, that is not the case with this stroller.
text_fidelity_b: ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls

Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count I'll admit it: I'm an adult who loves to color. I find it a great way to relax, and there are some amazing "coloring books for adults" gaining popularity these days (Johanna Basford, Angie Grace, etc.). And there are whole communities of "colorists" popping up on social media.

So naturally, I'm looking for different mediums to use when I color. I've used colored pencils and gel pens, so I figured it was time to branch out into the marker arena. Someone suggested starting with these as they're water-based rather than alcohol-based, and Amazon has them at a good price, so I got the 50-ct set.

Overall, I'm pleased. There is a good selection of colors, several shades of each, which helps to bring some variety into th mix.

What I DON'T like (and this seems to be a problem for ALL coloring mediums): the actual color of the pen/pencil/etc. almost NEVER matches the color of the cap/barrel/etc. I realize that colors will look different depending on the type a "color" of paper used as the background, but seriously, some of these are WAY off. I find myself having to make a "cheat sheet" on the paper I'm using just so I can get a clear picture of how the various colors REALLY look.

Like I said, this isn't just a problem with Crayola, but they make it a little more difficult because the pens have NO distinguishing markings on them whatsoever to designate a color number or code. I ended up putting little pieces of masking tape on each pen and numbering them myself just so I can keep the color charts coordinated.

All that aside, they work great once you figure out the colors. Colors are vibrant, and I had very little "bleed through" or feathering in an Angie Grace book. Bleed through and feathering depend a great deal on the paper used, so bear that in mind and ALWAYS test before coloring.

Overall​, I like these - don't "love" them, but they're good quality water-based markers at a very good price.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count

Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots We've only had this a few days so far, but my kids love it so far! They and their neighborhood friends were playing almost non-stop this entire weekend. It's a pretty unique concept and not at all what I expected coming from the original battleship: Rather than the game of strategy (and sometimes just luck!) that the traditional battleship is, this is mostly a game of skill. There is still some strategy in how you align your boats, but rather than try to determine where the other player's position is, you can see their board and have to toss one of the included ping-pong balls into the holes. Land a ball in all the boat's places, and you've sunk their ship! It is definitely reminiscent of beer pong in skillset, or perhaps one of those arcade games that require you to land a ball in a colored cup. You definitely need more space to play since there will be balls bouncing around if/when you miss, but it is a lot of fun. A creative twist on a classic game!
One thing that is a little strange to me however, is the advertising. The listing for this product says "Nostalgic tabletop gameplay meets interactive digital content for an immersive gaming experience". There's nothing digital about this, let alone interactive digital and immersive. It's a pretty fun analog pick-up-and-play game, which is what I like about it actually, but it was hard to determine what we were getting before we tried it.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots

Crayola Modeling Dough Pony Play Land - 33 pieces This is a cute modeling dough kit, and many toddlers and preschoolers will enjoy playing with it. But there are some issues for thrifty parents and grandparents to consider to determine if you are getting good value for your money:

What you are basically getting with this set that is hard to replicate at an arts and crafts store are the pony molds. The clay itself you can get by buying Play Doh, or making your own clay at home (typical recipes are very easy to find on the Internet). If you are at all artistic yourself, you could make your own molds of plaster. Though, granted, plastic molds like the ones in this kit are not breakable like plaster molds can be. Another question to ask yourself might be: Why bother with molds at all? Why not let small children model clay (which you can make yourself very cheaply) in any form they choose? This is much more creative than using someone else's molds and often much more fun.

Note that there are small pieces in this set that are a potential swallowing hazard, so it is not recommended for children under the age of 3, and even then, it is important to supervise small children when playing with this set.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Modeling Dough Pony Play Land - 33 pieces

text_fidelity_a:
Happy The Birthday Bird Stuffed Plush Animal with Interactive Book – Adorable Book Character Stuffed Animals with Birthday Theme - Soft Cuddly Fabric – Includes Memory Pages, Photo Storing Pocket I have had several friends who have given birth over the last year or so. Many of them have had all sorts of great ideas and things happen. When I saw this set, I knew one in particular had to have it.

WHAT THIS IS LIKE
This is in a really cool gift box as shown in the promo from the company. It is a clear front and the bird, balloon, and book are visible through the window. There is a ribbon handle at the top.

HOW THIS WORKS
This works so that you have the little doll, put the balloon on the doll which goes with the story. You hide a little gift in the bird and the child can have fun looking for it. The book allows you to document this journey every year.

BACK POCKET
The book has a back pocket so that you can put the picture in the book of that year. When the new year comes out, you repeat the journey and then take off the older picture, put it in the back pocket, and then put the newest picture documenting the even in its place.

HOW DO THEY LIKE THIS?
This was so well received. The bird is adorable. There are sparkles in his eyes, the sneakers are red metallic, and the design is appealing and really cute. The little backpack allows for a small gift, but nothing large. This is just what this particular family needed. They wanted to document their baby's growth and have a really alert a curious little one who loves things like this.

ADOPTION
If you happen to be someone who is involved in adoption, this also might be a great way for the open adoption to share the growth of the baby with the birth mom or family. It would be a great bridge between the mom and dear family who adopts the children.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I highly recommend this set. If you have a child age 2 or so you can start the tradition. You can start as a baby, but with restrictions on the journey. It is a really cool tradition to encourage kids to be who they are meant to be, have fun documenting the tradition and keep track of their growth for future reference as a family keep sake.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is endearing and I will be buying more of these for other families that I know who would love it.
text_fidelity_b: Happy The Birthday Bird Stuffed Plush Animal with Interactive Book – Adorable Book Character Stuffed Animals with Birthday Theme - Soft Cuddly Fabric – Includes Memory Pages, Photo Storing Pocket

All you do is stir the crystal powder in boiling water until it all melts. That's it, nothing else for the kids to do. Sit back and wait for the underwhelming results. The crystal forms  a square at the base, so you'll need to break it up in order to fit it on the circular display. The black base and clear dome display are cheap thin plastic. It just covers the base loosely, so if it moves, the crystal inside moves. We threw away the dome lids, and simply flip the base upside down to use as a tray to hold the crystal, and all it's broken crumbs. That's another thing, it's very brittle. The Science is interesting though. I think I'm most annoyed at the display cases actually. What you get is the type of thin plastics used as tray liners in packaging, the flimsy stuff you throw away. 2-Star.

That's right - Funko repeats TWELVE of the Pops in this calendar from years' past. I guess shame on me for buying it anyway, or genius of Funko to only have to make twelve really good new Pops so that people like me, who do own the previous calendars, are still willing to shell out for this one.

If you do not own any of the previous Funko HP advent calendars, then I would suggest this one over the others, hands down. The addition of flocked characters, and characters holding ornaments and presents, along with really the most iconic of the Pops from the 2018 calendar, IMO make this one far better than the last two calendars combined.

It gets 3 stars from me: 5 stars for this calendar on it's own, but 2 stars for value because of 50% repeats, and 1 star just for anger at Funko being shady and kind of kicking their loyal customers by giving them 50% of what they already previously bought.

Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA I think this kit is just "ok". My 6yo was far more impressed than I was.
My main problem with this kit is that there is no way anyone could string these beads. All thread included is far to thick for the tiny bead holes. My daughter was excited to use a real needle for the first time though. Pictured next to the needed is a needle threader (threaders can be picked up for $1 at your local box if they still have a sewing dept).
The string she used to make her bead bracelet was silky smooth. It made the beading process easier... but the bracelet broke three minutes after she finished. I triple knotting it off too and that wasn't strong enough to keep the knot together. I'd recommend dotting the knot with a drop of glue or clear nail polish to make it hold.
In addition, I think this kit is divided in half; made for two different age groups. Younger children who would be interested in beading part probably won't be ready for friendship braclet weaving for a few more years. And just the same, I think older girls might find the beading process too juvenile. So if your looking for a friendship bracelet kit, I don't see a lot of value in this kit.
These is also a lot of excess packaging to make what you get seem bigger than it is. I feel like this is something that I would have pick up at five below, so $13 feels overpriced to me.
(My daughter wanted to use her own round letter beads; but she could have used the square letter beads that came in this kit just the same)

Never Have I Ever Parent's Edition Card Game Set | Fun Game Night Party Games for Adults | for 2+ Players | Ages 17 + i thought this would be a fun gag game. If you are in mix company (right leaning vs left leaning), I would not recommend. The basic premise of the game is that each player votes on whether they think the card is true or false, but their votes don't actually matter. The person whose turn it is reads the card out loud, makes the final decision, and follows the action on the card (whether they are right or wrong). There is an action on the card for you to perform, which usually includes drinking.

First of all, this isn't much of a game because only 1 card out of 30 is false. There is so much content from the last four years and his numerous tweets that there is enough outrageous actions for all of the cards in the game. I was hoping for some outrageous cards that were false. So, you can laugh (or cringe) about all of the things he has done, but it doesn't make it fun since there isn't much strategy. If you guess that Trump said or did the things on the card, you will be right 95% of the time.

Then, on the lower right hand corner of each card you can tell if a statement is true or false depending on whether Trump is smiling or talking. Hopefully you have good eyes because they look very similar. Also, I know it is a total gag gift, but it makes no sense that the person that actually playing is the same person that is reading the card and the answer is staring them in the face.

If you are looking for an excuse to drink while reading Trump's crazy tweets over the last 4 years, this game is for you, but I can't imagine playing this game more than once.

Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red Pandemic has become a favorite on game nights in my circle of friends, and the On the Brink Expansion improves the experience in several ways. There are new game modes, new roles, new events, and all of them work well. On the most basic level, the ability to have five players is a big improvement. You have to relearn the board setup some to compensate for how many new events are included to keep from unbalancing the game, but none of the changes are so drastic as to be overwhelming.

Aside from this, most of the new material boils down to making the game more difficult. The most basic form of this is the addition of an additional Epidemic card to enable "Legendary" difficulty (I think we lost in ten minutes the first time we tried that mode). The Virulent Strain variation to the rules increases the power of one of the diseases. The Mutation variation adds a fifth disease. All of these are good for the increased challenge, but don't really change the core gameplay too much.

The one exceptionally different mode is the Bio-Terrorist variation, which makes one player an enemy to the rest of the group. I, like many of the other reviewers, love this mode. My friends and roommates don't all agree. It is the type of game mode that certainly has the potential to ruin friendships if you play it too often, but I think it injects some welcome variety into the game. That said, it's totally optional and the expansion has plenty of other improvements to justify buying it even if this game mode doesn't prove to be a hit with your crowd.

As a last, wonderful feature, the game box comes packaged with a tray that is capable of holding the materials not only for the expansion, but for the original game as well. This way you can actually store the original game and the expansion in a single box. It sounds like a small thing, but little touches and details like that are what separate the good game publishers from the great.
text_fidelity_b: Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red

The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up I think I'm just a bit too spoiled by the Pandemic Legacy games, Kings Dilemma, Crusoe Crew, Above and Below, and the like.

The Adventures of Robin Hood is a fine game that is meant to be a legacy-like experience - you play a pretty straightforward move-around-the-board style game, trying to stay inside the shadows printed on the board, until you need to pop out to land on one of a few dozen removable/flippable cardboard cutout pieces that populate the boards. Once you land there to complete objectives, you read a few lines from a book based on the mission at hand, and sometimes you need to perform well at a little combat or make a decision on what to say.

The game is easy to learn and offers a very different gaming experience for those who are unfamiliar with the aforementioned legacy games. Unfortunately, if you've played those, this one is likely just a bit too juvenile. Reading from the book is fun at first, until you find yourself going through the motions and making very similar decisions about completely uninteresting plot points as you progress. Characters largely say the same things, all lead you more or less directly to where you need to go, and when you get there and succeed, you get a "congratulations" rather than a different gaming experience (like in Pandemic), new challenges (like Kings Dilemma) or even a remarkable story experience (like Above and Below). Everything just kind of plays out on it's own.

If you have an impatient bunch, the "pick the next player" from the bag thing could leave people waiting quite a while between turns.

The other thing I don't like is that the rules are a bit interpretive in terms of how movement and the shadows rules affect players. If you want to play this "by the rules" and you have someone who wants to argue over a millimeter, the rules will allow the fudger to make pretty much any interpretation they wish. Most missions are also very much on the easy side.

As this is aimed at a younger audience (I think - the box says 10+ age), some of this is quite forgivable, but for the mature gamer, you have far better options, even if you're enamored with the theme, as I am, or the legacy style game, as my family is. The little one was bored by the long missions, Mom and Dad were thinking there should just be a little more punch to the story. We found this to be a 2/5 experience, but I think most would find it to be a 3/5 or so.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up

TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+ When I was in high school my senior class played an elimination game that was vaguely similar to this (and has been around for years and is still played across the country). Each person drew a name and that was the "target", and there were only loose rules on how to "eliminate" your target (most memorable weapon was a seltzer bottle), and graduation was the time limit. TAG is basically a formalization of that game, with fewer players and more specifics on elimination.

My graduating class had over 500 people, and not all of them played the game. Still, with 50+ players and months to play, it was unwieldy then. TAG limits the game to 10 players max, and the time frame can span anywhere from an hour or two to several weeks. Though the rules are flexible enough to allow for playing for months, this gets a bit cumbersome when having a small player pool.

Each player gets an ID card ("credentials") and a target name. Unlike the more informal version of the game, players are given specific instructions on how to eliminate their target. It might be luring the target to a location or lying in wait, getting the target to do something, or more. Nailing the target with the squirt gun or "poisoning" their food with salt might be fun but if it's not on the specific method card, it doesn't count. Once you've eliminated your target, your next target becomes whoever your original target was stalking. Gameplay continues until there's only one player left.

I like the way this game refines the elimination process, and I like the smaller, more limited scope. This makes it a good game for family events, fun in the dorms at school or even a company morale booster.

If you've ever played the old elimination game, this will be familiar territory. If you haven't it's a fun introduction. There's reasonably good replayability and there's enough flexibility to either play quickly or draw it out for days and weeks.
text_fidelity_b: TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+

The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game I am a board game afficionado. I own over 200 different strategy, social or silly games, and you'd better believe that my daughter is a gamer in waiting. Of course, as a young boy, Pretty Pretty Princess wasn't on my radar for myself, but I knew the name and the concept, and when it was my time to find a copy for my kid, there's no way I was paying the multiple hundreds for the original 80's item.

So I was thrilled when an appropriately priced remake made it's way to my house, and all it took was reading the name to hook my daughter (and interestingly, my wife as well) into a quest to become the most beautiful in all the realm.

The box for this one opens upside down for some reason, and one you get inside, you'll find a spinner, an odd, nearly blank game board, and some teeny tiny jewels to bling out your ensemble. Play is simple - you spin the spinner, attempt to move aroudn the circular board to earn all your gems, and the first one to get everything is crowned (literally) the prettiest princess.

Perhaps the most striking thing is the lack of effort they put into the board and spinner. Both are of reasonable thickness and sturdy, but there is almost nothing on the board in terms of graphic design outside of the logo on the field of white, and the spinner is literally numbers. They may have changed the font away from Times New Roman, but that's all there is to it. It looks like a high school kid's graphic design project, and not one that's going to earn high marks from the teacher.

That said, it's good to have this game back in print again, even if the game play is not particularly solid, and even if the graphics leave quite a bit to be desired. As I said, all I needed to do to get my little one to play was to tell her the name of the game, and my wife jumped right in on the nostalgia boat as well.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game

City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) It's fake LEGO. It may pretend it isn't, but it is,
As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!
text_fidelity_b: City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS)

Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn This busy barn is sturdy and heavy at 10.30 pounds. It sit's flush with the floor. Even though it is heavy, an overactive child may be able to tip or push this over especially if placed on a rug.

This educational toy is rated for 18 months and over and every side has an activity that will appeal to a toddler. There are 5 sides.

- The roof is the counting area from 1-10 with boxes that have those number of items. For example, number 9 has 9 leaves in a box. The pictures are left up to the imagination as numbers 3, 6, 7, 8 (perhaps what is shown is blue and yellow corn), and 10 are not obvious items to me.

- The front side has three doors that reveal various animals.

- The back side has three gears that turn and one of those gears is the sun.

- One side has an alphabet that can be turned to reveal an item that starts with that letter, like A for apple. The alphabet is displayed from left to right side with the last two letters at the bottom center. Since two tiles are left on the left and right of the long alphabet column, they are filled up with various shapes like a triangle, circle, rectangle, etc.

- The other side has a cow, tractor, and chicken that can be moved around on a vertical tract.

I do like that the alphabet side allows for a parent's hands to stick inside for cleaning should a child drop food or sticky items inside during play. This is a big plus to me.

The top appears to be made of plywood or particle board; I can't tell which. I think its plywood because it has several layers. Nevertheless, that is an engineered wood product; so to say this is wood is not a total lie but not a total truth either. I do think the rest of the activity barn is made with wood but it is hard for me to tell.

I do feel this activity barn will keep a young child engaged and learning and his or her motor skills going. Obviously mom or dad will have to point out how to count and what's on the other side of each alphabet and shape cube. I know my friend's boy who is just about 18 months is going to love this.

It's sturdy, heavy, and engaging but at the current price of $66.94 and the fact that it is not all solid wood makes this a bit steep for what this is. I feel it's about $22 overpriced. Other than this, it's perfect for toddlers 18 months and older. I also love that the barn is extremely colorful and I'm sure a toddler will be attracted to this as well.

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Wood, Busy Island Set The pictures I've shared show three different Thomas train sets and the new wood style of connector. The sets pictured in the photos I've included are the busy island set, the farm set, and the park set that just has a circular track included with the figure, a park bench, and the Thomas. Any of these sets on their own would not be quite enough to get kids started. My main complaint about all of the sets is that they don't include enough tracks. They have a lot of interesting and exciting components, but it takes a lot of hard work and thought to get all of the components together with the small number of tracks that are included, and then you don't get to build and rebuild as much as you'd like because there simply are not that many track configurations that actually work with the small number of straight tracks and curves included.

As for the new style of connector, many people have commented that this seems like a cash grab to make it so that you cannot use your old tracks. Fisher-Price continually says that with the included connectors, you can just connect up to your old style of track. Both of these complaints are a little bit right. The new track style has some things going for it and other things that are not my favorite. The thing going for it is that the tracks do connect together much more sturdily, and I really appreciate that this makes for a smoother run on the tracks than with brio and all of the other brands that use the other connection standard. Every set that you get from Thomas has two converters, and so in theory if you have an existing wooden Thomas set with the old connectors, you can connect up two different runs of the train with these couple of connectors, but you can't really integrate them all very well, and using the connectors and keeping the two types of train area distinct are something that smaller children will have issues with.

As for how it is to play with, my five-year-old loves how sturdy the connections are and how easy it is to build with them. My three-year-old finds it hard to get the pieces apart because you need to do a very clean hold and pull upward motion which I find very easy, my five-year-old finds very easy, but my three-year-old wants to pull apart while pulling up, and that little bit of motion of trying to pull them apart sideways makes it so that it is very tough for her to get them apart. Hopefully this will be something that clicks for her soon and she will be able to play with the trains independently. We've only had the set for less than a week.

The busy island set specifically is probably the number one set that you would want and need to get if you are getting the Fisher-Price wood set going. It has so many fun implements, an airport, the ferry boat which connects up to the train station, the little bridge piece with some water around it to where you can lift the bridge and let the ferry go through, giraffes and zebras and some little fenced areas with grass for them to go, some interesting diverter tracks that let you choose which direction the trains go, and a few fun trains, dual level supporting pieces, and just enough tracks to put it all together.

You will definitely need to buy additional sets or additional track packs in order to make this truly fun to play with and not just something the set up once and run your trains around.

The busy island set was definitely the one that included the most diverse and interesting pieces for play. The farm set was an exciting addition, but basically just added some more track pieces, some more fenced areas, some farm animals and an egg selling stand, and the dual level farm. These are all interesting pieces, but in all honesty doesn't offer a ton more play besides the imaginative variety. I definitely recommend getting it also, but the busy island set is the first one to get because it has the most interesting options for varied play.

Overall, we are delighted with this set and you probably could've heard my kids whooping with joy about a mile away when I pulled it out of the box and they realized just what was inside. We haven't done any other train sets yet, but my three-year-old has had so much fun with some tiny little roadbuilding toys that I thought she would particularly benefit from this, and I knew my five-year-old would also love it.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Wood, Busy Island Set

However, I got these for my train wreck 3yo because he managed to break crayons and loves to take things apart and hoping these would keep him entertained and focus for thirty minutes. I like how this is geared towards young kids have the sticker version of hidden pictures. However it's not every single page so out of each book you get four full paged stickers hidden pictures, the rest are just regular like what you'd get for your young elementary highlights. For my 3yo he's basically asking me to point out wherever things are..... I'm not sure if it's age or it's a personality issue since he's more of an outdoor child. There's also maze and learning letters, no learning numbers and the paper version of hidden pictures has stickers that's just decorative it appears to be. Also the funny scene to encourage kids talk about what's funny, which is usually not a hit in my house. The stickers for the hidden pictures are perforated for easy removal.
I didn't like the price. Just like always I still think highlights are quite expensive for paper and stickers, but I do understand ideas are pricey. The stickers for hidden pictures goes across the book making it difficult for sticker keeping. If you tear it down for easier stickers removal the other side inevitably falls off. If you leave it there it's very frustrating for a 3yo and you have to assist every single sticker. Stickers are not very sticky, which allows repetitive replacement but it's also very easy to tear it apart. Overall very fun set. I'd still purchase them if they're not over $50.

Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+ Mixed feelings on this one.

It can maybe speed up wrapping bracelets, necklaces, etc. But it also requires some patience and if you try to go too fast, you're just going to make a mess of things. So, honestly, you won't be going much faster than if doing this by hand. If you want a thicker cord it can be tricky to fit it through the holding slot (tip - instead of going through the slot on the top, go through the bottom).

Making anything longer than a bracelet will also take some serious patience and practice as it requires sliding your work up and therefore tying your already worked piece into place / slide it through the holding slot.

Once you get the hang of it, it does feel like this is almost a third hand. It's a great way to manage the cords while you work but it's definitely not going to be worth it for most people. It doesn't feel like the game changer that their Loopdeloom did. For me it's helpful as I do have problems with my hands at times. But for the kids that this is targeting, this is probably more trouble than it's worth.

Ontel Magic Tracks Police Chase Glow in The Dark Racetrack Set with 10 Feet of Speedway OK, first off - we really love Magic/Neo/Twister Tracks. We have a number of different sets. Recently we grabbed the one with the single car and remote, along with the Rocket Racers and an off brand, dinosaur-themed set. All of which were excellent! This however, has a major flaw.

The jump ramp seems like an afterthought. It looks nothing like the picture on the box. It's like the box graphics were designed before the physical product. Even worse, its the connection to the track makes zero sense, and the instructions are laughable to say the lease. Oddly enough, the ramp is able to move back and forth like a see-saw, yet, it's not meant to do that! It's a ramp - and it's supposed to let the truck fly off and onto the lower track. Here's the kicker: one side of the ramp is blocked, like a dead end, so the only way we got this to work was to lay the proceeding track over it so it the truck wouldn't be stopped. It's like the manufacture designed this ramp piece wrong. Between that, and the see saw spring built in, my bet is, this was meant to originally do something else, but it failed, so they left it that way and simply called it a jump ramp. At 29.95, that's a disgrace. This is the only set we sent back. Most of the high ratings you see are for the other themes (firetruck, police set, etc..), so proceed with caution.

Fortnite Baller (RC) Vehicle - Includes 4” Hybrid Action Figure, 4” Scaled Baller, Plus Remote Control Action toys are among the best. What kid doesn’t like a toy that includes movement, sounds, etc? If your child loves Fortnite characters and likes action, then he/she will love the Fortnite Baller Vehicle.

When I first saw this toy, I thought the clear globe inside the box was just for show but it is actually part of the vehicle. Contained inside is one Fortnite figure and the base that the figure and globe rest on is the actual vehicle itself. It comes with a remote control and you have to load batteries into both the vehicle and the remote control before you can use it.

With the remote control in hand, the Fortnite Baller Vehicle is ready for action. The remote has two knobs on it, similar to the controller for home video games. Kids can move each knob and control the movement of the vehicle. I discovered, too, that there is an adjustment level underneath that you can use if the vehicle isn’t moving the way you want it to. And since the inside accommodates Fortnite figures, kids can feel free to swap out the one that comes with this toy with another one from the set.

Fortnite fans have any number of toys they can buy that feature their favorite Fortnite characters, but the Fortnite Baller Vehicle is one of the cooler ones available. The remote-controlled movement sets this toy apart and it’s a great choice for fans of these action figures.

text_fidelity_a:
4M Snail Robot from KidzRobotics, A Fascinating Way to Learn About Mechanical Science! Build Your Very Own Pet Snail and Watch it Glide, Ages 8 I only paid $10 for this so I wasn't expecting lots, however I was expecting it to be decently made and a little more as described.

Putting that aside, if you plan to buy this I suggest you carefully look over the box and "in use" photos. On the box it does say you have to put the robot together and that it's meant for children over 8, those are very key points that I see were missed as I read the reviews. I wish I'd have really looked at the pictures myself, because I was expecting solid lines, not a bunch of dots, and from the given discription I thought the patterns would be more than just repeated crappy circles, also something you kind of see if you look at the pictures. Although even if you notice the pictures show dots and not lines, my dots were very widely spaced.

The things I couldn't have known from the pictures is how crappy it really is. The clear dome is thinner than your average disposable water bottle, everything that can be is shoddy plastic, and there is zero quality control. The wires on the one I got were attached to the wrong sides, thankfully they left the naked wires too long or it wouldn't have been useable at all because they needed to be crossed behind the motor to work at all. Plus, while this is technically buildable by children, the nuts, bolts and screws are so small that they are tricky to handle even for adults. It isn't hard to build at all, barely having enough parts to really be called buildable, so it isn't all that fantastic at what it's supposed to be, something to encourage children to think, build and experiment. Honestly if they included alternate uses or ways you can experiment with this it would be closer to worth while. Although since they sell other robots I guess that would cut into their bottom line.

This IS meant to be an educational toy, so it should be more educational, or not need to be put together at all and just be a toy. So if what you want is either a toy your kids will want to keep playing with, or a decent educationally toy, buy something else. We're hoping to find ways to experiment with ours, or at least hope the cats will find it fun.
text_fidelity_b: 4M Snail Robot from KidzRobotics, A Fascinating Way to Learn About Mechanical Science! Build Your Very Own Pet Snail and Watch it Glide, Ages 8

Educational Insights Pass The Peas This game has potential, but due to its flimsy nature and low quality of organization, we didn't enjoy it as much as we could have.

The peas are just press out cardboard pieces that sit on top of cardboard pods. They are slippery and as you pass the pods, the peas slide everywhere. If you are at any size table with people sitting average distance apart, the peas will easily slip off and get messed up as you pass them.

The little bags of peas also should be color coded. Instead all of the bags are supposed to match an individual pea pod, but you have to open them up every time to look as on the outside they are all identical. At very least, they should have put in different colored strings so you could see which was what.

If they made the pods so they would lay flat instead of bending closed somewhat, and maybe have something like Velcro or magnetic surface, it would be a lot better to use. As you move around the pods it would be more secure and not so stressful.

The game has potential to be fun, but a combination of the cheap way it is made and the frustration present when trying to play, it just isn't as nice as it should be. The game is somewhat fun at first, but soon after beginning to play we just lost interest.

When I first got this I thought it was as good as the Papo, until I started comparing the two more closely. Like the Papo brand, the jaw is articulated so it can be opened or closed. The Schleich is well made and better than many toy dinosaurs out there, but when compared side-by-side you can really see the difference between the two. The arms aren't as well done and wrinkles in the skin don't seem as real as they do with the Papo. Also, I realize we probably have no way of knowing the actual color of the dinosaurs but the red on this one makes it seem a little bit cartoonish.

This dinosaur will be great for kids that play with them regularly. They will love how realistic they look. However, if you're a collector and just want these for display, I'd suggest the Papo brand instead.

Others have complained that it opens the opportunity to eliminate characters based on skin color like that would somehow foster discriminatory children. Really? Would it really be so bad to recognize different skin colors? Last I checked blind people can’t play this game and we all know if you were questioned for a description of a person by police that if you really saw the person you’d be able to do so without any issues. If someone looks a certain way, it is what it is.

The first time I set this up to look at it, the "doors" would not latch shut, and then once I did get them latched, the left side got stuck and did not want to open.There are lights that flash on and off for about 5 seconds when a button is pressed. The sorting hat is attached the the wall and you can place one of the four figures under it, but it doesn't do anything else as far as I know. There is a wand YOU CAN BUY SEPARATELY that works with this playset, but I don't know what the wand can do that you cannot do manually by pushing a button or sliding a figure along. The figures included look ok, and you get Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Professor Dumbledore. No bag guy figures are included, which I feel is a missed opportunity for more play scenarios. If they threw in a Voldemort or even Snape or Draco Malfoy, there would be an antagonist other than the snake who is stuck to a tabletop and can be vanquished by flipping him upside down.
In short, I do not recommend this toy.

text_fidelity_a: Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players This is a great cooperative game for families.  Great for kids.  Great for adults. It's a lot harder than it first appears.  You need to work together to gather the treasures before the island sinks, and once it starts sinking, it just keeps sinking faster, first because as the water level rises you draw more cards, and each card means a section sinks a bit more, and second because once a section sinks you take its card out of play, spreading the increasing damage to a decreasing area.  You can set the difficulty, but even on the easiest setting, it's a challenge for first time players.  This is fast becoming my favorite cooperative tabletop game.  Fans of Pandemic will enjoy this.  I've heard Forbidden Desert is easier, but I haven't tried that one yet.  This one is quite the challenge.

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball I love geography and travel, and putting this together is both fun in a puzzle sort of way and great for reminiscing about past travels and dreaming about places yet to be seen in person. It's really cool - even cooler that it comes with a stand and you have a globe of your own afterward.

It is very up to date - it includes S. Sudan. And a warning to independence haters: Kosovo is shown as its own country. It is quite small and not labeled, but it has its own color.

We did the first half (the bottom) in the first night, but used the numbered backs as a guide as shown on the instruction sheet. It was fun, but left something to be desired. I wished they didn't have the numbers, and thought they would be impossible to ignore. After this, this was going to be the first Ravensburger puzzle I would have given less than five stars.

BUT the second night we finished it, but without the numbers. Turns out they were easy to ignore, and this allowed it to be what it should have been all along.

It might be overwhelming to not look at the numbers at first, but I suggest you do it that way. I suspect you still will have it done in 3-4 nights (assuming a few hours each night - it is addicting).

The pieces are plenty durable for snapping together, but many pieces are alike, so you could conceivably put the whole thing together as a sphere, but have it still be wrong. Anyone with any sense of geography would be able to catch a mistake like that. And when in doubt, the backs are numbered.

And when you're done, you have a nice little globe, textured to show it was a puzzle, and with a reasonably good looking stand. Very neat.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

I really appreciate that Barbie is come such a long way, and I feel excited to share the fun of this line with my kids.

MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys The box says that this Magnet Building Sticks set is for ages six and up, but I'm really enjoying playing with it as an adult. I think younger kids would need some help to do the suggested building projects, but using the set to build things is easy. The set includes 120 magnetic sticks, 40 steel balls, and a gray bag with a drawstring to hold the set if you don't want to use the original packaging. The balls are 1 inch across, and the sticks are 2.25 inches long and 1/4 inch across.

The magnets hold together strong enough to basically stay where you put them but not so strong that it's difficult to pull things apart. The more stable builds (which have many triangles instead of squares) hold their shape well as you build them. Some of the building projects that have a more open structure have a tendency to collapse during certain stages of building, and then they start to attach to parts that they aren't supposed to. It can be a mess to straighten out. Once I realized that this could happen, I was more careful to stabilize these open structures as I built them, so this hasn't been a problem since.

The set also came with pictures of a number of projects. The pictures show only the finished building projects, but they were not always clear about what went where when the lines overlapped in the picture. Still, I've been able to do most of the projects, and of course you can come up with your own ideas. Kids may become frustrated trying to figure out the pictures and prefer to make their own building projects. Overall, I've had a lot of fun with this as have a teenager and a tween that have played with it.
text_fidelity_b: MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys

The many small building projects are great for very young children. The building techniques are all basic, simple ones. The elements in the set are all standard LEGO elements (they’re NOT Duplo bricks), so they’re compatible with other LEGO sets you may already own.

Some people take too long to make decisions, don't play with someone like that in a group of more than 2 people as there's not much to do while waiting your turn. The game is pretty and well built, and the dice drafting mechanic is unique and fun.

I'm glad I bought the game and it's in our rotation, but it's not as good as games like Patchwork or Carcassonne because you're always trying to do the same thing- fill up your grid while maximizing your score. text_fidelity_a:
Brain Games - The Game - Based on the Emmy Nominated National Geographic Channel TV Series This game is rated for 3-6 players ages 14+. However, my boyfriend and I were able to play by just leaving out the head-to-head (challenge cards) for each category.

The object of the game is to be the first one to win a game piece in all four game categories. I love board games and so does my boyfriend, which is why I got this. At the beginning we found playing this game nearly impossible. Neither one of us watch TV (this is based on a TV series) nor have cable. Therefore, it took us a while to even understand what this was about and what many of the game cards were asking us to do. We kept asking ourselves “Are we really that stupid?” However, after playing for almost 2 hours, we were enlightened. Nevertheless, for the uninitiated, this game might be challenging and confusing the first time around. After that not so much because then one remembers how to solve most of the cards and when that happens, this game will have to be “retired” for a while.

Below is a sentence on the box top which provides a good, yet very simple, idea of what “brain games” are all about.
THINK YOU
YOU CAN'T
BE FOOLED?
You just were. Read it again.

If you did not find the double YOU in the phrase on the first try, then you were fooled.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX:
- 192 game cards consisting of 48 cards each in each of the 4 categories (mind & body, language, logic, vision)
- A "box topper" with 4 game slots to hold the cards
- 40 hexagon shaped game tiles (8 tiles for each category, 4 wild, and 4 lose-a-turn)
- 6 pawns (playing pieces)
- 6 score cards
- 1 game board in 4 puzzle pieces
- 1 die that holds numbers 1, 2, & 3 only (two times)

Everything is made of cardboard except for the pawns and die. The score cards and puzzle pieces are easily punched out of the cardboard card provided.

In summary, this game is good for those who like to be challenged or know what the game is about. However, if you play this several times, you'll probably remember the answers and have to put this away for about one year before playing it again.
text_fidelity_b: Brain Games - The Game - Based on the Emmy Nominated National Geographic Channel TV Series

There are several pegs on the bike that fit into holes in Duke's boots to make him at least look balanced. Duke's helmet doesn't come off.
The stunt cycle's performance is also faithful to the movie which is unfortunate. The launcher is more of a gimmick & isn't necessary to use the toy. All of the cycle's motivation comes from winding a spring inside the bike by rolling it backwards. It's actually hard to put the bike in the launcher after it is wound without releasing the stored energy.
The motorcycle isn't quite as detailed or faithful to the movie but it looks great & it can take a beating without breaking. The cycle also has an extendable stand & set of dolly wheels that allows it to emulate a wheel stand while either rolling or just posing.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO The Movie 2 Pop-Up Party Bus 70828 Building Kit, Build Your Own Toy Party Bus for 9+ Year Old Girls and Boys (1013 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I really enjoyed the Lego movie Lego kits, because they just add so much color, costuming and fun to normal building. The mini figures are much more like the Lego friends than like the normal ones, and the pink Afro, unicorn Kitty, robot, etc. added a lot of fun to the build process to have those as accessories.

My son at six has done hundreds of Lego sets because we are a homeschooling family and incorporate that into our curriculum. This build took him a few days of intermittent building and he felt enthusiastic and excited about the set and kept discovering cool new features and decorative accents to how it worked. The little light up brick inside was a really fun touch, also.

Once the bus is constructed, it has a little more play value than some of the other Lego vehicles and sets that we have built. So many toys once constructed seem to explode apart with the most gentle of play, while this party bus is built pretty sturdy. We've had a number of young friends visit and want to play with it, and while a few little pieces of broken off, it was in the realm of being very easy to repair rather than having major structural problems upon actual children actually playing with it.

Overall this is a really fun set, a fun build that is fairly straightforward, and results in a sturdy toy at the end. Little sister was particularly taken with the accessories.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO The Movie 2 Pop-Up Party Bus 70828 Building Kit, Build Your Own Toy Party Bus for 9+ Year Old Girls and Boys (1013 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Wiggle Car Ride On Toy, ANPABO 2 in 1 Wiggle Car with Rechargeable Battery and Pedal, Anti-Rollover Wheels with Colorful Lights, Swing Car for Toddlers and Kids Age 3 Years up Update: after a few months of off/on use- ours figured out how to ride on his own… don’t give up- kids can get the hang of it just fine!!!

Super excited in theory.. with ability to use manually or with electronic option as needed- it seemed ideal by just a flip of a switch on bottom. Only for some reason, pedal doesn’t respond every time like it should!! (Yes! battery is full when trying it- yet 15% of time it wont respond electronically- reason deducted x1 star!!?) When pedal engages- scooter is stable, easy to glide and maneuver.. and enjoyed. Battery outlasts our toddler whose rides for 15-25min straight and it hasn’t run out! (For reference: our little is 33mo, 36lb, 38” tall.. almost 3yr old.)

because of electronic component- ours struggles to grasp concept without using the pedal since he’s learned to ride with the electronic aid! So, when it fails to respond or we have pedal off- he just “jerks” scooter back/forth and side/side- its as if he’s trying to get it to do what it “should..” by tugging it into motion. For some reason.. he doesn’t naturally get moving scooter without electronic help so, it can leaves him fristrated.

Instructions are straightforward and connecting handle atop the scooter can be a tad tricky and tight.. Best if use included hardware to connect all screws loosely first THEN, tighten after all parts are aligned. Light up wheels are just extra!!! Not needed and not sure how long they’ll last esp. rider encountered water elements? I love the “long press” music feature- ha, it’s my fav. **bc, It shuts music all the way off!!

We’ve only used inside on tile and large smooth nape rug. No tire markings is nice.. I like inside option bc it’s winter here! I realize some issues had may be caused by our rider himself- but feel pedal should not be a problem we have to deal with if it’s charged. Hoping info can help decision.. stay safe everyone!

B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z Toddlers love to play and they benefit from toys that encourage learning or help in other areas of development. One toy that seems promising in these ways is the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers.

This puzzle has knobs on the pieces, making it easy for toddlers to grab each piece. It helps with coordination, too, as little ones will learn to fit the right shape into the right slot. However, the colors of the pieces are washed out and they really need to be an eye catching primary. Not only would it be more inviting to toddlers and preschoolers but it would provide an opportunity to not only teach numbers and counting, but color recognition too while playing.

Another issue with the pieces is that the details are lacking. If you are going to add detail make it something a child can recognize. But probably the most shocking oversight is the shapes and numbers that they are supposed to match. There is an octagon, for example, that represents the number 7, a five- pointed star that is used for the number 8, and so on. Why would you do this? The octagon should be the number 8 and the star should match with number 5. This is an oversight that someone should have caught.

Other issues I have are with the puzzle holes- they are a little too big and this would be hard to travel anywhere with. I do like that the numbers are nice and big and easy to see and that the knobs are big and tall enough for tiny fingers to grasp. While I haven’t seen it happen yet I do worry because, since they are very much like thumbtacks, they may come loose and eventually get lost. The pieces don’t hold in place as well as I would like.

Toddler toys that help kids learn are nice and while the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers does help with coordination and other skills, it lacks in other areas. The oversight with the numbers and shapes not matching is a big one and I have other issues, too. So, when I think of everything as a whole, this toy gets a thumbs down from me.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z
