text_fidelity_a:
Dungeons & Dragons: Lords of Waterdeep Board Game This is a worker placement game, which means that it is a lot more strategic than many people realize. It has some randomizers in that everything is presented through shuffled decks of cards (intrigues, quests and buildings) and that randomness can make what seems like a great strategy ultimately fail when the quest you need doesn't show up.

I think I like this a bit more than Stone Age. Lords of Waterdeep offers a lot more strategy than other worker placement games thanks to the quests since the players have some ability to choose which quests to undertake. Also controlling which building gets built can have a huge effect on the outcome as the buildings tend to be far more powerful than the base locations that are available at the start of the game.

This game isn't for everyone, but a love and knowledge of Dungeons and Dragons is not required (it adds flavor only). The key here is a patient and strategic mind and a willingness to use up 1-2 hours plotting your success while hopefully interfering just enough in the plans of the other players to come out on top at the end.
text_fidelity_b: Dungeons & Dragons: Lords of Waterdeep Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
The Settlers of Catan I have lost many a Sunday afternoon to Settlers. Do you know why I purchased Settlers? Because each of my friends has purchased our own set... we do not want to find ourselves at each others house and wanting to play but not have a board to set up. We have taken turns hosting and every time it has been fun.

It is a game of strategy, in my opinion a slightly more complicated/sophisticated version of Monopoly (although my friends vehemently disagree). Instead of building houses and hotels you build towns and cities, instead of collecting rent, you collect resources, and instead of chance cards you have victory cards... but somehow it seems more fun. There is an element of Chess- because you do have to build roads to tie your cities together, and to do that you have to have foresight and plan ahead.

This is a game of champions- and voted best Table Game by folks who vote on those things- be warned that once you start playing it may become addictive. Be prepared to be suckered into the sport for years to come.

I am reviewing this product in an effort to help other Amazon customers through relaying my experience with the product and providing any insight I garnered. Had I not liked this product, I would state so here in my review. I would really appreciate that if you found my review helpful, that you would please indicate so below by clicking the YES button below.
text_fidelity_b: The Settlers of Catan

We also have another 14 inch doll from a different brand, and these clothes fit her perfectly as well.

My daughter loves the fancy boots and the glittery pants. As with most of the shoes from this line, the glitter is kind of glued onto the bottom rim of the boots, and does feel a little bit rough and falls off if you are trying to manipulate the shoes onto the doll, but these are things that are easily repaired later with a little bit of Elmer's glitter glue, should that be needed ever. My daughter has some similar glittery pants from the Cat and Jack line and was pleased to have a pair of similar pants for her dolls.

The gradient dress is really cute, and the see-through jacket adds a special touch that I haven't really seen offered in doll clothes before. The one thing that I'm not a huge fan of, is why did they choose to put a giant shimmery GG on the back of the jacket. My three-year-old doesn't understand that she is playing with glitter girls, and I've tried not to introduce her to that specific of branding, so she is a little bit puzzled as to why the jacket says GG on it. I wish that instead of selfishly trying to go for increase brand recognition, they would've found something cute to put on there instead, like a star, heart, or cat face. I think that would've been a lot more thoughtful to their audience of parents and children.

Other than that, this is a really cute set that is fun as is, or fun to mix and match with other glitter girls outfits in this line.

GiiKER Electronic Bluetooth Speed Cube i3s, Real-time Connected STEM Smart Cube 3x3 for All Ages, Companion App Support Online Battle with Cubers Across The Globe, with Exclusive Charger [[VIDEOID:df61075bc0172b4d34aec64cd5ddd45b]] The concept of smart cubes are really cool: They connect over Bluetooth low power protocol to an app so that your movements are digitized. This opens up possibilities like training exercises and real-time online competitions. The app is actually pretty excellent here, unlike another cube we tried, this one actually has competitors and it seems to work (however my son is suspicious that they might not be real players. They could be AI, because how many people could there really be using this app at the same time he is?).
However, the hardware seems buggy on this. Sometimes the cube will move and the app won't register that movement. Try it again later with the same move, and it does. In the video here, my son demonstrates that it completely loses calibration as he solves the cube. We tried the app on a few different devices in our home, with processors from Qualcomm Snapdragon and other's with Samsung's Exynos (flagship Galaxy S level hardware). It doesn't seem to be the phone/tablet that is the problem, but rather that the cube isn't always registering the movement to send to the app. This causes things to get out of alignment relatively quickly, especially when speed solving, and renders the entire experience frustrating.
This had so much potential, we're really disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: GiiKER Electronic Bluetooth Speed Cube i3s, Real-time Connected STEM Smart Cube 3x3 for All Ages, Companion App Support Online Battle with Cubers Across The Globe, with Exclusive Charger

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder System Stunt Kit Playset This HOT WHEELS TRACK BUILDER SYSTEM STUNT KIT is one of the best "stunt kits" yet, because it can be set up in any of four (4) different gravity-defying configurations. You build a basic "stunt base", then choose the build that suits your numbered experience level: High Jump (1), Criss Cross (2), Long Jump (3), or The Drop (4). If you tire of one of the builds, you can easily take it apart and rebuild it into a different one. (The stunt pictured on the box is the High Jump.)

Because I'm experienced with the Track Builder System, I chose to build the Long Jump. (I passed on The Drop for now, because it requires a tabletop as well as floor space for the setup.) This is a high-performance stunt--you load a car into the rubber-band-powered launcher, hit the launcher release disk hard, and send the car up a ramp, around a loop-de-loop, over a wide gap to a ramp landing, and then down the track to exit the stunt into the rest of your Track Builder layout. You can use the "measuring stick" to measure and lengthen the gap (the distance to the ramp), once you master the launching technique needed to send the car through the entire stunt to a successful completion.

Unfortunately, this stunt kit is also one of the most difficult to build. The Hot Wheels instructions are always a bit confusing--the drawings are three-dimensional, but they lack the dimensional accuracy of LEGO drawings. The parts are shown in the instructions in their actual plastic colors, which helps, but the drawings don't always make it easy to identify the shapes of the parts or to see exactly how they go together. However, the Building Instructions and parts for this kit have a feature I don't remember seeing before: letters (A, B, C, etc.) molded into the parts, so you can match the letters (A to A; B to B: etc.) to connect the parts. This, too, helps with the building stage. (Always remember that if you can't get the car to complete the stunt--no matter how hard you try--you probably made a mistake in the build.)

The parts in the "stunt base" (see my first photo below) click together very tightly, and more or less permanently. I was unable to pry the parts apart, even using workshop tools. As a result, the assembled stunt kit cannot be taken completely apart for flat storage in the original box.

This stunt kit comes with only one Hot Wheels car, and you will need at least one more car to fully play with it. All four configurations have suggestions for using two cars (crashing at track crossings, comparing speeds, etc.). The kit has two (2) extremely powerful 4-speed launchers--I love these! The launchers are the best I've ever seen. (They are already set up when you take them out of the box--don't fool with the rubber bands.) Another new wrinkle in this Stunt Kit is that you can use the retail box itself to add interest and difficulty to your larger Track Builder System layout. There are printed ramps and "fire pits" that can be pushed up and locked together to make a platform with more obstacles for the cars.

This is an excellent choice for any Track Builder System layout, because of its versatility, economical use of floor space, and low price (about $24 on Amazon). The only drawback is that it's harder to build than most Hot Wheels stunts.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder System Stunt Kit Playset

I can't imagine how you manage some of the complicated designs without having it hiccup and go off-line.  the original spiro was much thicker and you could fly around the circles once you got the teeth on the cogs together and found the right pressure.  this is too thin and while amusing isn't clear or exact enough to be stable

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Party Board Game I gave this game to my teenage nephew, who played it with several family members and friends. They found the instructions not really hard, but very long and involved, and it took awhile for them to figure out how to play the game. They tried to follow the rules, but ended up playing the game according to their own "house rules."

The game comes with a timer, which makes a very loud noise. They eventually stopped using the timer because the noise was so annoying. One player even thought that the timer might have been broken. The timer went off completely on its own, making that obnoxious noise. Another player, an adult woman, did not enjoy the game at all, but the teens enjoyed the aspect of the game that required you to draw or to describe a product or the logo or symbol for a product. The game seems to be a combination of Pictionary and Charades and Trivial Pursuit. The kids thought this was a good, creative game, with a combination of old and new products. This aspect of the game made it good for mixed age groups. As other reviewers have said, this game is best played in teams. I have the feeling that this experiment may have gone better if at least one player had really understood how to play the game so that so much time would not have been consumed in trying to understand the rules.

The teens are willing to give this game another try. I am going to edit this review after they do to see if they enjoyed the game more. I have a feeling they will, especially as they become more familiar with it.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children

They are bright with a variety of colors including black and white. Crayola has never come across as a high-end brand, but in oil pastels they are highly regarded as some of the best, and I agree. If you watch some of the videos on YouTube about how to use oil pastels you will realize how great these are. You can also see comparison videos, and the crayola brand gets very high marks. Oil pastels don't make a mess unless you use your finger to blend them, and then your finger will be a big mess. But you can clean it with baby wipes or soap and water or lotion to get down into your skin if it's dry. You can use traditional rolled paper sticks for blending also. These come packaged neatly so you can keep them in their original slots in that packaging. Besides coloring with them you can also use a wet brush to blend them, and you can layer them on top of each other or blend them together with your finger. I have also seen them covered with a clear acrylic paint and then used again on top of that paint. You can see that on YouTube. These are an inexpensive way to enjoy yourself artistically and produce beautiful results just like painting when you add the water or vodka or a blender like turpenoid.

Unsolved Case Files: Cold Case Murder Mystery Game: Who Murdered Harmony Ashcroft? | Can You Solve The Crime? The only reason this isn't a 5-star review is the racist casting in the mystery that had nothing to do with the story.

A friend gave this to me knowing my love for true crime. I've always wanted to try the Hunt a Killer boxes, but was always put off by the price.

No spoiler review:
- The case file includes newspaper clippings, evidence files, interview transcripts, photos, and more. Your first puzzle is to prove the innocence of Bones, the only non-white person in the game who was a homeless drunk that was wrongfully accused and jailed for the crime. (Obviously, racism is very much a problem with our justice system in real life. However, depicting that in a fictional puzzle game? We'll never solve this problem if we continue to portray that happening. Furthermore, there was NO STORY REASON WHATSOEVER for it.)
- You select your answers to the puzzles on their website, and if you're right you can open the first seal additional evidence envelope. I was worried the answer selection would spoil the real answers, but we didn't have to worry about that at all.
- We ended up becoming so invested in the case, after a couple hours in we decided to sleep on it and solve the first puzzle the following day. We couldn't stop talking about it.
- Once you play it once, you can't play it again. However, you don't have to mark any of the evidence so you can easily just put everything back in the envelope and give it to a friend. For the price as well, that's a lot better than most true crime puzzle games that are WAY more expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Unsolved Case Files: Cold Case Murder Mystery Game: Who Murdered Harmony Ashcroft? | Can You Solve The Crime?

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game I played this when I was a kid and it's still a great game if you only have 30 minutes to spare. In 30 minutes you can easily get in 3-4 rounds of brain busting fun. This game is really about trying to mentally out maneuver your friends by coming up with words starting with whatever letter the die at the beginning of the round gave you that are unique enough to answer the prompt that no one else has thought of it. If no one else thought of your answer you get a point and so on down the prompt card each round. If your answer is the same as someone else's you both cross it out and lose that potential point.

What I love about this game is the creativity in answers and how far you can bend the rules. We always play that the group votes on whether your answer is valid or allowable since it always gets a little fuzzy as the game goes on and our competitive nature picks up. It's a mental gymnastic type of game that is face paced and frustrating but over all lots of fun and laughs with a good group. A real classic that has great replayability.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game

K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy [[VIDEOID:5795137e2a23bd3d76a56d2b9446c889]] If you’re already familiar with K’Nex building sets, this K’NEX THRILL RIDES-REVOLUTION FERRIS WHEEL is a simple, fast build. The Ferris wheel is big, but it doesn’t require a lot of pieces. Also, much of the assembly involves building duplicate parts that combine to make the wheel and its swinging gondolas.

The set is recommended for age 7+, and that sounds reasonable (assuming that an adult provides some initial help with making the connections, and assists with lifting the wheel onto the axle). Each shape of piece is a different color, which detracts from the appearance of the finished Ferris wheel, but makes the construction simpler. There aren’t many “snowflake” connections, which I usually have to puzzle over to get the right orientation. (K’Nex pieces are much harder to work with than LEGO pieces.) The instructions are reasonably clear. This set took me about 5 hours to build (from opening the box to completion, working at a leisurely pace).

Unfortunately, the finished “thrill ride” isn’t very thrilling. Like a full-sized amusement park ride, the Ferris wheel doesn’t do much—it just goes around and around in a circle. Also, it does NOT have a variable speed control—you cannot start, stop, or speed up the wheel gradually (like a real ride). Although the motor has a single speed, it does run in forward and reverse directions. The motor is powered by two AA batteries (not included).

For the Ferris wheel to turn properly, one edge of the inner wheel track must be settled into the groove on the “gear wheel” attached to the motor. You can easily fiddle with the base to adjust things so that the track and groove always make good contact. Because it’s sort of boring and lacks a variable speed control, I rate this K’Nex Ferris Wheel kit at 4 stars (“I like it” on the official Amazon scale).
text_fidelity_b: K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy

text_fidelity_a:
Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens I generally don't prefer electronic learning, but these are pretty cool. The Smart Letters each have three rubber feet that are spaced differently, and the tablet recognizes the letter when you gently place it on the tablet screen. It took about 10 minutes to download all 6 free apps (3 for letters, 3 for numbers) and to set up the quick profile. The apps are simple to use and well designed. Next is a summary of the 3 letter apps:

Bla Bla Box: spell out words and hear them read back to you
Alphamonster: choose a letter to hear the sound the letter makes and see a picture of a word beginning with that letter. See a picture of an item and identify what letter the item starts with. Hear a sound of a letter and identify the letter. See a cursive lowercase letter and identity the matching wooden uppercase letter. (In the settings you can pick which letters will appear throughout these challenges. The default is the entire alphabet but you can pick just a few if your child needs to focus on certain letters)
Vocabubble: game 1- pick any letter and as you repeatedly place the letter on the tablet, 8 different pictures of items beginning with that letter will fall down the screen. Game 2 - choose two letters, then pictures of items beginning with those two letters will fall down the screen and you tap the picture with the right letter in order for it to disappear. (This was a fun game my niece and nephew enjoyed playing together as they each held a letter. However, some pictures seemed too hard or random for a 5 year old, such as an Orca for the letter O... kids will think it's a Whale... or a Totem Pole or Quaill, etc)

My five year old niece and nephew enjoyed testing these for me and were definitely interested in the games. I'm excited to start my daughter with it when she turns three and I can see the number apps extending the usefulness of the product as she gets older. Four stars, not five, only because they do seem a bit pricey and also because the accent on the American English setting we tried out is a bit odd at times.
text_fidelity_b: Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens

Melissa & Doug Deluxe Multi Vehicle Activity Rug Play Set The size of this set is wonderful! The size of each wooden piece is perfect for toddler hands. The quality is really top-notch!! Every piece is smoothly sanded and the edges are rounded. Each piece is nicely painted. I like the color palette used for both the wooden pieces and play rug. The painted wooden pieces stand out against the rug.
The 4 piece train has rounded magnetic connectors which keep the cars attached when rolling over the curved tracks or just driving around on the rug or floor. The train tracks have nice grooves, which help little hands keep the train on the track. The puzzle ends of the train tracks are easy peasy for toddlers to attach. The RxR crossing track piece has moveable gates on each side. There is also a train track bridge that had a good size tunnel for the vehicles to go thru.

The plastic wheels on all the vehicles are securely attached and roll freely. There are 12 freestanding road signs that stand in square bottoms. The signs are the shapes and colors of actual road signs which is a nice learning feature. The words on the signs are large and easy to read.

The vehicles are very easy to wipe off. The rug is completely bound on all edges and had a non-slip rubber backing. All the images woven into the rug are crisp, large and easily identifiable. One of the best features of this set is the rug is machine washable.

I love this entire set for my grand daughter and highly recommend it. Hours of fun for kids and adults. Definitely stimulates the imagination.

Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension I grabbed one of these the same time as I purchased the Turn Kicker. Initially I thought this would somehow be similar, in that it would shoot the cars out of a curve, but this is different. Basically, your car goes up a small ramp, into an enclosed compartment which rotates 90 degrees and releases the car down a ramp on the opposite side of the track. The ramps's are not steep, so if you set up the Spin Turn at ground level, it won't travel too far when it gets released. What's cool is, you can either have it trigger another stunt, or set up the Spin Launch high off the ground (via books or trestles), so when a car gets dropped off on the opposite track, it will have lots of gravity to continue on.

The Usual Issue:
Upon assembly (which is super simple), once you attach the white roof to the Spin Turn's car base, you can't take it apart. It's already near impossible to put all pieces back in their box, but this just makes it a definite nope! Sounds like a recurring problem with many other Hot Wheel Sets... because it is.

I wonder if a better name could have been chosen than "Spin Launch"? It gives the impression that the car is getting launched like it does with many rubber band-triggered accessories. The car is only getting transported to another ramp. They should have called this the Turn Kicker, and the other accessory the Spin Launch.

Overall, I DO like the effect. Many stunts go so fast that it's over before you know it. This gives you a moment to at least watch it make the transfer. By all means, the transfer is quick, but not one of those blink of the eye or miss it stunts. A worthy add-on.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension

text_fidelity_a:
Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel) I've seen these decorative bookends before, but they're rather pricey. So when I saw one that wasn't as expensive and looked like it would be a fun project, I decided to give it a try. I've always enjoyed crafts and a recent project was assembling and decorating an entire dollhouse.
That project, which took a couple of months, was nowhere near as frustrating as this, which took two days (when I'm determined, I'm determined).
Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

text_fidelity_a:
IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens What a great creative art toy. You can do literally anything with this and takes your sketches off the paper and into three dimensions. I am amazed at the ways the kids put this into practice, and it kept them engrossed for hours with only a couple squabbles over people hogging this color or that. I'll get more into what we did below. But first, What you get and How this works.

This product is a hardening gel that can be squeezed into shapes using plastic forms. There are several forms that come with the kit, a flat sheet of plastic and a couple rounded forms for creating spherical shapes. The flat clear piece is great for tracing images so even young kids can achieve the shapes they desire. Also, we used it to make other curves to help flesh out animal shapes, but that proved a little more difficult.

Once you have drawn your shapes with one of the gel pens, you can use the UV flashlight to harden the pieces to make them retain the shapes you want. Then you can peel them off the plastic forms or sheet and cement elements together into three dimensional structures. The possibilities are endless and only limited by creativity. Our kids started out by tracing the provided dinosaurs and moved on to tracing other dinos from various books until they had a small forest of dinos and trees.

Warnings and caveats: I'm a little leery of the chemically nature of this toy. There are warnings to avoid skin contact in light. This put me a little on edge and I wanted to supervise our 8 through 14 year olds to make sure it was not getting on skin or other stuff. Also, this does take a bit of artistic ability. It can be as free form as you want it to be, but we did have some frustration when younger kids could not recreate the stuff the older kids were building. But for the most part it was very conducive to creativity.

Also, the end products are a little sticky. So they don't seem like you can play with your creations, but you can make wonderful visual art. We have a nice little dino diorama on our book shelf now and the kids seem pretty proud of it. The inks are also a little messy, so make sure your in a cleanable area.

Personally, I think this is one of the most wonderfully novel and creative ideas I've seen in a while. I will be picking up some for the kids on my Christmas list, and look forward to refilling our supply.
text_fidelity_b: IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens

Digital Coin Bank Savings Jar - Automatic Coin Counter Totals All U.S. Coins Including Dollars and Half Dollars - Original Style, Transparent Pink Jar UPDATE 6-20-2016:

Filltech read my review and reached out to me to make things right. I really appreciated that! They sent a replacement bank free of charge as the one I received was defective and wouldn't count coins right. The replacement is 100% working and is not as hard to insert the coins. It counts them as fast as you can put them in and it gets the pennies and dimes right every time. I recommend this bank and seller because if it's defective, they will make it right!

I had somewhat high hopes for this coin bank, but it's not 100% accurate. It's main problem is distinguishing between dimes and pennies. As far as I can tell it has a lever that is supposed to detect the size of the coin and add that denomination to the total. It doesn't always work. Dimes and pennies get miscounted no matter how slow or fast you put them in. I put in $2 worth pennies and the count was $2.64 because of it counting some of the pennies as dimes. I corrected the count, then added some dimes, which at least four of them were counted as pennies. I think it's overpriced for this reason. If it kept a better count and the jar was glass and came with batteries....then it would be worth $18. As it stands now it's maybe a $5 bank. It might be alright for some people and I like the design and size of it, but probably will pass on buying it again.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall) This unyielding, oversized beast hangs out in my daughter's room and watches her while she sleeps. It has given me pause a couple of times because it has a very serious, fierce Cheetah face. Angry even. This isn't your garden variety Beanie Boo or cute puffy kitty plush. This is a predator and it lets you know it.

Way back when I was a kid, back when we wore newspapers around our feet instead of shoes to trudge to school in 18 feet of snow, I had a panther like this. It was all black and scary enough to send the house cat running full speed out of the room with a puffy tail. I loved my Bagheera so dearly, like my daughter loves this Cheetah. Some sort of magic happens when little girls receive a giant stuffed cat for the Christmas of their 8th year. Alas, my Bagheera crossed the stuffed animal Rainbow Bridge many years ago, but he will always be fondly remembered.

I am very happy that my daughter is also able to shower her love on a giant, regal stuffed animal like I did as a kid, when we lived without electricity or indoor toilets, and my only source of heat was snuggling with my stuffed wild cat. I always took my Bagheera to the outhouse with me in the dead on the night to scare off the wolves, coyotes, and wild boar. That I am here writing this today is evidence that my stuffed cat had a huge impact on my young life. This stamp kit comes complete with nine different stamps, a small ink pad with pink and purple ink, and five colored pencils for your child's creative enjoyment.

Melissa and Doug toys are known for education, creativity, and durability and most every product the company makes can be counted on to posses at least two of these qualities. The Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set isn't big on educational quality, but it does encourage creativity and the set and storage container are made from wood, for better durability. text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

text_fidelity_a:
Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players My wife and I bought this as we are getting more into tabletop gaming (thanks Wil and Felicia!) and I wanted something adventurous and less involved than a city- farm- building simulation game.
This is fairly fun, but the main reason I am writing a review is to specify why I didn't give it four stars and who should get the most enjoyment out of it.
To start out, you choose (randomly for a bit of extra challenge) a character class. These are more realistic classes such as a SCUBA diver, rather than a mage or warrior. Each class has a different special ability, for example the diver can traverse water tiles more easily than other classes. Then you randomly generate the playing field by placing the heavier island cards in a specific formation. Combining the random character roles and the random board is a clever way to make every game different and make sure the players have to think critically rather than relying too much on rote strategies.
Your goal is to traverse the board to collect treasures, cooperating with your fellow players by using each person's ability and the convenience of their position on the board. You may even bail each other out of dire situations by airlifting them to safety or using your special ability, because while you are trying to reach the treasures the island is constantly flooding.
If you ever wanted to play Indiana Jones this is a pretty good start. But for my wife and I to keep it interesting, we have to play on the hardest difficulty level (starting out with more of the island in a flooded state) and even still we have succeeded at our task 100% of the time. Because of this, the game gets old too quickly, which is a shame since the premise is fun, the concept is exciting, the gameplay is perfectly tight, and the artwork is gorgeous.
I do think there is a more appropriate audience for this, which is kids of perhaps 9 years to 13 years playing with other kids or in a mixed group with adults. I think the game will be more challenging for kids and I think playing with kids will make it more fun for the parents/cousins/uncles and aunts etc.
For two adults who are strategy-oriented people, there are more complicated games that are perhaps less beautiful and tightly designed but nonetheless more consistently engaging.
text_fidelity_b: Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players

text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do Art 3D Gel Painting Let me start off by admitting that the kids DID have fun playing with it. That's why it deserves at least 3 stars. But it is surprisingly messy for a product that claims to be for kids. They had a really hard time washing it off their hands, and there's a big warning on the package (which we didn't notice until after opening it) that says it may stain fabrics. The paint really easily gets everywhere- we found more of it the day after cleaning it up that we didn't even notice. On that note, the 3D aspect of it is kind of gimmicky at best. You can't really make a three dimensional structure, at most you can make little mountain dollops (as pictured) which take forever to dry. As in, you might need to keep it in a safe place for a couple of days before anyone can touch it. To be fair, they call it "fluffy", which it is. But the marketing would have you believe it can be somehow used to create 3D depth sort of like play-doh, which isn't true. Actually, I think Play-doh would probably have been a better project than this. Easier to clean up, can mix colors and make shapes, and dries into solid 3D shapes. But then again you can't use that to paint a picture as well, which this sort of does. So I guess this is sort of a product in between paint and play-doh. Not really what we were expecting.

Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers Dance Champs 2pk - BUNNY PACK Kids often like toys best that offer movement of some kind. Flashing lights and sounds also have a certain appeal, but at the very least there needs to be some type of moving action. Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers is a toy that offers some action and many youngsters will take to this toy right away once they learn how it works.

Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers includes one pink and one purple bunny. To get the dancers dancing, all you do is insert one of the plastic slides into the bunny, then pull it out quickly. This gets the pointer on the base spinning fast. Like a top, you then place it on a smooth, flat surface and let it spin. The toy offers Mechanical operation, so no batteries are needed.

Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers are action- oriented and I was surprised by how long the dancers continue to spin like a top after a single pull from the plastic slide. Provided you pull the slide out quickly, the dancers will continue spinning for a while. One game my kids like is to spin both of them at the same time, then sit back and see whose bunny is spinning the longest. They have come up with a few other creative games also, and this surprised me a little at first because the toy seems so simple.

My girls find this toy amusing, but one thing I noticed is that, unlike their other toys, Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers has little staying power. That is, the spinning just isn't enough to keep my kids interested for long. At first, it seemed like fun watching the bunnies spin and making up games but after the first week, their interest had tapered off considerably. The simplicity of the toy is nice and I am grateful that it takes no batteries, but after one week, the bunnies have already been relegated to the bottom of the toy box.

Kids like toys that move, but apparently a toy that spins and does little else just doesn't have enough action to matter. I still find the Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers good enough to recommend a little, but I can understand why some people will rate this toy below average. Kids love it at first, but their interest falls rapidly once they realize how little these bunnies can actually do.
text_fidelity_b: Furreal Friends Dizzy Dancers Dance Champs 2pk - BUNNY PACK

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top Update:
I got a blue top this time to head-swap with Barbie Paleontologist. I really loved the pretty dimples of Blue Top Barbie. I hope to get another one soon. This one could even stand in flat shoes. Her ankles were just right. Some of the other Barbie Made to Move dolls had tricky little ankles with a mind all their own.
Also the peg inside their heads are slightly different, so the neck on one doll looks shorter now.
I just got Barbie Made to Move today. I read many reviews about Barbie Made to Move vs. Style Barbie. I just had to try her out. Most people who have the 2 dolls say Made to Move Barbie is a much better poser. This is very true.
I liked the rooted lashes and 2-toned hair on Style Barbie the best, so I can't say Style Barbie is a loser. Style also has the bending ankle and can wear both flats and heels. Made to move Barbie has choppy hair. I like it just the same, because my real hair is not all the same length. I thought it looked nice.
Made to Move Barbie can bend her knees all the way back and sit down on her knees. She can bend at the breast/ rib cage, but not at the waist. Style Barbie cannot do any of this.
Style Barbie can only bend her knees to sit down in a chair.
Made to Move Barbie can spread her legs out like in yoga or exercise class. Style Barbie can spread her legs very little in comparison.
Made to Move Barbie has much sturdier looking joints except in the ankles, they are almost the same. One thing I did notice was one of her ankles turns inward like she needs her electrolytes. I thought it was the shoes but I traded their shoes around and noticed the shoes were okay. I still like the natural looking poses for this doll. She is a much better choice for those who love doll dioramas and modelling clothes.

Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set I have bought three sets of magformers now for all of my grandchildren (3 to 14). Even toddlers can play with them because they are too large to swallow. They also like the solid shapes and colors of Magnatiles but those are more expensive. You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

Werewords is a lot like "20 questions". Players ask yes/no questions in an attempt to identify a word that could be anything from "spatula" to "Mjollnir". One player is a werewolf, who knows the word already, and is attempting to guide the players with their questioning closer to the actual word without them figuring out that they know the word already. They win if players can identify the word, but do not know which among them is the werewolf. If they do identify the werewolf, then the werewolf can also identify the "seer" player (another with information about the word).

The deluxe edition contains a few additional roles for players. If you already have the other version of this game, I don't think you need to own this version unless you're a completionist. If you don't own any versions of this game, I think it's quite good.

My concern remains the same as before - the app for this game is good, and it doesn't appear to be going anywhere, but if you don't want to run an app while playing this game, then I totally understand, and this game will not be for you at all. I think the app does a good job of balancing the words against one another, creating the ability to discern easy from very difficult words, but the same effect could have been accomplished with cards. I would prefer the cards as well, but the app has the advantage of saving shelf space and also having a larger directory of words. In the end, it's a toss up, but if you don't mind the app, then this is the best possible edition of the game to get.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition

First, it is very important that you carefully check the device list on the official website. These toys DO NOT WORK on the vast majority of tablets and phones. Unfortunately, they did not work on my son's tablet, an Acer Icona. We checked the product list and it listed the Samsung Galaxy 3, which I happen to have, so I downloaded the game to my phone so my son could play with his new toy.

Second, the toys are extremely difficult to teleport into the game. It takes several minutes of manipulating the direction you are holding the lens, the lighting in the room to get the toys to teleport into the game. It was impossible for my 5 year old to do it on his own, so we had to spend several minutes teleporting each character into the game.

The worst part is once you close the game, the characters you teleported in are deleted from the game, so if you want to use them again, you have to go through the process in the second paragraph all over again.

This additional toy added nothing but frustration to an otherwise fun game.

fansmart 39" Pull -Along Wagon for Kids with Pulling Wood Railing Panels Outdoor Wagon 10" All Terrain Air Tires 330 lbs Capacity for Beach, Garden, Sporting Events, Park（Red） I got this 'Lil Red Wagon' from Fansmart mainly for around the house use. I have a much MUCH larger garden wagon that can be pulled by hand or hooked up to your lawn and garden mower/tractor. But, it's just not convenient for doing simple things around the flower garden. This Fansmart wagon is great for that. Putting it together, I noted a few things. 1) Don't overtighten the acorn nuts. You will pop the caps right off. 2) The wood stake and slate side panels are NOT the most solidly built. The wood is soft pine and the panels are just stapled together. My advice would be to coat them very well with some clear polyurethane or other wood preservative before assembly. And, don't be too rough or careless when working with them. it's okay to put a load against them. Jut understand that there are limitations on how much abuse they can take. 3) When putting the cotter pins through the axles, to hold the wheels on, make sure you bend them all the way around the axles, to prevent any chance of a puncture or laceration from the sharp ends of the cotter pins. 4) Use your common sense in assembling the front yoke / truck assembly. The illustration is not that detailed. But, it's fairly simple. The finished front end will NOT be that tightly fitted when you're done. That's okay. It's the way it was designed. 5) The rounded pan head of all the bolts going through the pan of the wagon go ON THE INSIDE of the pan, not the outside. Even then, the heads do not seat perfectly into the holes. They do have an edge that can snag on bagged materials like mulch, potting soil, etc. My advice would be to lay a piece of cardboard or something in the bed of the wagon. The would both prevent tears in your bagged materials AND protect the finish of the wagon.

I've been using mine for hauling heavy plants around and even moving frozen goods from the deep freeze to the snow bank, during this 'winter storm of the century' that we had down here in Texas. The power was out for four days and I didn't want to lose roughly $700 in venison. Lil Red did the trick.

If anyone is old enough to remember the 'Radio Flyer' wagons that were sold a few decades ago, this wagon is kind of like that. But, not as big and not as heavily constructed. However, this wagon is good enough quality, for the price, to still earn a five star rating from me.

At first I was confused, because I didn't know that My Little Ponies could take human form. I did some research, and the Equestria Girls series was when something was out of balance in the human world, and so Twilight Sparkle, the main pony, jumps through a magic mirror and turns into a human. Her sidekick dragon comes too, and he transforms into a puppy. Somehow they save the day by throwing a pajama party.

I was really impressed with how many points of articulation that the Twilight Sparkle doll has. You'll be able to pose her into whatever position that you want to. She comes with a pajama dress, with bloomers, with two shoes, and with a mask. Spike the puppy doesn't move at all, but he comes with a pajama hat.

As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

Pros:
+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form
-Twilight Sparkle can't stand on her own, but this is typical for dolls like this

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game We also have this game in the Dr. Seuss theme, and they're both fun. They're very similar in both cards and directions, but this one is great for little fans of Marvel.

There's a note on the directions page to let you know it's fine to customize the rules for your family. (We tend to do that anyway, but it's a great reminder!) There are 3 stacks of numbered/colored cards(1-red, 2-blue, 3-green). The player turns over one card from each stack. They'll tell the player what to do with which objects. For example, the first card will tell you to "Do a push-up". The second card: "with Captain Marvel's energy ball", and the third card: "on your head". Some tasks are harder than others! Each card will get a certain amount of stars. (At the end of the game, the players will add the stars up. The player with the most wins.) If your child thinks he/she can do the specified task, they will say, "I Can Do That!" If not, they can exchange a card at a time until they feel they can do the task. One of my children was given the task of "Crab walk under the portal, with Spider-Man's web, between your elbows". None of us were talented enough to do that, so he picked again. This is also a great escape route for the shyer(or younger) little ones. Some things will be less embarrassing or more doable for them than others.

There are also "Battle" cards. If one of those are drawn, then any other cards drawn will be put back in the mix. The player will then try to knock down the Green Goblin card with the object specified on the card. If the task is completed, the card is set aside. If not, the player has to put that card in his/her pile as a reminder to discard 2 cards before counting stars at the end of the game. (That way, they can discard to 2 with the lowest number of stars.)

While it may get old with what the players do, it does create a variety of mix and match tasks. The cards are constantly being shuffled. The game ends when all the cards are gone.

This is a great game for when movement is needed. It's not one that the players just sit around and play. The players have to get up and move around. There's also a nice variety of types of objects. There's a plastic block that will need to be filled with air, along with a ball(that's already aired up). There's foam items and thick cardboard objects(Green Goblin and Captain America's shield). My biggest complaint is the "portal". This isn't the sturdiest of things. It's hard to get it to stand up straight, mainly because it has to be rolled up a bit to fit in the box. It makes it hard to get under at times. The bigger/older the child, the harder it will be to crawl under it, either way. This is definitely a game for littler/younger people. Also, I fear that the block won't last long, since objects that require air don't make it too long around my home, in general. (For it to fit back in the box after each game, the air will have to be released. That means you'll have to blow it up before each game. It's not huge, so it's not the biggest deal. Particularly if used in a classroom setting, though, germs/cleaning wipes would be something to put into consideration.)

My children(3, 5, and a tiny 8) have really enjoyed playing this game, though!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game

text_fidelity_a: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone Our family loves word games, and I was hoping this would be one we could add to our favorites. The idea is similar to other games out there - (first thing I think of is Scattergories) - where you have to quickly think of words that start with a specific letter for a particular category. In this case, the category might be "pizza toppings," and then you call out an item, tapping down the letter it starts with, and hand it off to another person who has to call out another item starting with another (non-tapped) letter, etc etc, until the timer buzzes. The concept is generally ok. But there are better versions of this type of game out there. More creative, I guess. And I honestly do NOT like the design of the Tapple board that gets handed around. It's nearly impossible to quickly pass it off without accidentally tapping down one of the letters in the process. Big design flaw. We *have* found an unexpected use for this game - it's been a fun way to help my 6yo expand his vocabulary. We don't play the game, per se, but do use it without the timer and have him think up different words within each category. But for a group game? I'll pass.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

text_fidelity_a:
SmartLab Toys That's Gross Science Lab this is still a good starter book on a difficult but important topic.
Science is a great subject that all need to learn better and That’s Gross Science Lab attempts to bring the fun of learning to curious kids. It encourages kids to conduct science experiments, each with an emphasis on learning and on creating something, well, gross and disgusting.

My girls love the subject of science and they did like this science set when it was introduced to them for the first time. I was a little disappointed when I opened the box and found it contained so little. You get three molds- one for barf, one for a centipede, and one for a maggot; a toilet mixer; a plastic jar; a bubble wand; spoon; two beakers and a stand. A small booklet with experiment ideas gets kids and parents started so they can create and laugh at so many gross things.

With the experiments, there are a total of 20 and some of them are fun for kids. But one problem I have is that every single one of them requires household ingredients, which you may or may not have. We were still able to do some of them right away because all they required was baking soda, corn starch, eggs, etc. But others required a special visit to the store and this could be upsetting to children and parents who want to open the box and start experimenting immediately.

What you get with this science kit isn’t much, but I must admit that it does get kids interested in science even more than before. In fact, that might be the most compelling reason to buy this science kit. It helps pique kids’ interests and makes them want to investigate more about the world around them. Other than that, this is a toy of average worth that may or may not satisfy those who buy it.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys That's Gross Science Lab

Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This is a good programmable movement game for 2 - 4 players. You draft a set of movement cards, then organize them into a plan of action for your turn, and you let your mole loose on the dirt. Everywhere you pass, you add to the pile of dirt until your dirt piles get so large that they topple over, which usually happens near the end of every game...

...but the real fun of this game is the rock. If your mole hits the rock, which moves around each round at the whim of the player who drafts the right card, then you bump, switch directions, and watch your plan fail and falter. It's funny, even for the person who gets messed up because of it.

So this is a very fun game that is light and easy to learn. I wish the underground was a little clearer in terms of where the spaces are, or that the moles were a little bit better sized for the pieces. It works though.

text_fidelity_a:
Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This is a really great idea for a children's bank and the top part, the counter, works really well. Unfortunately, there are a number of things here that made it not really work for my family. At least not at this time.

First, with little children in the house, the top buttons get pressed accidentally or on purpose when they are not supposed to and so the count has not been correct for that reason. I almost would've preferred some other method of managing bills and kept this as a coin counter only so that you have the immediate feedback putting something in, seeing the number change, and knowing that it's accurate. This would not be an issue in households only with bigger kids who can control themselves from pushing buttons inappropriately, but definitely made it not workable in my house during these years.

Next, I really hoped that the cool top would have threads so that they could fit on a mason jar of any size, so while the little ones are tiny they can have a little chart, and as they grow older they can have a large jar, but unfortunately it does not work with any size mason jar – the sizing, the threads, and the lip that hangs over are all totally different.

Lastly, and this is my main issue, the cheap, foggy, and unattractive plastic container that holds all of the money is so lightweight and is angled weird so that if there are primarily bills with only a few coins in there, the whole thing gets really top-heavy and wants to tip over. My son primarily gets money through finding change on the ground and through getting dollars or 20s on his birthday or Christmas. So there are a few coins in there, sure, but mostly single bills sent from afar through the mail. Had they made the top interchangeable with Mason jars, this would have been an issue because I just would put the whole thing on nice glass mason jar, probably one of those colored blue, purple, or green ones that they've come out with in recent years. Alas, you're really stuck with just the plastic container that the lid fits on. This limits how long anybody would want to use something like this, because I think most teenagers have slightly better taste than to want some cheap plastic thing of a single specific size sitting in their bedroom.

That said, for a very specific age range and if you don't have smaller children around the house, this could work really well and be a very fun way of having kids learn about saving and making it rewarding.
text_fidelity_b: Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size

Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

When this toy comes out of the box, you'll have to put together 3 different pieces. The head has to be attached to the body, and a little spring part attaches to the side. There are 6 different colored balls, too.

This toy does NOT come with batteries. You'll need 4 AA batteries, along with a small screwdriver(Phillips head or flat, either one) to get them into the toy.

LEGO Star Wars Solo: A Star Wars Story Kessel Run Millennium Falcon 75212 Building Kit and Starship Model Set, Popular Building Toy and Gift for Kids (1414 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This LEGO STAR WARS KESSEL RUN MILLENIUM FALCON BUILDING KIT (75212; 1414 pieces) is a great set—definitely one of my all-time favorites. When completed, the kit produces a large, heavy but solid, fun-to-play-with model of the “Kessel Run” Millennium Falcon that’s featured in the new Han Solo movie (“Solo: A Star Wars Story”, released on 5/24/2018). As an adult, I really love this Millennium Falcon, which has a large removable space shuttle in front that accommodates a minifigure, and two powerful, spring-loaded bolt shooters. The bolts always fly 18” or more (you get four bolts). There is also a gunnery pod for minifigures in the center circular area.

The build is fairly demanding, which makes it a lot of fun for experienced builders. The parts you assemble aren’t always symmetrical, and there are a lot of left- and right-handed components, so you have to pay attention to the instructions as you build. There are some “studs not on top” segments, and some components (like the removable transparent nose cone) that are attached “sideways” to vertical studs. There are also a few items (e.g., the lever-action doors at the top front) that attach with Technic parts.

Most of the “triangular” pieces on the top of the model swing up for easy access to the furnished interior. Inside there are chairs that accommodate minifigures, control panels (done with stickers), coffee bars, and engine parts storage boxes. The stickers aren’t excessive, and are easy to position. (I use a thin, flat, metal spudger to pick up and place the stickers accurately.)

The set has several specialized bricks that I haven’t seen before (e.g., the bricks that form a channel for the space shuttle to slide in and out of the front of the model). It also has some unusual building techniques that are used to link together pieces that are installed along a curved line. The model has four sturdy feet, which allow it to stand on a flat surface with space for the underbody gun turret.

The set has only 1414 pieces, but many pieces are very large (e.g., the triangles that open on top). The finished model is a big, substantial toy (the circle is 12” across).
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Solo: A Star Wars Story Kessel Run Millennium Falcon 75212 Building Kit and Starship Model Set, Popular Building Toy and Gift for Kids (1414 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game This is a fun game. My boyfriend and I played it. It is only a two-player match game like tic-tac-toe or battleship. The youngest player starts and both players get two cards which they keep face down until the end of the game. The first player pushes out a cube in the top left corner of the game grid. The next player then pushes out another cube on the board with that same cube. The play continues with each player pushing out the next cube with the previous cube just played without using the same grid hole. The idea is to match five of the same characters in a row either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. When one player indicates a match, the losing player turns over their cards and if the character on one of the cards matches the winning players match, then that person now wins the game. If there is no match, then the winner keeps his win.

The game is simple, yet fun, and is full of strategy. There are two negatives, however. The game case is difficult to open and it feels like I am going to break off the plastic prongs when I pull it apart. Also, the game wobbles a bit when the outside "wings" are down. Third, it is easy to knock all the cubes out of the game grid. As my boyfriend was playing, he titled the game just a bit to see the characters better and many of the cubes fell out. Other than the lackluster quality of the game parts, the game itself is wonderfully simple and tremendous fun.
text_fidelity_b: DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture This is a beautiful set, with the vast majority of the pieces being thoughtfully designed and thoughtfully put together. I like that each of the room sets goes together really well, so that you have a cohesive feel throughout your dollhouse without everything feeling identical.

The quality level on some of this is absolutely stunning given that it is at a reasonable price point and made for children. I really love some of the pullout drawers that are actually functional, and the upholstery on the bed and couch, chairs and Ottoman are incredible. I think my favorite piece might be the show off cabinet that has clear plastic windows, so that you can display things in the dollhouse. We have some miniature flower vases and things like that that fit perfectly.

There were a few things that came with the quality a little bit off. The toilet arrived broken, and not only was it broken, but I could tell that the way it was put together facilitated it arriving broken. The toilet seat pins were attached in a way that the toilet seat cannot close properly over the main body of the toilet, and the part that broke off, the back toilet tank, showed very cheap pressboard material underneath, which I did not expect from Melissa and Doug brand. There were a few doors, like the refrigerator, that were also put on a little bit diagonally in a way that would drive type a grown-up a bit crazy.

The vast majority of the things however appeared to be made of real wood and had a really incredible quality and design. I put them into a new dollhouse that I'm creating for fun to play with with my kids, and it's been really fun to accessorize and make everything fit into the dollhouse in a way that feels truly special.

The packaging is ready to be dressed up or wrapped as a gift. The packaging I got was a big, wide, flat cardboard box with a plain brown exterior that you lift the lid and find a bunch of brown paper wrapped furniture. If you wrapped this with wrapping paper, it would be perfect as a gift, but if given right out the box, it definitely lacks a little sparkle. That said, once anybody realizes what is inside, the excitement level of unwrapping each individual piece was kind of like Easter, or Christmas. Really incredible.

Overall I'm really pleased with this set, and so many of these special pieces seem heirloom quality and like things that we will be so happy to continue playing with or keep for grandchildren someday.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture

MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS The MACTANO Starry Night Building Kit is a micro brick set, so it’s not compatible with regular size building sets. And the bricks really are micro! I don’t recommend this set for kids or anyone with dexterity issues. Many of the pieces are smaller than the tip of a q-tip.

I’ve been building sets for three decades, and I’ll be honest, this one was a big challenge. Patience and attention to detail are extremely necessary. I keep looking at my finished set and noticing mistakes I made, or steps I missed.

The pieces do stay together, very important for an off-brand set. The kit includes a tiny brick separator, it’s cute and much needed.

If I have so much experience, why did I find this set so difficult? First, each step in the instructions is really 2 to 5 steps. For example, step 12 uses over sixty(!) pieces to put together four rows of the backdrop. Every step is like that, and you have to pay extremely close attention to figure out what pieces go where.

Second, sometimes it wasn’t clear what color to use or where a piece should go, but I couldn’t look ahead. Future steps greyed out the colors for previous steps, and sometimes didn’t show the complete build, part of it would be cut off.

Third, some of the colors are very hard to tell apart. I used the wrong shade of blue multiple times, but I quit caring. Most of the painting is blue, so only I know about those mistakes. But for the very dark blue and very dark green, it’s hard to see the outlines of the individual pieces in the instructions.

I build brick sets to relax. Working on this set was the opposite of relaxing for me, since I had to focus so much.
text_fidelity_b: MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS

The Stunt set has clear instructions for assembly, and if you follow them carefully, the stunt works exactly as promised. The stunt is fun by itself, but also connects to the track in your existing Hot Wheels layout, if you have one.

The stunt uses standard Hot Wheels cars. It comes with only one car, but it’s best with three cars, so that you don’t have to retrieve the car after each stage of play.
