text_fidelity_a:
Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009) This is a really cool and interesting game! I wasn't sure what to expect based on the box and description, but unlike other contraption based games I've played (like the classic "mouse trap" from my youth), this is more of a cooperative play game.
There are 4 strings that move a (clearly mission-impossible inspired) suspended character around the playing board, and it takes careful pulling and releasing each of them as a group effort to navigate properly, sort of like a marionette puppet meets a corporate team building activity. There are some things to do like remove security cameras and traps but the truth is, the real fun doesn't start until you open up the jewel cage.
Once the cage is open, there's a countdown (you can hear the spring noise whirring as soon as it opens) and the police car starts to slowly circle the board. If you make it to the getaway car with the jewel before the car makes it to block your path, you win! If, however, you take too long, the police car will spring into place and block your path. Hilarity ensues as players start to panic and lose their cool, and in the end, whether you make it or not, it felt exciting.
Things I like about the game:
- It is cooperative, not individual. So you don't "beat" another player, you work as a team to complete the task in time.
- The mechanical game board is unique and really fun to learn
- It does NOT require batteries! The board uses spring loaded timers where necessary, no electricity. This is cool in a decidedly analog way.
- People can walk over and see how it is played and join with very little instruction

Things I did not, however, like:
- The truth is, when playing with my kids, we sort of skipped the first part of the game and just jumped to the jewel part. The designers of this game tried to make it longer by adding disarming traps and pulling security cameras in particular order based on cards, but it felt tedious after a few rounds. Really the fun part is the end. The whirring police car gives a sense of danger and urgency that makes it fun.
- That little spy is suspended by strings that get tangled so quickly and easily. It feels like I sneeze and they are tangled. Out of the box, I had to spend time untwisting it before we played for the first time, so be careful.

That being said, the game is TON of fun for different ages and we actually had some guests come over who looked at it and wanted to play too (adults AND kids). They all asked where to to get it, so it might become a regular thing found in our neighborhood. I'd say it deserves 5 stars, it's been a while since a game sparked this much interest that wasn't on a screen.
text_fidelity_b: Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009)

text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay This is a really fun "spooky" game for kids. It's not really that "spooky", but it does require that you play in the dark, which can be a bit difficult for the very young, but fortunately the large hiding place pieces and the very cute shadowlings got our daughter to play the game willingly.

This is a hide-and-seek style of game in which one player moves a real, working lantern around the board trying to illuminate the shadowlings. It uses the old fashioned "roll and move" mechanic, but fortunately, the game does a good job of ensuring that you can usually get where you need to go. This is the role best suited to younger children.

Other children, or parents, will play as the Shadowlings. The lantern player closes their eyes, while the other players move shadowlings that are not illuminated in an attempt to hide them from the lantern-holding player. This role is better for adults because the rules are a little vague and open to interpretation in this area. Technically, you are allowed to move anywhere, so long as you are not illuminated and I think that's difficult for children to judge fairly (even the adults had an argument about it).

Overall, this is a good kids game, and adults can have some fun too. I wish the rules were a little clearer on how to lay out terrain, what "illuminated' really means, and so forth, but then again, too much of that would make the manual unreadable. Maybe some picture examples would have been ideal. As it is, your children will need some experience with this game with parents before you can let them play alone, but it is clever and, unlike many children's games, it's good for parents too.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay

We had a small birthday party for her at my Grandparents house since they cannot travel to come to her main birthday party.  We bought her a Power Wheels for her birthday, so I didn't want to spend a lot but needed something to give her at her "other" party. I am so glad I went with this!  Her and her 2 cousins (7 year old girl and 3 year old boy) had so much fun playing with this set.  When I was taking it out of the box and talking to my daughter about the dog shaking the water off my Mom kept saying there's no way that dog is going to move. We were all pleasantly surprised when I pushed down on the dog colar. I LOVE that there are no batteries, no winding it up, just push down and watch the dogs tail spin in circles and head go back and forth. I read several reviews that love the dog, but were dissappointed in the barbie.  I knew going in that her arms don't move from their position, so I wasn't thrown off by that feature, and I honestly don't think it's a big deal AT ALL. The kids didn't seem to mind one bit. The thing is, there are a million different barbies, that do a million different things. This Barbie is the designated dog washer in Barbie Land, lol. Her arms don't need to move for her to serve her purpose... Of course anything with water is going to hold a childs attention just a little bit longer than usual. The three kids sat on the bathroom floor for over an hour taking turns washing the dog!  Their favorite feature is the soap bottle. I will say that is the only thing that may become annoying to a parent over time. It's appropriately sized for the playset, but we found ourselves refilling that bottle about every 4-5 minutes while they played with it. If you have an older child who could fill it themselves with water and a drop or two of soap, then you have nothing to worry about. The soap bottle is actually a really ingenius feature. I filled it with water and added about a quarter pump of hand soap, put the cap back on and shook it up before giving it back to the kids. If you hold it upside down (cap side down) water comes out the holes, but if you hold it right side up (or sideways) and squeeze you'll only have bubbles coming out so you can "wash" the dog. This is hands down her favorite Barbie in her collection! Such a simple concept, yet it's provided hours of fun every day for the past week.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Splish Splash Pup Playset

Oltree | Cooperative Strategy Game for Teens and Adults | Ages 8+ | 2 to 4 Players | 60 Minutes Oltree is a cooperative board game based off of a French role playing game of the same name. I haven't heard of that game, but it's vaguely King Arthur-themed, and reeks of middle age knights and peasants stuff, minus the dragons.

I get the feeling that these are well-known characters in that universe, and I think that if you know who they are, that might add an extra layer of fun to the game. As it is, this game is very...dull. It has a story, and that story is quite predictable, and you'll end up replaying the same ten scenarios over again if you complete the campaign. The writing wasn't exactly bad, but nothing really stood out amongst any of the cards. The actions are largely mechanical, but it is fun the first few times you work to add a barracks to your castle or help a damsel in distress.

I will say that the best element of the game is the production value. This is the only version of this game (that I know of) and it feels like what you'd get from a $100+ Kickstarter campaign, with wooden everything and quality cards.

I think if the characters provided a bit more personality to the story, or if I knew something more about the world, I might really like this game, but I found it rather mechanical and slow moving, and the campaign didn't hook me as well as I'd hoped. It's not a bad game, but it wasn't for me.

PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player So I played Farkle a long time ago, and my family in another state has begun playing Farkle pretty regularly on family game nights. So I was excited to get Farkle Frenzy. But I have to admit we played the first four games with different rules each time as we figured them out (not sure that I have it completely correct now.) It is definitely not a true form of Farkle, but like I said, it's been a long time, but the scoring definitely is different. Not that that is completely bad. I just can't shake the feeling that I'm getting something wrong.

But as improvement to the game, the shared dice is great, the kids love to depress the bubble and can't wait for their turn to push it. The game board pyramid is also a nice addition in giving them somewhere to place the dice, but the score is difficult and beyond my 6 year old. But we had fun playing it in general and we are looking forward to taking it to Grandma's house where they fully understand Farkle.

Pros
+ Pushing the bubble on the shared dice was a big hit
+ Fast moving game
+ Captured the attention of the boys even if they didn't necessarily understand the scoring.

Cons
- A little confusing on the scoring

Summary
All in all a fun game, even if we are putting a bit of a spin on the game. The 3D game board adds to the interest of young kids and Farkle is a very playable and enjoyable game.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

text_fidelity_a:
Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity It's not wide enough to make a scarf, not for most kids. There is very little yarn included. You will need worsted weight for this kit.

The last point leads into my main issue with this. It does not provide enough information. You know you need yarn, but yarn varies in weight from lace (even gossamer) to super bulky. These terms refer to how thick the yarn is. Buy too thin, and the project will look terrible. Buy too thick and the yarn won't fit into the weft holes. You need worsted weight, and the only reason I know this is I knit and I recognized the yarn. The kit doesn't tell you.

If you hit a knot in the yarn, as I did, you should not keep going. Cut at the end of the row (the instructions don't tell you this) then start on the right side again (the instructions don't tell you this) and whenever you stop or start, leave a tail long enough to weave in later (nothing about weaving in tails is covered -- you're just supposed to know how to do that).

If you want to do the purse, for example, cut 15 strands at 32 inches each (not explained) so that they turn into 16 inch strands when doubled. You can get away with cutting 16 inch and having them single stranded, but it isn't optimal, especially when you are tying pairs at the end. And maybe do it with a yarn not in this kit. They barely provide enough yarn in this kit, and no one wants their kid playing yarn chicken and getting upset. It's cheap yarn. Get a good amount.

When you start the yarn, it is shipped in a center pull ball. While the value of balls is explained a little (I suppose over leaving it in a loose skein or hank to tangle on itself) the concept of center pull isn't touched on. Dig into the ball and get the end inside. That way the ball stays still while you work.

You don't really need the tool to guide the yarn back and forth, but it should have come with a comb to push it down and keep it even, a trick especially hard when you move the piece along down the thread. That's perhaps the biggest design flaw in this. It tends to make the work uneven because it's slid and it leaves gaps where the next section starts. That can mostly be worked out by blocking the piece after (another technique not covered -- wet it, stretch it into the shape you want and even out the rows, and pin it down to dry.)

This is a great kit for someone who already knows a lot about yarn projects like crochet or knitting, or of course weaving. For a first yarn craft, a kid is going to need some help, ideally from someone who knows a lot about yarn projects.
text_fidelity_b: Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity

Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother I have to say that my baby (and my toddler) liked this soother. I, however, wouldn't say it is very soothing. It has too much stimulation going on to be considered all that soothing. (Even the 3 calmer scenes are still very active, bright, and stimulating.

This thing eats batteries. It takes about a week for it to completely deplete the batteries. Do yourself a favor and either use rechargable batteries or the lithium batteries.

I like the way this soother attaches to the crib. I've had many crib soothers and this one is the best for attachment. It has a holder that attaches easily to the crib and the soother itself pops in and out so you can move it without uninstalling it every single time. (And since it is more of a toy than a soother, you'll want to move it.)

The buttons are fairly easy to figure out, but once baby can stand or reach the thing, they can easily push the buttons themselves and cause chaos. The baby doesn't know how it works, pushes the upper buttons and makes the image on the screen change, then baby gets mad because they want their image back and they've got no clue how to do it. But you can't get them to stop pushing the buttons.

The remote only turns the thing off or on. It can't change the image or pull up one of the scenes. So, if baby hits those blasted buttons and changes the scene and gets mad about that, you can't use the remote to fix that. You can only turn the soother off or on. (And turning it on, it goes to whatever it was on when you turned it off.)

Also, if baby gets excited and hits the soother, the soother blinks out. (It turns off and turns back on.)
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother

Fisher-Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home The Fisher Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home is a fun child's toy made for girls who love dolls and are always looking for new ways to play with them and enjoy them. This toy is a mobile home, but it is basically a child's dollhouse on wheels, folding open to reveal different rooms for hours of imaginative play.

My girls love their dolls and they own dozens of them, so they took an instant liking to this toy. Probably the most striking aspect of the toy is its colorful components. The interior features colors like green, pink, and blue and the accessories add some orange and other colors. The mobile home has some movable parts, too, like a microwave door that opens, an opening refrigerator door, turning steering wheel, and flipping toilet seat. The moving parts are few, but they still manage to stimulate the imagination. There are no included dolls with this toy, but most children will have no problem integrating the dolls they already have into the mobile home and enjoying the imagination that it inspires.

My kids like this toy and it is certainly an above average piece of fun, but if there is one way that Fisher Price could make it better, it would be to add some sounds, lights, or something else to stimulate the senses. Flashing lights would require batteries, which some may not like, but sound effects could be added without the need for batteries. The added sound of a honking horn, a motor starting up, flushing toilet, or something would make the toy more appealing to the average kid, most of whom still want something that appeals to the different senses.

Girls love dolls and the Fisher Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home is a good toy for young girls who want a new way to display and play with their assortment of dolls. There are no sounds or lights and no actual family of dolls included, but the toy does offer a fold- out interior house and several accessories that are good for hours of entertainment.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home

LEGO Marvel Spider Man Far from Home: Stark Jet and The Drone Attack 76130 Building Kit (504 Pieces) This LEGO SPIDER MAN FAR FROM HOME: STARK JET AND DRONE ATTACK 76130 BUILDING KIT (504 Pieces) lets kids recreate scenes from the “Spider Man Far From Home” movie, but it’s a great set all by itself. There are enough pieces to make it a satisfying build (moderate difficulty), and it’s fun to play with even if you haven’t seen the movie.

My favorite feature is the bomb hatch located behind the pilot/passenger compartment that seats the minifigs. You can seat Spidey in the hatch, press a button, and let him drop down on his web string to dangle beneath the plane. You can also use the hatch to drop brick-built energy bombs. Behind the hatch, there is another compartment that opens for storing bombs and weapons.

The two little drones are quick to build. The drones and the Stark jet are all equipped with stud shooters. (Stud shooters are special spring-loaded bricks that shoot off single studs that were loaded onto them, when you move a lever.)

The jet has a minimum of stickers (always a good thing, in my opinion). The “adjustable wings” are the two upper ones at the tail. They can be adjusted to different angles. The big wings at the sides, and their wingtips, are fixed in place.

The kit includes minifigs for Happy Hogan, Nick Fury, Spider-Man, and Mysterio, as well as their associated weapons.

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition My boyfriend and I never heard of this game and this is their 15th "Appleversary" Edition.

This game is for ages 12+ with 4-8 players. Included in the box are:
- One game instruction sheet
- 441 Black Apple Cards
- 63 White Apple Cards
- 25 Scoring Tokens

After all the like colored cards are combined and shuffled (good luck shuffling 441 cards; I couldn't do it), the cards get stored face-down in the plastic game tray/box they came in along with the tokens.

The game of play is as follows:
- Each of the 4 or more players are dealt 5 black cards each.
- The one player in each round who is the judge picks one white card and chooses one of the two words on the cards. He or she then says the word out loud and places the card face up on the table.
- The remaining players pick a black card from their hand that they think best describes the word being played. They put that card face own in the center and when all the players have submitted their card, the black cards in the center get mixed up.
- The judge then reads each card aloud and the player who submitted that card makes their case to the judge of why their card best exemplifies the word being played.
- The player who won their case with the judge gets a token.
- The play then continues to the left with the card decks and judging responsibility becoming the role of the next player. Each player whose card count is less than 5 black cards is dealt another card.
- The game ends when there is a winner with four tokens.

What makes this game so much fun is the conversation that occurs when convincing the judge. For instance, the judge might pick the word squishy and a player might pick the card about fish and say something like when you're preparing the fish and stretching it out for cooking it becomes all squishy.

My boyfriend and I loved it and found it hilarious. We even found it more challenging because the two other people we planned to play with weren't available. As a result, we wound up playing two hands a piece with one of us playing one hand when we were the judge. That brought another whole level of ridiculousness to the table. It was difficult not to pick our own selections as winners.

This game is only limited by each player's imagination and ability to argue their case. It's perfect for parties or large gatherings with 4 to 8 players.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition

Adora Playtime Collection Pink 13 Soft Baby Doll with Bottle This is a sweet, tiny baby girl doll about half the size of your average newborn. I expected the feet, hands, and head to be ever so slightly softer than they are, but it's not so hard that you'd be upset if you fell over on it or had your big brother bash you with it, hopefully accidentally.

The baby powder fragrance is a little overwhelming to start, but I'm hoping that will settle down in time. I'm not really used to a lot of artificial fragrances so it's definitely a lot stronger than any other scented item in our home. The fragrance is overall pleasant, just a little too much. It really sticks to your hands, too. I played with the doll for just a few minutes with my son, and after washing my hands twice with Dr. Bronner's peppermint soap, I can still smell the artificial baby powder fragrance.

The baby bottle included doesn't look very realistic in the sense that the entire thing is made of a pale pink plastic, so there's nothing that looks "milky" in there. There's also no differentiation between nipple, lid, and bottle. That said, it does fit into the baby's mouth and stay there nicely. I like that the baby's body is made of the silky material kind of like a ribbon, and the outfit she is wearing is easy to take off and put on for little hands. I wish there was not printing on the front of the shirt, as I'm not sure a baby doll needs to say "pretty girl" on the front. My son really enjoys taking off the headband and putting it back on.

The eyes open and close and if not perfectly upright, the baby has a generally heavy lidded disposition. The one unnerving thing is that when the eyes are opened/the baby is angled too quickly, the eyes make a clicking sound when the lids open fully. I wish they'd done a little more design testing to eliminate that minor flaw, because my toddler son was immediately entranced and wondered what the noise was and it caused some not very gentle experimentation with flipping the baby around to see what was going on with the sound.

Even with what I see as a few minor design flaws, overall this is a very sweet, nicely sized baby doll for a young one aged 1 to 3, and would be a good doll to put in a miniature baby carrier or generally to carry around and play with. I wish I had thought to get a doll like this prior to my son's baby sister arriving so that he could practice playing gently with doll and nurturing the doll.

The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box is styled and sculpted to be true to Mimic D&D monster lore. I count this as a plus, as nearly anyone can simply paint a plain trinket box and call it a Mimic. I am especially impressed with the interior sculpting, it's terrifying, especially the sculpted eye inside and 21 teeth inside the top lid. The interior bottom of the Mimic has 25 teeth and sculpted gross Mimic guts. Scary stuff for sure! The exterior painting is quite nice. It does not scratch away easily. By Merhoff & Larkin is proudly stamped into the resin of the bottom exterior. Each box will have some slight variations, as this is clearly a hand-crafted, hand-painted piece. I'm excited to bring The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box to the table, it's an impressive hand-crafted prop. AMIGO X-Code Cooperative Strategy Board Game, Black This is very different from anything we have played before. It is very quick to learn and very quick to play. I love that it is cooperative which keeps most hurt feelings down. It played well at a range of ages from 11 to 51 which was also fantastic. All in all, I am very impressed with this game.

The play is very easy...at first. Basically, you are passing cards to help each other make sets and cover the numbers on a phone keypad. There are rules governing how to pass and who to pass too and lots of communication as you try to get cards where they need to go. You can also make sets of cards that allow you to extend your game by flipping your one minute timer. We found the first round pretty easy actually, and then came the twists... It has a good variety of challenges that make a nice straight forward game more challenging.

I highly recommend this game. There are few games that can be learned so quickly, play accross some many ages, and be so fun and engaging. They hit it all on this one.

While I personally didn't play with Barbies as a young one, the fact that they have more normal body shapes with Daisy and others, different ethnicities, the sports Barbies who are able to actually move well, and Ken and Barbie doing ordinary, more usual things that kids would be familiar with like the set that has Ken doing the laundry, and this set that has Barbie being a chicken farmer. I love it!

Though I think of Barbies as being for slightly older children than my three-year-old daughter, she absolutely loved this set and knew exactly how she wanted to play with it. Putting the chickens in the nest, collecting the eggs into the bucket, moving Barbie around and having conversations with the chickens, making the chickens say peep peep peep!

As for the set, my only suggestion would be to make the eggs able to come out of the a container. Even if this means that most of the eggs immediately got lost, it would provide so much more opportunity for fun and creativity. In order to allow my daughter to collect eggs into the bucket, I made a few eggs out of oven baked clay so that she would have a little bit more opportunity for interactive play.

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games 1223 Kozo, Wood Grain Family game night is a big deal in our house when we’re all together and I have been looking for new games to keep things fresh. We have Jenga, a fun game in its own right, and Kozo on the surface appears to be very similar in concept. It’s a bit trickier, though it’s great fun. The one reservation I have is the sheer number of small parts – easy to misplace or lose if care isn’t taken with storage.

The concept is very similar to Jenga: stack and arrange your pieces and build your tower up without knocking it over. In concept, this is about as simple as it gets. However… Unlike Jenga, there are different sized pieces of different types, and as a result the placement is a lot trickier. Also, there are more rules to gameplay regarding what to place and when, and you don’t necessarily lose when the tower falls as there are multiple rounds to play (if you follow the rule set as specified). Overall, it’s a lot of fun.

My concern is that there are a number of small pieces and these can easily get lost or misplaced. If the tower falls, it doesn’t take much for some of the smaller black cubes to skitter away and end up under furniture where they’re more difficult to track down. This is unfortunately the nature of this game; making the pieces bigger would increase the cost.

Overall, fun game! It takes a little more strategy and effort than Jenga and the replayability is high. Be careful to keep track of the little pieces though.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games 1223 Kozo, Wood Grain

Nature Bound Bug Catcher Critter Barn Habitat for Indoor/Outdoor Insect Collecting with Light Kit, White Very cool when used with adult supervision and a LOT of info about what is humane and what isn't. I've definitely seen some kids use this type of cage as a permanent home for their reptiles or frogs, and that is 100% wrong. Animals need space, and while keeping a terrarium can be great for kids to learn about living things, life, death, responsibility, etc, parents are obligated to do research on what size is correct for what animal(s) to ensure they have a decent quality of life.

Having said all that, this is not meant to be a permanent home for any sort of reptile or amphibian. It's a place to observe creatures for a Short time, and then release them. For that use, it is fine. For anything longer than a couple of days, it is cruel.

Some neat features: the light (of course!), a ruler at the bottom so kids can measure the animal without handling or harassing them too much, a magnifying lens (but it only works a little--you need to be in the right spot for that to do anything), and a little mini lid on top, which is especially useful if there's a reptile, amphibian, or spider inside, and you want to introduce an insect for it to eat.

Nice hands-on educational potential!

text_fidelity_a:
Minnie Mouse's Home Sweet Headquarters is a 4-level dollhouse playset with five rooms of play and features three figures, 12 play pieces, an elevator, and Minnie's magic Turnstyler fashion closet. This little Minne Mouse playhouse is just adorable! Perfect for toddlers and preschool children. It is a replica of Minnie's house from the Disney Channel, Disney Junior show called, "Happy Helpers Adventures." The playhouse is called, "Minnie Mouse's Home Sweet Headquarters," and in the show it is located in the town of Hot Dog Hills. This house is not just Minnie's home on the show, but it is also the business headquarters for Minnie and Daisy Duck's business, "Happy Helpers." The house has five rooms and four levels. There is a cute elevator leading to the second floor, and a "Turnstyler" closet which contains three different Happy Helpers outfits (note they are pictures of clothing rather than actual clothing that a child could put on Minnie).

Minnie's Home Sweet Headquarters set includes three 3-inch poseable figures, Minnie, Daisy, and Figaro (the kitty from the film, Pinnochio), as well as 12 accessory play pieces, including two beds, a vanity, and two desks just like the ones on the Disney show. There are also a spa tub, a hairdryer, and an oven and serving cart in the kitchen, and Figaro has his own pet food and bowl.

This play house requires a small bit of assembly, but even I managed it easily, and I am definitely not good at putting things together.

I really appreciate that this is not a typical empty doll house. It's great that it comes with furniture and other interesting pieces and the three occupants, who are the main characters from a child-favorite Disney TV show, Daisy Duck, Figaro and, of course, Minnie Mouse. There are lots of lovely, bright colors throughout the house, with Minnie's signature color of pink predominating. I especially am impressed with the little elevator that goes up and down, the rotating closet and the fact that the house's doors open and close.

This has turned out to be a very popular gift with my 20-month-old granddaughter. She loves it now, and she can continue to enjoy for several more years to come.

A terrific Christmas present!
text_fidelity_b: Minnie Mouse's Home Sweet Headquarters is a 4-level dollhouse playset with five rooms of play and features three figures, 12 play pieces, an elevator, and Minnie's magic Turnstyler fashion closet.

Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.
text_fidelity_b: Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches

text_fidelity_a:
Haktoys RC Quadcopter WiFi HD Live Streaming Drone with Camera, Gesture Recognition, Optical Flow Positioning, Trajectory Plan, Take-Off & Return Key, 360°Flips, Headless Mode We have quite a few quadcopters in our house between my son and I- everything from micro drones that fit in the palm of your hand to foldables and RC car drone combos to full sized DJI Phantoms. So we have a bit of experience with these sort of things, and I have to say I really like this one.
The size is larger than the micro drones but smaller than the RC car combos and a fraction of the pro level ones. This makes it lean enough that we can fly it around indoors but substantial enough to hover and hold it's position properly (the micro drones sometimes shift when a fan turns on LOL). It does all the standard tricks a small Made-in-China drone can be expected to perform, including 360-degree flips, and even includes a surprisingly half decent camera that connects via their app from the play/app store. I mean, its obviously nothing close to my Phantom's camera, and you'd only ever use this for fun and not if you ever want to look at the pictures/video ever again... but it's probably one of the best cheap Chinese drone cameras I've seen yet. Sort of reminds me of a low end cell phone or dash cam in quality, whereas our other cheap drones have horribly grainy/noisy and pixely images with totally wrong and fluctuating color and blown out highlights/darks in any lighting (and one of them even only displays the camera upside-down for some reason- don't ask). The bottom line is, this one is NONE of those things, it's actually pretty decent for a hobby toy.
The ONLY thing I don't like about it, however, is the emergency shut off. Every drone, especially toy ones, need to have one of these features. Think of it like an ABORT button, that you press if something goes wrong such as getting too close to a person or ceiling fan blade, etc, or sometimes in our case if it got stuck somewhere and is about to grind off its propellers into a metal shelf. It is supposed to immediately shut all motors and allow the drone to fall from its position. But the shut off on this remote requires you to press and hold the button for a couple of seconds for it to stop. I thought maybe we were doing it wrong so I checked the instructions again, and sure enough it says "press and hold for a long time". I'm including a shot of the manual page, I couldn't believe it until I saw it. That's a horrible idea for an emergency and would likely be too late if you have to hold the button for a while hoping it stops before the drone damages itself or worse, a person.
So, I want to give this drone 5 stars, I feel like as a drone it is awesome and fantastic. Flies nicely, has great features and a fun camera, but that shut off is a design flaw worth removing at least one star.

Skull Party Game | Bluffing Game | Strategy Game | Fun Game for Game Night | Family Board Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 13+ | 3-6 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Space Cowboys I really loved this game. Will disclose, I've only played it once since I've got it, but it was very fun that one time.

It takes what I love from Liar's Dice, but gives it more suspense in my opinion. Liar's Dice can reach a point where for certain someone is losing a die, but in Skull, sometimes, it's just a challenge of what you pick up, and who you know for a fact has a skull on their mat. I love the suicide bluffs people pull with putting a skull down then bidding, and the whole bidding idea is really fun to me too.

The art is really pretty, though there are a few skulls I think that look more boring than others, all look good. The material is a hard cardboard with great texturing, feels like a coaster almost, I think it can be very durable, but getting them out of their original squares was a little bit of a challenge to not tear any. I also love how small the box is, you could carry this to any place you want rather easily. I almost am a little sad that it only has enough for 6 players, I could easily see this going further than 6 players, but playing with 6 players, it was very fun. I loved every second.

I rate this highly because I love the set, but I will admit, this game could be easily played with cards instead of this. It wouldn't be difficult not even slightly, with no rules adaptations other than changing the skulls to faces, and flowers to numbers. That shouldn't dissuade you from purchasing this though, this is a really cool set, that will last a good amount of time, and it is a nice bit of decoration anyway with that pretty box! This will likely become a board game of mine to play whenever I can, for a very long time.
text_fidelity_b: Skull Party Game | Bluffing Game | Strategy Game | Fun Game for Game Night | Family Board Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 13+ | 3-6 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Space Cowboys

Pink Racer This is a fun and powerful little racing ATV that my kids, ages nearly 5 and seven, have a lot of fun playing with. We have another power wheels vehicle that we call "purple thing" because it has three larger wheels and is set a lot closer to the ground. That one, grips onto our lawn and has a lot of power for going up and down the small hills in our grassy yard.

This one, seems to even have more power than our last one, but unfortunately the tires are less grippy, so it ends up spinning out and people get stuck trying to go up a hill and have to strategize about what long and circuitous route they can take to get up the hill kind of sideways so that it doesn't lose power or more usually, spin its wheels.

This thing goes a bit faster than our other one, and has a feel of power to it, so I really think the wheels and their slippery, hard surface, are the issue. This is gotten slightly better with use over the last few months, but unfortunately is still happening very frequently when in use. We have found the issue is just as bad on our concrete driveway as it is on our grass. Our grass is a bumpy, country lawn that is generally on watered in summer and goes kind of brown and dry.

I also think they could've improved it by potentially making it big enough to seat a second, smaller child. Our other one is big enough that when our son was five and our daughter was three, she could sit behind him as he drove around the yard.

Overall, if you have a very flat, large lawn that a child would be unlikely to spin out the tires on, this is a really fun, immediately thrilling toy to play with, has a ton of power, multiple settings that are fun for the kids to experiment with, and is very maneuverable and controllable. However, for bumpier lawns or yards with some minor grade changes and hills, this might not be the best choice for getting around.
text_fidelity_b: Pink Racer

text_fidelity_a:
Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. I'm sure there are cooperative ways to play too if that's more up someone's alley, like it was for us when the kids were younger.

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. We already had the matching jungle gym, so we didn't really want to get the larger monkey bar swingset. I found this one and thought it was perfect. I was right. Assembly was a bear. Based solely on the weight of the pieces, you need a few people to put this together. It takes some maneuvering to get the pieces together and in place, but once they are together, they are solid. The swings and ring were a bit high for my 4 year old, so we picked up four 6 inch sections of chain from the local hardware store and some quick links. Problem solved. We left one of the swings higher for the older kids. My son and I swing on it together, and it only moves a bit. We will likely anchor it in the future, but for small children, it stays in place well enough. The coating on the swings is much better than the normal covered chains which crack and come apart. This is thick rubbery substance that fully wraps around the chains. We didn't use the feet on the bottom as it allows the set to settle into the ground a bit as we use it. The set looks professional, not tacky, and unlike wood sets, I won't be out there trying to clean it and check for splinters constantly. I can see this being used for generations. Great item. Seems like commercial quality.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set

This new Lego Sith TIE Fighter is priced far too high. The price per brick (ppb) is about 16-17 cents, where in most sets, the ppb is 10 to 12 cents.

The finished build looks sleek, with its red piping edges and new pieces to finish off the points of the wedges. But the ship is small compared to other sets of a similar price, or even compared to previous versions of Lego TIE fighters.

The included minifigs are basic. A generic First Order TIE Pilot, Finn (a duplicate from set 75257), and a Knight of Ren.

I like the build. It’s a ship that actually looks good on display, which is what I do with most of my Lego sets. The build includes a display stand, as the ship can’t stand on its own without perching on the stand.

But I wish there were more details on the cockpit of the TIE, or even more engine details to make it a set more worthy of its high price tag.

SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for $80.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is large enough to make it feel like a nice machine, but small enough, especially when folded, to port around, which is nice because it lends itself to easy travel. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards seemed kind of flimsy, and didn’t stay on well, so I flew without them. The drone handled test crashes well. The propellers held up well, with only some minor scrapes after hitting the ground and nearby trees. The copter simply hit the ground and the arms folded in on impact.

Quiet - The drone has a relatively quiet sound, and isn't too loud. I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. When executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward or backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button at the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Tuning - This was easy to do, and I liked the tactility of the joystick buttons. I found it worked well.

Camera usability- The quality is good, and it is fun to use. However, I’m kind of in the middle on this, which is why the camera is in both the pros and cons. It does provide an accurate view of what the drone sees, and I didn’t have almost any lag. The picture resolution was nice. It’s not super easy to use, but I was able to figure out most of the controls while flying.

Battery: This had a nice battery life, with about 22 minutes of battery life to 1.5 hours charging time. I didn’t stream video, which I would imagine uses a bit more battery, bt for my medium intensity flight, I was very happy with the flight time, especially considering that they give you two batteries, which could give you about 45 minutes of flight time.

Cons:
Unstable/Jerky Camera - Because the camera is hard-mounted to the drone body, the video is very twitchy and jerky as the drone flies around and tilts, particularly when descending. The video became very shaky. I found myself more inclined to use the photo option over the video though, because of how unstable it was. I also found the field of view to be frustratingly narrow, and wanted a more upwards view from the drone.

Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as set up the camera, one of the main selling points with this drone. I’ve found this is a common issue with Syma instructions, and it just makes the products a lot harder to use. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries

text_fidelity_a: Foxnovo Universal Tall Landing Gear Skid for DJI F450 F550 Sk480 Multirotor Quadcopter These legs are the perfect upgrade for the Syma X8C (white) if you're going to be using a different camera. The stock legs are just too short to allow you to mount any kind of adjustable camera rigging and GoPro type camera. You will need to do some drilling in these legs (and shave off the mounting alignment flange of the quad) to make them fit. But, it's worth it. This pic is of the same legs (black) on my Syma X8G (same body as the C, just a different color) and these legs on my Syma X8C. These legs give you the spread and stability you need, as well as the height. They're rigid, strong and don't weigh much more than the stock legs. I've seen some negative reviews regarding 'flimsiness'. I think that anyone should keep in mind the original configuration calls for bracing between the legs, in such a way that actually provides more structural integrity to each leg. Therefore, no bracing means less rigidity, the greater the chances of breakage. Having said that, I've been flying my Syma X8 quads with these for a while now. One of which was totaled. Seriously, the quad dropped like a rock from about 150 feet, crashing through trees and broke HARD. I had to do a total rebuild with new body, motor mounts, gears, etc.The only parts re-used were the control board and motors and the LEGS, which DID NOT BREAK!

Terra by Battat – Wild Life Set – Realistic Animal Toy Figures with Elephant Toys for Kids 3+ (6 Pc) I have mixed feelings about this animal hospital. Overall, the structure itself is extremely sturdy and there are a lot of wonderful ideas in the construction. The roof swings up and down with a hinge, and while it's heavy enough that I have some cringes about someone getting a finger stuck, overall that concern has not panned out. The overall structure is very sturdy, but then the little animal pens have extremely flimsy doors, one of which didn't work right out the gate, and refuses to close. A second door also occasionally refuses to close, which makes me think that this is a design issue rather than a actual broken product. The really cool little deck that has a string fence is really a neat idea, but then it was implemented in such a flimsy fashion that it is really not that fun to play with because it keeps coming apart.

Overall I want to like this more, but when I compare it to something by Schleich which just has all of the details really dialed in to where nothing breaks or comes apart all the time, it's clear that there is a difference in quality. This is made nicely in some ways, but then falls short on some of those finished details.

I will also note that it took me a lot longer to assemble than I wish. I really think that they should have assembled some more parts of it and shipped it as a partly assembled things so that I didn't have to spend so much time putting it together. I have small children I would rather be hanging out with.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack The Barbie Dream Closet is indeed a very happy dream realized. There’s so much space to store all of the clothes and accessories, as well any additional clothing items you already own for Barbie. The mini hangers work great with the clothing rack, as there’s a bit of a grip to the hooks so the hangers stay in place, but are easy to put on and take off. The system is also super convenient to carry around due to its folded design, which latches in the front with a Barbie labeled lever, and the handle on top lets this go anywhere with ease. I do love that this set encourages all sorts of ways to be fun, adventurous, sporty, fancy, and smart with the closet decals, clothes and accessories (lab coat and shoes, laptop, fancy dress with jewelry and shoes, scuba gear, etc).

A few criticisms though…the nob on top to turn the clothing rack is a bit hard to spin, both in resistance and due to the short nob. I do wish it was a little bit looser and the nob was a little bit taller to make it easier to grab.
There are a few areas that fold in and out for storage, as well as shelves to place things, but I think it would have been nice for some sort of drawer system. The drawers would have been helpful for storing the mini bracelet, necklace, hair brush, sunglasses, etc to give them a good home when not in use. Using my imagination, it would have been extra fun if the full-length mirror had a battery operated set of mini Hollywood lights to add some flare. I think some extra touches like the drawers and mirror lights would make the price worth it. I think it’s just a tad on the expensive side for it lacking some details, although it's worth reiterating that the included pieces offer a lot of good play and imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack

Ice Cream Cart Kids Pretend Play Stand - Premium Wood 33+ Pc Realistic Wooden Toy Set w Money Box, Chalkboard, 30+ Icecream Accessories Like Popsicles, Cones & Unique Flavors, Role Play for Girls Boys Please note: I received this item at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

First, let me tell you that I expected nothing less than a miracle when I ordered this one. I thought, "surely it can't be as good as the photos depict!" I was wrong. It's JUST like the photos show and it is adorable.

This is our second Svan toy this week and we are happy with the quality of this product. There is a LARGE variety of wooden popsicles and ice creams in this set. They are exactly as pictured and the quality and finish is superb.

Our 10 month old is extraordinarily advanced and tall for her age so we bought this thinking she'll be ready for it soon. It has 4 pieces which may be choke hazards but the rest are a nice size. I can understand the 3+ advisory on this though because you wouldn't want your baby to trip while holding a wooden popsicle in their mouth.

I gave this item 4/5 stars for only one reason - the directions. They were not clear at all times. In fact, the diagram showed one problem in step one, but thankfully we were able to piece it together. It was NOT a one man job and definitely was not easy. My dad helped me and we had a hard time figuring it out at first and had to refer to the box, which only shows the front of the ice cream cart.

The diagrams were wrong in a few places, but we still thought the parts fit together beautifully. The problem was that there were no written instructions. It was just the one page diagram sheet. My daughter will enjoy this for years to come! It's cute, sturdy, and functional. The colors are vibrant and fun. I hope Svan begins selling dress up clothes to go with their toys.
text_fidelity_b: Ice Cream Cart Kids Pretend Play Stand - Premium Wood 33+ Pc Realistic Wooden Toy Set w Money Box, Chalkboard, 30+ Icecream Accessories Like Popsicles, Cones & Unique Flavors, Role Play for Girls Boys

Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - The Roundabout - Quality Time Playing Together Wooden Safe Play - Smart Play for Smart Families I was so glad I found this brand of marble maze. We have bought a few plastic versions but they have all been flimsy and not very engaging.

text_fidelity_a:
Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up Back in the late 1980’s and early 1990’s I used to play MASH in school. No, it had NOTHING to do with the sitcom that some might remember.

The MASH game was an acronym for:

Mansion
Apartment
Shack
House

It was sort of a future/fortune telling game mainly for giggles. The original paper game was of course to tell you what “crush” you ended up with, what kind of “housing” you resided in, what you drove, and how many kids you had. One person drew a circle/swirl, like in this game, and you said STOP to get the “counter” number to begin the fortune telling – crossing off at the count.

This is an updated version of that game, though in all honesty, not near as much fun.

The basic model was to list MASH and three other variables – kids, car – crush. Like this one; you swirled and counted until you came to the end.

This game, while more grown up, is nothing like the old game even with the introduction of “scenarios”. Sadly, this is pretty much paying for something that you can get for free – sometimes you can even add more to the choices – pets, location, job(s) … with the old version, the only limitation is imagination.

This game does pay homage to its origins and includes the ORIGINAL MASH “scenario” card though the choices for everything is left up to the “decks” and not the players’ imaginations. That was, again the entire fun of it.

Depending on exactly what you’re looking for with this game – it might be best to save your money and write it out like I did or look online for MASH game cards. There are really cute printable ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Board Game For what it is, a trivia game just based on popular brands, this is probably as good as it gets.

The gameplay is simple, and they've devised a way to play with only using cards and the board, so no die required. The board is a path made up of 4 colors that the instructions say are in 'random' order. And even though the random order would never pass any randomness tests, it makes for game play that moves along.

The cards are the best part. Each card is usually dedicated to a different brand, so you could just thumb through the cards and pick your favorite brands by the pictures on the faces of the cards.

And, you'll probably wonder, since playing this is really similar to watching a couple hours of commercials, "Shouldn't they be paying me to play this game?"

Pros:
+Tons of trivia about tons of different companies
+You can play without dice, so this will last a lot longer than most board games
+Both easy and hard trivia questions, so people don't feel too stupid
+Even if you are really bad at trivia, this game will only take about an hour to play (15 minutes if you're awesome)

Cons:
-All the standard cons that go along with a trivia game. It makes the smart people feel smarter, and the dumb people feel dumber. I'm pretty dumb at trivia, so it was nice to play a trivia game and only feel mildly dumb.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
CVCBSER Smooth Swing Dueling Lightsaber, Increase Motion Control 12 Sets Sound Effect Light Saber, with 16 Colors Changeable Premium Metal Handle Lightsabers for Adults and Boys Gift (Silver) [[VIDEOID:acf24d91cee31c0de845571b6cd24d7b]] This is a very nice light saber. Good heft to it with lots of features. There will be a learning curve, but hopefully my tips as well as the video demo will make it easier for you. Remember that it is all in the blinking:

After assembling and charging your saber, you start off in SLEEP mode, meaning NOTHING should be illuminated. Hold the power button until the power ring illuminates and you hear a voice saying POWER ON. Now this is called OFF/AWAKE mode. Off meaning the lights/effects are not turned on yet, but the power button ring is illuminated. More on this OFF/AWAKE state later. But here, you simply tap the button to turn on the lights and effects. Now you are in ON/AWAKE mode, and here are the commands for ON/AWAKE mode:

ON/AWAKE MODE COMMANDS:
-------------------------------------
ONE BLINK: Hold the button until it BLINKS one time, then release. LOCK-UP effect is now enabled. It basically sounds like your saber just hit some electrical wires and is going crazy. Tap the button to get out of it.

TWO BLINKS: Hold the button until it BLINKS twice, then release. The saber will cycle through the color choices. Once you like a color, tap to set your color choice.

THREE BLINKS: Hold the button until it BLINKS three times, then release. You will hear a quote from the movies. To hear a different quote, hold until it BLINKS three times again, then release. Basically keep holding and releasing after three blinks to cycle through the quotes.

FOUR BLINKS: This turns OFF the lights/effects. But, the power ring is still illuminated, which means you are back to OFF/AWAKE mode, and here are the commands for OFF/AWAKE mode:

OFF/AWAKE MODE COMMANDS:
--------------------------------------
ONE BLINK: This allows you to set the sound volume. You can set between NO SOUND, LOUD SOUND, and SOFT SOUND.

TWO BLINKS: This is for light effects. You can have it STABLE, UNSTABLE, or PULSE. Stable gives a consistent solid light, which is what I have on during my demo because it's easier to capture on video.

THREE BLINKS: This is for setting a theme music. You can cycle through 5 songs, and the 6th is no music. So if you leave it at any one of the songs, whenever to turn on the lights/effects, music will be on too. So if you don't want any music, make sure you cycle all the way to no music.

FOUR BLINKS: You can cycle through more movie quotes, one of which is, "The force is with you Luke..."

LASTLY, to put it sleep. Hold the button for 10 seconds, so when you do this. It will go through its blinking, but just disregard them until the red illumination is completely off. This takes about 10 seconds. You are now in SLEEP mode. The same mode as when you first assembled and charged the saber. To play again, hold the power button until it illuminates, and you are back to OFF/AWAKE mode.
text_fidelity_b: CVCBSER Smooth Swing Dueling Lightsaber, Increase Motion Control 12 Sets Sound Effect Light Saber, with 16 Colors Changeable Premium Metal Handle Lightsabers for Adults and Boys Gift (Silver)

Spontuneous - The Song Game - Sing It or Shout It - Talent NOT Required - Family Party Board Game… Spontuneous is a fresh, clever & fun new family board game. You start by coming up with a list of words. Each word needs to be found in a song. Then once a word (trigger word) is given, the first person to come up with the lyrics that uses that words (in a phrase/line of at least 5 words) gets to roll the dice & advance. My 14 year old daughter LOVED the game. Even after our game was finished, she begged us to keep throwing out trigger words for her. She can't wait to play it with her friends. My 17 year old son is not a fan of most family games and although he did play with us, he couldn't wait to finish. He claimed that he didn't know enough songs to play. My husband & I both enjoyed it, though we did find that the 15 second allotment was hard at times. The directions weren't too complicated which was a big plus! There are challenge cards to get if you land on a certain spot. There was one penalty card which you could use if you caught someone on their cell phone! The game is designed for 4-10 players and is relatively short with games lasting about 30 minutes. It was interesting how we would all come up with different songs for each trigger word!

*I received the game for the purpose of trying out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.
text_fidelity_b: Spontuneous - The Song Game - Sing It or Shout It - Talent NOT Required - Family Party Board Game…

Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min

Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive] My oldest son turns 4 in just over a week, and he absolutely LOVES this toy! It's one of the few toys that he goes back for again and again.

There are two doors on the ship. One is to the back of the cabin and one is over "tick-tock"(the crocodile) who pops out with the press of a button. These doors come off pretty easily, BUT they pop right back on just as easily. There's also 3 "missiles" that shoot out of the cannon on the front of the boat with the press of a button. These worked great for us, but to be honest, those small pieces get lost pretty quickly. My son usually plays with the ship without those.

My favorite feature is the pegs that are placed ALL over the ship. There are little holes on the bottom of Jake and Skully's feet, so you can place them on the pegs and hold them in place while playing. There's even a little clear bar at the very top of the ship that you can put them on, so it looks like they're flying. I think it's a really cool feature!! I also really like the "rocking" motion of the ship when it moves. It kind of wobbles back and forth to look like it's floating on waves.

My only complaints is the sound, first of all. The music sounds kind of like it's coming from cheap speakers, and I find it annoying. My son loves it and likes to press the buttons to hear the music and phrases. If you really didn't like that feature, the batteries could be taken out. (I haven't resorted to that, but it is an option, since my son knows how to swap the on/off switch). Secondly, I do wish that this set also came with Izzy and Cubby, instead of just Jake and Skully. There are stickers on the side of the boat of Izzy and Cubby to look like they are looking out the window waving. I guess that's an attempt to make up for not having them as figurines. I know that you can buy separate figurines, but I don't know if they have pegs on the bottom of their feet to work with this ship.

Overall, our whole family gives it 2 thumbs up! We all love it, and definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive]

The little details just make me swoon! On this one, the adorable little potters wheel has a clay Lego minifigure that you can turn around as though you were sculpting the figure. And the pattern changing textile which reveals a pattern when wet, is absolutely adorable! I would've just love to have toys like this when I was young, and my kids are completely charmed. My kids are still young enough, my oldest is 5 1/2, that they totally appreciate all of this, but then there's still so much time that they will get to grow into and play with these sets.

My 5 1/2-year-old had no problem putting the set together from the instructions. I really appreciate about actual Legos rather than some of the other brands, that they number the bags and that all of the bricks just fit together so seamlessly and well, to where my kids don't have to constantly bring the bricks and asked me to snap them together. Everything just works. I found the instructions really clear, and while I helped with one or two small places, overall it was easy for my 5 1/2-year-old brick veteran to put together, and a fun build with few to no areas of frustration.

This would make a super gift for an art loving girl. I already have somebody in mind who I might want to purchase the set for for an upcoming birthday.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Friends Emma’s Art Studio 41365 Building Kit (235 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

LeapFrog On-The-Go Story Pal Green This reader is pretty neat.
It has a lot of functionality built into it.
It’s also pretty small.
It’s like a portable toddler story/radio!
There are multiple settings
Stories (37), Music/Poems (25), Bedtime (10), Create your own Playlist (allows for 10 minute recordings!).

I think the create your own playlist setting would be awesome for any parent that has to travel a lot or for a service member that is deployed.
The stories are easy to understand and they use voice changes for different characters.
The volume control is nice - I like that it shows the volume number in case the kid is using headphones - you can check the volume without much effort.

If I could change anything about this it would be that it used a USB type cable to charge it. It has a port for downloading additional content from online - but not for charging. It uses 3 AA batteries.
I also wish that during the bedtime setting it would not use the lights on the front screen - the lights are great during day use but not when trying to get the kids to sleep.
It is nice to have the timer setting for bedtime.

Overall, very satisfied. It is a 4/5 for us and would get a 5/5 if the controller came with batteries and USB charger had a wall plug.

You can keep the cider vinegar in the garage if that's where all you swim gear gets dumped out when you come home and just take care of it right away. I hope this helps!

text_fidelity_a:
Girl Scouts Cookie Oven Reminiscent of the iconic Easy Bake oven, this toy is a fun way for kids to learn about baking. small but sturdy, it has a thick and durable plastic housing. The green color is similar to a girl scout's uniform. It is accented with purple and pink. Baking is actually easy. One starts by preheating the oven by turning the pink plastic dial on the front. It takes roughly five minutes for the oven to preheat. the LED light in the oven comes on when it is ready and is designed to help gauge the progress of the cookies. Unfortunately it fails to illuminate much of the oven. a brighter light cold help you see more than maybe the closest two cookies.

Making the cookies is simple. The included pan feels like heavy aluminum foil. give it a generous shot of cooking spray before use. It is not dishwasher safe and you will probably want to hand wash it between batches. There is a syringe with which to measure the water that is required for the mix. The syringe is actually kind of cool. The markings are easy to read. Caution your child to resist the temptation to shoot it out into the bowl (or at you) as it will make a mess. Stir and drop on the cookie sheet. Insert the sheet into the oven and set your timer. a timer/clock is not included in the device which is a pity. It takes about ten minutes for them to bake. They are then slid into the cooling chamber where they sit for another ten minutes. the cookies are then ready to come out of the oven. There is a pink spatula like tool which can help pull the tray out or you can just use a potholder or oven mitt. The cookies are then placed on a plate lined with waxed paper. the thin mint mix which came with the oven also has a pouch of chocolate chips for the frosting. The chips are melted on warming station on the top of the oven. the outside and the warming station do not get hot which is great for safety. But that is not great for melting things. After ten minutes, the chips still were not melted to so I popped them in the microwave. The frosting spread easily and the cookies tasted good. the cookies are small and, frankly, the Girl Scout cookie monopoly has nothing to fear.

This is a fun toy for a child, boy or girl, interested in baking. It is easy to use and the outside does not get too hot. the measuring is fun with the syringe and the child is rewarded with a tasty treat for following the directions. there are a wide variety of replacement mixes available including oatmeal, peanut butter, trefoils, sugar, chocolate chip, coconut caramel and PB sandwich. they range in price from around 46.99 for a single pack to 14.99 for a three pack and are available on amazon as well as retailers like Walmart and Toys R Us.

The downside is that it does take time so be sure to have other activities for the kids during the baking and cooling processes. I wish the oven light was brighter and that it had a built in timer/clock. It takes quite a bit of time for six little cookies. while the color scheme makes sense since it is marketed under the Girl Scout label, it may be off putting to boys. Younger ones probably won't care but the older ones may object to the vivid pink spatula and feminine styling. The cookies are not an exact replica but an approximate. tasty but definitely not the real deal. I would have liked to see some "from scratch" recipes included. Children will learn some basic concepts about baking here including timing, preheating, measuring and mixing. But they won't learn about temperatures, ingredients and nutrition. But this is a toy that may encourage a baby baker to hone the craft as he gets older and develop an understanding and appreciation for the art.
text_fidelity_b: Girl Scouts Cookie Oven

I do NOT recommend this for three-year-olds for two reasons. #1, I think the pieces are a Choking Hazard. #2, I really don’t think they are going to “get” the game. If you follow the instructions, I think it’s really WAY too complicated for such a young age. Granted, instead of playing the game, kids could just play with the pieces in other ways.

Finally, I think this item is WAY overpriced, at least at the current price, for a Made In China toy. If you can get it cheap, then you might want to pick it up.

Nature Bound Ant Treehouse Habitat Kit with Sand, Connector Tube, Feeding Stick & Insect Instructions, One Size This ant home(tree house) is much smaller than I was expecting, but it's not tiny. Make sure you look at the measurements, though, so your little ones aren't disappointed.

This comes with great directions, so you're led through what you need to do. You can order ants, but the directions are clear for if you chose to collect your own. The kit comes with a coupon to get cheaper ants. (I can't imagine anyone wanting ants bad enough to pay almost $20 for them.) The coupon and the first order page on the website says you'll get 5-10 ants, but then the main page says 30. Even with the coupon code, you're still paying $9.95 for ants(shipping IS included in that price). I can't pay that much when ants are in such abundance around our home. Again, though, I DO give them credit for the great directions for just using ants from the yard. You aren't expected to buy the ants, but you do have that option. Also, to make it clear, you won't get a queen ant if you order. You'll only get non-reproductive ants. (That information is from the website page for ordering the ants.)

It only took my boys a few minutes to come running with more than enough ants to fill their new little home. Unfortunately, our ants have been very slow to feel at home. One died, though we followed directions exactly. They aren't working together like I thought they would, either. That said, so far it has been greatly exciting to watch what little they have done. One ant looks like Goliath upside the other ants, so he's been easier to watch. It's surprisingly fascinating to watch ants move sand around! I assume there will be more efforts from the other ants with time, but I was expecting quicker results. (I don't blame that on the ant farm, by any means!)

One other complaint is the fact that the bottom goes on so loosely. I kept working with it thinking it should be tighter, but had no luck. This is something that will be best watched without too much handling from children, since there are 4 pieces that are easily removed. This kit comes with a tube, which can connect to another tree house if you chose to buy more. (The 2 side pieces can be removed for this connection.)

Overall, this is a fun kit for kids, but it could have been better designed. Every child needs to have the joy of watching ants work, though! ;)

Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!
