text_fidelity_a: Barbie Fashionistas Doll 112 I am a long time Barbie fan. I loved playing with them when I was young, in the 70's. Then in the 90's I collected them. Then in the 2000's I bought them for my little girl. She's graduating from high school next month, but I still love Barbie! I got these for my 5 year old niece to play with when she visits us. I love the variety of body types in this set. I think that's one of the best changes to happen to Barbie ever! This set has 4 different dolls. There's the traditional Barbie that we all love. Then there's the curvy African American doll, a short, petite doll that looks like she could be Hispanic, and a tall , dark hair doll. The thing I love about them (their differences) is also slightly problematic. They all wear different size clothes/shoes. While, that's pretty normal in the real world, it's more difficult in the Barbie world. Some of the dolls could probably get away with sharing clothes, but curvy doll is out of luck. I hope to see more curvy doll size clothes in the future! And if you are planning to gift this, be aware that they don't come in the typical pink Barbie box. They're mounted on brown cardboard that folds into a box shape. There's no colorful pictures or a plastic window. Other than that, I think this is a wonderful set and has been long needed!

Stomp Rocket Original Stunt Plane Refill - 1 Looper Plane Only - Performs Giant Loop - Gift for Boys or Girls Age 5+ Years Old - Active STEM Play Per my 6 year old: He loves his Stomp Rocket Stunt Planes because of being able to run, jump, and stomp on it. He also LOVES the green plane.

Per this mama: I bought this on Prime Day for a birthday gift for my son. I thought being able to run and jump for hours only to see a rocket pop up in the air would be worth every penny. Turns out I was right. The only downside is that I would not use this if you have small backyard. I live in the city, but I have fairly large yard. The rockets fly all over the place because they are stunt planes as opposed to rockets that are supposed to pop straight up into the sky. Think of the Stomp Rocket like a sewing machine. There's a pedal that you "stomp" to make the rocket go. Instead of electricity, air in the pedal flows into a tube and propels the rocket outward. The harder you stomp the higher it goes. The softer, then it doesn't go very far.

All of the planes are shaped differently and they each do different tricks. We haven't figured out all the best angles yet, but my son loves watching them go and then he runs after them. I would rather have just rockets because I hate having to traverse the poison ivy hill on the outskirts of my lawn, but you know whatever keeps the kids happy.
text_fidelity_b: Stomp Rocket Original Stunt Plane Refill - 1 Looper Plane Only - Performs Giant Loop - Gift for Boys or Girls Age 5+ Years Old - Active STEM Play

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player I looked forward to playing this game, but was very disappointed. It sounds fun - each player rolls five dice and adds their roll to the roll of a common die. I thought it would be more like Yahtzee, but it was not nearly as fun as that classic game. The common die gives the chance for each player to double their score, which helps someone come from behind and catch up with the player that is leading. However, when rolling only 5 dice, the odds of getting a decent roll were slim. It was almost impossible to get anything more than a three of a kind, and that was hard to do. This made the game more frustrating than fun. I've never played the original Farkle, and we had to make some house rules because many portions of the instructions were unclear, which added to my frustration. The instructions referred to online video directions being available, but I didn't think it was worth having to watch a video to learn to play what should have been a very simple dice game.

For those familiar with Farkle, the common die may add an interesting twist, but the bubble-popper and dice risers are unnecessary. The bubble-popper for the common die does not roll the die well and seems like it would break after a few uses. We took the die out and rolled it by hand. This was much easier and kept the game moving more quickly. (On a side note, when we removed the die from the bubble-popper, it looked dirty!) The dice risers are rickety and make the play of the game more confusing. Since you can't combine the numbers you get on individual rolls, it's necessary to keep track of what you got on each roll within a round. It was impossible to do this on the risers, so we just started putting the dice aside from each roll and not using the risers at all.

The dice themselves are sturdy, even though the white coloring started coming off the numbers after only a couple of uses. I like that there are four sets in different colors so each player can have their own color. However, the red and orange were too similar in color and it was hard to tell them apart.

Overall, I think the dice risers and bubble-popper are flimsy and just a gimmick to make more out of the game than there is. It's not an exciting game and became very boring when it became clear it was too hard to get a decent score from an individual roll.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle that is sure to be a hit with young princesses everywhere who are addicted to the Disney Princesses and love anything associated with them. This castle is much like other Disney castles available on the market, with a few added accessories and everything a young girl needs to enjoy hours of imaginative play.

I have two girls who have been Disney fanatics since a young age and still love anything related to Disney- especially the princesses. Their love of Belle, Snow White, Sleeping Beauty, Aerial, and the other princesses was reason enough to bring this toy into the house. Taking it from the box and assembling a few items was all it took to get the castle ready for play. In no time at all, they were running upstairs to find all of their Disney Princess dolls and bringing then downstairs to play with their new castle.

Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle and very girly in appearance, making it just right for Disney Princess fans. My girls like the castle and they love anything that accommodates their Disney princess dolls. They also like making up stories as they play, but they and I both agree that this castle isn't they greatest one with which they have played. One reason is the lack of any sound effects, movements, etc. I am thankful that the castle includes no lights or anything that requires batteries, but it would be nice if it at least offered some mechanical movements, sound chips, or something else. Another issue is the small upper level. This is where the bedroom is located and it is much smaller than the area below. It would be better if the two levels were a little more even.

My girls love anything Disney Princess related and they like this castle, but they do not rank it among their favorites and it is easy to see why. The lack of at least a simple sound effect, the small number of accessories, and the lack of folding or another way to make storing easier all add up to an average toy overall.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle

Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

text_fidelity_a: DohVinci Spotlight Spin Studio The idea behind this is good. The execution is not so good. I tried this product with my 6, 8, and 9 year olds. They could not get the thing to work well for them. You put cardboard cut outs on a plastic vase or bowl. Then you use a syringe/pen thing full of slightly thinner playdoh to decorate the plastic and cardboard vase or bowl while it spins on a little turntable. First, it is hard to get the playdoh to come out in even streams to make a design. It is difficult not the knock over the very lightweight vase or bowl while you are decorating. And then once you do manage to get the things decorated, what on earth are you going to do with them? They are lightweight plastic and cardboard and playdoh. Not exactly fit for keeping around. It was very frustrating for the kids. And not all that much pay off for the work you put in.

text_fidelity_a: Super Mario 70843-4L Nintendo Deluxe Mushroom Kingdom Castle Playset with 5 2.5" Articulated Action Figures & 4 Accessories (Includes Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Bowser) I’m not thrilled with this Mario & friends castle at all. I purchased it for my 4yo Grandson for Christmas. Truly to sum up my dissatisfaction is the pictures on the box are deceiving as to what can be done with this castle. You don’t realize it until you get it & open it. There’s no playing inside the castle. The pieces of castle are just sides as you can see in my picture. The descriptive picture shows a FLAT background paper picture which the castle can be placed up against via the adhesive tape they give you. Well the background paper will no way look flat like the picture shows because as you see in my picture it comes folded up making it difficult to work with due to the folds & the quality of the paper is poor. The castle itself is cheap plastic which I could see breaking easily. It’s just cheaply made & so disappointing that what you see is not what you get inside. A positive are the characters are all are very nice looking but not worth $40. This toy is outrageously overpriced. I realize I’m paying for a Mario product hence an increased price but surely not worth what I paid. I’m sure my Grandson will be creative & enjoy it. The paper background will be useless though. I don’t recommend this but like me our little ones see it & love it.

text_fidelity_a: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ I selected this game for my young cousin Brandon, who is just a few weeks shy of five.  I am happy to report that he loves this game and has played it 6 times in less than 24 hours!  The object of the game is for the dog, Shelby, to steal as many bones as possible.  The bones are made of rubber, not plastic, and the dog dishes are sturdy cardboard (which may or may not hold up, given that many pre-schoolers are hard on games and toys.  However, the game is designed to teach counting and simple math skills, and it does this quite well.  Since the dog steals bones from other dishes, the children learn to do simple addition and subtraction.  At the end, children count the number of bones Shelby has stolen, practicing their counting skills in a fun way.  I recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a fairly sturdy educational game that a pre-schooler will love.  A testimony from Brandon's mom, Laura:  "I love this game!"

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

Winning Moves Games Brainspin Creativity Game (1198) Such a simple yet creative little game. It literally takes seconds to explain the game and just a few rounds to master the idea. I love that it opens the mind to creative imagination.

The goal is to look at a simple glyph, then right doen as many unique things it reminds you of. For example, a simple square could be a sandbox, a sandwich or a corral. Each person writes as many of these as they can in a minute then take turns reading their list. If your idea is unique and no one else came up with it, you get a point. If someone else has it, you both cross it out. Ideas are juried by yhe players so you can't just say ridiculous stuff to be unique.

We played a number of rounds and they were boisterous and sometimes heated when people refused to count questionable ideas. But for the most part it was a great, quick game with more than a few laughs.

Only thing I wish was that it came with its own timer. We ended up grabbing one from another game.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Brainspin Creativity Game (1198)

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide The 3Doodler Create + is both a toy and an artist's tool. While trying it out the hours flew by, I felt like a little kid playing with new toys on Christmas morning. Despite the fact that it will take a lot of practice before I can make anything useful or artistic, I'm having a blast trying to learn how to make various shapes. The instructions are very basic, but the website has lots of hints, tips, projects, and stencils to download for free. There are quite a few YouTube videos as well.

As the packaging states, the tip gets incredibly hot. However, the pen's design makes holding it and using it comfortable without risk of a burn. There are 2 types of filaments in the kit; ABS and PLA.

PLA is made from sugarcane and cornstarch and is used for plastic cups, cutlery, and other food grade plasticware. It has a lower melting point and a slightly glossier finish but is not as strong as ABS.

ABS requires a higher melting point and has a chemical smell but it is stronger and less likely to break if dropped.

Cleaning it after use is easy. If there is still some of the plastic sticking out from the unheated end of the pen you simply tap one of the speed buttons twice and it goes in reverse. Once the filament clears the gear mechanism, which can be seen through a clear window, it's easy to pull out. If there is no plastic sticking out then simply use the rest of it up or the long tool can be used to push the remainder out once the tip is removed. The kit has tools to accomplish this and more. The website has good visual instruction for removing the plastic.

So far I wrote my dog's name. The second try was legible but more practice is needed. I then made a pyramid. Not too difficult but a bit rough...more practice needed. I have tried to make a long vertical spiral...haven't figured that out yet. I think it's best if I stick with 2 dimensional objects until I am better able to control the pen and it's flow. Once I master that - look out! I'd like to make a small lampshade, Christmas ornaments, and focal beads for jewelry.

Just what I need, another hobby!!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide

text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.

Kano Harry Potter Coding Kit – Build a Wand. Learn To Code. Make Magic. This KANO HARRY POTTER CODING KIT works as advertised. It requires an app (Win10, FireOS, Android, iOS) for operation and play. (The Kano Code app for the iPad seems to work well.) The wand is fairly large--big enough to look and feel like a real magic wand.

The kit includes a booklet with instructions for assembling the wand. You insert batteries into a circuit board, put a button piece and the circuit board into a part of the wand, and close the wand with another piece. Adding the last wand piece is a bit tricky, but the finished wand looks nice and doesn’t fall apart. A button on the end of the wand opens it up for battery changes. Two sets of batteries are included.

The app allows a child to create a Kano account, but sends an email to a parent’s email address to allow the parent to set the child’s privileges. The app opens to an illustrated map of the Hogwarts campus. The map has colored spots that you tap or select to open the “challenges”.

For example, an early challenge teaches the child to change the colors on a drawing of an owl. The coding is accomplished by dragging and dropping code blocks until they click together and add the color-changing capability to the wand.

As an adult who knows almost nothing about coding, I didn’t fully understand how the coding blocks went together or how the wand was supposed to be used once a new coding feature was added. With a little more study time, I’m sure that I would have figured out how to do the coding. However, if the wand is intended for a very young child, an adult with minimal coding knowledge will probably be required to help the child get started.

The coding kit also includes a nice chart of the wand motions required to execute the spells used in the Harry Potter books and movies. This kit should keep a child busy for hours, if the child is motivated to learn to use the wand.
text_fidelity_b: Kano Harry Potter Coding Kit – Build a Wand. Learn To Code. Make Magic.

Rockin' Inflatable Lounge, 74" X 39" I'm not ashamed to say I'm a larger woman (200lbs).
This lounger is fantastic, amazing, wonderful, etc.
I am a sunbather and this lounger allows me to lay all day and be super comfortable.
There is a small bolster pillow that blows up separately underneath you lumbar area.
This feature is FANTASTIC !!! It allows you to sit more upright than you do on other loungers.
I however am I sloucher. I had my husband deflate that bolster pillow (while I laid on it) and found my perfect angle.
One thing I can guarantee ... people WILL fight over this raft. Establish ownership immediately hahahahaha
One of the BEST features - the actual depth of this lounger is INSANE !!! When fully blown up (I prefer a little less air for a softer surface) this lounger will keep you nearly perfectly dry and up off the water !!! Seriously, if you don't want to get wet, no problem (unless there's splashers in pool with you).
I'm a bit klutzy and even I can manage to get on and off this lounger without getting totally soaked.
The thickness of this raft does have tiny drawback. when you're hot, you will have to reach down and splash yourself to cool off because that's how high you are off the water.
If it's windy, you will blow across pool, lake or river with the greatest of ease, with or without you on it!!!
I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this lounger and I am tempted to buy another just to have an extra in case mine meets with demise (Minnesota winter storage)
Well worth the money !!! Would buy again in a heartbeat !!!
text_fidelity_b: Rockin' Inflatable Lounge, 74" X 39"

text_fidelity_a:
Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+ Initially I bought Snap-Circuits for my 4 and 5 year old boys. I found the collection of capacitors, resistors, integrated circuit modules, and transistors was a little too abstract, and I was thinking I really wanted more stuff like electro-magnets, relays, motors, generators, switches, potentiometers, and maybe resistive loads like light bulbs and diodes -- more basic electrical stuff, of which there's some in the circuit kits but not a lot.

My boys are 5 and 6 now. I added Snaptricity to our collection of mostly unexplored Snap-Circuits, and suddenly they're creating all kinds of basic circuits with switches, buttons, lights, motors, and electro-magnets. They're starting to understand the flow of electricity, polarity, magnetism, and resistance (as they add more loads to their circuits). I've set the transistors and stuff aside for now, because there's tons of stuff to do with these more basic components first. For older children, they might be ready for the electronic components sooner, but with my younger kids, these electrical parts are great.

We do not follow the instructions. So it helps to have extra components on hand instead of the minimum number required for the book experiments. Some of our circuits are more than elegant and minimalist. I recommend buying two kits, or this kit and another one like the 100 or 300.

The brilliant thing about these components is the incredibly simple and effective button snap-connectors. The only downside to these components is they are encased in plastic for durability. The plastic is clear so the internal components can be seen. This is really a good thing, but it's worthwhile to have a coil/electromagnet that is un-encased, as well as a speaker/microphone (electromagnet with a diaphragm) that is not encased, and a motor that can be disassembled/dissected.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+

Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

I think the issue is that in order to get the even three color lines when writing or stamping or coloring, you have to hold the marker perfectly upright and ensure all three tips are somewhat evenly on the paper. It's much easier to end up with 2 of the colors in a line or even one depending on how you hold the marker.

SIZE - BIG I got exclusively for putting on envelopes, and most of them where so big, I could only put on back to seal. You may consider that a plus or minus, but they STICK out!

ADHESIVE - I noticed someone put they just have PAPER on the back and they had to glue them down. I have a feeling they just didn't realize you have to pull the paper off. The adhesion is GREAT.

VARIETY - WOW, nothing was repeated and there are ones for different age groups. Some regular Halloween type, some gross (teens and preteens would love those) and some in the middle.

ONLY CONS:

BOTTOMLINE: WOULD DEFINITELY GET THESE AGAIN! and they were a REALLY GOOD price for what you get.

Schleich Dinosaurs, Dinosaur Toy, Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls 4-12 years old, Tyrannosaurus Rex, Green, 11.2" x 5.6" x 3.8" This is an impressive dinosaur figure. My son has been a long time Schleich fan, but we have had discussions several times that Papo makes a much better dinosaur than Schleich. Papo's main advantage was that they created articulated, detailed replicas of the dinosaurs of Jurassic Park. Schleich's tended to be static, less detailed and just generally clumsier reproductions. This has drastically changed with this new series of dinosaurs.

The addition of the moveable jaw and finer details has really brought the Schleich dino line up several notches. We still favor the Papos but the details in the facial features on this T Rex are great. The Jaw action is good, but the teeth are a still a little crude in their molding. The body position is gook, coloration is somewhat bold with the tannish scales. But all in all this is a great figure. Definitely a figure deserving of the Schleich tag.

Probably still second best to Papo's two T Rex figures, but heads and shoulders above the older Schleich offerings.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Dinosaur Toy, Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls 4-12 years old, Tyrannosaurus Rex, Green, 11.2" x 5.6" x 3.8"

Alex DIY Paper Swirls Project Pack Kids Art and Craft Activity My 5 1/2-year-old son especially couldn't get enough of this cool quilling project. I've done crafts with this myself in the past, and really enjoyed making lots of different flowers and animals on paper. I really like how they elevated the craft options with this, by providing the little animal forms to glue quills onto. It really helps make it fun to make 3D figures out of the paper swirls.

The quilling machine itself is a little bit hard to use, but my five and half-year-old was able to do the swirling part if I loaded the paper. I think that a slightly older kid, even 6 1/2 or seven, should be able to handle the whole thing with no problem. My son is almost there.

They provided an ample quantity of paper strips to use, and the paper strips had some really fun colors and even textures and fun finishes to them.

The one place they fell a little short for me was on the instruction book. The instruction book appears to be covering a number of different craft kits with the paper swirls, and so it has instructions for using things that were not in this kit, and not very clear instructions on how to make some of the projects they suggest. I really would've liked a little bit more specific instruction and step-by-step on how to do some simple things with the swirls once they are done.
text_fidelity_b: Alex DIY Paper Swirls Project Pack Kids Art and Craft Activity

There are enough materials for about one project in the kit, which also serves as a convenient storage bag.  The yarn is pre-cut for the primary project, which is a two-sided pillow.  There are suggestions for four other projects in the kit such as a rug, all you would need is more yarn (and maybe some non-slip underlay).  I think you can make the project as informational as you want, enjoying something creative on a wintery day, or a casual side project in front of the tv.  There are elements of design, math, even programming if you want to use a pattern App; planning, logistics, graph-paper design the oldschool way- there are a plethora of possibilities.

CTSC 75FT 95FT 110FT 250FT Zipline Kit with Stainless Steel Spring Brake and Seat My kids love this. I had a couple of trees a bit over a hundred feet apart on a shallow incline, which seemed pretty perfect.

I did end up putting this together and taking it apart about ten times before I was satisfied with it, so I definitely dumped more time than I intended into it. Making adjustments is often almost as big a job as starting from scratch. The loop at the top of the line was small, and that wanted to attach to a giant redwood, so I had to switch trees, though I'm sure I could've bought a longer section of cable. The bottom end seems like it would be able to handle a big tree fine. Maybe I could've swapped ends, but it doesn't indicate that as an option anywhere. The instructions are a bit sparse, but mostly sufficient. I hadn't realized initially that the big velcro pads had a slot for the cable to go through to keep it from slipping off the pad. By the time I got everything attached high enough, I had a lot of trouble pulling all of the slack out of the line. The turnbuckle was way too short for the task. I eventually had to get creative with clamps and bungee cords to get enough mechanical advantage to pull it tight enough to clamp it down.

The included seat is nice for when you want both adults and kids to be able to use it. It allows it to be attached up high enough to be out of the way and usable by adults, while still being low enough for smaller kids to ride on the seat. My kids use it more than the trampoline, so it's a hit.

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 50 cars is too much at once.

Days as a five year old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 50 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 50 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels Basic Car 50-Pack."

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ As usual with Schleich toys, you can’t fault the durability or the quality. I’ve reviewed a number of them, and I can’t speak highly enough of their quality builds. They are made to last, even if roughly played with. We’ve had several now for about a decade, and they look no different than when they arrived, despite having gone through a number of dino “battles” and the like. This one is no exception. One issue I suppose is that it may be a little over-built in that it has quite a heft to it, which may preclude younger children from playing easily with it. It’s sizable already, but add the weight and I can see small hands having a difficult time picking it up and moving it around, or certainly moving it smoothly. Once you move past the toddler years, though, that will be much less of an issue.

In terms of looks, it’s nicely painted (again, as usual with Schleich), with the blue cuts running down central area from head to tail tip standing out particularly nicely. The pose is as if it is about to take a step forward or perhaps step on something (someone?). The face is my one real complaint about this model. It’s a raw sort of red color, which isn’t all that aesthetic. It almost looks like it’s been flayed, or perhaps is furiously angry. And there’s something about the mouth being open in the manner it is that just seems a bit off-putting.But at least the teeth look like the right sort (I hate when one has, for instance, obviously carnivorous teeth on herbivores).

It’s nice to have a new model and a relatively unknown one at that. Outside of the head/face, which is a relatively minor complaint, the barapasuaruk is another fine addition to a great line of toys/models.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+

We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive) The Barbies in my day were just ridiculously shaped, so much so that even in the third grade I rejected them as a model that I would never live up to in my own feminine figure. I remember wishing that I could play with Barbies, but the body shapes made me feel unhappy and inadequate – you might think girls aren't aware of this kind of thing at a young age, but I certainly was. I owned one or two, but they were never something I love for this reason.

So just imagine my delight to realize that Barbie has created so many interesting and diverse dolls now to play with. This Daisy figure has really just a normal kind of shape that you would see on many, many ladies and moms at the grocery store. She looked beautiful, and also has a much more realistic form. I love the styling of her outfit, and her gorgeous pink hair just straight up makes me happy to look at and brush.

The way that they chose to craft Barbies slightly bigger thighs was interesting to me, so I took a photo of it. Overall, this feels like a really body positive, average pretty Barbie to play with, who is stylish and fun and attractive yet doesn't set up my daughter with completely ridiculous ideas of what women might look like.

Even the normal Barbies, I have a chicken farmer Barbie, and a Barbie who runs a doggy daycare, seem like their proportions have evolved somewhat, and then the fact that they are doing normal things like cleaning up dog messes and collecting eggs really goes so far in my book. I also love the Ken doll who is doing his own laundry in his very own washing machine. My husband is a little flummoxed by my absolute flat out glee at seeing such a thing, but I think setting the expectation that Ken will enjoy doing his own self-care chores is an excellent one for young ladies.

Overall, from having the impression that I would never let my children play with Barbies, I've come a long way, and that's because Barbie has come a long way to. I'm delighted with Daisy, and her cool accessories and great look.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive)

LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Clock Tower 75948 Build and Play Tower Set with Harry Potter Minifigures, Popular Harry Potter Gift and Playset with Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger and More (922 Pieces) I’m a massive Harry Potter fan and a massive Lego fan, so naturally I was stalking stores last year, when the first wave of new sets was released. And naturally I’ve been looking forward to another wave ever since.

Coming in at 922 pieces, the Hogwarts Clock Tower is the biggest set in the summer 2019 wave. If you have the other Hogwarts sets (75954: Great Hall and 75953: Whomping Willow), this set can connect to them and make an impressive Hogwarts spread.

There are 8 minifigs in this set: Harry, Ron, Hermione, Cedric, Viktor, Fleur, Dumbledore, and Maxime. Each minifig has a double-sided head. I thought Fleur’s dress bottom was boring, but the detail on Dumbledore and Maxime’s pieces made up for Fleur.

The build itself is pretty simple, no advanced or really interesting techniques. There are 6 numbered bags and 2 sticker sheets. The instructions were in a sort of cardboard pocket built into the box, something I haven’t seen before but appreciated, since I dislike curled or bent pages.

I’ve been dinging Lego on this a lot lately -- but I really wish they used less stickers. Especially for some of the pieces that show up repeatedly in Harry Potter sets, such as the bricks. I decided to assemble this set the first time without applying any of the stickers (I’m quite particular about putting them on perfectly) and it just doesn’t have the same magic without the stickers. Dumbledore’s office is bland without Fawkes and the Sorting Hat in the background. Happily, the clock face is a printed piece.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Clock Tower 75948 Build and Play Tower Set with Harry Potter Minifigures, Popular Harry Potter Gift and Playset with Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger and More (922 Pieces)

Ninja Warrior Obstacle Course for Kids - 2X50FT Double Ninja Slackline with Most Complete Accessories for Kids, Swing, Trapeze Swing, Rope Ladder, Obstacle Net Plus 1.2M Arm Trainer I am hoping to upgrade my rating to 4-5 stars after my 9 year old has had time to play on this a few times. A few initial thoughts:

The instructions included were not great, I had to find a YouTube video and watch it a few times to figure out assembly. I’m not the engineering type and no, it’s not hard, but it still took me multiple tries to get it right.

After finally getting it set up, we realized the obstacles were still too far apart for my child. However, the tension is way too tight once it’s locked and loaded so you can’t just easily slide the metal bracket things. Which means you have to loosen the entire ratchet thing and basically start over again. We did this a few times which is a bit frustrating. It definitely takes some trial and error and if you have an excited and antsy kid who can’t wait to get on this thing, it makes it even more stressful.

My 9 year old is a bit tall and during the trial and error period we realized it was too low, so then I had to go get the big ladder and shimmy the slack lines up another 2 feet on both trees. Everything added together just took a lot of time.

That being said, everything looks well made and durable at this point. I still need to make a few adjustments so that hopefully she can play on it this weekend. We will then decide whether to keep this thing or not. The monkey grip is tough and the cargo net is super swingy so it’s tough, she said. We are not planning to use the swing but we did buy a separate wheel thing from the same company.

I do plan on installing the lower slack line, I think that will help her move from obstacle to obstacle while also working her core at the same time. Hoping to provide an update in a week or so.

We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.

It had really informational highlights about each country, such as eskimos and igloos in Greenland.

This came packaged extremely well. I was very surprised that the edges weren't bent at all after I opened it, and this was because of the high quality packaging. The packaging from T.S. Sure had multiple layers of cardboard surrounding this puzzle, and then it was all contained inside of a nice big amazon box. So, there was no chance of this getting damaged during shipment. And, that was a possibility. This is pretty heavy, about ten pounds. And, it has a high quality wood backing. It looks very nice, back and front.

Pros:
+Very solid
+Great world map, that shows Africa as its true size in comparison to the US
+Or in other words, doesn't use the Mercator Projection
+Has very informative information about each country
+You can stick the magnets to your fridge, too
+Extremely excellent packaging
+Very high quality wood backing

Cons:
-The magnets aren't very strong, so you'll be rearranging them a lot

PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) Mattel has brought a new world to target practice and just plain fun with soft dart guns with this BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster. With no batteries required, the fun is endless. Instead of batteries to power the gun, it is air powered. You have to pump the gun to get enough air pressure to fire the soft darts. Mattel states the gun is for ages 6 and up, but this gun is on the heavy side and requires a bit of strength just to pump it, so I feel ages 7 and up would be a better fit. Even though our 6 year old neighbor didn't want to put this gun down, it was difficult for him to pump it for firing.

The gun is very sturdy being large and made of a heavy plastic. I can see this gun lasting quite a bit of use and not ending up in the trash for a long while. Once pumped it is easy to fire, whether firing one dart or the entire 20 dart clip. At the end of the gun is a special shield you can open up to not only protect yourself from oncoming darts, but your opponents darts will actually stick to this protective shield, allowing you to capture his darts.

Besides the gun there are 30 Smart Stick darts, a 20 dart clip and a Smart Stick target included. The target is great for improving your aim, especially firing one dart at a time. The 20 dart clip is really fun, whether firing at the target or your opponent, as it fires all 20 darts in a matter of a few seconds. It literally fires up to 50 feet, as we shot all 20 darts and several darts went well over 45 feet away. The rapid fire at such a distance is really a lot of fun for the backyard.

Even though these darts are really soft plastic, you will find out that once the children find out how much fun it is to shoot darts at both the target and each other, you may want to purchase the safety eye gear. I don't know if having all 20 darts coming at you from 50 feet away would need some type of eye protection, but I feel it's better to have some type of eye gear on. There is no doubt, this is a safe, sturdy toy with your children wanting to run around and play with this outdoors, gives it 5 Stars. Just getting the kids off the couch away from video games makes it a 5 Star toy, as the exercise alone is worth 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition Werewolf is not usually a "game night" game that you play with a group of friends. I've always used it in classroom settings, or with larger groups, usually upwards of 10 people, where this game really shines. Ultimately, Werewolf is a deduction game in which most players are Villagers, unwittingly being killed or eliminated by a sect of Werewolf players. Using very limited clues and knowledge, it's up to the Villagers to unmask the Werewolves and eliminate them from the game before they themselves are eaten.

The only real issue that I have with Werewolf is that there is player elimination, although since Werewolf is not a particularly long game, it's usually OK, and bystanders often have as much fun as the players.

There are plenty of versions of this game available out there, but I think that Bezier's "Ultimate" is certainly the way to go. The bits are durable and well made, and there are enough cards to play an 80 person game. That said, there is less content in here as compared to the "Revised Edition" that came out a few years ago. I still think that this is the box to get, however, as the roles and unique playing styles presented in the "Revised" box are more complicated, and not really in line with the casual spirit of the game. I think they certainly provide more variety, but at the expense of complicating the players and making it far more difficult for the moderator. As it's impossible to answer questions mid-game, it's best to leave the complicated roles to a different genre of game.

A 5-Star Product for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition

text_fidelity_a:
The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up Several years ago there was a British series about Robin Hood, and my family and I have been hooked ever since seeing that series. This game seemed like a good fit for my family based on our interests, and so far it has been a good addition to family game night. That said, this game tends to be on the easy side and the replayability isn't great if you want a varying experience.

In a nutshell, this is a basic move-around-the-board game at its heart, though it requires cooperation instead of competition and it relies on a story book to further the game along. Some real time and attention to detail went into the design and it shows.

Though the game does not require following a path without turning to the left or right, it does follow a basic flow and the story book is designed to help guide and direct. That said, it essentially is a map of how to get through each step and it does not vary from game to game so once the game has been played the book could potentially slow down a game instead of moving it along at an interesting pace since previous players will know what to do.

This is certainly not a bad game. It's a good family game and is worth running through as a group. However, for those looking for replayability, this one lacks variety.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up

text_fidelity_a:
UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls I absolutely love dolls of all types and own hundreds of them. They range from inexpensive off-brand play dolls, legitimate BJDs, to high-end handmade artist dolls. This is likely the worst designed doll I have ever handled.

This doll has a very cute face and poses well. However, the deal-breaker is that she has No Neck! Her head sits right on her shoulders. This is very distracting because it makes it hard to look at her. I would be able to overlook so many of the other negative aspects to this doll if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. This is very disappointing. It's such a pity as she has a very pretty face.

This is not a BJD (ball-jointed doll). This doll shares a similar aesthetic to some BJDs, but she does not have even a single ball joint. She has hinge and swivel joints only. The doll is made from at least three different types of plastic. One maybe ABS plastic, but there are no silicone components to this doll.

Her hair is pretty rooted plugs. The description led me to believe it may be a wig, but no. The plugs are evenly spaced and I do not see any bald spots. The hair fibers are soft. The eyelashes are glued strips and the eyes are inset acrylics. She has very pretty face that is painted symmetrically. The joints were very, very stiff and difficult to loosen with force. Once loosened, she does pose decently and can touch her face. She has a full outfit that is made with flawed fabric. Several threads are missing in the weave of the fabric of the skirt. The flawed fabric is very noticeable. The outfit has a shirt, vest, skirt, bloomers, knee socks and a hat. It would be a very cute outfit if the stitching was a little more straight and the fabric was not deeply flawed fabric. The material is incredibly low quality. Her shoes are light purple canvas, do not match the outfit, but are fair quality and fit her flat feet snugly.

A packet of 'accessories' are included and is confusing. They are thin plastic, various shades of pink and not to scale with the doll. The comb and 4 little hair elastics may be useful to play with the doll but otherwise they would likely not be much fun for playing with the doll and I feel would be better left out of the package. Some heeled shoes were also included in the packet and although I could put them on the doll, the straps were useless and they looked odd as she has flat feet. Little fingers would likely become frustrated trying to fasten the straps.

I looked into the UCanaan brand after ordering this doll. I was disappointed to learn that the company uses re-casted parts from legitimate BJD makers without permission. This is very sad/bad news. I would have expected better from a US retail site and find it deeply disappointing. I do not know that any pieces are made from the re-casted parts from other companies for this particular doll, but it's a serious negative point that should be noted. I cannot say with confidence this is not a re-casted doll. I would not be surprised to learn that it is.

I cannot recommend this doll. The primary reasons being she has no neck, is not as described and the company does shady business practices. This makes me very uneasy as it sets up customers for some serious disappointment. If you are looking for a budget-friendly legitimate BJD, there are other companies that make very nice lower-cost dolls. It takes a minimum amount of looking off the site to find them. If you are looking for a nice doll for display, or posing and play, please note this one has no neck and uses poor quality materials. Your money would be better spent elsewhere. I do not find this to be a good value in the least. She would be enjoyable for display if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. I hope that this can be remedied in the future. I find this doll very disappointing and it's such a pity as she would otherwise be very cute with an alternative outfit.

I do hope you have found my honest review helpful. If you do, please click the Helpful button below. Thank you for reading my review.
text_fidelity_b: UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls

text_fidelity_a:
NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin We've only had the game for a few days, but so far we've played it a total of six times, you figure each game is one hour long, so basically we've gotten six hours of fun for the affordable price of under twenty bucks. So, way less than we'd spend if my family went out to see a movie and best of all, we didn't even have to leave the house.

A little bit about the game, it seemed a bit complicated at first.

We followed the directions, give each player four cards each from the two stacks, that part was basic, but we ended up folding and unfolding the game play instructions trying to figure out what to do next.

Basically, each player tries to level up. Levelling up can be achieved in just a few ways, 1. defeating a monster (which you can only do if you have enough levels, which means you may need to, 2. buy a level, by selling magical items or 3. get a level up treasure card.

The game seemed a bit slow at first because each player starts with just one level which is too low to start fighting monsters. But the game picked up when we'd all gotten to level three. The monsters can be defeated by more than one player, so one minute I was sabotaging my son's chances at winning another level, the next we were fighting flying frogs together and sharing in the loot!

The cards themselves give you directions, telling you to add 5 to fight a monster (very useful card to use against your opponents) or that certain magical items can only be used by certain characters; dwarves, elves, etc.

By the time we played a third time, we knew the game well enough to start levelling curses at each other and how to steal each others treasures.

Munchkin has a lot of extender packs, munchkin zombie, munchkin the guild (I just bought this one, yay!) etc. that add to the original game set.

Since we play a lot of games here at home, monopoly, settlers of catan, telepathy, zombie dice, risk, etc. figuring out the basic rules wasn't terribly difficult, but I think looking at a few munchkin blogs could prove helpful (yep, there really are munchkin blogs.)
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin

Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

text_fidelity_a: Little Tikes Cozy Truck Ride-On with removable floorboard I only give two stars rather than one because it looks cool. Putting this thing together is a royal pita. First of all you better have some tools because parts do NOT fit correctly. The left front wheel assembly slides up from the bottom and is attached with a pressed on fastener which was no problem for the right side however the left side did not have any metal sticking up past the bushing. I had to take a Dremel tool and cut the pinched metal that stops the washer so that I could get enough of the rod to attach a fastener. The steering wheel is locked in place with a clip that is inserted into the plastic rod that goes into the dash and is supposed to go through a plastic ring that you place on the rod from the other side of the dash. Well I pushed as hard as I could and there is no way this was going to connect. If it would have connected there is no way a child would be able to turn the steering wheel. I had to elongate the holes in the steering column in order to get this connected. Bottom line is this product is severely lacking in quality control. I would not buy another one because of this problem By the way, I'm not someone who usually has trouble putting things together and I have quite a large collection of tools that I know how to use otherwise I don't see anyway this thing gets put together.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Cozy Truck Ride-On with removable floorboard

text_fidelity_a: PHYWESS RC Cars Remote Control Car for Boys 2.4 GHZ High Speed Racing Car, 1:16 RC Trucks 4x4 Offroad with Headlights, Electric Rock Crawler Toy Car Gift for Kids Adults Girls I LOVE RC 4WD off road racing! I'm building quite a nice little garage of different buggies. This one by PHYWESS is a very good addition to my shop. It's very similar to another one that I have from another company. But, has a few differences, enough to make it interesting. This one is VERY well built with quality materials and construction. The body is very rugged, of a good sturdy and heavy weight resin material. The motor has a nice large heat sink, letting your run till you drain the battery without the fear of overheating. The steering servo is strong and responsive. The drive components are solid steel. The shocks are spring over oil capped pistons. The receiver / ESC is very reliable. All electronics are waterproofed. It's built for mud running and has no problem with puddles. I wouldn't recommend going into water above the axles. But, up to that depth is not a problem. You will love seeing it sling mud and water as you speed through the muck. I've flipped it, rolled it and crashed it a few times. It's TOUGH. The canopy got dinged up a little. But, otherwise, not a problem. The bonus running lights are a little tricky to install. But, work just great. The controller is better than with a lot of others at this price point with great range and some fine tuning options. Overall, this PHYWESS off road racer is just great fun. Five stars.

LEGO Disney Ariel’s Storybook Adventures 43176 Creative Little Mermaid Building Kit (105 Pieces) At first glance, the Lego series of Disney Storybook Adventures looks neat. Putting a mini playset inside a book? I think it’s fitting. Aside from Ariel in this set, the other storybooks include Anna and Elsa, Belle, and Mulan.

One of the better features of the storybooks is that the entire set fits inside. So that makes it easy for kids to take them to anywhere, without the fear of losing pieces.

There’s not a lot of actual building in the set. It’s definitely geared towards play rather than assembly. The instructions are merely a double-sided poster instead of the usual instruction booklet. There are a LOT of stickers, which I’m personally never a fan of, but at least here most of the stickers don’t have to be applied perfectly straight for the set to look okay.

The set includes 3 micro-dolls, which are just a bit smaller than Lego’s mini-dolls found in the Friends sets. The micro-dolls do not have moveable arms, movable legs, and their hands are circles, so they can’t hold a lot of accessories. There are 2 versions of Princess Ariel (one with a closed-eye wink, one with a normal expression), and Prince Eric. Small versions of Sebastian and Flounder are here, too.

When first hearing about the Storybook Adventures sets, I had hoped they could make cute gifts for friends who are fans of Disney and Lego. But when I have the set in front of me, I’m just not impressed by it. The micro-dolls aren’t great and there’s not a lot of assembly (my favorite part of Lego).
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Ariel’s Storybook Adventures 43176 Creative Little Mermaid Building Kit (105 Pieces)

4DV2 Foldable Mini Drone with 720P Camera for Kids,2.4G FPV Video,Nano Portable Pocket RC Quadcopter Beginners Toys,3D Flip,Altitude Hold,Headless Mode,Trajectory Flight,3D Flips,3 Battery [[VIDEOID:8a35051fba3b622e613e552275a81a53]] This is a great starter drone, in theory. I have flown many of these and my son wanted to try one to get started with. He picked it up really quickly and together we were able to fly it around the house indoors without hitting anything. The camera is gimmicky at best, but for the price I'd say get it for the drone flight fun and forget the camera.
UNTIL... within 2 days of owning it, something seemed to go wrong with the height sensor (barometer?), and it not only wouldn't hold the correct height like it did the day before, but suddenly it shot straight UP. No pressing down on the joystick seems to change anything. Its as if the unit felt like it was falling and needed to compensate by flying more aggressively upwards. It hit the ceiling, and we promptly hit the kill switch. I took a look at it, pulled off the propellers to look, and tried again. Same thing - it shot straight UP. Hit the ceiling. I tried cleaning any hair/debris from the blades and again- straight up until it hit. But this time, it started making a funny noise. Upon closer inspection I found one of the pins that the propeller sits on has been bent.
