text_fidelity_a: Lovinouse 1500 Pieces Jigsaw Puzzle Board with 2 Sorting Tray, Portable Puzzles Storage Case Saver, Non-Slip Surface I have been using a large, wooden puzzle board with trays for the pieces. When I saw this, I was intrigued with the ability to tightly close it up without destroying the work in progress. The wooden one will keep the puzzle safe, but you have to find a large place to set it when you're not working on it. So I started a 500 piece puzzle on this board. It's got a fuzzy surface which makes it non-slip. That is good at times, but there are times when I will work on a section of a puzzle and slide it to it's destination. That's difficult to do with this one. Instead of puzzle trays, it has flat fuzzy pieces that you can put the pieces on and move around as needed. With my 500 piece puzzle, I couldn't get all of the pieces spread out flat on the combined boards. I had to have some stacked on top of one another. After I had completed the border, I decided to stop for the evening. I put the puzzle boards on top of the main puzzle area where my work was. Then I closed everything up and made sure the velcro pieces were secure. Then I tilted the whole unit at a 90 degree angle. I heard pieces moving around. My heart sank. The border is always a lot of work! I opened it back up and while the pieces had moved around, it was only the pieces that hadn't been assembled yet. The work area with my completed border was still in tact. I think I will feel better leaving this on a flat surface, such as a table when it's not in use. It does keep the cats from sitting on my work and that's a plus. I always had to cover my work with a towel or something with the wooden tray. This is also weighs less than the wooden one which makes it easier to move. Overall, I am pleased with this puzzle storage piece.

Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink This convertible car for 14 inch dolls is completely awesome. We have a number of glitter girls dolls and two of them can fit into this convertible with ease, along with one of the glitter girls puppies sitting on a lap.

My kids saw this in a Christmas catalog and were completely enchanted with it, asking for it over and over again. It's about as big as you would expect given that the glitter girls both have to fit in there, and it has a dashboard that opens, a little side container that opens in between the two seats, two cupholders, and the trunk.

We have the glitter girls sweetshop and the accessories sweetshop that has some delightful cups of confectionery beverage, and I was delighted to find that these sweetshop beverages fit into the cupholders perfectly. (They also fit into the girls hands). The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. Same thing with the little container in between the two seats, if that could have been just a little bit wider, it would get used even more.

The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.

However, we discovered the problem with this stuff about 1/2 hour after cleaning up. I walked past the hard floor area where we had cleaned up afterwards, and nearly fell on my butt. I had already, I thought, cleaned up all the pieces of clay on the floor and given one or two areas a quick wipe down with cleaner, so I was puzzled as to why the floor was so slippery. I cleaned the floor there, and walked around and forgot about it for about five more minutes, when I walked by and almost fell on my butt in another spot. Then my husband almost fell. Then my child did fall. I cleaned the floor thoroughly and there were still patches of occasional area that were just ridiculously slippery, and I don't really understand how it withstood numerous attacks with normal household cleaners. But for days we were discovering slippery areas on our floor that made it really not safe.

So I would give the caveat that if you are going to allow your children to play with kinetic sand, do so outside so that you do not end up with a dangerous situation on your own hard floors.

text_fidelity_a:
Bop It XT Finding a children's toy that can actually entertain....especially during a time (in our country) where kids spend most of there time on the IPod Touch, Xbox, WII, PSP, computers etc. is difficult. We live in a society of computer generated video games, computer enhanced movies, 3D, 4D, special effects, etc, and I find myself asking my kids -what happened to Connect 4, Twister, Simon, UNO, Clue, Life, Scrabble, PAC Man and Monopoly? Basically my childhood was filled with memories of playing these kinds of games, meaning those that essentially force you to interact with people. Under this belief, seeing the "Bop It " I thought maybe ...just maybe my kids (10 & 13) would enjoy playing this on family night. Believe it or not, while it is not animated and gloomy, it gave us hours of pure, clean fun. We battled each other. We laughed and teased. While the game kind of reminded me of Simon, it was surprisingly a bit more complicated. For Simon you just have to remember the color sequences, while the Bop challenges you to complete several tasks.....to pull, twist, flick, roll... quickly or you're out. The minute you miss, you have to start again. There is also a commentator giving the score, and teasing the player. My 13-year-old thought that this would be fun game to take on road trips (to play between all of his other electronics), while my 10-year-old is more determined than ever to beat his present score. Both found "Bop It" to be an easy to understand/fun game that promotes coordination and interacting with others. I highly recommend it.

It's light-weight and easy to carry.
It's stylish. Looks a little Jazzy...each task is a different color and shape.
It would definitely teach kids to listen. Following directions is a crucial element for playing the game.
text_fidelity_b: Bop It XT

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Hearing Things Game My teenage daughter loves games. I thought this would be something different. Basically, you wear special headphones while your teammate whispers a phrase. You try to figure out what the phrase is by reading lips. The headphones require batteries. You press a button on one of the ear cups, and it starts playing a somewhat noisy and annoying background sound. There is a timer feature built in, so the noise stops after a minute has passed which signals that your turn is over. The headphones don't feel very sturdy, but they are okay. There are 600 cards which have four phrases on each card. We found it difficult to hear the whispering when wearing the headphones, which is desired. If you correctly guess the right phrase, you get to keep the card which is later counted as points. Team with the most points at the end wins. There's instructions for playing with 4 to 8 people as well as for just two. It was funny what some of us thought was being whispered! My daughter is looking forward to playing this at her next game night with friends.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Hearing Things Game

Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple I got the Easy Bake Ultimate Oven for my little boy. What woman doesn't love it when a man can cook?! ;) He's almost 3, so not quite the targeted age, but we still had fun with it.

What we like:
-I like that it's purple, which is a LITTLE bit more on the neutral side.
-It cooks very quickly. You preheat for 20 minutes and then cook an average of 10 minutes or so. You get exact directions, though. I was expecting a MUCH longer cook time.

What we didn't like:
-You can't watch the food while it cooks. I wish the front was clear, and it would have made this a much better learning tool, and made it a lot more fun.
-The portions are TINY! Seriously, I don't think it would fill up a mouse! But, I guess I have to expect tiny portions for it to cook so quickly. And, I think it's more of a "time together" kind of activity!

Just some neutral information we learned. You can cook "regular" food in the oven. If you're like us, you can't pay a lot of money for tiny mixes that produce 1/10th of the size of a normal cookie. Just save a little batter from when you cook. I also learned that you CAN burn food in this oven. :) So make sure you set a timer.
The pictures in the directions have cute, perfect little cookies and cupcakes. Ours didn't even come close to looking that great. Maybe with a little more practice?!
This oven comes with a batch of cookies and cupcakes w/frosting, sugar crystals, and cupcake wraps. It also has two cooking pans and an "arm" to push the pans into the oven. It has spots marked to make sure you get them to the correct spot to cook and cool. Overall, we've had a lot of fun with it!

And this is probably obvious, but it's electric. ;)

Thames and Kosmos Remote-Control Machines DLX It came with a defective remote. Emailing the committee company did nothing, but when I called they shipped me out a new one right away. There is an led on top of the remote. If it doesn't light, you have a bad remote.

The manual starts with a system test and then goes through the projects. The projects are rated in difficulty one through three and the first one on the book is a level the robotic arm that does not balance well as designed. It can be fixed easily, and figuring out how is very educational. If it is too difficult, I suggest start with a level one project. Of course, once you get it running, you've got a new RC toy to play with, and this kit can make at least 20 of them. More if your child designs her own.

The directions are just clear enough to build all of the projects, but they don't entirely spoon feed you. This toy demands your child think and reason; following instructions blindly won't be good enough. The higher the difficulty, the more the builder is required to reason on her own.

Robotics is the next big technical revolution, and this is a brilliant, affordable introduction to the field. I would say this class of toy is as important for today's kids as the Commodore 64 was for budding computer programs back is the 1980s, and this particular kit is a brilliant example of the type. It also happens to be fun for kids and adults, so much so the kids won't realize they're learning.

You will need a lot of batteries for this, five AA to be exact, and they are not included. Rechargeables will make this so much easier.
text_fidelity_b: Thames and Kosmos Remote-Control Machines DLX

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball Unlike traditional jigsaw puzzles, the pieces are made of hard plastic rather than cardboard or foam, which means it's more durable. I remember growing up with jigsaw puzzles where the pictures got chipped because the paper would peel off the cardboard. The colors are bright, shiny and very decorative. Also unlike cardboard jigsaws, the pieces actually stay together and the ball can be held up when finished. Very cool.

On the negative side, I don't like the fact that the pieces are numbered on the back. For me, this takes away the challenge of being detail-oriented and noticing the tiny details that make one piece go with another. It feels like a dumbing-down to me. I could see the numbered sequence being good for younger kids, but not for something that's geared to 10 and older.

Other than that, this is a high quality, solidly made puzzle that families would enjoy doing together.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a: Hands Craft DIY Miniature Dollhouse Kit - Holiday Party Time 3D Model Tiny House Building with LED Lights Wood Prefabricated Pieces Puzzle 1:24 Scale Crafts for Adults and Teens DG153 I like having a variety of crafting types of things around, especially during the winter. I recently heard about these little kits and got a few to try. Books are one of my greatest joys, so I couldn't help but include this one in the mix. I thought they'd be great for doing while I'm listening to an audio book. They're a little different than I thought they'd be, but I do still like them. They take much longer to complete than I thought and they're much more detailed. (For example, I make most of the items. I don't just put miniatures into place.) They also require more concentration while reading and following the directions. Because of that, this isn't the best project for me to do while listening to an audiobook. It's still nice with music, though. All kits are different, but this particular one comes with most, but not all, of the things needed to complete it. (Of course, you're always free to add your own special touches.) Tools not included are a precision knife, scissors, a ruler, screwdriver, cutting pliers, and needle nose pliers. Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players This is a very cute concept and something out-of-the-ordinary for a board game! The object of the game is to make it out with the least amount of goo on your shoe. This is represented by actual pieces of putty that you place on the board and squish with your pawn as you land on a square (thus sticking the goo to your, erm, shoe).
My kids really enjoyed it, but I can't help feeling like there are some design flaws that could have been prevented. For example, the spinner needs to be deconstructed to put away in the box. The way the board folds (see picture), the crease is over the spinner area, and with the bars on the spinner (which I like, as it looks like a playground toy) won't fit, which means you have to totally take that apart and rebuilt it each time. On that note, it isn't much of a spinner at all, but just a wheel. There is no clicker or arrow that sticks out to slow it down as it spins... it basically spins until momentum from your push wears out, sort of like spinning a top. It takes a while to finally stop on its own, which makes the game feel like it is moving slowly. I was very tempted to just stop it manually a few times, but that might bring up the possibility of cheating.
Meanwhile, I wish the goo had more colors, or at least colors that matched the shoes in the game. I can say on the positive note, the goo is very kid friendly!
My daughter lost one of the colors and it turns out she was SITTING on it and it was all stuck in her dress. I suddenly had flashbacks of when silly putty got stuck on her clothing and bed and we had to toss them both because it never came off... but this stuff comes off! It easily rolls into balls with your fingers and comes right off clothing in the process. So, definitely some extra points for that! I just wish the game board and spinner were designed a little better, that would make it a lot more fun to play (and put away!).
text_fidelity_b: Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players

text_fidelity_a:
K.T. Fancy 35 PCS Doll Clothes and Accessories 5 Fashion Clothes Sets 5 Fashion Skirts 14 Outfit Accessories10 Shoes and A Dog for 11.5 inch Doll I recently got name-brand Barbie clothes, and I also tried this generic aftermarket version. Here’s how they compare:

Value:
This set comes with 35 pieces for $17, while the Barbie brand comes with about the same amount for $40. As far as quality goes, the Barbie brand far exceeds this in materials and construction, and it also includes things that fit the male dolls, where as this one doesn’t. With the Barbie brand, you also know exactly what you’re getting, whereas with this one, it’s more of a grab bag, where some of the outfits pictured arrive, and others are substituted for similar items (but definitely not the same). For value, it’s a draw.

Quality:
In terms of textiles, construction, and details, Barbie wins by a lot. These are OK, with some that are pretty great actually, but some that are not. For example, a few of these have vinyl appliqués that don’t look quite right, as well as other small irregularities. At the same time, there’s nothing huge as far as quality goes that would make me think these are bad. They’re fine, and many are quite cute!

Accessories:
New her Barbies tend to have flat feet, so the high heels mostly don’t work, and this assortment primarily comes with the super high heels that work with the old fashion Barbies. As cute as these are, they’re generally not going to work. Also, there wasn’t any jewelry really in this mix. The Barbie mix had a lot of matching bracelet and necklace sets, which I liked; The namebrand also had more flat shoes, which means the flat footed Barbies had plenty to wear. Barbie wins this category as well.

Overall:
If you are on a budget, and you are not trying to dress any male dolls, this is a perfectly fine assortment. There are plenty of neat designs and cool fabrics. If you have male dolls that want outfits, however, and you prefer more quality over quantity, I recommend the Barbie set.
text_fidelity_b: K.T. Fancy 35 PCS Doll Clothes and Accessories 5 Fashion Clothes Sets 5 Fashion Skirts 14 Outfit Accessories10 Shoes and A Dog for 11.5 inch Doll

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly This NEUSCHWANSTEIN CASTLE XXL puzzle is not for beginners, or for the faint of heart! Any 2000-piece Ravensburger puzzle is difficult, simply because of the number of pieces, but this puzzle is probably above average in difficulty.

The puzzle measures 52" wide by 24" high--it's a panoramic puzzle--so make sure you have cleared a wide space for it. The XXL size means that the fine photo details are spread over more than one puzzle piece, and this increases the difficulty. The puzzle is easiest to assemble if you stand over it as you go, so that you can see the bigger, overall picture.

Ravensburger puzzles always have color areas to help you. That's true of this puzzle, but the sky--there's lots of it!-- has less color variation than usual. The border pieces are easy to find and assemble, but when you start on the remaining puzzle, it really dawns on you what a challenging task you have undertaken. There are piles of dark blue, light blue, autumn-colored, and mostly-white pieces that look very much alike. For me, the hardest area was the lower left side, with all of the blue trees; and the big snow-covered tree at the right was far more difficult than I expected. The castle was easy, and the autumn-colored trees were easier than you would think from looking at the box photo.

Despite its difficulty, this puzzle was a pleasure to work. The photo is just so beautiful! Working at a comfortable pace (one to several hours at a stretch, but not every day), I needed about a month to finish this one. As usual, I found the Ravensburger craftsmanship to be extraordinary--the pieces fit together so nicely that mistakes were few and far between. I highly recommend this puzzle for expert (addicted) jigsaw puzzle enthusiasts.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a:
Crazy Aaron’s Thinking Putty (1.6 oz) Precious Metals - Good as Gold - Soft Texture, Never Dries Out At first I thought the review mentioning that this wasn't gold was goofy, but it's on target. What I expected was a gold-colored putty with some fine glitter. What I received was clear putty with a ton of cheap glitter. We're talking about dollar-store kids' craft set glitter, not the nice glitter used for embossing. This basically looks like someone squirted a bottle of glitter glue into a putty tin.

Now you may be thinking, "Seriously? You're pitching a fit about glitter?!" Well, when the price is marked up, I expect that the product's going to be of higher quality than the standard version. Not only that, but I played with it for a minute and glitter already started coming off in my hand. It probably wouldn't take long for this to lose its luster.

Thinking Putty is fun stuff, so I suggest passing this up and getting a tin of the Super Oil Slick instead.
text_fidelity_b: Crazy Aaron’s Thinking Putty (1.6 oz) Precious Metals - Good as Gold - Soft Texture, Never Dries Out

text_fidelity_a:
Lost Cities - The Board Game You can move your five explorers (you don't need to use them all) on any of five paths. You can move one square forward on each color if you play a card of that color that is higher than the last card you played. So if you play a two, you can play a three or a four etc, to move forward. You can't play a lower card, but you can discard it, and your opponents can pick it up. Along the way you get bonus points and artifacts to raise your score. Three rounds makes a game.

This game is supposed to take 30 minutes to an hour, but I have yet to find even a three player version go that fast. There is too much strategy and planning involved. You need to think about what cards you need now, what you need later, what your opponents might use if you discard a card, and how many "for later" cards you can retain. You need to decide when to bite the bullet and take a big number jump (limiting your later moves) and when to hold off.

It definitely plays better with more than two players. It's fast to learn, and a lot of fun.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game

Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions I am always looking for fun games that my family and I can enjoy together on game night and having not heard of Selfie I decided to give it a shot. It is a fun game but seems based on some other popular games that have been around for a while.

“Selfie” could just have easily been called “Apples to Apples Meets Charades!” which is a fairly concise way to describe it. Each player is dealt a set of cards describing a scenario where one would make some kind of facial expression, and then takes a selfie shot of that expression. After looking at the selfie shot, everyone else then plays one of their own cards to describe the expression, from which the original player selects a winner he/she likes most. Each person takes a turn taking a selfie and selecting others’ cards.

The game can be played without a phone or camera but it’s a lot easier with such a device which will help eliminate disagreements.

It should be obvious that this is not a game for the self-conscious individual.

Though I don’t think this game is all that original, it is a fun game and works in a crowd. This is the kind of game to break out during a party in the dorms or on a Saturday night with the family. It’s fun, gameplay is lively and fast-paced.
text_fidelity_b: Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions

text_fidelity_a:
AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5 This was delivered to my house about an hour ago, and my 6 year old daughter is about to put it away. She's just now finishing up the hardest puzzle included in the kit.

I'm torn on how to review this. It's clearly a nice toy for a lot of kids. The pieces are nice and chunky, the puzzle cards have vibrant artwork, and the app works smoothly. That said, though, there are 12 puzzle cards in the box, and yes, they can be solved multiple ways, but there is no guidance for different combinations of blocks to use to complete the puzzles, so there isn't much incentive to take them off and try again. Also, for someone who is not too far removed from the minimum age range suggested though, it's really easy. Like, a puzzle in two minutes for almost every combo in the deck, except for the boat, which is in the middle of the difficulty spectrum. On the box, with an oddly small top, there are images of three-dimensional shapes made out of the aniblocks, flying around, and the actual blocks do not connect in this way to form them, which was probably the most disappointing part.

The app deserves some special mention. It's certainly good, and easy to use, but it's still an app, and so, of course, it defeats the purpose of having a screen avoidant time to include it. There's also another disadvantage, which is that there are tons of apps that do this same game already, with digital blocks. They offer more puzzles, with more diverse colors of blocks, in more diverse shapes, and a wider variety of difficulty levels.

Overall, I think there are better toys for your money that do very similar things and offer a lot more variety than this. The phone apps, as mentioned before. We have a board game called Blokus 3D (or Rumis) which have a similar pattern-matching idea, but allow for 3D building. There's also Kanoodle Junior, for example, which is excellent, cheaper, ready to travel, and doesn't require an app. 12 puzzles and a handful of two-colored blocks is just not enough for the price. For that reason, I cannot recommend this...but there are far worse options.
text_fidelity_b: AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5

Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset Littlest Pet Shop Fairy Fun Roller Coaster Set is a girl's toy featuring the Littlest Pet Shop characters. It is a colorful, cute toy that offers action without the need to purchase batteries. The operation is mechanical so kids can play as long as they want without the worry of batteries dying out.

This toy is nice for many reasons and besides the lack of batteries, the toy offers some simple operation and continuous action. All your girl has to do is press the lever, which moves the stairs upward and slowly transfers the small figures and their vehicles to the top of the slide where they glide around and wind up back at the base of the stairs. If you continue to press the lever, it will gradually pick up the next Littlest Pet Shop figure and send it up the stairs to the top of the slide where it will, once again, make its way around the slide to the base of the stairs.

My girls like this toy and both they and I find it to our liking. If I had to find some type of fault, it would be the tendency for the small vehicles to sometimes get out of place when they reach the base of the stairs. I haven't witnessed any problems with the vehicles gliding smoothly down the slide- the only problem I notice is that the little vehicles will sometimes get out of place at the stairs, requiring some manual assistance to re- position them. This is most likely to happen if kids get carried away and move the lever too quickly. Keep the speed at a moderate to slow rate, and there shouldn't be any problem.

Mechanical toys are nice and even though the Fairly Fun Roller Coaster Set has little or no educational value, it is still a nice toy for girls in the target age group. It is cute, colorful, and provides hours of simple amusement without the need to purchase batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Lost Cities - The Board Game Lost Cities TBG is a lot like the original Lost Cities Card Game, but it supports more than 2-players. That's a nice feature.

For those who don't know, Lost Cities the Card Game is considered legendary among hobby board gamers because it's simple, but deep, meaning that anyone can pick up the rules to the game quite quickly, but there's interesting decision-making and complex outcomes to worry about based on your decisions. Of course, it's only a 2-player game, which can be a downfall for many.

The Board Game version is similar in terms of gameplay. If you've already experienced the card game, I could teach you this version in about 30 seconds. Unfortunately, you'll soon want to be back playing the card game. This game lacks a certain something to make it really fun. It works, and it's still easy to learn and play, but I don't think I'll come back to it all that often unless I'm playing with my daughter. For those who are into more complex games, this one just feels...old fashioned. In all the ways that the card game has aged well, this one hasn't.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game

SHASHIBO Shape Shifting Box - Award-Winning, Patented Fidget Cube w/ 36 Rare Earth Magnets - Transforms Into Over 70 Shapes, Gift Box, Download Fun in Motion Toys Mobile App (Black & White, 4 Pack) This is much more fun than I thought it would be.

It's easy to get started, but gets really tough to figure out all the shapes when you know that there are *allegedly* over 70 shapes to make with it.

Right out of the box, it looks a lot like a weird little cube. It's maybe a little smaller than a standard Rubik's cube for comparison. But this cube is more complex, even though it doesn't have as many permutations as Rubik's.

The printed portions have nice patterns (on this cube, there are three different patterns depending on the configuration). Once you start playing with it, you can't put it down.

Even though it says in the instructions that you might have trouble getting it back to its cubic form, it's really not that hard and it also seems to be the default shape that you will keep returning to again and again, even when you're obsessing about discovering another shape.

I'd recommend this for anyone who enjoys puzzles and mind games. Even if they don't, this might get them thinking more spatially. There's a certain thrill of finding a new shape that you never knew was there. And the satisfying *click* sound when you get one. So far, I'm nowhere close to the 70+ that the box mentions. I can make a couple dozen, but then it's back to a cube. It's very weird even to try to duplicate the same shape you just had only a few seconds ago.

Nothing negative about this that I could find except maybe if the cube starts to wear out after a ton of usage. It seems to be made with vinyl stickers that will hopefully last a long time, though.

And one word of warning: I can imagine certain personality types getting frustrated with this and tearing it to a pile of tiny little plastic pyramids.

Overall, this gets a solid 5-stars. I'll probably get at least one more of these since they can be combined to create even more variations.
text_fidelity_b: SHASHIBO Shape Shifting Box - Award-Winning, Patented Fidget Cube w/ 36 Rare Earth Magnets - Transforms Into Over 70 Shapes, Gift Box, Download Fun in Motion Toys Mobile App (Black & White, 4 Pack)

The design almost works, but in the final assembly steps, I found the whole thing started to come apart around the middle of the undercarriage. It's a pretty common problem, but much worse than usual. Upon completion, I immediately took it all apart and built a nice little hinged treasure box that looks like it is made of some kind of stone inlay with petrified wood interior. That's the beauty of this kind of toy. Not just that it can be mixed into the ol' brick box for future creations, but also that a set like this provides a lot of parts that are already designed into a pleasing color scheme.

The colors are actually the first thing that caught my eye when I saw the box art.

There’s a fair amount of playability in the set, but it would also look good on display, if you have a Lego city set up. You can actually serve ice cream from the truck and drive it around.

The box includes 2 numbered bags and 2 instruction books. Both books build the truck. As usual with Lego, the instructions are clear, and should be doable by 5+.

There’s a big sticker sheet with this set, which I wasn’t super happy to see. Several of the stickers, such as the menu boards, need to be aligned or the truck looks a bit off. I’m quite the perfectionist with sticker placement. If you are too, I recommend using Windex on the piece to be stickered, and then you can slide the sticker around so that it’s in the exact spot you want it.

There are 2 included minifigures. They have one-sided faces and printed torso pieces. There’s also a cute little dog figure.

ThinkFun HypnoGraph Drawing Machine and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 8 and Up - Creates Mesmerizing Mechanical Art First, I recommend going to ThinkFun’s website and watch one of their setup videos because the directions that come in the box are missing some important steps. It was really frustrating trying to put this thing together the first time before I realized there were important steps missing in the written instructions.

The box I received said for ages 8 to Adult, but the picture on Amazon says for ages 14 to Adult. I believe this is a better product for older kids. The precision and accuracy needed to be successful with setting this up would frustrate a younger child. I’m going to try it in my 4th grade classroom and I foresee some loving it, and some getting really frustrated with it.

The really good thing about this is that eventually it becomes easier to setup as you practice and learn from it. So, once you play around with it and make some sloppy pictures, you start to make some really cool pictures. Once a child figures out how this works, they will be able to make tons of different pictures as they experiment with different combinations of gears.

text_fidelity_a:
Revell SnapTite Build & Play Rebel U-wing Fighter Building Kit This is a nice little introduction to Scale Models. You do not need anything that doesn't come in the box, and can easily build the model in a half hour. I grew up making Revell scale models and have tried several times to get my oldest son into them with some success. I wish I had these when I was trying to get him started on the hobby. The construction is easy and with no glue or painting needed it, it is pretty frustration free.

The model is not the finest craftsmanship, but the resulting model is decently detailed and has playability. The inclusion of a sound and light chip makes it more interactive than other scale models. Repositionable wings and removable landing gear also make it fun to play with after the build.

It is still a long way to from here to an actual scale model, but it was nice seeing my son confidently construct the model which has not happened with harder models. Hope this moves him further into the hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Revell SnapTite Build & Play Rebel U-wing Fighter Building Kit

UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Series: Overdrive Kit/App-Enabled Building and Coding STEM Learning Kit (410 Parts and Connectors), Yellow I really like the JIMU robots, because they're interesting to build, robust when completed, and easy to drive (using the free iOS or Android app). This UBTECH JIMU ROBOTS BUILDERBOTS SERIES OVERDRIVE KIT (410 Parts and Connectors) has everything you need to build a dump-truck robot (Dirtbot) or a dirt-mover robot (Dozerbot). It's a great kit for people (like me) who love building models of heavy construction equipment.

If you want, you can build one model, take it apart, and build the other model. However, be warned that the components are extremely hard to take apart. The components are completely interchangeable with the components in other JIMU robot sets. (The components are NOT compatible with LEGO Technic elements.) Combining JIMU sets gives you more flexibility if you want to create your own robots.

JIMU robots are controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once they're turned on or plugged into a power source. They don't have separate controllers, so you need a tablet or smartphone to work them. It’s a good idea to charge the controller cubes before you start building--charging takes about an hour--so that you can play with the robot as soon as you're finished building it.

Building instructions are NOT included in the box, except for a Quickstart guide that tells you where to get the detailed instructions. You have to download the JIMU app to get the building instructions. The detailed instructions are presented in 3D--at each step you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

The JIMU robots are moderately difficult to build, but older kids should be able to complete them. Once the robots are complete, you can use the Blockly coding system to program robotic moves beyond the models’ basic built-in moves. Blockly is part of the downloaded JIMU app.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Series: Overdrive Kit/App-Enabled Building and Coding STEM Learning Kit (410 Parts and Connectors), Yellow

Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab Fisher-Price Imaginext toys in general are great toys. Durable, bright colored plastic that often take after popular shows and movies such as Batman and Superman, Power Rangers, or in this case, Jurassic World. These toys have allowed my son's imagination to run wild and be creative as he plays for many hours with these. We often play together, but for the most part he's very happy to play with these on his own for hours at a time. I probably purchased my first Imaginext toy about 3 years ago, Batman and his Batcycle. It has held up to the test of time and a very rough preschooler. My son is now 6 with multiple sets.

Jurassic World has been all the rage in my house this summer because little boys love dinosaurs and that is certainly true of mine! So, take his love for Imaginext toys and mix that with his love for dinos and it's the perfect mashup! The only caveat is that on Amazon I have found the prices to vary greatly from in stores. Toys R Us (R.I.P.) was a great source for Imaginext because they always had the best and lowest price on these. They also had more selections. So, I would caution anyone to first look around Target or Walmart first. I once bought Batgirl and her Batcopter for $30 on Amazon and it was in Toys R Us for $15. I regularly see Imaginext toys in Target selling for $5-10 cheaper than on Amazon.

With the Fisher Price Imaginext Jurassic World Research Lab you get one T-Rex, one scientist, one harpoon, and one claw. There is a "decontamination" chamber for the scientist to get clean to study his subject. Simply turn the powerpad and the blue decontamination spiral gets the scientist ready. There is a powerpad to open and close the cage for the T-Rex. But watch out! The T-Rex might get loose! the lab is not that big. It's smaller than all of the Batcaves I've ever purchased. It's no bigger than any of the Paw Patrol sets I've purchased as well. So, it's east to tuck it away in a corner. All of the pieces, including the T-Rex, we've placed in a plastic show box for organization and storage. Overall, it's a fun play-set that provides hours of entertainment and keeps kids away from screens!

SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop A simple way to amuse and practice your shot, the SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop offers glow in the dark appeal, easy assembly, and hours of fun. It hooks on the top of most doors so you can lie in bed and practice shooting or attach it to your office door at work for some quick stress relief.

Out of the box, this basketball hoop requires some assembly, but it shouldn’t take long to attach the parts and prep it for use. The hooks that attach it to a door are not adjustable, but they are designed to fit a wide range of door thicknesses. After attaching, you may notice that it lacks stability. I noticed it, too, but I also found that it didn’t matter. It doesn’t need to be completely stable because the weight of the included basketball is so light. Throw after throw results in no bouncing or other movement for me, so don’t worry if the hoop seems less secure than you would prefer. Unless your door is very thin, it should be fine.

Once you have the ball inflated, the toy is ready for use. You may want to set everything in direct light for a few hours at first, to help with the glowing. If you don’t, then the glow will be very faint. Still, it should be enough to make it visible in the dark so that, if you use this at home, you or your kids can see it in the dark and play before you fall asleep. One thing that new buyers need to realize is that, due to the thickness of the hooks, it may not be possible to close the door to which this is attached. My door won’t close, but I attached it to a door that normally stays open all of the time anyway. If your door won’t close with this attached, then you will have no choice but to go back and forth, taking it down and putting it back up.

Overall, this seems like a good toy and it should be fun for the basketball enthusiast in your home. There is no glass and the construction is made to last. The glow in the dark feature could be better, but other than that, it seems like an entertaining way to pass the time.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop

Her red plastic shoes are removable as are her clothes- red pants, a lace trimmed pink polka dotted top with brown polka dotted bow and a beige canvas looking summer cap trimmed with a red ribbon and red and black fabric feathers. What makes the original Midori dolls so special are the personalities they have and happily they kept those personalities with these remakes. This adorable little Gege sucks her thumb. You may have to bend the arm with her thumb out a bit towards the doll before inserting her thumb, so it will stay in her mouth. However, to get the full karaoke effect you need the CDG disk. CDG stands for CD plus graphics, and that's where you get the lyrics and the little bouncing ball. There is an option to go to a web page and type in the date code and receipt number. The manufacturer promises the CDG in 4-6 weeks once the information has been confirmed. So, if you're purchasing this for a gift, open it and send off for the free disc before you lose your receipt. If you purchase this on Amazon, you should be able to retrieve your receipt number from your purchases list.

The unit itself is very portable and easy for children to handle. The microphone is small enough that they can hold it easily. The volume for the unit is acceptable, but it doesn't get so loud that it will give parents or neighbors a headache. I wish they had included the disc rather than have the mail in option. However, there are many Disney Karaoke discs available to be purchased separately.

This is a very fun product that will entertain your kids. It does involve a bit of screen time with the lyrics, but I feel singing is a very social activity that provides a lot of positive stimulation. Singing is a creative pursuit, and this is a fun toy for parties. Your kids will have a blast, and they might even learn the introductory elements of audio engineering as a bonus.

text_fidelity_a:
4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens My kids like their science, particularly my youngest who envisions, among other things, working for the government and taking part in the first mission to Mars. So, given my kids interest in all things scientific, the Tin Can Edge Detector looked like something they would enjoy building and examining from a scientific point of view.

Putting this little machine together takes some effort and one reason it takes more work than it should is the instructions. They are not written as clearly as they should be. It would not have been that difficult for the manufacturer to get this right, but it seems they put little effort into it. You have to supply your own battery and a can, but most importantly, you have to be patient and give it time. It’s also best to have an adult take charge, as young children will grow frustrated if they attempt this on their own.

Once assembled, you just place the robot on a table and let it do its thing. As expected, it moves across the surface until it detects an edge, then it reverses itself. It seemed to have no trouble doing what it claimed, and that is detecting when it reached the table’s edge and not falling off. In that respect, the robot functions as it should.

Now, what about the science? Well, It can teach a little bit about robotics, but that is about the extent of the educational value. There isn’t much else to it. Oh, and green advocates will like that it requires you to provide your own soda can because it encourages recycling

Science is a popular subject with my kids but they had a difficult time getting fired up over the Tin Can Edge Detector. The problem, from a kid’s perspective, is that it doesn’t really do enough to make it interesting. Simply crawling around on a table and not falling off just didn’t cut it for my kids. Adults will dislike the assembly more than anything and the limited educational value is also a drawback. Still, it does offer kids and parents an excuse to spend a little time together and it does what the manufacturer claims, so I’m going to give it a middle rating and a passing grade. There are better educational toys, but there is enough here to keep kids semi- interested for a low price.
text_fidelity_b: 4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens

text_fidelity_a:
The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends…… If you're familiar with the game Spyfall, then you're going to be able to jump right into this game. This one is quirkier, faster, but fortunately, has more replayability than Spyfall does.

In The Chameleon, each player is given a code card, or a card that says "You're the Chameleon." If you have a code card, you look up a word on a shared board, and if you're The Chameleon, you attempt to blend in with everyone else. After a little bit of finding and thinking time, each player says one word, even the Chameleon. Each player is then to attempt to argue and deduce who the Chameleon player is. Everyone votes, and that player is revealed. If it's not the Chameleon, then that player has done a good job of blending in and is the winner of the round. If it is the Chameleon, then that player gets the opportunity to guess the secret word that everyone else knew. If they get it right, they win. If not, everyone else wins.

Rounds of this game are fast, and that's a great thing. After repeat plays, it becomes fairly easy to identify the Chameleon player, but that's when the game really starts. Were you vague enough with your words so that they cannot figure out the secret code word?

There is enough replayability in this box to make the game fun for a wide range of groups, and a larger number of players. There are 40 different category clues, which means that there are 640 different possible words you could have, and that far exceeds the 20 locations of Spyfall.

Two issues prevent this from being a 5* game. The first is component quality. It's bad. Cards are awkwardly sized and flimsy, there are remainder marks on the edges of some cards from where they were cut. The second issue is that there simply aren't enough mapping location cards in the box. There's really only two possible sets of locations, and while there are no players who will be able to memorize the exact locations of words, it's possible that repeat mappings occur, and Chameleons with outstanding memories will be able to guess with regularity by reading the dice.
text_fidelity_b: The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends……

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

This is a better travel set than most, and it is larger than most I have seen too. It is well made and priced reasonably with the quality.

LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces) This LEGO CREATOR EXPERT VESTAS WIND TURBINE BUILDING KIT (10268; 826 Piece) is a fascinating set that’s much more fun than the advertising makes it appear. Its best feature is also its greatest drawback--the huge turbine blades take a lot of space to display and operate. The blades are motorized (with a servo hidden in the “Vestas” box at the top), and when they’re turning, the two house entrance lights turn on. What better way to dramatize the point that a single huge wind turbine can power thousands of homes?

The model is slightly challenging to build, because it calls for a lot of studs-not-on-top assembly. It’s especially interesting to see how the heavy wind turbine assemblage is secured to the base with only LEGO elements. The set does use specialized large green elements around the shaft to hide the battery box and to help hold the wind turbine firmly.

The model also demonstrates the one feature that bothers me about wind turbines as a source of electricity--they are huge, and loom over their surrounding landscape. The little house is dwarfed by the wind turbine. The house is cute, with windows and door that open, a range and sink, a lamp on a table, and a patio with a table and chairs (created from “repurposed” wheel-well elements).

The minifigs (two Vestas engineers, a female homeowner, and a dog) are great. The engineers have a van that holds their work bench and a hand truck loaded with service tanks and a big assortment of tools. The instruction book includes several pages describing the development of wind turbines as a power source, and showing diagrams of how they work to create electricity from wind currents.

The wind turbine on the model can be rotated by hand atop the shaft. Only the wind turbine blades are motorized. The blades are operated by a switch at the bottom of the shaft. The motor and lights run on 6 AA batteries (not included). The trees in the set are made from plants. (My LEGO Wind Turbine set was purchased from a LEGO Shop.)
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces)

We rated the other two 5 stars. This one is 3.5 to 4 stars. Generously rounded up to 4 stars.

The company did a good job of designing a realistic looking fire truck. They may have overdone the features. The hose is our main complaint. The crank handle was difficult for an adult to turn. This problem appears to vary with each unit. For example, others complained about hard to turn cranks on the garbage trucks. Ours was very smooth on the garbage truck. The hose looks very fragile. We elected not to put water in the reservoir. Unfortunate, because it would have been a fun feature.

Other than the hose issue, it’s a nice item. The main ladder cranks up easily, and then a second, smaller crank handle take another section higher. That is a very nice feature that our grandsons enjoy. The doors open, the lights go on when the engine is started, and the horn beeps. It is not motorized and the engine starts, but the truck does not move unless pushed.

Durability?

In addition to questionable durability on the hose, rough play may damage the large ladder which is the best feature of the truck. To date, the Fire Engine has stood up well to a 2 and 4 year old.

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ We absolutely love our dinosaurs, dragons, and lifelike statues of real animals from this brand, and this extra-large dinosaur is no exception. The thing you should know about these is that they are a very hard resin like material. This makes them much better for children who are old enough to use the statues responsibly and not bash them on things such as their little sister, because they are very hard and heavy and have absolutely no give to them. On this particular model, the end of the tail is the most dangerous part aside from the sheer size and weight of the overall piece.

This dinosaur is much larger than the cheapo dinosaurs that you get in multi-packs that are made in China, and the level of craftsmanship and detail here is sufficient for even the most exacting dinosaur connoisseur. That said, though the description talks about scoop shaped teeth being a major part of what makes this dinosaur cool, I was unable to really discern much scoop detail on the teeth, given the relative size of the teeth versus the relative size of the dinosaur. Just something to be aware of. But that's not me complaining about the level of detail.

I love the artistic detailing on the hide, the bluish bumps on the back, the little spines, and the huge amount of expression in the face. My toddler son is just beginning a dinosaur phase and enjoyed stomping this large dinosaur through his truck collection and roaring with great feeling. I think that as his knowledge of dinosaurs expands, so will his appreciation of all the small differentiating details that give this dinosaur personality, character, and most importantly, accuracy.

As long as you are aware of the hard and heavy resin material used to create these, you will be deeply impressed by the detailing, durability, and potential for imaginative play inherent in the figure.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+

text_fidelity_a:
Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up My oldest son(5) recently started daily injections. As you would expect, he hates them. We try to do something fun after each of them, and this was used as one of his "surprises". It did the trick and took his mind off that mean needle.

This game is really fun! Not only did my children enjoy it, but I did, too. It does come with a few issues, though.

First of all, as I put the thing together, the instructions say to never use your mouth to blow up the balloon. You must use a balloon pump. A balloon pump isn't included, so I chose to use my mouth to blow up the balloon, since I had excited children waiting to play. It went fine. I was able to blow up the balloon while it was in the frame without any problem.

Secondly, we couldn't get the top clip piece to stay put. There's a clip that holds the 3 pieces of the frame together at the top. It kept coming lose no matter how tight I tried to get it. When I took the thing apart, I couldn't get one frame piece to come apart. So, 2 were so lose the whole thing kept coming apart, but one was so tight I had to put it in the box together, and therefore, couldn't close the lid.

Third, one of the sticks was broke within minutes of playing the game. Thankfully, there are 4 extras included, so we can still play. Plus, the recommended age is 8 and up. I played this game with my 2 and 5 year olds. The 2 year old is the one that broke the stick, so I'm not taking stars off for that issue or anything. It's simply to warn you that they do break pretty easily.

There are 12 balloons included. They are all the same: blue, with a face. They are the regular sized balloons, so I imagine this game will work perfectly fine with store bought replacement balloons. You just probably won't have a face on there.

I know it sounds like a lot of complaining up there, but we really enjoyed this game!

The basics: You put the thing together, which is really simple. You put the balloon in the frame, blow it up, and then wrap it around the "hook" at the bottom to keep the air in without having to actually tie it. Super simple. You take the sticks and put them in the holes(6) until you hear the first click. Then you take turns rolling dice. Whatever number it lands on is the amount of times you push in a stick. It can be the same stick or one click each on different sticks. Whoever pops the balloon first loses(or wins if you're my children).

Overall, it's a fun game that's worth the issues that come with it.
text_fidelity_b: Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up

LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces) As a child, I loved pop-up books, so of course I love all of the LEGO pop-up book building kits. The first one (see [[ASIN:B07GYB8D34 LEGO Pop-Up Book]] originated as a fan model submitted to the LEGO Ideas fan-voting site (if you want to participate, just google for LEGO Ideas). This DISNEY MULAN’S STORYBOOK ADVENTURES 43174 BUILDING KIT (New 2020 (124 Pieces)) is a smaller, simpler version of the original pop-up book, but it’s still a lot of fun.

The basic pop-up feature is the arched bridge that goes from the center--the book’s stationary spine, where Mulan’s buildings are--to the little “tea service” island in the left half of the book. The bridge goes up and down on a LEGO hinge, and snaps into place when the book is completely open.

There are LEGO studs strategically placed around the open book, so that the three dolls, Mulan’s pony, and Mulan’s cricket cage can all be firmly attached at once. This way, they don’t rattle around loose (or get lost) when the book is closed to be put away. When the book is open for play, the dolls fit on the bridge, under the arches, and can stand anywhere on the book surface.

The assembly instructions are reasonably easy to follow--just look closely at the pictures. I had to take my book covers apart and reassemble them because I got the left (blue water) and right (white land) sides switched, so that the water was on the wrong side when the book was opened.

There are quite a few stickers, but only a few that need to be carefully placed on LEGO elements. The instructions aren’t terribly clear on where to place the stickers that go onto the book’s interior surfaces (e.g., the swimming Koi fish, the lily pads, Mulan’s bed roll, the campfire, the cooking supplies). You can consult the box photos, or even the photos in the online LEGO Shop, if you want extra guidance for these.

One of my favorite features is the two little tassels or bells that swing from Mulan’s temple-like building. I don’t know whether this is an entirely new LEGO element, or whether it has appeared in other sets, but it was new to me. There are enough LEGO pieces in the set to make the book interesting to assemble; and the book is fun to play with after it’s built.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Aori Sleeping Reborn Baby Dolls 22 Inch Lifelike Newborn Baby Girl Doll Real Life Weighted Reborn Baby Toddler with Closed Eyes Christmas Baby Doll Deer Gift Set for Kids Age 3 + PROS

1. This doll has adorable, lifelike features. Its hair and eyelashes are made of realistic-looking mohair, and it has half-moon-shaped fingernails and toenails. The head, arms, legs, hands and feet are made of smooth, soft, silicone vinyl.

2. This doll is 22 inches long, as advertised, which is the size of a typical newborn baby. For changes of clothing, you can purchase newborn or size 0-3 months clothing.

3. The arms and legs are poseable. The body is of stuffed fabric, and it is slightly weighted (4 lbs), which gives the doll a realistic feel when cuddled in the child’s arms. When completely undressed, the cloth body gives the appearance that the doll is wearing a “onesie” with short sleeves. Note: because it has a cloth body, this is not an “anatomically correct” baby doll.

4. This doll comes in an attractive gift box with the following accessories included: 1 set of clothing (a beanie hat, a shirt, and pants), 1 baby blanket, 1 plush lion toy, 1 pacifier, 1 baby bottle, 1 birth certificate.

5. The price is quite reasonable for what you get.

6. This manufacturer offers a wide selection of different types of newborn baby dolls.

CONS

1. The hair is too fragile to be combed. Though the doll comes with instructions that clearly warn against doing that, the problem is, how do you convince a very young child not to comb this particular doll’s hair when it is safe for them to comb the hair of the majority of their other dolls? If all else fails, and the child accidentally pulls out this doll’s hair while combing it, the beanie hat that comes with this doll can be used to cover its resulting baldness.

NEUTRAL

1. Similar to every other doll of this type of construction, with a stuffed, cloth body, this doll should not be immersed in water to clean it. Most especially, it should NOT be put in the washer. Here are some alternatives I have personally found useful over the years for cleaning this type of doll:

Vinyl body parts: You will need baby wipes or a thin, soft, cotton baby washcloth and a soft-bristled toothbrush or a straw brush. Moisten the washcloth with warm water (it should not be dripping wet, just damp) or use a pre-moistened baby wipe to gently cleanse the doll’s vinyl surfaces. Use a dampened (not dripping wet) toothbrush or straw brush to get inside the mouth, inside and around the ears, and between the fingers and toes.

Cloth body: Ideally, if the child can be convinced to keep this doll clothed at all times (a tricky proposition), its cloth body is less likely to get soiled. If it does get dirty, you can use this stain-removing trick to clean the cloth: squirt a teaspoon of dish soap into a bowl, add a teaspoon of hydrogen peroxide and a teaspoon of baking soda, then stir these ingredients into a paste. Insert your pointer finger inside a regular washcloth and wet the portion covering your finger. (It should not be dripping wet, just damp.) Dip the damp portion of the washcloth into the paste, then rub the paste into any existing stains on the cloth body of the doll. Most stains will rub right out, but if it is a stubborn stain, allow the paste to sit on the cloth for an hour or so. Wet another clean portion of the washcloth and gently wipe away the paste. If the paste doesn’t all come out the first try, repeat the process using another clean, damp area of the washcloth.

Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart This CRAFT-TASTIC 3D STRING ART KIT provides an inexpensive (about $6.25 on Amazon) introduction to the string art craft. It includes a snap-together plastic frame, plenty of colored embroidery floss for string, and reasonably clear instructions. The box says it's for ages 8 and up, which seems about right. (Adult help might be needed to assemble the frame, which requires the pegs to be properly oriented upwards or downwards for everything to snap together tightly.)

There is some artistic creativity involved with this kit, as there are no stringing diagrams to follow. Instead, the instructions say to knot your string to a peg in the frame, and then "wrap the thread from a peg in one (upper) heart to a peg on the other side (the lower heart)." This is simple enough, but it's up to you to choose the pegs so that you get an eye-pleasing criss-crossing of the thread.

Personally, I don't care for the color combinations: bright blue small inside heart, purple edge for the large outside heart, yellow front of large outside heart, pink back of large outside heart. When you're finished with all the stringing, you can set the big heart up on a little plastic stand.

A small child might enjoy this project a lot. However, being an adult, I was bored by the time I'd finished the small blue heart. Because this kit persuaded me that I don't care for the string art craft, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale). However, the budget price probably makes it a reasonable purchase if the intent is to keep a small child busy.
text_fidelity_b: Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart
